It also inserts a new section 14-A restricting election eligibility for individuals who were office bearers immediately before the society was taken over, unless Government permission is obtained. The Act came into force immediately but is deemed effective from September 24, 1985.

metadata.short_title: The Coastal Development Authority (Amendment) Act, 2006
metadata.long_title: An act to amend the Coastal Development Authority Act, 1994.
metadata.one_line: Amends the Coastal Development Authority Act, 1994 by renaming the authority and restructuring its governing body.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the Coastal Development Authority Act, 1994 to change the name of the authority from 'Coastal Development Authority' to 'Sindh Coastal Development Authority'. It restructures the Governing Body to include secretaries from ten specific government departments, district coordination officers, provincial assembly members, and eminent persons. The Act also defines the powers of the Director General as the Chief Executive and assigns the Minister for Planning & Development Department as the Chairman.

metadata.short_title: The Coastal Development Authority Act, 1994
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for development, improvement and beautification of the coastal areas of the Districts Thatta and Badin and to establish an Authority for such purpose.
repeals: The coastal Development Authority Ordinance, 1994
metadata.one_line: Establishes the Coastal Development Authority to develop and beautify coastal areas in Thatta and Badin districts.
metadata.summary: This Act establishes the Coastal Development Authority to oversee the development, improvement, and beautification of coastal areas in the Districts of Thatta and Badin. The Authority is a body corporate with a Governing Body comprising government secretaries, district deputy commissioners, assembly members, and eminent persons. It empowers the Authority to acquire property, prepare master plans, and manage funds while submitting annual reports to the Government.

name: CODE OF CIVIL PROCEDURE (SINDH AMENDMENT) ACT, 2018

metadata.short_title: The Code of Civil Procedure (Sindh Amendment) Act, 2018
metadata.long_title: An Act Further to amend the Code of Civil Procedure Act (Act No. V of 1908).
amends: The Code of Civil Procedure Act (Act No. V of 1908)
metadata.one_line: Amends the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908 to incorporate Alternative Dispute Resolution mechanisms in Sindh.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908 to further integrate Alternative Dispute Resolution (ADR) methods into the legal framework of Sindh. It defines key terms such as mediation and conciliation, mandates courts to refer civil or commercial cases to ADR under specific circumstances, and establishes rules for the appointment and conduct of mediators/conciliators. The Act also ensures the confidentiality of ADR proceedings and outlines eligibility criteria for mediators, including accredited organizations and trained individuals.

name: CODE OF CRIMINAL PROCEDURE (SINDH AMENDMENT) ACT, 2017

metadata.short_title: The Code of Criminal Procedure (Sindh Amendment) Act, 2017
metadata.long_title: An Act to amend the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1898, in its application to the Province of Sindh.
metadata.one_line: Amends the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1898 in Sindh to mandate DNA testing for rape cases.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1898 specifically for its application to the Province of Sindh. It mandates that DNA testing be conducted on rape victims within seventy-two hours by a Police Officer using recognized laboratories. The Act also requires the preservation of DNA samples and results in privacy at hospitals or forensic labs, with records maintained confidentially at the Central Police Office.

metadata.short_title: The Colonization of Government Lands (Amendment) Act, 2010
metadata.long_title: An Act to amend the Colonization of Government Lands Act, 1912.
metadata.commencement: at once and shall be deemed to have taken effect on and from 10th day of October, 2010
metadata.one_line: Amends the Colonization of Government Lands Act, 1912 to allow the Chief Minister to extend project completion periods for education and health land grants.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the Colonization of Government Lands Act, 1912 by modifying Section 10. It empowers the Chief Minister to extend the period for completing projects on land granted for education and health purposes. This extension applies specifically when delays are not caused by negligence on the part of the grantee.

metadata.short_title: The Colonization of Government Lands (Amendment) Act, 2009
metadata.long_title: An Act to further amend the Colonization of Government Lands Act, 1912.
amends: The Colonization of Government Lands Act, 1912
metadata.one_line: Amends the 1912 Act regarding land colonization, deposit timelines, and resumption of misused government land in Sindh.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the Colonization of Government Lands Act, 1912 to introduce stricter conditions for land grantees in Sindh. It mandates that failure to deposit occupancy prices within three months or failing to use land for its intended purpose within two years will result in automatic withdrawal or cancellation of the grant, along with forfeiture of deposits. Additionally, it inserts a new section allowing the resumption of land granted for specific purposes if used for any other purpose, while preserving rights for agricultural lands on a permanent basis.

name: COLONIZATION OF GOVERNMENT LANDS (SINDH AMENDMENT) ACT, 1995

metadata.short_title: The Colonization of Government Lands (Sindh Amendment) Act, 1995
metadata.long_title: An Act to amend the Colonization of Government Lands Act, 1912.
amends: The Colonization of Government Lands Act, 1912
repeals: The Colonization of Government Lands (Sindh Amendment) Ordinance, 1995
metadata.one_line: Amends the 1912 Colonization Act to prohibit exchanging specific government land with private or kabuli land.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the Colonization of Government Lands Act, 1912 by inserting a new sub-section in section 10 and adding a proviso to section 17. The amendments explicitly forbid the exchange of certain government lands with private or kabuli land. Additionally, the Act repeals the earlier Colonization of Government Lands (Sindh Amendment) Ordinance, 1995.

name: COLONIZATION OF GOVERNMENT LANDS (SINDH AMENDMENT) ACT, 2011

metadata.short_title: The Colonization of Government Lands (Sindh Amendment) Act, 2011
metadata.long_title: An Act to amend the Colonization of Government Lands Act, 1912, in its application to the Province of Sindh.
metadata.one_line: Amends the Colonization of Government Lands Act, 1912 regarding time limits for Sindh.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the application of the Colonization of Government Lands Act, 1912 to the Province of Sindh. It substitutes 'three months' with 'six months' and 'two years' with 'five years' in specific clauses of section 10. The amendments came into force immediately upon enactment.

metadata.short_title: The Colonization of Government Lands Act, 1912
metadata.long_title: An Act to make better provision for the Colonization and administration of Government lands in Sindh.
metadata.territorial_extent: the whole of the Province of Sindh
repeals: Act III of 1893
metadata.one_line: This Act regulates the colonization and administration of government lands in Sindh, defining tenant rights and proprietorship.
metadata.summary: The Colonization of Government Lands Act, 1912 provides for the better administration of government lands in the Province of Sindh. It establishes rules regarding tenancy conditions, succession rights for tenants and proprietors, and penalties for breaches or false information. The Act also defines specific terms such as 'Colony' and 'Improvements', and bars civil court jurisdiction over matters arising under it.

name: COMMECS INSTITUTE OF BUSINESS AND EMERGING SCIENCES ACT, 2009

metadata.short_title: The Commecs Institute of Business and Emerging Sciences Act, 2009
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the establishment of Commecs Institute of Business and Emerging Sciences, Karachi
establishes: Commecs Institute of Business and Emerging Sciences, Karachi
metadata.one_line: Establishes the Commecs Institute of Business and Emerging Sciences in Karachi and defines its powers, structure, and functions.
metadata.summary: This Act establishes the Commecs Institute of Business and Emerging Sciences in Karachi as a body corporate with perpetual succession. It outlines the institute's powers to conduct education, research, and examinations while ensuring openness to all regardless of background. The legislation creates governing bodies including the Board of Governors, Academic Council, and Finance and Planning Committee to manage the institute's operations.

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Companies Profits (Workers Participation) (Amendment) Act, 2017
metadata.long_title: An Act to amend to the Sindh Companies Profits (Workers Participation) Act, 2015.
metadata.commencement: at once and deemed to have taken effect on 1st day of July 2011
amends: The Sindh Companies Profits (Workers Participation) Act, 2015
metadata.one_line: Amends the Sindh Companies Profits (Workers Participation) Act, 2015 regarding jurisdiction and wage references.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the Sindh Companies Profits (Workers Participation) Act, 2015 to remove geographical restrictions on 'in Pakistan' and update references to minimum wages and workers welfare funds. It specifically deletes the phrase 'in Pakistan' from section 2 of the parent Act and substitutes references to the Sindh Minimum Wages Act, 2015 and the Sindh Workers Welfare Fund Act, 2014 in the Schedule. The amendment came into force immediately upon enactment but is deemed effective from July 1, 2011.

name: CONSTITUTION OF THE SEARCH COMMITTEE ACT, 2022

metadata.short_title: The Constitution of the Search Committee Act, 2022
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the constitution of the Search Committee for appointment and evaluation of the performance of the Vice Chancellors and other officers of the universities in public sector universities in the Province of Sindh.
metadata.one_line: Constitutes a Search Committee in Sindh to appoint and evaluate Vice Chancellors and officers of public sector universities.
metadata.summary: This Act establishes the Constitution of the Search Committee for the Province of Sindh. The committee is tasked with appointing Vice Chancellors and other officers in public sector universities by setting recruitment criteria, shortlisting candidates, conducting interviews, and evaluating performance. It consists of members from the Sindh Higher Education Commission, various government departments, and co-opted experts nominated by the Chief Minister.

name: CONSTITUTIONAL BENCHES OF HIGH COURT OF SINDH (PRACTICE AND PROCEDURE) ACT, 2025

metadata.short_title: The Constitutional Benches of High Court of Sindh (Practice and Procedure) Act, 2025
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for practice and procedure of the Constitutional Benches of the High Court of Sindh.
metadata.commencement: at once and deemed to have taken effect on and from the date of commencement of the Constitution (Twenty-seventh Amendment) Act, 2025
repeals: The High Court of Sindh (Practice and Procedure) Ordinance, 2025
establishes: Committee for Constitution of Constitutional Benches
metadata.one_line: This Act regulates the practice, procedure, and administration of Constitutional Benches of the High Court of Sindh.
metadata.summary: This Act provides for the practice and procedure regarding the Constitutional Benches of the High Court of Sindh. It establishes a Committee to assist in constituting these benches and defines the roles of the Head and nominated Judges. The Act outlines jurisdiction, case transfer powers, honorariums, and administrative support while repealing the previous 2025 Ordinance.

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Consumer Protection (Amendment) Act, 2019
metadata.long_title: An Act to amend the Sindh Consumer Protection Act, 2014.
metadata.one_line: Amends the Sindh Consumer Protection Act, 2014 to update definitions and court jurisdictions.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the Sindh Consumer Protection Act, 2014 to introduce new definitions for 'Consumer Court' and 'claim'. It substitutes references to the Consumer Council with the Consumer Court and changes jurisdiction from the Sindh High Court to the District and Sessions Court. The amendments apply to proceedings at any stage of trial rather than just the pre-trial stage.

name: CONTROL OF NARCOTICS SUBSTANCE (SINDH AMENDMENT) ACT, 2021

metadata.short_title: The Control of Narcotics Substance (Sindh Amendment) Act, 2021
metadata.long_title: An Act to amend the Control of Narcotics Substance Act, 1997, in its application to the Province of Sindh.
metadata.max_penalty: death or imprisonment for life or imprisonment for a term which may extend to fourteen years and fine up to one million rupees
metadata.one_line: Amends the Control of Narcotics Substance Act, 1997 to include new definitions and prohibitions on narcotics in Sindh.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the Control of Narcotics Substance Act, 1997 specifically for its application to the Province of Sindh. It introduces new definitions for substances like methamphetamine and midomafetamine and adds a prohibition on manufacturing or selling psychotropic substances. The Act also substitutes existing sections to update punishments for contraventions based on drug quantities.

name: CRIMINAL PROSECUTION SERVICE (CONSTITUTION, FUNCTIONS AND POWERS) (AMENDMENT) ACT, 2025

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Criminal Prosecution Service (Constitution, Functions and Powers) (Amendment) Act, 2025
metadata.long_title: An Act to amend the Sindh Criminal Prosecution Service (Constitution, Functions and Powers) Act, 2009.
amends: The Sindh Criminal Prosecution Service (Constitution, Functions and Powers) Act, 2009
metadata.one_line: Amends the 2009 Sindh Criminal Prosecution Service Act regarding supervision and subsections.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the Sindh Criminal Prosecution Service (Constitution, Functions and Powers) Act, 2009. It substitutes Section 5 to clarify that prosecutors perform functions under the control of the Prosecutor General and general superintendence of Government. Additionally, it modifies Section 5 sub-section (4) references and omits specific subsections from Sections 5 and 6 of the parent Act.

name: DADABHOY INSTITUTE OF HIGHER EDUCATOIN ACT, 2003

metadata.short_title: The Dadabhoy Institute of Higher Education Act, 2003
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the establishment of an Institute at Karachi known as the Dadabhoy Institute of Higher Education.
repeals: Sindh Ordinance No.III of 2003
establishes: Board of Advanced Studies and Research
metadata.one_line: Establishes the Dadabhoy Institute of Higher Education in Karachi and defines its structure, powers, and governance.
metadata.summary: This Act establishes the Dadabhoy Institute of Higher Education at Karachi as a body corporate with perpetual succession. It outlines the institute's powers to conduct education, examinations, and research while remaining under the general control of the Government of Sindh. The legislation defines the composition and functions of key authorities including the Board of Governors, Academic Council, and various committees responsible for finance, faculty selection, and academic planning.

name: DAWOOD UNIVERSITY OF ENGINEERING AND TECHNOLOGY ACT, 2013

metadata.short_title: The Dawood University of Engineering and Technology Act, 2013
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the establishment of the University known as the Dawood University of Engineering and Technology at Karachi.
establishes: Dawood University of Engineering and Technology
metadata.one_line: Establishes the Dawood University of Engineering and Technology at Karachi and defines its authorities, functions, and regulations.
metadata.summary: This Act establishes the Dawood University of Engineering and Technology located in Karachi. It creates various governing bodies including the Senate, Syndicate, and Academic Council to manage university affairs. The legislation also outlines procedures for affiliating educational institutions, managing the university fund, and establishing disciplinary committees.

name: DENNING INSTITUTE OF TECHNOLOGY AND ENTREPRENEURSHIP ACT, 2025

metadata.short_title: The Denning Institute of Technology and Entrepreneurship Act, 2025
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the establishment of the Denning Institute of Technology and Entrepreneurship at Karachi.
establishes: Denning Institute of Technology and Entrepreneurship
metadata.one_line: Establishes the Denning Institute of Technology and Entrepreneurship at Karachi as an autonomous body owned by the Foundation.
metadata.summary: This Act establishes the Denning Institute of Technology and Entrepreneurship at Karachi as a body corporate owned and administered by the Denning Educational Foundation. The Institute is granted autonomy to promote learning, conduct research, award degrees, and manage its property while adhering to general instructions from the Government of Sindh. It defines various internal authorities including the Board, Academic Council, and Chancellor, and outlines powers for curriculum development and campus expansion.

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Digital Technology Board Act, 2022
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for establishment of a Board to be known as the Sindh Digital Technology Board; for promotion, planning, execution, supervision, evaluation and regulations of digital technologies to boost the digital economy by enabling e-government, promoting innovation, capacity building, supporting IT sector and collaborating with stakeholder at Province, Federal and International level; and to provide for matters ancillary thereto.
metadata.territorial_extent: the whole of Province of Sindh
metadata.administering_body: Information, Science and Technology Department, Government of Sindh
metadata.one_line: Establishes the Sindh Digital Technology Board to promote digital technologies and boost the digital economy in Sindh.
metadata.summary: This Act establishes the Sindh Digital Technology Board to promote, plan, execute, supervise, evaluate, and regulate digital technologies. The Board aims to boost the digital economy through e-government initiatives, innovation promotion, capacity building, and supporting the IT sector. It collaborates with stakeholders at provincial, federal, and international levels and provides for the constitution of a Governing Body, rules-making powers, and administrative procedures.

metadata.short_title: The Domestic Violence (Prevention and Protection) Act, 2013
metadata.long_title: An Act to make provisions for protection against domestic violence.
metadata.territorial_extent: the whole of the Province of Sindh
metadata.one_line: This Act provides protection against domestic violence through protection orders, residence orders, and monetary relief.
metadata.summary: The Domestic Violence (Prevention and Protection) Act, 2013 institutionalizes measures to prevent and protect women, children, and vulnerable persons from domestic violence within the Province of Sindh. It establishes a Commission to review laws and advise on planning for safe environments, while constituting Protection Committees to oversee implementation. The Act empowers courts to grant protection orders, residence orders, custody orders, and monetary relief, and defines the roles of Protection Officers and service providers in assisting aggrieved persons.

name: DOW UNIVERSITY OF HEALTH SCIENCES (AMENDMENT) ACT, 2005

metadata.short_title: The Dow University of Heath Sciences (Amendment) Act, 2005
metadata.long_title: An act to amend the Dow Preamble. University of Heath, Sciences Act, 2004.
amends: Dow University of Heath Sciences Act, 2004
subjects: exercise of option within ninety days
metadata.one_line: Amends the Dow University of Health Sciences Act, 2004 regarding personnel transfer options to the Health Department.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the Dow University of Health Sciences Act, 2004 to introduce provisions for personnel transferred to the university. It allows such individuals, including those who have not yet reported, to opt to serve in the Health Department instead. The option must be exercised and submitted to the Government within ninety days of the Ordinance's commencement, after which the decision is final. Upon receipt of this option, the Government may transfer the person or allow them to continue service in the Health Department.

name: DOW UNIVERSITY OF HEALTH SCIENCES (AMENDMENT) ACT, 2022

metadata.short_title: The Dow University of Health Sciences (Amendment) Act, 2022
metadata.long_title: An Act to amend the Dow University of Health Sciences Act, 2004.
amends: Dow University of Health Sciences Act, 2004
key_definitions: Director Office of Research Innovation and Commercialization
metadata.one_line: Amends the Dow University of Health Sciences Act, 2004 to add new officers, expand financial powers, and list constituent colleges.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the Dow University of Health Sciences Act, 2004 to introduce new administrative roles such as Chief Information Officer and various Directors. It expands the University's financial powers regarding property management, investments, and corporate partnerships. The legislation also updates the list of constituent colleges and modifies the role of the Chief Minister in university governance.

name: DOW UNIVERSITY OF HEALTH SCIENCES ACT, 2004

metadata.short_title: The DOW University of Health Sciences Act, 2004
metadata.long_title: An Act to establish a University known as the Dow University of Health Sciences.
metadata.commencement: at once and be deemed to have taken effect on and from 29th March, 2004
establishes: Dow University of Health Sciences, Karachi
metadata.one_line: Establishes the Dow University of Health Sciences in Karachi and defines its structure, authorities, and functions.
metadata.summary: This Act establishes the Dow University of Health Sciences as a body corporate with perpetual succession. It outlines the composition of the university, including the Chancellor, Vice-Chancellor, Senate, Syndicate, and Academic Council. The legislation also details the powers and duties of these authorities, provisions for staff, assets, and financial management, as well as mechanisms for student discipline and affiliation of colleges.

name: DR. ZIAUDDIN POST GRADUATE INSTITUTE OF MEDICAL SCIENCES ACT, 1994

metadata.short_title: Dr. Ziauddin Post Graduate Institute of Medical Sciences Act, 1994
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the establishment of Dr. Ziauddin Post-Graduate Institute of Medical Sciences.
repeals: Dr. Ziauddin Post Graduate Institute of Medical Sciences Ordinance, 1994
establishes: Dr. Ziauddin Post-Graduate Institute of Medical Sciences
metadata.one_line: Establishes Dr. Ziauddin Post-Graduate Institute of Medical Sciences in Karachi with powers to award degrees and manage research.
metadata.summary: This Act establishes the Dr. Ziauddin Post-Graduate Institute of Medical Sciences at Karachi as a corporate body with perpetual succession. It confers powers on the Institute to provide post-graduate medical education, conduct research, hold examinations, and award degrees and diplomas. The Institute is open to all persons regardless of sex, religion, race, caste, creed, colour, or domicile, and its activities are overseen by a Board of Governors chaired by the chief Trustee.

metadata.short_title: The Drugs (Sindh Amendment) Act, 2020
metadata.long_title: An Act to amend the Drugs Act, 1976 (Act No. XXXI if 1976), in its application to the Province of Sindh.
metadata.one_line: Amends the Drugs Act, 1976 in Sindh by substituting Provincial Government for Federal Government and transferring Drug Court powers.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the Drugs Act, 1976 as it applies to the Province of Sindh. It substitutes 'Provincial Government' for 'Federal Government' throughout the amended sections and changes references to 'members' to 'full-time members'. Additionally, it transfers all powers exercisable by the Federal Government regarding existing Drug Courts in Sindh to the Provincial Government upon commencement.

metadata.short_title: The Education City (Amendment) Act, 2020
metadata.long_title: An Act to amend the Education City Act, 2013.
metadata.one_line: Amends the Education City Act, 2013 by substituting the composition of the Board.
metadata.summary: This Act amends Section 3 of the Education City Act, 2013 to update the composition of the Board. The amendment specifies new members including government secretaries from various departments, representatives from the Provincial Assembly and National Assembly, and nominees from the corporate sector. It also includes a Vice Chancellor or Dean and a nominee from the Higher Education Commission.

metadata.short_title: The Education City (Amendment) Act, 2021
metadata.long_title: An Act to amend the Education City Act, 2013.
metadata.one_line: Amends the Education City Act, 2013 by updating definitions and Board composition.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the Education City Act, 2013 to update specific definitions regarding the Project Director and Project Implementation Unit. It also substitutes Section 3 to redefine the composition of the Board, including new members from government departments and stakeholders. The amendments come into force immediately upon enactment.

metadata.short_title: The Education City Act, 2013
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for establishment of education cities in the Province of Sindh and to provide for matters connected therewith or ancillary thereto.
metadata.territorial_extent: the whole of the Province of Sindh
establishes: Sindh Board of Investment (Education City Board)
metadata.one_line: Establishes the Education City Board to manage education cities in Sindh, including land allotment and infrastructure.
metadata.summary: This Act provides for the establishment of education cities within the Province of Sindh. It constitutes a Board responsible for strategic vision, land management, and infrastructure development within these cities. The Board has powers to grant permits, oversee master plans, and enforce compliance regarding water conservation and building standards.

name: EMAAN INSTITUTE OF MANAGEMENT AND SCIENCES AT KARACHI ACT, 2018.

metadata.short_title: The EMAAN Institute of Management and Sciences at Karachi Act, 2018
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the establishment of the EMAAN Institute of Management and Sciences at Karachi.
establishes: EMAAN Institute of Management and Sciences at Karachi
metadata.one_line: Establishes the EMAAN Institute of Management and Sciences at Karachi as an autonomous body owned by the AL HAMD Educational Society.
metadata.summary: This Act establishes the EMAAN Institute of Management and Sciences at Karachi as a body corporate owned and administered by the AL HAMD Educational Society. The Institute is granted autonomy to manage its affairs, establish faculties, prescribe curricula, award degrees, and maintain an institute fund derived from fees and donations. The Act defines various authorities including the Board of Governors, Academic Council, and committees for finance and discipline, while also providing for the enactment of statutes, regulations, and rules to govern the Institute's operations.

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Employees Social Security (Amendment) Act, 2018
metadata.long_title: An Act to amend the Sindh Employees Social Security Act, 2016.
metadata.administering_body: Labour and Human Resources Department, Government of Sindh
metadata.one_line: This Act amends the Sindh Employees Social Security Act, 2016 to update definitions, benefits, and administrative structures.
metadata.summary: The document serves as an amendment to the Sindh Employees Social Security Act, 2016. It updates various sections regarding contributions, wage limits, trade union definitions, and the composition of governing bodies. The Act also introduces new definitions for terms like 'Self-Assessment Scheme' and modifies provisions related to benefits payable in cases of sickness, maternity, or death.

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Employees Social Security (Amendment) Act, 2021
metadata.long_title: An Act to amend the Sindh Employees Social Security Act, 2016.
amends: The Sindh Employees Social Security Act, 2016
metadata.one_line: Amends the Sindh Employees Social Security Act, 2016 to include self-employed workers and introduce smart cards.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the Sindh Employees Social Security Act, 2016 to expand coverage to self-employed workers. It defines 'self-employed worker' to include daily wages, construction, home-based, transport, fisheries, agriculture, and seasonal workers. The Act also introduces a new section requiring these workers to pay contributions at a fixed rate of fifteen hundred rupees per month.

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Epidemic Diseases (Amendment) Act, 2020
metadata.long_title: An Act to amend the Sindh Epidemic Disease Act, 2014.
repeals: The Sindh Epidemic Disease (Amendment) Ordinance, 2020
metadata.max_penalty: fine up to rupees one million or attachment of movable, immovable, perishable property or both
metadata.one_line: Amends the Sindh Epidemic Diseases Act, 2014 by expanding officer powers and increasing penalties.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the Sindh Epidemic Diseases Act, 2014 to include Assistant Commissioners in enforcement orders. It substitutes Section 4 to increase penalties for disobeying government orders to a fine of up to one million rupees or property attachment. The Act also repeals the corresponding Ordinance from 2020 and comes into force immediately.

name: ESSENTIAL COMMODITIES PRICE CONTROL AND PREVENTION OF PROFITEERING AND HOARDING (AMENDMENT) ACT, 2023

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Essential Commodities Price Control and Prevention of Profiteering and Hoarding (Amendment) Act, 2023
metadata.long_title: An Act to amend the Sindh Essential Commodities Price Control and Prevention of Profiteering and Hoarding Act, 2005.
amends: Sindh Essential Commodities Price Control and Prevention of Profiteering and Hoarding Act, 2005
repeals: The Sindh Essential Commodities Price Control and Prevention of Profiteering and Hoarding Ordinance, 2005
metadata.max_penalty: Upto Rs.100,000
metadata.one_line: Amends the 2006 Act to strengthen price control, allow warrantless searches/seizures, and add new essential commodities.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the Sindh Essential Commodities Price Control and Prevention of Profiteering and Hoarding Act, 2005. It expands the definition of hoarding, substitutes terms for revenue officers with 'authorized officer', and grants powers to search without warrants and seize articles. The Act also introduces provisions for auctioning seized goods, summary trials, and adds a list of essential commodities including medical supplies and food items.

name: ESSENTIAL COMMODITIES PRICE CONTROL AND PREVENTION OF PROFITEERING AND HOARDING ACT, 2005

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Essential Commodities Price Control and Prevention of Profiteering and Hoarding Act, 2005
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for price control and prevention of profiteering on and hoarding of essential commodities and to provide for matters ancillary thereto
metadata.max_penalty: Upto Rs.100,000
metadata.one_line: This Act provides for price control and prevention of profiteering and hoarding of essential commodities in Sindh.
metadata.summary: The Sindh Essential Commodities Price Control and Prevention of Profiteering and Hoarding Act, 2005 establishes a legal framework to regulate the prices, production, movement, and distribution of essential commodities within the province. It empowers District Controllers and authorized officers to issue orders regulating transactions, conduct searches, seize articles, and impose fines for violations such as hoarding or selling above notified prices. The Act defines key terms including 'dealer', 'essential commodity', and 'hoarding', and outlines specific offences with corresponding penalties ranging up to Rs. 100,000.

name: ESTABLISHMENT OF THE OFFICE OF OMBUDSMAN FOR THE PROVINCE OF SINDH ACT 1991

metadata.short_title: The Establishment of the Office of Provincial Ombudsman for the Province of Sindh Act, 1991
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the Establishment of the Office of Provincial Ombudsman.
metadata.territorial_extent: the whole of the Province of Sindh
repeals: Sindh Ordinance, IX of 1991
establishes: Office of Provincial Ombudsman for the Province of Sindh
metadata.one_line: Establishes the Office of Provincial Ombudsman for Sindh to investigate mal-administration and redress injustice.
metadata.summary: This Act establishes the Office of the Provincial Ombudsman for the Province of Sindh. The Ombudsman is appointed by the Governor to diagnose, investigate, and rectify injustices caused by mal-administration within provincial agencies. The Act defines mal-administration broadly to include decisions contrary to law, arbitrary actions, neglect, and inefficiency. It outlines the tenure, powers, remuneration, and code of conduct for the Ombudsman and their staff, while also repealing a previous 1991 Ordinance.

name: ESTABLISHMENT OF THE OFFICE OF OMBUDSMAN FOR THE PROVINCE OF SINDH (AMENDMENT) ACT, 2012

metadata.short_title: The Establishment of the Office of Ombudsman for the Province of Sindh (Amendment) Act, 2012
metadata.long_title: An Act to amend the Establishment of the Office of Ombudsman for the Province of Sindh Act, 1991.
amends: The Establishment of the Office of Ombudsman for the Province of Sindh Act, 1991
metadata.one_line: Amends the 1991 Ombudsman Act to extend the Ombudsman's term and allow reappointment by the Governor.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the Establishment of the Office of Ombudsman for the Province of Sindh Act, 1991. It specifically alters Section 4 regarding the tenure of the Ombudsman. The amendment extends the standard office period to four years and grants the Governor power to extend the term or reappoint the Ombudsman on the advice of the Chief Minister.

name: ESTABLISHMENT OF THE OFFICE OF THE OMBUDSMAN FOR THE PROVINCE OF SINDH (AMENDMENT) ACT, 2020

metadata.short_title: The Establishment of the Office of the Ombudsman for the Province of Sindh (Amendment) Act, 2020
metadata.long_title: An Act to amend the Establishment of the Office of the Ombudsman for the Province of Sindh Act,1991.
amends: The Establishment of the Office of the Ombudsman for the Province of Sindh Act, 1991
metadata.administering_body: Office of the Ombudsman for the Province of Sindh
metadata.one_line: Amends the 1991 Act to replace references to the Governor with the Chief Minister and sets qualification criteria.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the Establishment of the Office of the Ombudsman for the Province of Sindh Act, 1991. It primarily substitutes references to the 'Governor' with the 'Chief Minister' throughout the parent Act. Additionally, it inserts a new qualification requirement for the Ombudsman, mandating they be a former or qualified High Court Judge, a senior civil servant (BS-20+), or a person of known integrity and social eminence.

metadata.short_title: The Etihad University Act, 2017
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the establishment of the Etihad University, Karachi.
metadata.one_line: Establishes the autonomous Etihad University in Karachi and defines its structure, officers, and functions.
metadata.summary: This Act establishes the Etihad University in Karachi as an autonomous body fully funded by the BB Foundation. It outlines the university's powers to confer degrees, manage property, and set up campuses across Pakistan. The legislation defines the roles of key officers including the Chancellor, Vice Chancellor, and Board of Governors, while also establishing various academic and administrative committees.

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Explosive Act, 2019
metadata.long_title: An Act to regulate the manufacture, possession, use, sale, transport and import of explosives.
metadata.territorial_extent: the whole of the Province of Sindh
metadata.max_penalty: death or imprisonment for life
metadata.one_line: Regulates the manufacture, possession, use, sale, transport and import of explosives in Sindh.
metadata.summary: This Act regulates the manufacture, possession, use, sale, transport, and import of explosives within the Province of Sindh. It defines various terms related to explosives and establishes punishments for causing explosions or possessing them with malicious intent. The Act also grants powers to the Government to make rules regarding licensing, inspection, and prohibition of dangerous explosives.

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Factories (Amendment) Act, 2022
metadata.long_title: An Act to further amend the Sindh Factories Act, 2015.
metadata.one_line: Amends the Sindh Factories Act, 2015 regarding registration certificates and omits specific sections.
metadata.summary: This Act further amends the Sindh Factories Act, 2015 to streamline the issuance of registration certificates by the Directorate of Labour in conjunction with water supply agencies. It achieves this by adding a proviso to section 11 requiring certificates to be issued within fourteen days. Additionally, the Act omits clauses (d) and (e) from section 15 and entirely repeals section 24 of the parent Act.

metadata.short_title: The Sind Finance Act, 1972
metadata.long_title: An Act to abolish, continue and levy certain taxes, duties and fees in the Province of Sind.
metadata.territorial_extent: the whole of the Province of Sind
amends: West Pakistan Motor Vehicles Taxation Act, 1958
repeals: section 11 and the Fourth Schedule of West Pakistan Finance Act, 1965 (in application to Sind)
the Fifth Schedule and Sixth Schedule of West Pakistan Finance Act, 1964 (in application to Sind)
section 6 and the Third Schedule and Fourth Schedule of West Pakistan Finance Ordinance, 1969 (in application to Sind)
metadata.one_line: Abolishes, continues and levies specific taxes, duties and fees in Sindh while amending existing provincial laws.
metadata.summary: This Act abolishes, continues, and levies certain taxes, duties, and fees within the Province of Sind. It amends several existing statutes regarding local taxation, motor vehicle fees, and electricity duties to update rates and procedures. The legislation also establishes revenue-sharing mechanisms between the government and local councils.

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Finance Act, 2019
metadata.long_title: An Act to rationalize, levy and enhance certain taxes and duties in the Province of Sindh and to amend certain laws in the Province of Sindh.
amends: Sindh Development and Maintenance of Infrastructure Cess Act, 2017
metadata.one_line: This Act rationalizes taxes in Sindh and amends stamp duty, motor vehicle tax, and infrastructure cess laws.
metadata.summary: The Sindh Finance Act, 2019 was enacted to rationalize, levy, and enhance specific taxes and duties within the Province of Sindh. It amends existing legislation including the Stamp Act, 1899, the Sindh Motor Vehicles Taxation Act, 1958, and the Sindh Development and Maintenance of Infrastructure Cess Act, 2017 to update tax rates and schedules. The Act introduces new stamp duty categories for trust funds and places of worship, adjusts motor vehicle taxation based on engine capacity and age, and sets specific cess rates for goods transported within the province.

name: FISCAL RESPONSIBILITY AND DEBT MANAGEMENT ACT, 2022

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Fiscal Responsibility and Debt Management Act, 2022
metadata.long_title: An Act to impose the fiscal and debt constraints to ensure the public financial management of the province in a prudent, disciplined and sustainable manner.
metadata.territorial_extent: the whole of the Province of Sindh
metadata.administering_body: Finance Department of Government of Sindh
metadata.one_line: This Act imposes fiscal and debt constraints to ensure prudent public financial management in Sindh.
metadata.summary: The Sindh Fiscal Responsibility and Debt Management Act, 2022 establishes a framework for the Government of Sindh to manage its finances prudently. It sets specific quantitative targets for budget deficits, debt servicing costs, and guarantee stocks relative to total revenue. The Act mandates the establishment of a Debt Management Unit within the Finance Department and requires the periodic issuance of Medium Term Debt Strategies and Budget Strategy Papers.

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Food Authority Act, 2016
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the safety and standards of food and for establishment of an Authority known as the Sindh Food Authority.
metadata.territorial_extent: the whole of the Province of Sindh
metadata.commencement: on such date as the Government may, by notification, specify
repeals: The West Pakistan Pure Food Ordinance, 1960
metadata.one_line: Establishes the Sindh Food Authority to ensure food safety and standards in the Province.
metadata.summary: This Act establishes the Sindh Food Authority to regulate the safety, hygiene, and standards of food within the Province. It defines key terms such as 'food', 'adulterated food', and 'food business' to set a clear regulatory framework. The Authority is empowered to issue licenses, conduct inspections, frame regulations on labeling and additives, and prosecute offences related to unsafe food.

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Forensic Science Agency Act, 2017
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the establishment of an Agency known as the Sindh Forensic Science Agency for forensic examination of documents, materials, equipment, impressions or other objects.
metadata.territorial_extent: the whole of the Province of Sindh
metadata.max_penalty: imprisonment which may extend to one year or with fine which may extend to Rs.1,00,000/- or with both
metadata.one_line: Establishes the Sindh Forensic Science Agency to examine forensic material and render expert opinions for courts.
metadata.summary: This Act establishes the Sindh Forensic Science Agency within the Province of Sindh. The Agency is responsible for examining forensic materials, rendering expert opinions, maintaining records, and promoting awareness on forensics. It defines the roles of the Director General and experts, outlines procedures for re-examination of material, and prescribes penalties for rendering false opinions or destroying evidence.

metadata.short_title: The Forest Act (Sindh Amendment) Act, 1994
metadata.long_title: An Act to amend the Forest Act, 1927, in its application to the Province of Sindh.
metadata.max_penalty: imprisonment for a term which may extend to four years and with fine which may extend to twenty thousand rupees or with both
metadata.one_line: Amends the Forest Act, 1927 regarding penalties and confiscation in Sindh.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the Forest Act, 1927 specifically for its application to the Province of Sindh. It introduces stricter penalties for offences involving reserved or protected forests where the value of timber or produce exceeds ten thousand rupees. The amendments also mandate the confiscation of stolen timber and tools used in committing offences, allow courts to sanction rewards for informants, and enable the recovery of government expenditure on removing encroachments from convicted persons.

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Fund Management House Act, 2021
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the establishment, functions and rules of the Sindh Fund Management House.

metadata.one_line: Establishes the Sindh Fund Management House to manage government investment funds within Sindh.
metadata.summary: This Act establishes the Sindh Fund Management House as a unit within the Finance Department of the Government of Sindh. It defines the composition and powers of the Board, which includes high-ranking officials such as the Chief Minister and Finance Minister, along with members from various departments and the Provincial Assembly. The Act provides for the constitution of Investment Committees to manage designated funds in accordance with approved investment policies. It also outlines the functions of the House regarding investing, managing financial assets, and performing ancillary matters, while repealing the previous 2013 Act.

name: GAMBAT INSTITUTE OF MEDICAL SCIENCES (AMENDMENT) ACT, 2015

metadata.summary: This Act amends the Gambat Institute of Medical Sciences Act, 2005 to update the institution's name. Specifically, it substitutes the words 'The Sindh Act No. V Gambat Institute of Medical Sciences' with 'Pir Abdul Qadir Shah Jeelani Institute of Medical Sciences, Gambat' throughout the original Act. The amendment came into force immediately upon enactment.

name: GAMBAT INSTITUTE OF MEDICAL SCIENCES ACT, 2006

metadata.short_title: The Gambat Institute of Medical Sciences Act, 2005
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the establishment of an Institute known as the Gambat Institute of Medical Sciences, Gambat.

metadata.summary: This Act establishes the Gambat Institute of Medical Sciences at Gambat by reconstituting existing local health facilities. The Institute is created as a body corporate with perpetual succession to manage property, conduct research, and provide medical training. It operates under a Board of Governors and a Director, with funds derived from government grants, donations, and fees. The Act also empowers the Board to make regulations for the Institute's administration.

It grants the authority to hold examinations and confer degrees, diplomas, and certificates. The Act also substitutes the Chief Minister for the Governor in specific sections and replaces a committee member title.

It consists of various government officials and members appointed by the Government of Sindh.

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Goth-Abad (Housing Scheme) (Amendment) Act, 2023

The amendments also incorporate provisions regarding limitation periods governed by the Limitation Act, 1908.

metadata.summary: This Act establishes the Greenwich University at Karachi as a body corporate with perpetual succession. It defines the structure of the university, including the Patron, Chancellor, Vice-Chancellor, and various committees like the Board of Governors and Academic Council. The Act grants the university powers to confer degrees, affiliate institutions, and manage its own finances while ensuring it remains open to all persons regardless of religion or race.

metadata.short_title: The Habib University Act, 2012

metadata.summary: This Act establishes the Habib University at Karachi as a body corporate owned by the Habib Foundation. It defines the university's powers to impart education, prescribe curricula, and award degrees while ensuring open admission regardless of sex or religion. The legislation outlines the structure of authorities including the Board of Governors, Academic Council, and various committees for finance, discipline, and affiliation.

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Habitual Offenders Monitoring Act, 2022
metadata.long_title: An Act to check the menace of street crime and ensure safer cities and neighborhoods especially the urban areas of the Province of Sindh and for the purpose to ensure the effective monitoring of habitual offenders by using the modern technology;
metadata.territorial_extent: the whole of the Province of Sindh
metadata.max_penalty: imprisonment for a term not exceeding three years and fine of one million rupee
metadata.one_line: This Act establishes electronic monitoring for habitual offenders in Sindh to curb street crime.
metadata.summary: The Sindh Habitual Offenders Monitoring Act, 2022 aims to reduce street crime and ensure safer urban areas in the Province of Sindh. It provides a legal framework for attaching electronic monitoring devices to habitual offenders who have been arrested more than once for specific serious offences. The Act outlines procedures for declaring habitual offenders, attaching monitoring devices, maintaining a registry, and imposing penalties for non-compliance or tampering with the devices.

metadata.summary: This Act establishes the Hamdard University at Karachi as a body corporate with perpetual succession. It defines the university's officers, including the Patron, Chancellor, Vice-Chancellor, and Board of Governors, and outlines their powers and functions. The Act grants the university autonomy to confer degrees, affiliate institutions, and manage its own fund while ensuring it remains open to all regardless of religion or race.

name: HANDS INSTITUTE OF DEVELOPMENT STUDIES ACT, 2023

metadata.summary: This Act establishes the HANDS Institute of Development Studies at Karachi as a body corporate owned by the Sponsor. It grants the Institute autonomy to provide instruction, conduct research, award degrees, and manage its own finances and staff. The Act defines various authorities including the Board of Governors, Academic Council, and specific committees for discipline and affiliation.

metadata.short_title: The Sindh High Density Development Board (Amendment) Act, 2021

metadata.summary: This Act amends the Sindh High Density Development Board Act, 2010 to update the constitution of the Board. It omits clause (ii) of section 2 and substitutes the entirety of section 3 with a new list of members including the Chief Minister, Local Government Minister, and representatives from relevant authorities. The Act applies to the Province of Sindh and comes into force immediately upon publication.

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Hindus Marriage (Amendment) Act, 2018
metadata.long_title: An Act to amend the Sindh Hindus Marriage Act, 2016.
metadata.territorial_extent: all Hindus in the Province of Sindh

metadata.one_line: Amends the 2016 Act to regulate Hindu marriage conditions, registration, and remedies in Sindh.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the Sindh Hindus Marriage Act, 2016 to establish uniform laws protecting Hindu marriage rights in Sindh. It sets conditions for solemnization including age, consent, and witness requirements, while mandating registration within 45 days. The legislation also outlines procedures for judicial separation, annulment, remarriage rights for widows, and penalties for contraventions such as bigamy or false statements.

name: HOLY QURAN (PRINTING, RECORDING AND DISPSAL OF DAMAGED OR SHAHEED AND SACRED AURAQS) ACT, 2018

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Holy Quran (Printing, Recording and Disposal of Damaged or Shaheed and Sacred Auraqs) Act, 2018
metadata.long_title: An Act to ensure publication of the text of the Holy Quran free from errors of printing, recording and proper disposal of damaged or shaheed copies of the sacred Auraqs.
metadata.territorial_extent: the whole of the Province of Sindh
repeals: The Publication of Holy Quran (Elimination of Printing and Recording Errors) Act, 1973
key_definitions: damaged or shaheed copy of the Holy Quran or sacred Auraqs
metadata.administering_body: Religious Affairs and Auqaf Department, Government of Sindh
metadata.one_line: This Act regulates the printing, recording, and disposal of Holy Quran copies in Sindh to ensure accuracy and sanctity.
metadata.summary: The Act ensures the publication of the Holy Quran text free from printing or recording errors and mandates proper disposal of damaged copies. It establishes a Quran Board comprising prominent Ulama to authenticate standard copies and supervise error-free production. The legislation regulates publishers and recording companies, requiring registration and adherence to specific standards regarding paper, layout, and textual accuracy.

name: HYDERABAD DEVELOPMENT AUTHORITY (REVIVAL AND AMENDING) ACT, 2013

metadata.summary: This Act revives the Hyderabad Development Authority Act, 1976, which had been repealed, to give impetus to the housing industry and provide shelter. It amends the revived Act by inserting new clauses related to land consolidation and substituting the constitution of the Authority with specific members including government nominees and civil society representatives. The Act also validates all orders and proceedings made between July 1, 2002, and the date of this Act's commencement.

metadata.short_title: The Hyderabad Development Authority Act, 1976

The Authority is a body corporate with powers to acquire property, levy betterment fees, and regulate building construction. It outlines the constitution of the Authority, its functions regarding land acquisition and water supply, and provides for the repeal of previous ordinances and acts applicable to the division.

name: HYDERABAD WATER AND SEWERAGE CORPORATION ACT, 2023

metadata.short_title: The Ibn-e-Sina University, Mirpurkhas Act, 2021

metadata.summary: This Act regulates the District Police in Sind concerning public nuisances and maintenance of order. It addresses issues such as unauthorized construction on thoroughfares, accumulation of offensive matter, and improper disposal of dead animals or refuse. The legislation also empowers Magistrates to order the removal of vegetation like prickly-pear from common lands if it threatens health, imposing fines or short-term imprisonment for non-compliance.

The Act outlines rates for tolls, exemptions, appointment of servants, and penalties for offenses such as taking unlawful tolls or carrying passengers without a license.

metadata.short_title: The Sind Hindu Heirs' Relief Act, 1866
metadata.long_title: An Act to limit the liability of a son, grandson or heir of a deceased Hindu for the debts of his ancestor, and the liability of the second husband of a Hindu widow for the debts of her deceased husband, and otherwise to amend the law of debtor and creditor.

metadata.summary: This Act limits the personal liability of sons, grandsons, or heirs of a deceased Hindu to the extent of assets received from the deceased. It also protects the second husband of a Hindu widow from liability for her first husband's debts. The legislation applies to undivided families and protects members who were unborn or under twenty-one when a debt was contracted.

The Act provides for the constitution, functions, disqualifications, and remuneration of members, as well as powers to make rules and regulations. It also includes provisions for recovery of dues, immunity from court jurisdiction regarding acts done under the Act, and the repeal of previous laws applicable to Larkana Division.

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Lawyers' Welfare and Protection Act, 2021

It provides for the constitution of the Sindh Advocates Welfare Fund, which is administered by a Trustee Committee established by the Government. The Fund receives contributions from the Government, Bar Council, voluntary donations, and fees collected under the Act to support Advocates upon cessation of practice or other welfare needs.

name: LIAQUAT AND DOW MEDICAL AND HEALTH SCIENCES UNIVERSITIES (AMENDMENT) ACT, 2006

metadata.summary: This Act amends two existing laws governing medical universities in Sindh: the Liaquat University Ordinance, 2001, and the Dow University Act, 2004. It primarily updates provisions related to the appointment of Vice Chancellors, the role of the Pro-Chancellor, and the status of the Registrar. certificate granted under section 46 of the Agriculturists' Relief Act, 1879

metadata.summary: This Act amends the Limitation Act, 1908 to exclude specific time periods when computing limitation for mortgage foreclosure or sale suits requiring a certificate under the Agriculturists' Relief Act, 1879. It applies to suits instituted within six months of the Act's commencement and prevents dismissal based on missing certificates obtained within the preceding year. Additionally, it provides mechanisms for restoring dismissed claims if specific grounds related to limitation periods or certificate timing are satisfied.

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Livestock Breeding Act, 2016
metadata.long_title: An Act to regulate the livestock breeding services in the Sindh.

The legislation aims to improve genetic potential while protecting indigenous breeds and prohibits business activities without proper registration or licensing.

metadata.summary: This Act amends the Sindh Local Government Act, 2013 to update references from the Delimitation of Constituencies Act, 1974 to the Elections Act, 2017. It introduces new provisions for handling equality of votes in council elections, defines specific acts constituting undue influence during elections, and outlines offences related to tampering with election papers. The Act also specifies penalties for election-related crimes and procedures for drawing lots when vote counts are equal.

It omits specific clauses from section 18 and inserts a new section 18-B requiring elected officials to be council members within six months of taking office. The legislation applies to all constituted local bodies in Sindh including Metropolitan Corporations, Town Municipal Corporations, District Councils, and various committees.

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Local Government (Third Amendment) Act, 2023

It grants Inspectors the authority to take cognizance of offences under Schedule-VI and impose fines up to fifty thousand rupees, or file cases for higher penalties involving imprisonment up to three years. The Act also modifies trial procedures to allow summary trials by a Special Magistrate within thirty days and updates schedules regarding Metropolitan Corporations.

name: LYARI DEVELOPMENT AUTHORITY (REVIVAL AND AMENDING) ACT, 2013

metadata.one_line: Amends the Sindh Shops and Commercial Establishment Act, 2015 regarding registration forms and fees.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the Sindh Shops and Commercial Establishment Act, 2015 to update section 24 and Form-A in the Schedule. It substitutes specific wording regarding employer applications for establishment registration and omits references to certain fees. Additionally, it updates a footnote in Form-A concerning the submission of statements to the Deputy Chief Inspector of Shops. The Act also repeals the Sindh Shops and Commercial Establishment (Amendment) Ordinance, 2020.

metadata.short_title: The Sind (Amendment of Laws) Act, 1974
metadata.long_title: An Act to amend certain laws applicable to the Province of Sind, for conferring powers on Commissioners.
amends: The Karachi Essential Articles (Price Control and Hoarding) Act, 1953
The Sindh Court of Wards Act, 1905
repeals: Sind Ordinance III of 1972
Sindh Ordinance XVII of 1974
metadata.one_line: Amends various Sind laws to confer powers on Commissioners and repeals two specific Ordinances.
metadata.summary: This Act amends numerous federal and provincial acts applicable to the Province of Sind to transfer authority from the Provincial Government to the Commissioner. It specifically confers powers on Commissioners regarding project inspection, land acquisition, and appeals. The Act also repeals the Sind (Amendment of Laws) Ordinance, 1972 and the Sind (Amendment of Laws) Ordinance, 1974.

name: SIND (TEACHING, PROMOTION AND USE OF SINDHI LANGUAGE (APPLICATION) ACT, 1972.

metadata.short_title: The Sind (Teaching, Promotion and Use of Sindhi Language) (Application) Act, 1972
metadata.long_title: An Act to make certain provision in relation to the application of the Sind (Teaching, Promotion and Use of Sindhi Language) Act, 1972.
metadata.territorial_extent: the whole of the Province of Sind
amends: Sind (Teaching, Promotion and Use of Sindhi Language) Act, 1972
repeals: Sind Ordinance XI of 1972
metadata.one_line: Clarifies the application of the Sindhi Language Act to ensure no discrimination against Urdu speakers in civil service.
metadata.summary: This Act provides specific provisions regarding the application of the Sind (Teaching, Promotion and Use of Sindhi Language) Act, 1972. It ensures that no person qualified for appointment or promotion in the Province of Sind is discriminated against solely due to a lack of knowledge of Sindhi or Urdu. Furthermore, it protects existing civil servants from removal based on their language proficiency. The Act also clarifies that these measures should not prejudice the use of Urdu as a national language and repeals a conflicting ordinance.

name: SIND ABOLITION OF LAND REVENUE AND AGRICULTURE INCOME TAX ACT, 1977

metadata.short_title: The Sind Abolition of Land Revenue and Agriculture Income Tax Act, 1977
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the abolition of land revenue and agriculture income tax.
repeals: Sind Abolition of Land Revenue and Agriculture Income Tax Ordinance, 1977
key_definitions: land revenue payable for Rabi Crop of 1976-77
metadata.one_line: Abolishes land revenue and agriculture income tax for Sindh lands from the Rabi Crop of 1976-77 onwards.
metadata.summary: This Act abolishes land revenue and agriculture income tax payable under previous laws for any land in Sindh starting with the Rabi Crop of 1976-77. It specifies that where a flat rate system applies, fifty percent of the total land revenue due for perennial canal lands and twenty-five percent for non-perennial canal lands shall be deemed payable for that specific crop season. The Act also repeals the Sind Abolition of Land Revenue and Agriculture Income Tax Ordinance, 1977.

metadata.short_title: The Sind Agricultural Income Tax Act, 1994
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for imposition of tax on income from agricultural land in the Province of Sindh.
metadata.territorial_extent: the whole of the Province of Sindh
metadata.administering_body: Government of the Province of Sindh
metadata.one_line: Imposes tax on income from agricultural land in Sindh and outlines assessment, collection, and exemption procedures.
metadata.summary: This Act provides for the imposition of tax on income derived from agricultural land situated in the Province of Sindh. It defines key terms such as 'land', 'owner', and 'Collector' and establishes the rates and methods for tax assessment and collection. The legislation also covers exemptions, appeals, and the power to make rules necessary to carry out the Act's purposes.

metadata.short_title: The Sind Agricultural Supplies Organization Act, 1973
metadata.long_title: An Act to establish an Agricultural Supplies Organization in the Province of Sindh.
metadata.territorial_extent: the whole of the Province of Sind
repeals: Sind Ordinance XXIV of 1972
metadata.one_line: Establishes the Sind Agricultural Supplies Organization to procure and distribute agricultural inputs in Sindh.
metadata.summary: This Act establishes the Sind Agricultural Supplies Organization as a body corporate within the Province of Sindh. The organization is empowered to procure and distribute seeds and fertilizers to increase agricultural production. It outlines the constitution of a Board, appointment procedures for officers, financial management rules, and audit requirements.

metadata.short_title: The Sind Agriculture University (Amendment) Act, 1986
metadata.long_title: An Act to amend the Sind Agriculture University Act, 1977.
repeals: Sind Agriculture University (Amendment) Ordinance, 1986
metadata.one_line: Amends the Sind Agriculture University Act, 1977 to insert references to the Pro-Vice-Chancellor and repeals a related Ordinance.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the Sind Agriculture University Act, 1977 by inserting references to the 'Pro-Vice-Chancellor' in various sections. It grants the Chancellor the power to appoint a Pro-Vice-Chancellor for specific campuses with terms not exceeding four years. The Act also repeals the Sind Agriculture University (Amendment) Ordinance, 1986.

metadata.short_title: The Sind Agriculture University Act, 1977
metadata.long_title: An Act to establish an Agriculture University in Sind.
repeals: Sind Ordinance V of 1977
metadata.one_line: Establishes the Sind Agriculture University in Sindh and defines its structure, powers, and authorities.
metadata.summary: This Act establishes an Agriculture University at Tandojam in the Province of Sindh. It creates a body corporate with perpetual succession to manage instruction, research, and degree conferment in agricultural sciences. The Act defines the composition and powers of various authorities including the Senate, Syndicate, and Academic Council, while also providing for the transfer of existing properties and employees from the University of Sind.

metadata.short_title: The Sind Agriculturists' Relief Act, 1879
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide relief to agriculturists in Sindh.
repeals: The Dekkhan Agriculturists' Relief Act, 1879 (as adapted for Sindh)
metadata.max_penalty: penalty for contravention of Sections 64 to 66
metadata.one_line: This Act provides legal relief, procedural protections, and debt management mechanisms for agriculturists in Sindh.
metadata.summary: The Sind Agriculturists' Relief Act, 1879 was enacted to provide specific legal protections and remedies for farmers (agriculturists) in the province of Sindh. It establishes special courts and procedures for suits involving agriculturists, regulates mortgages and debt recovery, and introduces mechanisms for conciliation and insolvency. The Act also mandates written receipts, annual accounts, and restricts the attachment of certain agricultural produce to ensure the livelihood of farmers.

metadata.short_title: The Sind Amendment of Laws Act, 1976
metadata.long_title: An Act to amend certain laws in pursuance of clause (4) of Article 8 of the Constitution of the Islamic Republic of Pakistan.
amends: The Sind Industries (Control on Establishment and Enlargement) Ordinance, 1963
The Privately Managed Schools and Colleges (Taking Over) Regulation, 1972
repeals: The Sind Amendment of Laws Ordinance, 1976
key_definitions: prior permission of the Provincial Government
metadata.one_line: Amends specific laws regarding societies, industries, and private schools in Sindh while repealing a related ordinance.
metadata.summary: This Act amends several existing laws in Sindh to align them with constitutional requirements. It introduces provisions for the supersession of society governing bodies by the Provincial Government under certain conditions and modifies regulations concerning privately managed schools and colleges. Additionally, it repeals the Sind Amendment of Laws Ordinance, 1976.

name: SIND ASSEMBLY MEMBERS (SALARIES AND ALLOWANCES) (AMENDMENT) ACT, 1985

metadata.short_title: The Sind Assembly Members (Salaries and Allowances) (Amendment) Act, 1985
metadata.long_title: An Act to amend the Sind Assembly Members (Salaries and Allowances) Act, 1974.
metadata.commencement: at once and deemed to have taken effect on and from the date of the first meeting of the Assembly after the tenth day of March, 1985
amends: The Sind Assembly Members (Salaries and Allowances) Act, 1974
metadata.one_line: Amends the 1974 Act to increase salaries, allowances, and accommodation subsidies for Sindh Assembly members.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the Sind Assembly Members (Salaries and Allowances) Act, 1974 to update financial provisions for assembly members. It increases specific salary amounts, raises transport allowances per kilometer, and introduces a daily subsidy for members without government accommodation during sessions.

name: SIND ASSEMBLY MEMBERS (SALARIES AND ALLOWANCES) ACT, 1974

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Assembly Members (Salaries and Allowances) Act, 1974
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for salaries, allowances and other facilities to members including the Leader of the Opposition of the Provincial Assembly of Sind.
repeals: Sind Act 5 of 1972
metadata.one_line: Provides salaries, allowances, and facilities to members of the Provincial Assembly of Sindh.
metadata.summary: This Act establishes the salary structure, daily allowances, and various facilities for members of the Provincial Assembly of Sindh. It specifically grants privileges to the Leader of the Opposition comparable to those of a Provincial Minister. The legislation also outlines rules for travel, accommodation, office maintenance, and medical benefits, while repealing the previous Sind Provincial Assembly (Salaries and Allowances) Act, 1972.

name: SIND BOARD OF INTERMEDIATE AND SECONDARY EDUCATION (AMENDMEN T) ACT, 1972.

metadata.short_title: The Sind Boards of Intermediate and Secondary Education (Amendment) Act, 1972
metadata.long_title: An Act to amend the Sind Boards of Intermediate and secondary Education Ordinance, 1972.
amends: Sind Boards of Intermediate and Secondary Education Ordinance, 1972
metadata.one_line: Amends section 4 and the Schedule of the Sind Boards of Intermediate and Secondary Education Ordinance, 1972.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the Sind Boards of Intermediate and Secondary Education Ordinance, 1972. It substitutes a specific clause in section 4 regarding nominees of the Vice-Chancellor of the University. Additionally, it modifies paragraphs 4 and 5 within the Schedule to the Principal Ordinance with similar substitution.

name: SIND BOARD OF INTERMEDIATE AND SECONDARY EEUCATION (AMENDMENT) ACT, 1973

metadata.short_title: The Sind Boards of Intermediate and Secondary Education (Amendment) Act, 1973
metadata.long_title: An Act to further amend the Sind Boards of Intermediate and Secondary Education Ordinance, 1972.
amends: The Sind Boards of Intermediate and Secondary Education Ordinance, 1972
repeals: The Board of Intermediate and Secondary Education Hyderabad Ordinance, 1961
The Board of Intermediate and Secondary Education Karachi Ordinance, 1962
metadata.one_line: Amends the 1972 Ordinance to establish new Boards in Karachi and Hyderabad and creates an Academic Co-ordination Committee.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the Sind Boards of Intermediate and Secondary Education Ordinance, 1972 to further regulate the structure and functions of education boards. It establishes specific Boards for Secondary and Intermediate education in Karachi and a combined Board in Hyderabad. Additionally, it creates a Joint Academic Co-ordination Committee to oversee teaching standards and examination maintenance across these boards.

name: SIND BOARD OF TECHNICAL EDUCATION (AMENDMENT) ACT, 1974

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Board of Technical Education (Amendment) Act, 1974
metadata.long_title: An Act to amend the Sind Board of Technical Education Ordinance, 1970.
amends: Sind Board of Technical Education Ordinance, 1970
repeals: Sind Board of Technical Education (Amendment) Ordinance, 1974
metadata.one_line: Amends the Sind Board of Technical Education Ordinance, 1970 by substituting names and adding new members.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the Sind Board of Technical Education Ordinance, 1970 to update member composition and terminology. It substitutes 'Sind University Engineering College' for 'Sind Engineering College' and adds representatives from the Institute of Engineers Pakistan and the Directorate of Vocational Institutes for Girls. The Act also replaces references to 'Government' with 'Controlling Authority' in several sections and adds a saving clause regarding actions taken by the West Pakistan Board of Technical Education.

name: SIND BOARD OF TECHNICAL EDUCATION (AMENDMENT) ACT, 1975

metadata.short_title: The Sind Board of Technical Education (Amendment) Act, 1975
metadata.long_title: An Act further to amend the Sind Board of Technical Education Ordinance, 1970.
amends: Sind Board of Technical Education Ordinance, 1970
repeals: Sind Board of Technical Education (Amendment) Ordinance, 1975
metadata.max_penalty: imprisonment of either description which may extend to one year or with fine which may extend to fifty thousand rupees or with both
metadata.one_line: Amends the 1970 Ordinance regarding diploma issuance and apprenticeship exemptions while repealing a 1975 Ordinance.
metadata.summary: This Act further amends the Sind Board of Technical Education Ordinance, 1970. It adds an exemption for persons undergoing apprenticeship training and inserts new sections restricting diploma issuance and defining offences with penalties up to one year imprisonment or a fine of fifty thousand rupees. The Act also repeals the Sind Board of Technical Education (Amendment) Ordinance, 1975.

name: SIND BOARDS OF INTERMEDIATE AND SECONDARY EDUCATION (AMENDMENT) ACT, 1974

metadata.short_title: The Sind Boards of Intermediate And Secondary Education (Amendment) Act, 1974
metadata.long_title: An Act to further amend the Sind Boards Of Intermediate And Secondary Education Ordinance, 1972.
amends: Sind Boards Of Intermediate And Secondary Education Ordinance, 1972
repeals: Sind Boards of Intermediate and Secondary Education (Amendment) Ordinance, 1974
subjects: Boards of Intermediate and Secondary Education
key_definitions: quorum for meetings of a Board
metadata.one_line: Amends the 1972 Ordinance regarding board composition and meeting quorums while repealing a 1974 Ordinance.
metadata.summary: This Act further amends the Sind Boards of Intermediate and Secondary Education Ordinance, 1972. It modifies section 4 to add a new clause regarding the Chairman of all other Boards and changes the quorum requirement in section 8 to fifty percent of total members. Additionally, it repeals the Sind Boards of Intermediate and Secondary Education (Amendment) Ordinance, 1974.

name: SIND BORSTAL SCHOOLS AND THE SIND CHILDREN (AMENDMENT) ACT, 1975

metadata.short_title: The Sind Borstal Schools and the Sind Children (Amendment) Act, 1975
metadata.long_title: An Act to amend the Sind Borstal schools Act, 1955 and the Sind Children Act, 1955.
repeals: Bombay Borstal Schools Act, 1929 (as applicable to Karachi)
Sind Borstal Schools Act, 1929
metadata.one_line: Amends the Sind Borstal Schools Act and Sind Children Act of 1955 and repeals earlier Bombay and Sind borstal acts.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the Sind Borstal Schools Act, 1955 and the Sind Children Act, 1955 to update references from 'Sind' to 'the Province of Sind' and align provisions with current laws. It substitutes specific sections in both Acts to reflect changes in court jurisdictions and repealed legislation. Additionally, it repeals the Bombay Borstal Schools Act, 1929 (as applicable to Karachi) and the Sind Borstal Schools Act, 1929.

metadata.short_title: The Sind Children (Amendment) Act, 1974
metadata.long_title: An Act to amend the Sindh Children Act, 1955.
repeals: Sind Children (Amendment) Ordinance, 1974
metadata.one_line: Amends the Sindh Children Act, 1955 to include Khairpur District and repeals a 1974 Ordinance.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the Sindh Children Act, 1955 by adding 'including Khairpur District' to section 1. It also explicitly repeals the Sind Children (Amendment) Ordinance, 1974. The amendments came into force immediately upon enactment.

metadata.short_title: The Sind City Survey Act, 1987
metadata.long_title: An Act to regulate the survey of lands other than agricultural lands and provide for the matter connected therewith.
metadata.one_line: Regulates the survey of non-agricultural lands in Sindh, defines terms, appoints officers, and sets fees for sanad issuance.
metadata.summary: This Act regulates the survey of lands other than agricultural lands within the Province of Sind. It empowers the Board of Revenue to direct surveys and appoint Survey Officers who have powers to fix city limits. The Act establishes a fee structure for obtaining a 'sanad' (title document) and provides a mechanism for appeals against orders made by Survey Officers.

metadata.short_title: The Sind Civil Servants (Amendment) Act, 1988
metadata.long_title: An Act to amend the Sind Civil Servants Act, 1973.
repeals: Sind Civil Servants (Amendment) Ordinance, 1988
metadata.one_line: Amends the Sind Civil Servants Act, 1973 regarding retirement procedures and repeals a related Ordinance.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the Sind Civil Servants Act, 1973 to ensure civil servants are informed of grounds for retirement and given an opportunity to show cause. It inserts a proviso into section 13 of the 1973 Act regarding these procedural safeguards. The Act also repeals the Sind Civil Servants (Amendment) Ordinance, 1988.

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Civil Servants Act, 1973
metadata.long_title: An Act to regulate the appointment of persons to, and the terms and conditions of service of persons in, the service of Pakistan in connection with the affairs of the Province of Sindh.
repeals: The Sindh Civil Servants Ordinance, 1973
establishes: Sindh Public Service Commission (as selection authority)
metadata.one_line: Regulates the appointment, terms, and conditions of service for civil servants in the Province of Sindh.
metadata.summary: This Act regulates the appointment of persons to, and the terms and conditions of service of persons in, the service of Pakistan connected with the affairs of the Province of Sindh. It defines key terms such as 'civil servant' and 'Government', establishes rules for probation, promotion, pay, leave, and pension, and outlines conduct and discipline requirements. The Act applies to all civil servants wherever they may be and came into force immediately upon enactment.

name: SIND CIVIL SERVANTS WELFARE FUND (AMENDMENT) ACT, 1985

metadata.short_title: The Sind Civil Servants Welfare Fund (Amendment) Act, 1985
metadata.long_title: An Act to amend the Sind Civil Servants Welfare Fund Ordinance, 1979.
amends: Sind Civil Servants Welfare Fund Ordinance, 1979
metadata.one_line: Amends the Sind Civil Servants Welfare Fund Ordinance, 1979 regarding nominee distribution of funds.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the Preamble and Section 8 of the Sind Civil Servants Welfare Fund Ordinance, 1979. It specifically adds a new sub-section to Section 8 concerning the distribution of fund amounts paid to nominees. The amendment mandates that such amounts be distributed among all heirs of the deceased civil servant according to their personal law.

metadata.short_title: The Sind Co-operative Societies (Amendment) Act, 1977
metadata.long_title: An Act to amend the Sind Co-operative Societies Act, 1925.
metadata.one_line: Amends the Sind Co-operative Societies Act, 1925 by substituting specific words in sections 7, 9, and 71.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the Sind Co-operative Societies Act, 1925 to update numerical limits and terminology within specific sections. It substitutes the word 'ten' with 'thirty' in section 7 and section 9, and changes 'person' to 'person or persons' in section 71. The legislation was enacted by the Provincial Assembly of Sindh and came into force immediately upon promulgation.

metadata.short_title: the Sind Co-operative Societies Act, 1925
metadata.long_title: An Act to consolidate and amend the law relating to co-operative societies in the Province of Sind.
metadata.territorial_extent: the whole of the Province of Sind
repeals: Co-operative Societies Act, 1912
metadata.one_line: This Act consolidates and amends the law relating to co-operative societies in Sindh, covering registration, rights, duties, and liquidation.
