metadata.summary: The Sind Co-operative Societies Act, 1925 is a consolidation act designed to facilitate the formation and working of co-operative societies for thrift and mutual aid. It establishes the Registrar's powers regarding registration, audit, and inquiry into society affairs. The Act outlines the rights and liabilities of members, restrictions on borrowing and investment, procedures for liquidation, and provisions for distraint against delinquent members.

metadata.short_title: The Sind Court of Wards (Amendment) Act, 1974
metadata.long_title: An Act to amend the Sind Court of Wards Act, 1905.
metadata.one_line: Amends the Sind Court of Wards Act, 1905 regarding property assumption for disqualified land-holders.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the Sind Court of Wards Act, 1905 to modify conditions under which property is assumed by the Court of Wards. It specifically addresses cases involving land-holders or pension-holders who are disqualified under specific clauses of Section 5. The amendment restricts such assumption to instances where the Provincial Government deems it expedient in the public interest to preserve the property for the family's benefit and where economical management is practicable.

metadata.short_title: The Sind Court of Wards Act, 1905
metadata.long_title: An Act to establish a Court of Wards in Sind
metadata.one_line: Establishes a Court of Wards in Sind to manage the property and persons of disqualified land-holders or pension-holders.
metadata.summary: This Act establishes a Court of Wards in the Province of Sind to assume superintendence over the property and persons of disqualified land-holders or pension-holders. It defines who qualifies as a Government ward, land-holder, or pension-holder and outlines the powers of the Court regarding property management, eviction, rent recovery, and guardianship. The Act also empowers the Provincial Government to make rules for carrying out its purposes.

metadata.short_title: The Sind Crimes Control Act, 1975
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide effective machinery of law to prevent the commission and repetition of crimes and to consolidate the law relating to anti-social elements and dis-orderly persons in the Province of Sind.
repeals: The West Pakistan Control of Goondas Ordinance, 1959
metadata.max_penalty: imprisonment of either description which may extend to five years and with fine which may extend to ten thousand rupees
metadata.one_line: Establishes a Tribunal in Sindh to prevent crimes and control anti-social elements, repealing the 1959 Goondas Ordinance.
metadata.summary: This Act provides effective legal machinery to prevent crime and consolidate laws regarding anti-social and disorderly persons in Sindh. It establishes a Tribunal empowered to inquire into reports of such acts, summon persons, and order bonds for good behavior or detention. The Act outlines procedures for appeals to the Commissioner and repeals the West Pakistan Control of Goondas Ordinance, 1959.

name: SIND CRIMINAL LAW (AMENDMENT) (VALUATION OF TRANSFER OF CASES) ACT, 1972.

metadata.short_title: The Sind Criminal Law (Amendment) (Validation of Transfer of Cases) Act, 1972
metadata.long_title: An Act to validate transfer of cases under the West Pakistan Criminal Law (Amendment) Act, 1963
repeals: Sind Criminal Law (Amendment) (Validation of Transfer of Cases) Ordinance, 1972
metadata.one_line: Validates transfers of cases under the West Pakistan Criminal Law (Amendment) Act, 1963 in Sindh.
metadata.summary: This Act validates the transfer of cases from Tribunals to criminal courts under the West Pakistan Criminal Law (Amendment) Act, 1963. It deems such transfers valid as of February 13, 1971, regardless of whether findings were submitted to the District Magistrate. The legislation also repeals a corresponding Ordinance passed in 1972.

metadata.short_title: The Sind Orphanages (Supervision and Control) Act, 1976
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the establishment of a Board to supervise and regulate the working and control of orphanages in Sind.
metadata.commencement: on such date as Government may, by notification, appoint
repeals: The West Pakistan Control of Orphanages Act, 1958
The Control of Orphanages (Karachi Division) Ordinance, 1958
The Sind Orphanages (Supervision and Control) Ordinance, 1976
establishes: Sind Orphanages Supervision and Control Board
metadata.max_penalty: imprisonment up to two years or fine up to five thousand rupees or both
metadata.one_line: Establishes a Board to supervise and regulate orphanages in Sind through licensing and inspection.
metadata.summary: This Act establishes the Sind Orphanages Supervision and Control Board to oversee and regulate orphanages within the province. It defines the composition of the Board, outlines procedures for issuing licenses to run orphanages, and mandates regular inspections and financial audits. The legislation also creates a specific fund for the Board's operations and prescribes penalties for non-compliance with its provisions.

metadata.short_title: The Sind Employees Special Allowance (Payment) Act, 1986
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for payment of a special allowance to employees.
metadata.commencement: at once and deemed to have taken effect on 1st day of July, 1986
metadata.max_penalty: simple imprisonment for a term which may extend to six months, or with fine which may extend to one thousand rupees, or with both
metadata.one_line: This Act mandates employers in Sindh to pay a special allowance to employees earning up to a certain wage limit.
metadata.summary: The Sind Employees Special Allowance (Payment) Act, 1986 was enacted to provide for the payment of a special allowance to employees in the Province of Sindh. It defines key terms such as 'employee', 'employer', and 'undertaking' to determine who is covered under the law. The Act specifies that employers must pay a special allowance equal to fifty rupees per month or at a rate that brings total wages to one thousand rupees, depending on the employee's current wage level. It also outlines procedures for recovering withheld allowances and imposes penalties, including imprisonment or fines, on employers who contravene its provisions.

name: SIND FANCY THERAPEUTIC SUBSTANCES, MAGIC REMEDIES, MIRACLE CURES AND GUARANTEED RELIEFS ADVERTISEMENT (CONTROL) ACT, 1973

metadata.short_title: The Sind Fancy Therapeutic Substances, Magic Remedies, Miracle Cures and Guaranteed Reliefs Advertisement (Control) Act, 1973
metadata.long_title: An Act to control the advertisement of fancy therapeutic substances, magic remedies, miracle cures and guaranteed reliefs in the Province of Sind.
repeals: The Sind Drugs Advertisement Control Act, 1948 (Sind Act II of 1948)
metadata.max_penalty: imprisonment of either description for a term which may extend to two years and fine which may extend to ten thousand rupees
metadata.one_line: This Act controls advertisements for fancy therapeutic substances, magic remedies, miracle cures, and guaranteed reliefs in Sindh.
metadata.summary: This Act establishes a Board to regulate and control the advertisement of fancy therapeutic substances, magic remedies, miracle cures, and guaranteed reliefs within the Province of Sind. It prohibits any person from making or publishing such advertisements without prior approval from the Board. The Act defines specific terms related to these substances and remedies, outlines the constitution and powers of the Board, and prescribes penalties for contravention, including imprisonment and fines.

metadata.short_title: The Sind Finance (Amendment) Act, 1985
metadata.long_title: An Act to amend the Sind Finance Act, 1964.
metadata.one_line: Amends the Sind Finance Act, 1964 by substituting the Seventh Schedule with new tax rates for various professions and entities.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the Sind Finance Act, 1964 by replacing its Seventh Schedule. The amendment establishes specific annual tax rates for professionals, public and private limited companies, factory owners, contractors, and agents operating within Sindh. It categorizes taxpayers based on their business type, income tax status, and employment scale to determine applicable levies.

metadata.short_title: The Sind Finance Act, 1985
metadata.long_title: An Act to rationalize and abolish certain taxes in the province of Sind.
amends: Sind Urban Immovable Property Tax Act, 1985
metadata.one_line: This Act rationalizes and abolishes certain taxes in Sindh while amending existing finance acts.
metadata.summary: The Sind Finance Act, 1985 was enacted to rationalize and abolish specific taxes within the Province of Sind. It comes into force on July 1, 1985, and immediately omits a subsection from the Sind Urban Immovable Property Tax Act, 1985. The Act amends previous legislation regarding income tax assessments for professionals, companies, contractors, and hoteliers by substituting specific serial numbers and schedules.

metadata.short_title: The Sind Finance Act, 1973
metadata.long_title: An Act to levy or enhance certain taxes and duties in the Province of Sind.
metadata.one_line: This Act levies or enhances certain taxes and duties in the Province of Sind.
metadata.summary: The Sind Finance Act, 1973 was enacted to levy or enhance specific taxes and duties within the Province of Sind. It amends several existing West Pakistan Acts regarding urban immovable property tax, entertainments duty, and finance acts applicable to Sind. The Act introduces a betterment tax on commercial and industrial plots with specific exemptions for smaller areas and establishes rules barring civil suits against tax assessments.

metadata.short_title: The Sind Finance Act, 1974
metadata.long_title: An Act to rationalize, enhance and levy certain taxes, duties and fees in the Province of Sind.
metadata.one_line: This Act rationalizes, enhances, and levies various taxes, duties, and fees in the Province of Sind.
metadata.summary: The Sind Finance Act, 1974 was enacted to rationalize, enhance, and levy specific taxes, duties, and fees within the Province of Sind. It amends several existing laws regarding court fees, immovable property tax, entertainments duty, motor vehicle taxation, and hotel taxes applicable in the province. The Act establishes new fee structures for civil suits and defines terms such as 'covered area' and 'payment of admission' to clarify the scope of duties.

metadata.short_title: The Sind Finance Act, 1975
metadata.long_title: An Act to rationalize, enhance and levy certain taxes, duties and fees in the Province of Sindh.
metadata.one_line: This Act rationalizes and enhances taxes, duties, and fees in Sindh while amending existing court and stamp acts.
metadata.summary: The Sind Finance Act, 1975 was enacted to rationalize, enhance, and levy specific taxes, duties, and fees within the Province of Sindh. It came into force on July 1, 1975, shortly after its promulgation in June 1974. The legislation amends several existing statutes, including the Court Fees Act, 1870, the Stamp Act, 1899, and the Sind Urban Immovable Property Tax Act, 1958, to update fee structures and tax rates for various commercial activities and legal proceedings.

metadata.short_title: The Sind Finance Act, 1976
metadata.long_title: An Act to rationalize, levy and enhance certain taxes and fees in the Province of Sind.
metadata.one_line: This Act rationalizes and enhances various taxes and fees in Sindh by amending existing provincial legislation.
metadata.summary: The Sind Finance Act, 1976 was enacted to rationalize, levy, and enhance specific taxes and fees within the Province of Sind. It achieves this purpose by amending five previous Acts and one Ordinance related to urban immovable property, motor vehicles, tobacco vending, finance schedules, and cotton control. The Act also introduces a new penalty section for non-payment of fees under the Cotton Control Ordinance and adds a schedule listing various commercial categories with their respective tax rates.

metadata.short_title: The Sind Finance Act, 1986
metadata.long_title: An Act to rationalize and abolish certain taxes and duties in the Province of Sind to amend certain laws.
repeals: W.P Act IX of 1963
metadata.one_line: This Act rationalizes and abolishes certain taxes in Sindh while amending specific laws regarding property and entertainment duties.
metadata.summary: The Sind Finance Act, 1986 was enacted to rationalize and abolish specific taxes and duties within the Province of Sind. It amends the Stamp Act of 1899 and the Sind Entertainment Duty Act of 1958 to update valuation methods and duty rates for immovable property and entertainment admissions. Additionally, the Act repeals the earlier Sind Finance Act of 1963 to supersede its provisions.

metadata.short_title: The Sind Fisheries (Amendment) Act, 1976
metadata.long_title: An Act to further amend the Sind Fisheries Ordinance, 1961.
repeals: The Sind Fisheries (Amendment) Ordinance, 1976
metadata.administering_body: Government or any Officer authorized by it
metadata.one_line: Amends the Sind Fisheries Ordinance, 1961 regarding licensing, lease conditions, and fishing seasons.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the Sind Fisheries Ordinance, 1961 to replace references to District Councils with Government or authorized officers. It also updates lease conditions for catching fish and changes the month of August to July in the First Schedule. The Act repeals the earlier Sind Fisheries (Amendment) Ordinance, 1976.

metadata.short_title: The Sind Goth-Abad (Housing Scheme) Act, 1987
metadata.long_title: An Act to make provision for housing facilities to the deserving persons in the rural areas of the Province of Sind.
repeals: The Sind Goth-Abad (Housing Scheme) Ordinance, 1987
metadata.one_line: Provides housing facilities to deserving persons in rural areas of Sindh through land allotment and grants.
metadata.summary: This Act establishes a framework for providing housing facilities to deserving persons residing in rural areas of the Province of Sind. It empowers the Collector, in consultation with an Allotment Committee, to allot land free of cost to eligible individuals who are in genuine need of residential accommodation. The Act outlines procedures for granting proprietary rights, cancelling allotments due to false information or breach of conditions, and re-entering resumed lands. It also provides for appeals, overriding effects on previous colonization laws, and the power to make rules to give effect to the Act's purposes.

metadata.short_title: The Sind Highway Act, 1883
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide Funds maintaining Provincial Roads used for local purposes.
metadata.one_line: An Act to provide funds for maintaining provincial roads used for local purposes in Sindh via vehicle taxation.
metadata.summary: This Act provides additional funds for the construction, maintenance, and repair of public roads in Sindh used primarily for local convenience. It imposes a tax on carriages, coaches, vans, carts, horses, and ponies within notified local areas. The Provincial Government is authorized to levy this tax according to specified rates while exempting government vehicles, bona fide dealers, agricultural workers, and petty traders.

name: SIND INDUSTRIAL AND MINERAL DEVELOPMENT CORPORATION ACT, 1988

metadata.short_title: The Sind Industrial and Mineral Development Corporation Act, 1988
metadata.long_title: An Act to establish an Industrial and Mineral Development Corporation in the Province of Sind.
metadata.territorial_extent: the whole of the Province of Sind
establishes: Sind Industrial and Mineral Development Corporation
metadata.one_line: Establishes the Sind Industrial and Mineral Development Corporation to promote industrial and mineral development in Sindh.
metadata.summary: This Act establishes the Sind Industrial and Mineral Development Corporation as a body corporate with perpetual succession. The Corporation is responsible for promoting socio-economic, industrial, and mineral development, particularly in underdeveloped areas of Sindh. Its functions include planning agro-based industries, exploiting fisheries, developing minerals, and assuming control of the Sind Sugar Corporation. The Act also outlines the Corporation's powers to acquire property, enter contracts, and make rules or regulations.

name: SIND INDUSTRIAL TRADING ESTATE RECOVERY OF DUES ACT, 1973

metadata.short_title: The Sind Industrial Trading Estate Recovery of Dues Act, 1973
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for recovery of the dues of the Sind Industrial Trading Estate.
metadata.territorial_extent: the whole of the Province of Sind
repeals: Sind Ordinance, VII of 1973
metadata.one_line: Provides for the recovery of dues of the Sind Industrial Trading Estate as arrears of land-revenue.
metadata.summary: This Act facilitates the recovery of dues owed to the Sind Industrial Trading Estate by treating them as arrears of land-revenue. It defines key terms such as 'defaulter' and 'Government', and empowers the Government to declare specific dues recoverable via notification. The Act also grants the Government authority to make rules for implementing its provisions and repeals a previous ordinance.

metadata.short_title: The Sind Irrigation (Amendment) Act, 1976
metadata.long_title: An Act to further amend the Sind Irrigation Act, 1879.
metadata.max_penalty: imprisonment for a term which may extend to one year or with fine which may extend to two thousand rupees
metadata.one_line: Amends the Sind Irrigation Act, 1879 regarding module repair costs and penalties.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the Sind Irrigation Act, 1879 to address the recovery of costs for repairing tampered modules as land revenue arrears. It increases penalties for offences related to irrigation modules and introduces provisions for punishing abetment of such offences. Additionally, it establishes a mechanism for serving notices by publication when a person's whereabouts are unknown.

metadata.short_title: The Sind Katchi Abadis Act, 1987
metadata.long_title: An Act to make provision for the development and improvement of the areas of the Katchi Abadis and regularization of such Katchi Abadis and to establish an Authority for the purpose
metadata.territorial_extent: the whole of the Province of Sind
metadata.commencement: at once and deemed to have taken effect on and from the 7th day of April, 1986
repeals: The Sind Katchi Abadis Ordinance, 1986
metadata.one_line: Establishes the Human Settlement Authority to develop and improve Katchi Abadi areas in Sindh.
metadata.summary: This Act establishes the Human Settlement Authority to oversee the development, improvement, and regularization of Katchi Abadi areas in the Province of Sindh. It defines the composition and powers of the Authority's Governing Body, including members from various divisions and local councils. The legislation also provides for financial management through a Fund, mechanisms for recovery of dues, penalties for offenses, and repeals the previous 1986 Ordinance.

metadata.short_title: The Sind Land Revenue (Amendment) Act, 1976
metadata.long_title: An Act to further amend the Sind Land Revenue Act, 1967.
metadata.commencement: at once and shall be deemed to have taken effect on and from the tenth day of November, 1975
repeals: The Sind Land Revenue (Amendment) Ordinance, 1976
metadata.max_penalty: simple imprisonment for a term which may extend to one year, or with fine, or both
metadata.one_line: Amends the Sind Land Revenue Act, 1967 by defining land types, setting revenue exemptions and enhanced rates, and repealing a 1976 Ordinance.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the Sind Land Revenue Act, 1967 to define irrigated and un-irrigated land. It introduces exemptions from land revenue for owners of small plots and mandates enhanced revenue rates for larger holdings. The legislation also establishes procedures for furnishing ownership information and provides mechanisms for appeals regarding revenue assessments.

name: SIND LAND REVENUE FIRST DRAFT ASSESSMENT LISTS (VALIDATION) ACT, 1974.

metadata.short_title: The Sind Land Revenue First Draft Assessment Lists (Validation) Act, 1974
metadata.long_title: An Act to validate the first draft assessment lists made under the Sind Land Revenue Flat Rate Assessment rules, 1973.
repeals: Sind Ordinance X of 1974
key_definitions: Sind Land Revenue Flat Rate Assessment Rules, 1973
metadata.one_line: Validates first draft land revenue assessment lists in Sindh made under the 1973 rules and repeals a conflicting ordinance.
metadata.summary: This Act validates the first draft assessment lists created under the Sind Land Revenue Flat Rate Assessment Rules, 1973. It deems these lists valid and legally effective even if the required public notice was not given. Additionally, the Act repeals the Sind Ordinance X of 1974.

name: SIND LANDING AND WHARFAGE FEES ACT, 1882

metadata.short_title: The Sind Landing and Wharfage Fees Act, 1882
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the levy of fees for the use of Public Landing-places.
metadata.territorial_extent: any ports in the Province of Sind
repeals: Bombay Act III of 1879
metadata.one_line: This Act provides for the levy of fees for the use of public landing-places in ports in Sindh.
metadata.summary: The Sind Landing and Wharfage Fees Act, 1882 establishes a legal framework for levying fees on goods, passengers, animals, vehicles, and vessels using public landing-places in the Province of Sind. It empowers the Government to define port limits, determine which locations are public landing-places, and fix specific fee amounts, with a cap of six paisa per passenger. The Act also authorizes the creation of bye-laws by the Chief Customs-authority to regulate the use of landing-places and mandates the maintenance of distinct accounts for fees realized at each port.

metadata.short_title: The Sind Laws (Amendment) Act, 1985
metadata.long_title: An Act to amend the Sind Cotton Control Ordinance, 1966 and the Sind Finance Act, 1975.
metadata.one_line: Amends the Sind Cotton Control Ordinance, 1966 and the Sind Finance Act, 1975 regarding fee usage for local development schemes.
metadata.summary: This Act amends two specific laws: the Sind Cotton Control Ordinance, 1966, and the Sind Finance Act, 1975. It modifies provisions related to fees collected from cotton factory occupiers and dealers. Specifically, it directs that twenty-five percent of these fees must be allocated for local area development schemes undertaken by councils constituted under the Sind Local Government Ordinance, 1979.

name: SIND LOANS FOR AGRICULTURAL PURPOSES ACT, 1974

metadata.short_title: The Sind Loans for Agricultural Purposes Act, 1974
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for credit facilities to members of the co-operative societies and co-operative banks in Sind for agriculture purposes.
repeals: The Sind Loans for Agricultural Purposes Ordinance, 1974
metadata.one_line: Provides credit facilities to members of co-operative societies and banks in Sind for agricultural purposes.
metadata.summary: This Act establishes a framework for providing credit facilities to members of co-operative societies and banks within the province of Sind specifically for agricultural purposes. It defines key terms such as 'advance', 'borrower', and 'land' while outlining mechanisms for loan repayment, including the delivery of agricultural produce towards settlement. The legislation also empowers the Government of Sind to make rules for its implementation and repeals a previous Ordinance on the same subject.

metadata.short_title: The Sind Local Government (Amendment) Act, 1986
metadata.long_title: An Act to amend the Sind Local Government ordinance, 1979
metadata.commencement: at once and deemed to have taken effect on and from the 30th day of December, 1985
repeals: Sind Local Government (Amendment) Ordinance 1986
metadata.one_line: Amends the Sind Local Government Ordinance, 1979 by omitting specific clauses and repeals a previous amendment ordinance.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the Sind Local Government Ordinance, 1979 by omitting specific clauses from sections 21, 37, 37-A, and 51. It also repeals the Sind Local Government (Amendment) Ordinance of 1986. The Act came into force immediately but is deemed to have taken effect from December 30, 1985.

metadata.short_title: The Sind Local Government (Amendment) Act, 1987
metadata.long_title: An Act to amend the Sind Local Government Ordinance, 1979.
repeals: Sind Local Government (Amendment) Ordinance, 1987
metadata.one_line: Amends the Sind Local Government Ordinance, 1979 by adding provisions for an Advisory Committee and repealing a previous amendment ordinance.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the Sind Local Government Ordinance, 1979 to modify section 10 regarding the appointment of persons to exercise powers after council supersession. It inserts a new section 58-A establishing an Advisory Committee to advise the appointed person or authority on functions and powers. The Act also repeals the Sind Local Government (Amendment) Ordinance, 1987.

metadata.short_title: The Sind Local Government (Fifth Amendment) Act, 1987
metadata.long_title: An Act to amend the Sind Local Government Ordinance, 1979.
repeals: Sind Local Government (Fifth Amendment) Ordinance, 1987
metadata.one_line: Amends the Sind Local Government Ordinance, 1979 regarding council dissolution and repeals a previous amendment.
metadata.summary: This Act amends section 16 of the Sind Local Government Ordinance, 1979 to allow the Government to dissolve councils upon term expiry. It also appoints authorities to perform council functions after such dissolution. The Act repeals the Sind Local Government (Fifth Amendment) Ordinance, 1987.

metadata.short_title: The Sind Local Government (Fourth Amendment) Act, 1987
metadata.long_title: An Act to amend the Sind Local Government Ordinance, 1979.
repeals: Sind Local Government (Fourth Amendment) Ordinance, 1987
metadata.one_line: Amends the Sind Local Government Ordinance, 1979 regarding local bodies, elections, and taxation.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the Sind Local Government Ordinance, 1979 to update definitions for workers and zonal municipal committees. It introduces restrictions on political party symbols during elections and clarifies the relationship between the metropolitan corporation and zonal municipal committees regarding tax levies and functions. The Act also repeals the earlier Sind Local Government (Fourth Amendment) Ordinance, 1987.

metadata.short_title: The Sind Local Government (Second Amendment) Act, 1988
metadata.long_title: An Act to amend the Sind Local Government Ordinance, 1979.
metadata.commencement: at once and deemed to have taken effect on and from 29th September, 1988
repeals: The Sind Local Government (Second Amendment) Ordinance, 1988
metadata.one_line: Amends the Sind Local Government Ordinance, 1979 by omitting a subsection and repeals a previous amendment ordinance.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the Sind Local Government Ordinance, 1979 by omitting sub-section (3) of section 26. It also repeals the Sind Local Government (Second Amendment) Ordinance, 1988. The Act came into force immediately and is deemed effective from September 29, 1988.

metadata.short_title: The Sind Local Government (Second Amendment) Act, 1991
metadata.long_title: An Act to amend the Sindh Local Government Ordinance, 1979.
metadata.commencement: at once and deemed to have taken effect on and from 1st January, 1991
repeals: The Sindh Local Government (Second Amendment) Ordinance, 1991
metadata.one_line: Amends the Sindh Local Government Ordinance, 1979 regarding tax collection rights and validates council contracts.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the Sindh Local Government Ordinance, 1979 by adding specific wording to section 45 regarding leasing out rights to collect taxes. It validates contracts entered into by councils on or after January 1, 1991, without inviting officers in auction, deeming them valid despite contrary rules. The Act also repeals the Sindh Local Government (Second Amendment) Ordinance, 1991.

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Local Government (Second Amendment) Act, 1994
metadata.long_title: An Act to amend the Sind Local Government Ordinance, 1979.
repeals: The Sindh Local Government (Sindh Amendment) Ordinance, 1994
metadata.one_line: Amends the Sind Local Government Ordinance, 1979 by adding provisions for an Advisory Council and repealing a previous amendment ordinance.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the Sind Local Government Ordinance, 1979 to introduce new sub-sections regarding the appointment of an Advisory Council. It grants the Government power to assign functions to this council and defines the tenure and resignation process for its members. Additionally, it explicitly repeals the Sindh Local Government (Sindh Amendment) Ordinance, 1994.

metadata.short_title: The Sind Local Government (Sixth Amendment) Act, 1987
metadata.long_title: An Act to amend the Sind Local Government Ordinance, 1979.
repeals: Sind Local Government (Sixth Amendment) Ordinance, 1987
metadata.one_line: Amends the Sind Local Government Ordinance, 1979 regarding council membership limits and repeals a previous amendment ordinance.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the Sind Local Government Ordinance, 1979 to restrict individuals from holding membership in more than one council or electoral unit of the same council. It includes an exception for members of Zonal Municipal Committees who become members of the Karachi Metropolitan Corporation. The Act also repeals the Sind Local Government (Sixth Amendment) Ordinance, 1987.

metadata.short_title: The Sind Local Government (Third Amendment) Act, 1987
metadata.long_title: An Act to amend the Sind Local Government Ordinance, 1979.
repeals: The Sind Local Government (Third Amendment) Ordinance, 1987
metadata.one_line: Amends the Sind Local Government Ordinance, 1979 regarding council supersession and repeals a related 1987 Ordinance.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the Sind Local Government Ordinance, 1979 to modify provisions concerning the reconstitution of councils when their term is expiring. Specifically, it adds a proviso preventing reconstitution if supersession is expiring within four months of the normal term expiry. Additionally, it substitutes figures in Schedule I and repeals the Sind Local Government (Third Amendment) Ordinance, 1987.

name: SIND MINISTER’S (SALARIES, ALLOWANCES AND PRIVILEGES (AMENDMENT) ACT, 1975

metadata.short_title: The Sind Ministers (Salaries, Allowances and Privileges) (Amendment) Act, 1975
metadata.long_title: An Act to amend the Sind Ministers (Salaries, Allowances and Privileges) Act, 1975.
amends: The Sind Ministers (Salaries, Allowances and Privileges) Act, 1975
metadata.one_line: Amends the Sind Ministers (Salaries, Allowances and Privileges) Act, 1975 by substituting 'first' for 'economy' in section 9.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the Sind Ministers (Salaries, Allowances and Privileges) Act, 1975. It specifically targets section 9, sub-section (2), clause (a) of the parent Act. The amendment substitutes the word 'first' for the word 'economy'. The Act came into force immediately upon enactment.

name: SIND MINISTERS (SALARIES, ALLOWANCES AND PRIVILEGES) (AMENDMENT) ACT, 1977

metadata.short_title: The Sind Ministers (Salaries, Allowances and Privileges) (Amendment) Act, 1977
metadata.long_title: An Act to amend the Sind Ministers (Salaries, Allowances and Privileges) Act, 1975.
amends: The Sind Ministers (Salaries, Allowances and Privileges) Act, 1975
metadata.one_line: Amends the 1975 Act regarding Sind Ministers' salaries, allowances, and official residence provisions.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the Sind Ministers (Salaries, Allowances and Privileges) Act, 1975 to update definitions of maintenance and official residence. It substitutes specific clauses in section 2 and completely rewrites section 7 of the parent Act. The amendments detail financial limits for rented accommodation, government bearing of furnishing costs, appliance specifications, and entitlements after leaving office.

name: SIND MINISTERS (SALARIES, ALLOWANCES AND PRIVILEGES) (AMENDMENT) ACT, 1985

metadata.short_title: The Sind Ministers (Salaries, Allowances and Privileges) (Amendment) Act, 1985
metadata.long_title: An Act to amend the Sind Ministers (Salaries, Allowances and Privileges) Act, 1975.
metadata.commencement: at once and deemed to have taken effect on and from the date the first Chief Minister assumed office after the tenth day of March, 1985
amends: The Sind Ministers (Salaries, Allowances and Privileges) Act, 1975
metadata.one_line: Amends the 1975 Act regarding Sind Ministers' salaries, allowances, privileges, and official residence rules.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the Sind Ministers (Salaries, Allowances and Privileges) Act, 1975 to update financial provisions for Chief Ministers and Ministers. It revises equipment allowances, discretionary grants, official residence costs, furnishing limits, and leave allowances. The amendments also clarify definitions regarding 'furnishing' and establish audit requirements for discretionary grants.

name: SIND MINISTERS (SALARIES, ALLOWANCES AND PRIVILEGES) ACT, 1972.

metadata.short_title: The Sind Ministers (Salaries, Allowances and Privileges) Act, 1972
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the salaries, allowances and privileges of the Chief Minister and Ministers.
metadata.one_line: This Act determines the salaries, allowances, and privileges for the Chief Minister and Ministers of Sindh.
metadata.summary: This Act provides for the salaries, allowances, and privileges of the Chief Minister and other Ministers in the Province of Sindh. It specifies exact monetary amounts for salaries, sumptuary allowances, and various travel expenses including air, rail, and road journeys. The legislation also outlines provisions for official residences, medical facilities, leave, personal staff, and the General Provident Fund.

metadata.short_title: The Provincial Motor Vehicles (Sind Amendment) Act, 1976
metadata.long_title: An Act further to amend the Provincial Motor Vehicles Ordinance, 1965, in its application to the Province of Sind
metadata.one_line: Amends the Provincial Motor Vehicles Ordinance, 1965 regarding unmanned railway crossings and speed limits in Sindh.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the Provincial Motor Vehicles Ordinance, 1965 specifically for its application to the Province of Sind. It substitutes text in Section 91 to address 'un-manned' railway crossings and adjusts monetary figures in Section 107 from one hundred/five hundred to five hundred/one thousand respectively. The Act came into force immediately upon enactment.

name: SIND PARLIAMENTARY SECRETARIES (SALARIES, ALLOWANCES AND PRIVILEGES) (AMENDMENT) ACT, 1985

metadata.short_title: The Sind Parliamentary Secretaries (Salaries, Allowances and Privileges) (Amendment) Act, 1985
metadata.long_title: An Act to amend the Sind Parliamentary Secretaries (Salaries, Allowances and Privileges) Act, 1974.
amends: The Sind Parliamentary Secretaries (Salaries, Allowances and Privileges) Act, 1974
metadata.one_line: Amends the 1974 Act by increasing salaries and allowances for Sind Parliamentary Secretaries.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the Sind Parliamentary Secretaries (Salaries, Allowances and Privileges) Act, 1974. It substitutes specific monetary amounts in sections 3 and 4 of the parent Act to increase the salaries and allowances payable to parliamentary secretaries. The amendments came into force immediately upon enactment.

name: SIND PARLIAMENTARY SECRETARIES (SALARIES, ALLOWANCES AND PRIVILEGES) (AMENDMENT) ACT, 1987

metadata.short_title: The Sind Parliamentary Secretaries (Salaries, Allowances and Privileges) (Amendment) Act, 1987
metadata.long_title: An Act to amend the Sind Parliamentary Secretaries (Salaries, Allowances and Privileges) (Amendment) Act, 1974.
metadata.commencement: at once and deemed to have taken effect on and from the 26th day of April, 1987
amends: The Sind Parliamentary Secretaries (Salaries, Allowances and Privileges) (Amendment) Act, 1974
repeals: The Sind Parliamentary Secretaries (Salaries, Allowances and Privileges) (Amendment) Ordinance, 1987
metadata.one_line: Amends the 1974 Act regarding salaries, allowances, and privileges for Sind Parliamentary Secretaries.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the Sind Parliamentary Secretaries (Salaries, Allowances and Privileges) Act, 1974 to update salary figures and introduce new benefits. It grants official residence or house rent allowance, provides specific staff facilities like a steno-typist, defines leave entitlements up to three months, and sets travelling allowance scales. The Act also repeals the corresponding 1987 Ordinance.

metadata.short_title: The Sind People's Local Government (Amendment) Act, 1974
metadata.long_title: An Act to further amend the Sind People's Local Government Ordinance, 1972.
amends: The Sind People's Local Government Ordinance, 1972
repeals: The Sind People's Local Government (Amendment) Ordinance, 1974
metadata.one_line: Amends the Sind People's Local Government Ordinance, 1972 regarding council contracts and repeals a 1974 Ordinance.
metadata.summary: This Act further amends the Sind People's Local Government Ordinance, 1972. It specifically modifies section 42 to allow councils to enter contracts without inviting offers with government approval. The Act also repeals the Sind People's Local Government (Amendment) Ordinance, 1974.

metadata.short_title: The Sind People's Local Government (Amendment) Act, 1975
metadata.long_title: An Act to further amend the Sind People's Local Government Ordinance, 1972.
amends: The Sind People's Local Government Ordinance, 1972
repeals: The Sind People's Local Government (Second Amendment) Ordinance, 1974
metadata.one_line: Amends the Sind People's Local Government Ordinance, 1972 and repeals a 1974 Ordinance.
metadata.summary: This Act further amends the Sind People's Local Government Ordinance, 1972 by substituting specific clauses regarding local council administrators. It clarifies that officers performing duties until councils are constituted shall continue in office unless replaced by government appointment. Additionally, the Act repeals the Sind People's Local Government (Second Amendment) Ordinance, 1974.

metadata.short_title: The Sind People's Local Government (Amendment) Act, 1976
metadata.long_title: An Act to further amend the Sind People's Local Government Ordinance, 1972.
amends: The Sind People's Local Government Ordinance, 1972
repeals: The Sind People's Local Government (Amendment) Ordinance, 1976
metadata.max_penalty: fine which may extend to one thousand rupees
metadata.one_line: Amends the Sind People's Local Government Ordinance, 1972 to redefine local bodies and urban areas.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the Sind People's Local Government Ordinance, 1972 to redefine terms for cities, corporations, and municipalities. It establishes new sections regarding the constitution of councils in urban areas and clarifies the succession of existing councils. The legislation also updates schedules related to functions, taxes, and fees levied by local authorities.

metadata.short_title: The Sind People's Local Government (Amendment) Act, 1973
metadata.long_title: An Act to amend the Sind People's Local Government Ordinance, 1972.
repeals: Sind People's Local Government (Amendment) Ordinance, 1973
metadata.max_penalty: imprisonment for a term which may extend to three months or with fine which may extend to one thousand rupees or with both
metadata.one_line: Amends the Sind People's Local Government Ordinance, 1972 by increasing penalties and adding new offences regarding objectionable writings.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the Sind People's Local Government Ordinance, 1972 to increase the penalty for certain offences from a fine up to five hundred rupees to imprisonment up to three months or a fine up to one thousand rupees. It also adds two new entries to Schedule X of the said Ordinance concerning objectionable slogans on buildings and the failure to remove such writings. The Act repeals the Sind People's Local Government (Amendment) Ordinance, 1973.

name: SIND PRIVATE SCHOOLS (MANAGEMENT AND CONTROL) ACT, 1974

metadata.short_title: The Sind Private Schools (Management and Control) Act, 1974
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for control over and management of private schools in Sind.
metadata.administering_body: Minister for Education, Government of Sind
metadata.one_line: This Act establishes a Board of Governors to manage and control private schools in Sindh.
metadata.summary: The Sind Private Schools (Management and Control) Act, 1974 provides for the control and management of private schools within the Province of Sindh. It establishes a Board of Governors consisting of members nominated by the Parent Body, the Controlling Authority, elected parents/guardians, and elected teachers. The Act outlines the constitution, powers, duties, and tenure of the Board, as well as provisions regarding school funds, staff councils, inspections, and financial reporting requirements.

metadata.short_title: The Sind Provincial Assembly (Members) Privileges Act, 1975
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the privileges of the members of the Provincial Assembly of Sind.
repeals: The Provincial Assembly of Sind Privileges Act, 1972
The Provincial Assembly of Sind Privileges (Amendment) Act, 1972
metadata.max_penalty: imprisonment up to six months or fine up to five thousand rupees or both
metadata.one_line: This Act defines and grants privileges, immunities, and protections to members of the Provincial Assembly of Sind.
metadata.summary: The Act provides specific privileges for members of the Provincial Assembly of Sind, including immunity from civil or criminal proceedings related to their official duties. It restricts detention during assembly sessions, limits court appearances, protects salaries from attachment, and grants VIP status. The legislation also outlines penalties for breaching these privileges and establishes procedures for summoning witnesses.

name: SIND PROVINCIAL ASSEMBLY (MEMBERS) WELFARE FUND ACT, 1975

metadata.short_title: The Sind Provincial Assembly (Members) Welfare Fund Act, 1975
metadata.long_title: An Act to establish a fund for providing financial aid to Members of the Provincial Assembly and their heirs.
metadata.one_line: Establishes a welfare fund for financial aid to Sindh Assembly members, ex-members, and their heirs.
metadata.summary: This Act establishes the Members Welfare Fund to provide financial assistance to Members of the Provincial Assembly of Sind, ex-Members, and their heirs. The Fund is financed by monthly contributions from Members and grants from the Government. A Committee comprising the Speaker, Chief Minister, and other officials manages the Fund and sanctions financial aid for members facing disability, illness, or death.

name: SIND PROVINCIAL ASSEMBLY (SALARIES AND ALLOWANCES OF MEMBERS) ACT, 1972.

metadata.short_title: The Sind Provincial Assembly (Salaries and Allowances of Members) Act, 1972
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the salaries and allowances of the Members of the Provincial Assembly of Sind
repeals: The Sind Provincial Assembly Members (Salary, Allowances and Privileges) Order, 1972
metadata.one_line: This Act defines salaries, allowances, and privileges for members of the Provincial Assembly of Sind.
metadata.summary: This Act provides for the salaries and allowances of Members of the Provincial Assembly of Sind. It specifies rates for monthly salary, daily allowances, travelling and mileage allowances, free transit by railway, and medical facilities. The Act also outlines conditions under which salary is not payable, such as during detention or failure to attend meetings, and allows members to opt for a consolidated salary.

metadata.short_title: The Sind Public Authorities Seals Act, 1883
metadata.long_title: An Act to enable Government to prescribe the Official Seals of Sessions Judges, Magistrates and other public authorities.
metadata.commencement: on such date as the Provincial Government shall therein fix
repeals: Bombay Act 2 of 1870
metadata.repealed_by: Sind Laws (Adaptation, Revision, Repeal and Declaration) Ordinance, 1955 (Sind 5 of 1955)
metadata.one_line: This Act empowers the Provincial Government to prescribe official seals for various public authorities in Sindh.
metadata.summary: The Sind Public Authorities Seals Act, 1883 enables the Provincial Government of Sindh to prescribe official seals for Sessions Judges, Magistrates, and other public authorities. The Government may issue notifications in the Official Gazette to define which seals specific authorities shall have and use. These notifications can be modified or rescinded at any time by a subsequent notification from the Provincial Government.

metadata.short_title: The Sind Public Conveyances Act, 1920
metadata.long_title: An Act to amend the Law relating to the regulation of public conveyances.
repeals: Sind Act No. VII of 1920
metadata.one_line: This Act regulates public conveyances in Sindh through licensing, fare fixation, and penalties for unlicensed operation.
metadata.summary: The Sind Public Conveyances Act, 1920 amends the law regarding the regulation of public conveyances in Sindh. It establishes a licensing system for vehicles, horses, and drivers, requiring them to be licensed by the Superintendent (Commissioner of Police). The Act empowers the Superintendent to fix legal fares, appoint stands, and inspect conveyances. It also defines various offences related to unlicensed operation, failure to produce documents, and misuse of licensed vehicles, prescribing penalties for such violations.

metadata.short_title: The Sind Public Service Commission (Amendment) Act, 1974
metadata.long_title: An Act to amend the Sind Public Service Commission Act, 1973.
amends: The Sind Public Service Commission Act, 1973
metadata.one_line: Amends the Sind Public Service Commission Act, 1973 to add functions prescribed by rules.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the Sind Public Service Commission Act, 1973 to expand the scope of the Commission's duties. It specifically adds a provision allowing the Commission to perform other functions as may be prescribed. The amendment came into force immediately upon enactment on November 26, 1974.

metadata.short_title: The Sind Race-Courses Licensing Act, 1912
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the licensing of race-courses in the Province of Sind.
metadata.territorial_extent: the whole of the Province of Sind
metadata.max_penalty: one thousand rupees
metadata.one_line: This Act regulates horse racing in Sindh by establishing a licensing system for race-courses and prescribing penalties for unlicensed races.
metadata.summary: The Sind Race-Courses Licensing Act, 1912 provides for the regulation of horse-racing within the Province of Sind. It establishes a licensing system where only licensed race-courses can host horse-races, prohibiting betting or wagering as a condition of the license. The Provincial Government is empowered to grant, withhold, or cancel licenses and may issue exemptions. Offenses include participating in unlicensed races, holding such races without a license, or contravening license conditions, punishable by fines up to one thousand rupees.

metadata.short_title: The Sind Regional Plan Organization (Amendment) Act, 1986
metadata.long_title: An Act to amend the Sind Regional Plan Organization Act, 1975
metadata.one_line: Amends the Sind Regional Plan Organization Act, 1975 to designate the Chief Minister as Chairman.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the Sind Regional Plan Organization Act, 1975 by substituting the Chief Minister of Sindh as the Chairman in section 4. It was enacted on October 25, 1986, and came into force immediately upon enactment. The legislation specifically targets the administrative structure of the regional planning organization within the province.

metadata.short_title: SIND REGULATION VIII OF 1827
metadata.long_title: A Regulation to provide for the formal recognition of heirs, executors and administrators, and for the appointment of administrators and managers of property by the Courts.
repeals: Sindh Regulation No.VIII of 1827
metadata.one_line: Provides for the formal recognition of heirs and administrators and the appointment of managers by courts in Sind.
metadata.summary: This Regulation establishes procedures for the formal recognition of heirs, executors, and administrators of deceased persons' estates. It outlines the process for obtaining certificates from District Courts to manage property or sue for recovery without court interference when rights are undisputed. The document also details mechanisms for appointing administrators when no competent claimant exists, succession is disputed, or heirs are incompetent, ensuring proper management of estates.

metadata.short_title: Sindh Regulation Act, 1827
metadata.long_title: A Regulation to declare and define military authority, in its relations to the civil power and to the community at large.
repeals: Act XIII of 1889
metadata.status_evidence: PREAMBLE, Rep. Act XIII of 1889. CHAPTER I TO VI 1 to 39. Rep. Act XIII of 1889. 44 to 55 Rep. Act. XIII of 1889.
metadata.one_line: Defines military authority and procedures for civil aid to marching troops in Sindh.
metadata.summary: This Regulation declares and defines military authority in relation to the civil power. It outlines the process for obtaining civil aid, such as guides and provisions, when military forces march through a district. The text also details rules for impressment during emergencies and establishes mechanisms for compensation to individuals suffering damage from troop movements.

metadata.short_title: Sind Regulation VIII of 1827
metadata.long_title: A Regulation to provide for the formal recognition of heirs, executors and administrators, and for the appointment of administrators and managers of property by the Courts.
repeals: Succession Certificate Act, 1889
metadata.one_line: Provides for formal recognition of heirs and appointment of administrators by Courts in Sind.
metadata.summary: This Regulation establishes the legal framework for recognizing heirs, executors, and administrators of deceased persons' estates in the Province of Sind. It outlines procedures for obtaining certificates of heirship or administratorship from District Courts when rights are undisputed or disputed. The document also details the process for appointing administrators when no competent claimant exists or when heirs are incompetent to manage affairs.

metadata.short_title: The Sind Rented Premises (Amendment) Act, 1986
metadata.long_title: An Act to amend the Sind Rented Premises Ordinance, 1979.
metadata.one_line: Amends the Sind Rented Premises Ordinance, 1979 regarding execution of orders and Controller authority.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the Sind Rented Premises Ordinance, 1979 to clarify the role of the Controller in executing final orders. It stipulates that all questions arising between parties regarding the execution, discharge, or satisfaction of such orders must be determined by the Controller rather than through a separate suit. Additionally, it mandates that any payment, compromise, or agreement in ejectment proceedings is invalid unless made before or with the permission of the authority passing the order.

metadata.short_title: The Sind Revenue Jurisdiction Act, 1876
metadata.long_title: An Act to limit the jurisdiction of the Civil Courts in Sind in matters relating to the land-revenue, and for other purposes.
repeals: Act XXIII of 1871
metadata.one_line: Limits Civil Court jurisdiction in Sind regarding land revenue and defines related terms.
metadata.summary: This Act limits the jurisdiction of Civil Courts in Sind specifically concerning matters of land revenue. It establishes procedures for appealing to the High Court on questions of jurisdiction and grants specific privileges to the Provincial Government when defending suits. The Act also defines key terms such as 'land', 'land-revenue', and 'Revenue-officer'.

metadata.short_title: The Sind Securities Contracts Control Act, 1925
metadata.long_title: An Act to regulate and control certain contracts for the purchase and sale of securities in the Province of Sind.
metadata.territorial_extent: the whole of the Province of Sind
metadata.commencement: on such date as the Provincial Government may, by notification in the Official Gazette, appoint
metadata.one_line: Regulates and controls contracts for the purchase and sale of securities in Sindh.
metadata.summary: This Act regulates and controls specific contracts involving the purchase and sale of securities within the Province of Sind. It defines key terms such as 'securities', 'stock-exchange', and 'ready delivery contract'. The Act empowers the Provincial Government to recognize stock exchanges and sanction rules governing their operations, including the making of non-ready delivery contracts. Contracts entered into after a notified date that do not comply with sanctioned rules are declared void.

metadata.short_title: The Sind Seed Corporation Act, 1976
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the establishment of a Corporation for production, procurement, processing, marketing and distribution of seed for the Province of Sind.
metadata.commencement: on such day as Government may, by notification, appoint
metadata.one_line: Establishes the Sind Seed Corporation for seed production, procurement, processing, marketing and distribution in Sindh.
metadata.summary: This Act establishes the Sind Seed Corporation as a body corporate to handle the production, procurement, processing, marketing, and distribution of seeds within the Province of Sindh. The Corporation is governed by a Board consisting of government officials and private sector members, with powers delegated to an Executive Authority for policy guidance and financial approval. It outlines the financial structure, including budget preparation, annual audits, and the recovery of dues as arrears of land revenue.

metadata.short_title: The Sind Service Tribunals (Amendment) Act, 1974
metadata.long_title: An Act to amend the Sind Service Tribunals Act, 1973.
repeals: The Sind Service Tribunals (Amendment) Ordinance, 1974
key_definitions: post in Grade 16 or an equivalent or a higher post
metadata.one_line: Amends the Sind Service Tribunals Act, 1973 regarding definitions, appeals, and procedural rules.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the Sind Service Tribunals Act, 1973 to update definitions of civil servants and posts. It modifies provisions regarding appeals against departmental authority decisions and inserts new sections on limitation periods for appeals. The Act also repeals the corresponding Amendment Ordinance from 1974.

metadata.short_title: The Sind Service Tribunals (Amendment) Act, 1988
metadata.long_title: An Act to amend the Sind Service Tribunals Act, 1973.
metadata.one_line: Amends the Sind Service Tribunals Act, 1973 by substituting 'two members' with 'not more than two members' in section 3.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the Sind Service Tribunals Act, 1973 to alter the composition of service tribunals. Specifically, it substitutes the phrase 'two members' with 'not more than two members' in clause (b) of sub-section (3) of section 3 of the 1973 Act. The amendment came into force immediately upon enactment.

metadata.short_title: The Sind Service Tribunals (Second Amendment) Act, 1974
metadata.long_title: An Act to further amend the Sind Service Tribunals Act, 1973.
repeals: The Sind Services Tribunals (Second Amendment) Ordinance, 1974
establishes: Committee consisting of three persons headed by a person not below the rank of the Chairman
metadata.one_line: Amends the Sind Service Tribunals Act, 1973 regarding appointment terms and removal procedures for tribunal members.
metadata.summary: This Act further amends the Sind Service Tribunals Act, 1973 to extend the term of office for Tribunal Chairmen and members. It establishes a committee procedure to inquire into physical/mental incapacity or misconduct by tribunal members, allowing their removal if such issues are confirmed. The Act defines 'misconduct' to include acts prejudicial to service discipline, political influence, conviction for moral turpitude, sectarian participation, disregard of business rules, or living beyond means.

name: SIND SMALL INDUSTRIES AND HANDICRAFTS DEVELOPMENT CORPORATION ACT, 1972

metadata.short_title: The Sind Small Industries Corporation Act, 1972
metadata.long_title: An Act to establish a Small Industries Corporation in the Province of Sind.
metadata.territorial_extent: the whole of the Province of Sind
metadata.commencement: at once and shall be deemed to have taken effect on and from the first day of July, 1972
repeals: Sind Ordinance XXIII of 1972
metadata.one_line: Establishes the Small Industries Corporation in Sindh to promote small and cottage industries.
metadata.summary: This Act establishes the Small Industries Corporation, Sind as a body corporate with perpetual succession. It defines the constitution, management, and functions of the Corporation, including powers to grant loans and manage estates. The Act also facilitates the transfer of assets from the defunct West Pakistan Small Industries Corporation located in Sindh.

metadata.short_title: The Sind Small Industries Corporation (Amendment) Act, 1987
metadata.long_title: An Act to amend the Sind Small Industries Corporation Act, 1972
metadata.one_line: Amends the Sind Small Industries Corporation Act, 1972 to redefine 'small industry' regarding capital investment limits.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the Sind Small Industries Corporation Act, 1972 by substituting clause (n) of section 2. The amendment redefines a 'small industry' as one engaged in handicrafts or the manufacture of consumer or producer goods with fixed capital investment not exceeding ten million rupees. It allows the Government to fix higher amounts via notification in the Official Gazette from time to time.

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Societies Registration (Amendment) Act, 1912
metadata.long_title: An Act to amend the Societies Registration Act, 1860.
metadata.one_line: Amends the Societies Registration Act, 1860 regarding property distribution upon dissolution.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the Societies Registration Act, 1860 to allow members of a dissolved society to vote on distributing remaining property to the Government. The amendment applies to societies dissolved under section 13 of the said Act after satisfying all debts and liabilities. It requires previous sanction from the Governor-General as per the Indian Councils Act, 1892.

name: SIND SPEAKER’S AND DEPUTY SPEAKER’S (SALARIES ALLOWANCES AND PRIVILEGES) (AMENDMENT) ACT, 1976

amends: The Sind Speaker's and Deputy Speaker's (Salaries, Allowances and Privileges) Act, 1975
metadata.one_line: Amends the 1975 Act to assign maintenance of Speaker/Deputy Speaker residence to the Government.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the Sind Speaker's and Deputy Speaker's (Salaries, Allowances and Privileges) Act, 1975. It adds a new provision stating that the maintenance of the residence of the Speaker or Deputy Speaker shall be undertaken by the Government. The amendment is deemed to have always been part of the original Act.

name: SIND SPEAKER’S AND DEPUTY SPEAKER’S (SALARIES, ALLOWANCE AND PRIVILEGES) ACT, 1972.

It specifies exact monetary amounts for salaries and allowances for taking up office, as well as provisions for official residence, transport, medical facilities, and leave. The Act also outlines rules regarding the use of government property and repeals a previous Order from 1972.

name: SIND SPEAKER’S AND DEPUTY SPEAKER’S (SALARIES, ALLOWANCES AND PRIVILEGES) (AMENDMENT) ACT, 1985

metadata.summary: This Act amends the Sind Speaker's and Deputy Speaker's (Salaries, Allowances and Privileges) Act, 1975 to update financial provisions. It introduces a new section granting an equipment allowance and increases various salary figures and residence allowances. The amendments apply specifically to the office of the Speaker and Deputy Speaker within the Provincial Assembly of Sindh.

metadata.summary: This Act amends the Sind Speaker's and Deputy Speaker's (Salaries, Allowances and Privileges) Act, 1975. It specifically targets section 9, sub-section (2), clause (a) of the parent Act. The amendment substitutes the word 'first' for the word 'economy'. The Act came into force immediately upon enactment.

name: SIND STANDARD WEIGHTS AND MEASURES ENFORCEMENT ACT, 1975

metadata.short_title: The Sind Standard Weights and Measures Enforcement Act, 1975
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the enforcement of standard weights and measures in the Province of Sind and matters connected therewith.
metadata.commencement: on such date as Government may, by notification, appoint

establishes: Assistant Inspector of Weights and Measures
metadata.max_penalty: fine which may extend to two thousand rupees
metadata.one_line: This Act enforces standard weights and measures in Sindh, establishing controllers and inspectors to regulate trade transactions.
metadata.summary: The Act provides for the enforcement of standard weights and measures within the Province of Sind. It establishes a hierarchy of officials including Controllers and Inspectors responsible for verifying, stamping, and regulating commercial weights and measures used in trade. The legislation outlines specific prohibitions against using non-standard or unstamped instruments, mandates licensing for manufacture, and prescribes penalties for various offences related to fraudulent weighing or failure to comply with regulations.

metadata.short_title: The Sind Tax Evasion (Punishment) (Amendment) Act, 1976
metadata.long_title: An Act to amend the Sind Tax Evasion (Punishment) Act, 1974.
metadata.one_line: Amends the Sind Tax Evasion (Punishment) Act, 1974 by adding new entries to its schedule.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the Sind Tax Evasion (Punishment) Act, 1974 by adding three new entries to its Schedule. The added entries relate to fees under the Sind Cotton Control Ordinance, 1966, the Sind Finance Act, 1975, and the Workers Children (Education) Ordinance, 1972. It came into force immediately upon enactment.

metadata.short_title: The Sind Tax Evasion (Punishment) Act, 1974
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide deterrent punishment for evasion of tax payable under certain laws and to make Special provision for trial of defaulters.
metadata.max_penalty: imprisonment for a term which may extend to two years or with fine which may extend to the amount not less then the amount of tax due from him or with both
metadata.one_line: Provides deterrent punishment for tax evasion and special trial provisions for defaulters in Sindh.
metadata.summary: This Act establishes deterrent punishments for evading taxes payable under specific scheduled laws. It defines key terms such as Government, Scheduled Law, and Tax, and outlines penalties including imprisonment and fines for those who withhold information or furnish false data to evade tax payments. The Act also specifies that cognizance of offences shall be taken by a specially empowered Magistrate of the first class upon written complaint.

name: SIND TEACHING PROMOTION AND USE OF SINDHI LANGUAGE ACT, 1972

metadata.short_title: The Sind (Teaching, Promotion and Use of Sindhi Language) Act, 1972
metadata.long_title: An Act to prescribe measures for the teaching, promotion and use of Sindhi language.
metadata.one_line: This Act prescribes measures for the teaching, promotion and use of the Sindhi language in Sindh.
metadata.summary: The Act provides for the compulsory teaching of Sindhi and Urdu in schools from class IV to XII. It establishes Academies and Boards for the cultural advancement of the Sindhi language. Furthermore, it authorizes the Government to progressively use Sindhi in government offices, courts, and the Assembly.

metadata.short_title: The Tenancy (Amendment) Act, 1974
metadata.long_title: An Act to amend the Sind Tenancy Act, 1950.
metadata.one_line: Amends the Sind Tenancy Act, 1950 to extend its application to the whole Province of Sind.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the Sind Tenancy Act, 1950 by substituting subsection (2) of section 1. The amendment extends the territorial jurisdiction of the 1950 Act to cover the entire Province of Sind. It came into force immediately upon enactment on March 21, 1974.

metadata.short_title: The Sind Town-Planning Act, 1915
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the making and execution of town-planning schemes.
metadata.max_penalty: fine which may extend to Rs.1,000 and, in the case of a continuing contravention, an additional fine which may extend to Rs.10 for every day during which such contravention continues after conviction
metadata.administering_body: local authority (People's Municipality or People's Town Committee)
metadata.one_line: This Act provides for the making and execution of town-planning schemes in Sindh to regulate development, sanitation, and amenity.
metadata.summary: The Sind Town-Planning Act, 1915 empowers local authorities to prepare and execute town-planning schemes for areas within Sindh. It outlines procedures for declaring intentions, preparing drafts, handling objections, and obtaining Provincial Government sanction. The Act covers financial aspects like cost calculation and compensation, establishes an Arbitrator and Tribunal of Arbitration to resolve disputes, and grants powers for compulsory acquisition and eviction to enforce the final scheme.

metadata.short_title: The Sind Universities (Amendment) Act, 1976

metadata.summary: This Act amends the University of Sind Act, 1972 and the University of Karachi Act, 1972 to facilitate the establishment of Additional Campuses. It introduces new roles such as the Pro-Vice-Chancellor and Board of Governors for these campuses while updating administrative structures and retirement ages. The legislation also repeals a previous Ordinance on the same subject.

metadata.short_title: The University of Sind Act, 1972

repeals: West Pakistan (University of Sind) Ordinance, 1961
Sind Ordinance XVI, 1972

metadata.summary: The University of Sind Act, 1972 was enacted to reconstitute and re-organize the University of Sind for greater autonomy. It establishes various governing bodies including the Chancellor, Vice-Chancellor, Senate, and Syndicate, along with committees for finance, affiliation, and discipline. The Act defines key terms, outlines the powers of different authorities, and repeals previous ordinances related to the university.

name: SIND UNLAWFUL SALE AND STOCKING FOR SALE OF MEDICAL EQUIPMENT AND DRUGS ACT, 1974.

metadata.summary: The Act provides punishment for the unlawful sale and stocking for sale of drugs and medical equipment that belong to the Government of Sind. It defines key terms such as 'drug', 'equipment', and 'official mark' and prescribes penalties including imprisonment up to three years or fines up to ten thousand rupees. The law also authorizes the confiscation of seized items and empowers the government to make rules for its implementation.

name: SIND URBAN IMMOVABLE PROPERTY TAX (AMENDMENT) ACT, 1987

metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the eradication and curbing the menace of involuntary donation or forced "Chanda" in the Province of Sindh.
repeals: The Sindh (Eradication and Curbing the Menace of Involuntary Donation or Forced Chanda) Ordinance, 2002
metadata.max_penalty: simple imprisonment which may extend to three months and with fine which may extend to ten thousand rupees
metadata.one_line: This Act prohibits involuntary donations and forced Chanda in Sindh, prescribing penalties and repealing the 2002 Ordinance.
metadata.summary: The Act aims to eradicate involuntary donations or forced 'Chanda' within the Province of Sindh. It defines key terms such as donor, door step, and fund, while prohibiting the collection of funds at a donor's premises. Any collected funds in contravention are forfeited to the Government, and offenders face imprisonment up to three months and a fine up to ten thousand rupees.

name: SINDH (MARTIAL LAW ORDER NO.227) REPEAL ACT, 1989

metadata.short_title: The Sindh (Martial Law Order No.227) Repeal Act, 1989
metadata.long_title: An Act to repeal Martial Law Order No.227 issued by Martial Law Administrator Zone 'C'
repeals: Martial Law Order No.227
metadata.one_line: This Act repeals Martial Law Order No.227 issued by the Martial Law Administrator Zone C in Sindh.
metadata.summary: The Sindh (Martial Law Order No.227) Repeal Act, 1989 was enacted to repeal a specific martial law order issued by the Martial Law Administrator for Zone C. The legislation applies to the Province of Sindh and came into force immediately upon enactment. It serves to remove the legal effect of the specified martial law order from the statute book.

metadata.short_title: The Sindh (Poultry Vaccine Centre) Act, 1995
metadata.long_title: An act to provide for the establishment of Poultry Vaccine Centre in the province of Sindh.
repeals: The Sindh (Poultry Vaccine Centre) Ordinance, 1995
metadata.one_line: Establishes the Sindh Poultry Vaccine Centre as a body corporate to produce vaccines and conduct research.
metadata.summary: This Act establishes the Sindh Poultry Vaccine Centre in Karachi as a body corporate with perpetual succession. The Centre is administered by a Board comprising government officials, university representatives, and industry leaders. Its functions include accelerating vaccine production, undertaking scientific research, and promoting joint ventures. The Act also provides for the Centre's finance, audit, accounts, and powers to make rules and regulations.

name: SINDH (PROHIBITION OF TAKING MINERALS INCLUDING RETI (SAND) AND BAJRI FROM ANY LAND) ACT, 2003

metadata.short_title: The Sindh (Prohibition of taking minerals including reti (sand) and bajri from any land) Act, 2003
metadata.long_title: An Act to provides for the prohibition of taking minerals including reti (sand) and bajri from any land by excavation or otherwise, in the Province of Sindh.
repeals: The Sindh (Prohibition of taking Minerals including reti(sand) bajri from any land) Ordinance, 2003
metadata.max_penalty: imprisonment up to one year and fine not exceeding twenty thousand rupees
metadata.one_line: Prohibits taking minerals like sand and bajri from Sindh land without government sanction.
metadata.summary: This Act prohibits the excavation or removal of minerals, specifically reti (sand) and bajri, from any land in the Province of Sindh. It mandates that no person may take these minerals without prior sanction from the Government of Sindh, provided such sanction does not adversely affect topography, archaeology, ecology, or the environment. The Act establishes punishments for contravention, including imprisonment and fines, and grants immunity to officers acting in good faith under its provisions.

name: SINDH (REGULARIZATION OF ADHOC AND CONTRACT EMPLYEES) ACT, 2013

metadata.short_title: The Sindh (Regularization of Adhoc and Contract Employees) Act, 2013
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for regularization of the services of certain employees appointed on adhoc and contract basis or otherwise (excluding the employees appointed on daily-wages and work-charged basis).
metadata.one_line: This Act regularizes adhoc and contract employees in the Government of Sindh appointed on BS-1 to BS-18 scales.
metadata.summary: The Sindh (Regularization of Adhoc and Contract Employees) Act, 2013 provides for the regularization of services for certain employees appointed on an adhoc or contract basis within the Province of Sindh. It specifically excludes employees appointed on a daily-wages or work-charged basis from its provisions. The Act deems eligible employees in service immediately before its commencement as having been validly appointed on a regular basis against posts in BS-1 to BS-18 or equivalent basic scales.

name: SINDH (REPEAL OF THE POLICE ORDER, 2002 AND REVIVAL OF THE POLICE ACT, 1861) ACT, 2011

metadata.short_title: The Sindh (Repeal of the Police Order, 2002 and Revival of the Police Act, 1861) Act, 2011

The Sindh (Repeal of the Police Order,2002 and Revival of the Police Act,1861) Ordinance,2011
repeals: The Police Order, 2002 (Chief Executive's Order No.XXII of 2002)
The Sindh (Repeal of the Police Order,2002 and Revival of the Police Act,1861) Ordinance,2011
metadata.one_line: This Act repeals the Police Order 2002 and revives the Police Act 1861 in Sindh with immediate effect.
metadata.summary: The document repeals the Police Order, 2002 (Chief Executive's Order No.XXII of 2002) to the extent it applies to Sindh. It simultaneously revives the Police Act, 1861 as it stood on August 13, 2002, treating it as if never repealed. The Act ensures that all orders, proceedings, and appointments made under the repealed Order between August 14, 2002, and the commencement of this Act remain in force until altered by the Chief Minister.

name: SINDH (REPEAL OF THE SINDH LOCAL GOVERNMENT ORDINANCE, 2001 AND REVIVAL OF THE SINDH LOCAL GOVERNMENT ORDINANCE, 1979) ACT, 2011

metadata.long_title: An Act to repeal the Sindh Local Government Ordinance, 2001 (Ordinance No.XXVII of 2001) and revive the Sindh Local Government Ordinance, 1979 (Ordinance No.XII of 1979).

metadata.summary: The document repeals the Sindh Local Government Ordinance, 2001 and immediately revives the Sindh Local Government Ordinance, 1979 as it stood on August 5, 2001. It ensures that all orders, proceedings, and appointments made under the repealed ordinance between August 6, 2001, and the Act's commencement remain in force until altered by the Chief Minister. The Act also empowers the Chief Minister to remove any difficulties arising from its provisions via notification.

metadata.summary: This legislation was enacted to repeal the Sindh Peoples Local Government Act, 2012 and simultaneously revive the Sindh Local Government Ordinance, 1979 as it stood on September 7, 2012. It ensures that all orders, proceedings, appointments, and legal instruments made under the repealed Act between September 7, 2012, and the commencement of this Act remain in force until altered by the Chief Minister or authorized authorities. The Act also provides for the removal of any difficulties arising from its provisions through notifications issued by the Chief Minister.

metadata.commencement: at once and deemed to have taken effect on 1st January, 2003
metadata.one_line: This Act regulates the appointment, powers, functions, and privileges of Advisors to the Chief Minister of Sindh.
metadata.summary: This Act provides for the appointment, powers, functions, salaries, allowances, and privileges of Advisors to the Chief Minister of Sindh. It defines key terms such as 'Advisor', 'Chief Minister', and 'Family' within the context of this legislation. The Act grants the Chief Minister discretion over appointments while limiting the number of advisors to five and bars court jurisdiction over decisions made under its powers.

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Agricultural Income Tax Act, 2025
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the modification of tax on agricultural income in the Province of Sindh.
metadata.territorial_extent: the whole of the Province of Sindh
repeals: The Sindh Agricultural Income Tax Ordinance, 2000
key_definitions: Agriculture Income Tax officer or AITO
metadata.one_line: This Act modifies agricultural income tax in Sindh, establishing rates and repealing the 2000 Ordinance.
metadata.summary: The Sindh Agricultural Income Tax Act, 2025 provides for the modification of tax on agricultural income within the Province of Sindh. It defines key terms such as agricultural income, assessment years, and the Board (Sindh Revenue Board), while establishing specific tax rates for individuals and companies. The Act also introduces a super tax for high-earning owners and outlines penalties for non-compliance, including failure to file returns or concealment of income.

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Agricultural Supplies Organization (Amendment) Act, 1989
metadata.long_title: An Act to amend the Sind Agricultural Supplies Organization Act, 1973.
metadata.one_line: Amends the Sind Agricultural Supplies Organization Act, 1973 by deleting specific words in section 5.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the Sind Agricultural Supplies Organization Act, 1973. It specifically targets section 5, sub-section (1) of the parent Act. The amendment involves deleting the words 'not exceeding seven' from the text.

name: SINDH ALLOPATHIC SYSTEM (PREVENTION OF MISUSE) ACT, 2014

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Allopathic System (Prevention of Misuse) Act, 2014
metadata.long_title: An Act to prevent the misuse of the allopathic system of medicine and to provide for matters connected therewith.
metadata.territorial_extent: the whole of the Province of Sindh
metadata.max_penalty: imprisonment which may extend to one year or with fine not exceeding forty five thousand rupees or with both
metadata.one_line: Prevents misuse of allopathic medicine in Sindh by regulating titles, degrees, surgeries, and drug prescriptions.
metadata.summary: This Act prevents the misuse of the allopathic system of medicine within the Province of Sindh. It prohibits unqualified persons from using the title 'doctor', claiming medical qualifications, performing surgeries (except minor ones), prescribing dangerous drugs, or selling certain medicines without proper labeling. The law empowers the Government to make rules and imposes penalties for contravention.

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Animals Slaughter Control (Amendment) Act, 2004
