metadata.summary: This Act amends the Sind Animals Slaughter Control Act, 1963 by substituting specific clauses regarding government notifications. It also repeals the Sindh Animals Slaughter Control (Amendment) Ordinance, 2004. The legislation comes into force immediately upon enactment.

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Arms (Amendment) Act, 2014
metadata.long_title: An Act to further amend the Sindh Arms Act, 2013.
metadata.one_line: Amends the Sindh Arms Act, 2013 to allow license extension to whole of Pakistan.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the Sindh Arms Act, 2013 by adding a new sub-section to Section 12. The amendment empowers the Licensing Authority to extend a license to the whole of Pakistan upon receipt of an application with sufficient and valid reasons. It came into force immediately upon enactment.

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Arms (Amendment) Act, 2015
metadata.long_title: An Act to amend the Sindh Arms Act, 2013.
repeals: Pakistan Arms Ordinance, 1995 (in its application to the Province of Sindh, except provisions relating to manufacturing including conversion, export or import of arms and ammunition)
metadata.one_line: Amends the Sindh Arms Act, 2013 and repeals specific provisions of the Pakistan Arms Ordinance, 1995 in Sindh.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the Sindh Arms Act, 2013 to further regulate arms control within the province. It specifically repeals certain provisions of the Pakistan Arms Ordinance, 1995 that applied to Sindh, excluding those related to manufacturing, conversion, export, or import of arms and ammunition. The Act ensures that actions taken under the repealed ordinance remain valid until amended by this legislation.

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Arms (Amendment) Act, 2016
metadata.long_title: An Act to amend the Sindh Arms Act, 2013.
metadata.one_line: Amends the Sindh Arms Act, 2013 to mandate ballistic signature registration for firearms.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the Sindh Arms Act, 2013 to introduce new provisions regarding the registration of firearms. It requires arms dealers to collect verified thumb impressions and CNIC copies from purchasers via NADRA before selling weapons. Additionally, dealers must submit two empty cartridges fired from the weapon for ballistic signature registration at a Forensic Lab immediately after the sale.

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Arms (Amendment) Act, 2017
metadata.long_title: An Act to amend the Sindh Arms Act, 2013.
metadata.one_line: Amends the Sindh Arms Act, 2013 to exclude certain personnel and tax payers from permanent residency conditions.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the Sindh Arms Act, 2013 by adding a proviso to Section 8. The amendment specifies that conditions regarding permanent residence in the Province of Sindh do not apply to specific groups. These groups include Armed Services personnel, Civil Armed Forces employees, Federal Government employees, autonomous body staff, directors or senior management of public and private companies, and tax payers who paid at least five hundred thousand rupees in income tax in the last financial year.

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Arms (Amendment) Act, 2021
metadata.long_title: An Act to amend the Sindh Arms Act, 2013.
metadata.one_line: Amends the Sindh Arms Act, 2013 to update terminology and add clauses regarding weapon disposal and technological advances.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the Sindh Arms Act, 2013 to replace the word 'enshrining' with 'including' in section 39. It adds new clauses concerning the disposal of firearms and weapons not required before any Court of Law in cases, appeals, or revisions. Additionally, it includes provisions for rules regarding technological advances used for the purposes of the Act. The legislation came into force immediately upon enactment by the Provincial Assembly of Sindh.

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Arms Act, 2013
metadata.long_title: An Act to reform the legislation pertaining to the arms and ammunition in the Province of Sindh.
metadata.territorial_extent: the whole of the Province of Sindh
metadata.commencement: on such date as Government may notify in the official gazette
repeals: Pakistan Arms Ordinance, 1965
metadata.one_line: This Act reforms legislation on arms and ammunition in Sindh to curb proliferation and ensure licenses are issued to bona fide persons.
metadata.summary: The Sindh Arms Act, 2013 was enacted to reform existing laws regarding arms and ammunition in the Province of Sindh. It aims to curb the proliferation of licensed and unlicensed arms that disrupt social harmony and contribute to violence. The Act establishes a framework for licensing the acquisition, possession, manufacture, sale, import, and export of firearms and ammunition by bona fide persons. It also outlines offences related to unauthorized possession or use of arms and provides penalties for contraventions.

name: SINDH ASSEMBLY MEMBERS (SALARIES AND ALLOWANCES) (AMENDMENT) ACT, 1990

It increases specific salary amounts, introduces free travel vouchers or cash alternatives, and establishes a new office maintenance allowance. The amendments also expand the definition of 'Member' to include various officials like Ministers and Advisors.

metadata.summary: The Act establishes a Parliamentary Committee to recommend salaries and allowances for members of the Provincial Assembly of Sindh. It defines specific entitlements such as house rent, utilities, and conveyance allowances, while granting special privileges to the Leader of Opposition comparable to Provincial Ministers. The Act also outlines provisions for members holding committee chairmanships regarding official car usage and repeals the previous 1974 legislation.

The amendment grants medical facilities to assembly members, their spouses, minor children, unmarried daughters, and wholly dependent family members residing with them. These facilities are provided as admissible under the Special Medical Attendance Rules, 1950.

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Bank Act, 1995

metadata.summary: This Act establishes the Sindh Bank as a body corporate with perpetual succession to carry on commercial and investment banking business. The bank's authorized capital is two and a half billion rupees, with the Government holding up to fifty-five percent of the paid-up capital. The Act defines the structure of the Board, shareholder qualifications, audit procedures, and powers to make bye-laws for the regulation of the bank's business.

The legislation empowers designated authorities, including Deputy Commissioners, to implement these provisions while establishing Vigilance Committees to monitor compliance and assist freed labourers.

metadata.summary: This Act amends the Sind Buildings Control Ordinance, 1979 by substituting a proviso in section 19 to prevent compounding of certain building offences. It also repeals the Sindh Building Control (Amendment) Ordinance, 1997. The Act comes into force immediately upon enactment.

metadata.short_title: The Sind Buildings Control (Second Amendment) Act, 1990
metadata.long_title: An Act further to amend the Sind Buildings Control Ordinance, 1979.
repeals: Sindh Buildings Control (Second Amendment) Ordinance V of 1990
metadata.one_line: Amends the Sind Buildings Control Ordinance, 1979 regarding suspension of certificates and repeals a related ordinance.
metadata.summary: This Act further amends the Sind Buildings Control Ordinance, 1979 by adding provisions for the government to suspend or cancel no objection certificates if construction is not in the public interest. It defines 'completion of building' as finishing according to the approved plan with an occupancy certificate issued. The Act also repeals the Sindh Buildings Control (Second Amendment) Ordinance V of 1990 and came into force on August 27, 1990.

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Child Marriages Restraint Act, 2013
metadata.long_title: An Act to restrain the solemnization of child marriages.
repeals: Child Marriage Restraint Act, 1929
metadata.max_penalty: rigorous imprisonment for three years and fine
metadata.one_line: This Act restrains the solemnization of child marriages in Sindh and prescribes punishments for offenders.
metadata.summary: The Sindh Child Marriages Restraint Act, 2013 aims to prevent child marriages by defining a child as anyone under eighteen years of age. It imposes rigorous imprisonment and fines on male contracting parties, those who solemnize such marriages, and parents or guardians who facilitate them. The Act empowers courts to issue injunctions against impending child marriages and mandates that trials be concluded within ninety days.

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Child Protection Authority (Amendment) Act, 2021
metadata.long_title: An Act to amend the Sindh Child Protection Authority Act, 2011.
amends: The Sindh Child Protection Authority Act, 2011
metadata.one_line: Amends the Sindh Child Protection Authority Act, 2011 to update definitions, establish special courts, and mandate FIR registration for missing children.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the Sindh Child Protection Authority Act, 2011 to expand definitions of abuse and missing children. It mandates the registration of First Incident Reports (FIRs) within four hours for abducted or missing children and establishes Special Courts for speedy justice. The amendment also updates data protection clauses and clarifies the roles of various government departments and law enforcement agencies.

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Child Protection Authority Act, 2011
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the establishment of an Authority known as the Sindh Child Protection Authority.
key_definitions: Child in need of special protection measures
metadata.one_line: Establishes the Sindh Child Protection Authority to protect children from abuse, trafficking, and exploitation.
metadata.summary: This Act establishes the Sindh Child Protection Authority as a body corporate to ensure the rights of children in need of special protection. It defines various terms related to child abuse, trafficking, and care, and outlines the composition, functions, and powers of the Authority. The Act also provides for the establishment of Special Courts to try offences committed under it and creates a fund for the Authority's operations.

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Civil Courts (Amendment) Act, 1991
metadata.long_title: An Act to amend the Sindh Civil Courts Ordinance, 1962.
repeals: The Sindh Civil Courts (Amendment) Ordinance, 1991
metadata.one_line: Amends the Sindh Civil Courts Ordinance, 1962 regarding jurisdiction and fees, repealing a prior 1991 Ordinance.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the Sindh Civil Courts Ordinance, 1962 to alter the original jurisdiction of the District Court in Karachi and adjust monetary limits for civil suits. It substitutes specific sections within the Ordinance to increase value thresholds for High Court jurisdiction and court fees. The Act also repeals the Sindh Civil Courts (Amendment) Ordinance, 1991.

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Civil Courts (Amendment) Act, 1994
metadata.long_title: An Act to further amend the Sindh Civil Court Ordinance, 1962.
repeals: The Sindh Civil Courts (Amendment) Ordinance, 1994
metadata.one_line: Amends the Sindh Civil Courts Ordinance, 1962 by increasing a monetary limit and repeals a previous 1994 amendment.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the Sindh Civil Courts Ordinance, 1962 by substituting the words 'five hundred thousand' for 'two lacs and fifty thousand' in section 18. It also repeals the Sindh Civil Courts (Amendment) Ordinance, 1994. The Act came into force on April 1, 1994, despite being enacted on July 27, 1994.

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Civil Courts (Amendment) Act, 1996
metadata.long_title: An Act to amend the Sind Civil courts Ordinance, 1962.
metadata.one_line: Amends the Sind Civil Courts Ordinance, 1962 regarding jurisdiction transfer for suits under five lacs in Karachi.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the Sind Civil Courts Ordinance, 1962 to address specific civil proceedings pending in the High Court. It mandates the transfer of civil suits and proceedings with a value not exceeding five lacs of rupees, pending in the High Court immediately before the commencement of the Sindh Civil Courts (Amendment) Ordinance, 1991, to the concerned District Courts of Karachi for disposal. The Act came into force at once upon its enactment on April 24, 1996.

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Civil Courts (Amendment) Act, 2010
metadata.long_title: An Act to amend the Sind Civil Courts Ordinance, 1962.
metadata.one_line: Amends the Sindh Civil Courts Ordinance, 1962 regarding District Judge and High Court jurisdiction limits.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the Sindh Civil Courts Ordinance, 1962 to adjust original jurisdiction limits for civil suits. It substitutes section 7 to define jurisdiction thresholds for District Judges in Karachi versus other districts and updates monetary values in section 24 from thirty lacs to fifteen million rupees.

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Civil Courts (Amendment) Act, 2021
metadata.long_title: An Act to amend the Sindh Civil Courts Ordinance, 1962.
metadata.one_line: Amends the Sindh Civil Courts Ordinance, 1962 by updating monetary limits and dates.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the Sindh Civil Courts Ordinance, 1962 to update specific financial figures and dates within the legislation. It substitutes 'fifteen million' with 'sixty five million' in sections 7 and 24, and updates the year from '2010' to '2021'. The Act was passed by the Provincial Assembly of Sindh and came into force immediately upon publication.

name: SINDH CIVIL SERVANT (REGULARIZATION OF ADHOC APPOINTMENTS)(APPOINTMENT) ACT, 2014.

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Civil Servants (Regularization of Adhoc Appointments) (Amendment) Act, 2014
metadata.long_title: An Act to amend the Sindh Civil Servants (Regularization of Adhoc Appointment) Act, 1994.
amends: The Sindh Civil Servants (Regularization of Adhoc Appointment) Act, 1994
metadata.one_line: Amends the 1994 Act to substitute 'initial appointment date' for 'commencement date' in section 3.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the Sindh Civil Servants (Regularization of Adhoc Appointment) Act, 1994. It specifically targets Section 3, Sub-section (1), of the parent Act. The amendment substitutes the phrase 'the date of his initial appointment' for 'the date of the commencement of this Act'. The law came into force immediately upon enactment.

name: SINDH CIVIL SERVANTS (REGULARIZATION OF ABSORPTION) ACT, 2011

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Civil Servants (Regularization of Absorption) Act, 2011
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for regularization of the services of certain employees absorbed as civil servants, in various departments of Government.
repeals: The Sindh Civil Servants (Regularization of Absorption) Ordinance, 2011
metadata.one_line: This Act regularizes the services of employees absorbed as civil servants in Sindh government departments.
metadata.summary: The Sindh Civil Servants (Regularization of Absorption) Act, 2011 provides for the regularization of services for certain employees absorbed as civil servants in various Sindh government departments. It deems such employees to have been validly absorbed on a regular basis from their original absorption date and grants seniority benefits based on equivalent posts held before absorption. The Act applies to employees holding sanctioned posts in connection with the affairs of the Province on or before its commencement.

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Civil Servants (Amendment) Act, 2014
metadata.long_title: An Act to amend the Sindh Civil Servants Act, 1973.
subjects: transfer of federal to provincial service
metadata.one_line: Amends the 1973 Act to allow appointment of former federal civil servants to provincial posts following the 2010 Amendment.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the Sindh Civil Servants Act, 1973 to address the transfer of services from the Federation to the Province resulting from the Constitution (Eighteenth Amendment) Act, 2010. It empowers the Government to appoint individuals holding federal posts prior to 2010 to provincial civil services or posts connected with provincial affairs. The Act also mandates that the Government determine the terms and conditions of service, including cadre and seniority, for these appointed personnel in a prescribed manner.

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Civil Servants (Amendment) Act, 2004
metadata.long_title: An Act to amend the Sind Civil Servants Act, 1973.
metadata.one_line: Amends the Sindh Civil Servants Act, 1973 by omitting specific words regarding pay scales in section 5.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the Sindh Civil Servants Act, 1973 to remove a proviso concerning posts in basic pay scale 15 and below. The amendment applies to the Province of Sindh and comes into force immediately upon enactment. It was passed by the Provincial Assembly of Sindh on July 28, 2005.

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Civil Servants (Amendment) Act, 2013
metadata.long_title: An Act to amend the Sindh Civil Servants Act,1973, to regulate the appointments and promotions and certain actions taken thereunder.
metadata.one_line: Amends the Sindh Civil Servants Act, 1973 to regularize out-of-turn promotions for Sindh Police personnel.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the Sindh Civil Servants Act, 1973 to regulate appointments and promotions within the Sindh Police Department. It specifically addresses out-of-turn promotions made immediately before its commencement under section 9-A of the 1973 Act, regularizing them from their original dates. The legislation affirms all related notifications and orders as validly made while allowing aggrieved persons to file appeals in the Sindh Service Tribunal within thirty days.

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Civil Servants (Amendment) Act, 2021
metadata.long_title: An Act to amend the Sindh Civil Servants Act, 1973.
metadata.one_line: Amends the Sindh Civil Servants Act, 1973 to mandate transgender appointments in specific pay scales.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the Sindh Civil Servants Act, 1973 by adding a new proviso to section 5. The amendment requires that 0.5% of appointments in basic pay scale 15 and below be made from amongst transgenders. These appointments are subject to availability and require medical examination and certification by the Standing Medical Board.

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Civil Servants (Amendment) Act, 2025
metadata.long_title: An Act to amend the Sindh Civil Servants Act, 1973.
metadata.one_line: Amends the Sindh Civil Servants Act, 1973 regarding retirement conditions for civil servants.
metadata.summary: This Act amends section 13 of the Sindh Civil Servants Act, 1973. Specifically, it substitutes clause (b) to define retirement eligibility based on completing twenty-five years of qualifying service or attaining the age of fifty-five years, whichever is later. The amendment also introduces a provision for the imposition of a reduction factor as prescribed by rules.

name: SINDH CIVIL SERVANTS (REGULARIZATION OF ADHOC APPOINTMENTS) ACT, 1989

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Civil Servants (Regularization of Adhoc Appointments) Act, 1989
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for regularization of the services of certain civil servants appointed on adhoc basis.
metadata.one_line: This Act regularizes adhoc civil servants appointed before October 12, 1988, subject to scrutiny by a Special Committee.
metadata.summary: The Act provides for the regularization of services of certain civil servants who were appointed on an adhoc basis in Sindh. It establishes a Special Committee to scrutinize qualifications and other antecedents before orders are made. The Act also outlines procedures for terminating junior adhoc servants if necessary to accommodate regularized personnel and defines the seniority ranking of regularized officers.

name: SINDH CIVIL SERVANTS (REGULARIZATION OF ADHOC APPPOINTENTS) ACT, 1994

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Civil Servants (Regularization of Adhoc Appointments) Act, 1994
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for regularization of the services of certain civil servants appointed on adhoc basis.
metadata.one_line: This Act regularizes adhoc civil servants in BS-16 or above posts who were employed at its commencement.
metadata.summary: The Sindh Civil Servants (Regularization of Adhoc Appointments) Act, 1994 provides for the regularization of services for certain civil servants appointed on an adhoc basis. It applies to those holding adhoc appointments against posts in BS-16 or above who were in employment when the Act commenced. Before orders are made, a Special Committee appointed by the Government must scrutinize antecedents, academic qualifications, experience, age, and place of domicile.

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Civil Servants (Second Amendment) Act, 2013
metadata.long_title: An Act to amend the Sind Civil Servants Act, 1973.
metadata.one_line: Amends the Sind Civil Servants Act, 1973 to regularize services and empower appointment of retired civil servants.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the Sind Civil Servants Act, 1973 to provide for the regularization of services for certain employees absorbed or promoted under section 9-A. It grants the Government power to appoint retired civil servants whose expertise is required in the public interest. Additionally, it deems specific absorbed or promoted employees as validly holding their posts on a regular basis from the date of absorption or promotion.

name: SINDH CIVIL SERVANTS HOUSING FOUNDATION ACT, 2005

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Civil Servants Housing Foundation Act, 2005
metadata.long_title: An act to provide for the establishment of a Housing Foundation for providing houses on no profit no loss basis to the civil servants and the retired civil servants in the province of Sindh.
metadata.commencement: at once for this section; remaining provisions on such date as may be notified by Government
metadata.one_line: Establishes a Housing Foundation in Sindh to provide houses on no profit no loss basis to civil and retired civil servants.
metadata.summary: This Act establishes the Sindh Civil Servants Housing Foundation to provide residential units to civil servants and retired civil servants in Sindh on a no-profit, no-loss basis. The Foundation is a body corporate with a Board of Directors comprising ex-officio members appointed by the Government and other directors appointed for specified periods. The Board has powers to establish a fund, acquire land, allocate housing units based on seniority or special circumstances, and manage accounts audited as prescribed.

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Co-operative Housing Authority (Amendment) Act, 1989
metadata.long_title: An Act to amend the Sind Co-operative Housing Authority Ordinance 1982.
metadata.commencement: at once and deemed to have taken effect on and from the 27th day of June, 1988
metadata.one_line: Amends the Sind Co-operative Housing Authority Ordinance 1982 to require government hearings before action against societies.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the Sind Co-operative Housing Authority Ordinance, 1982, in response to Supreme Court directions. It mandates that the Government must afford an opportunity of hearing to a society before taking action under section 6(2). The amendment allows for dispensing with this hearing only as an emergent measure but requires it to be afforded immediately thereafter. Additionally, the Government is empowered to pass interim orders to prevent mischief or abuse if a proper hearing was conducted beforehand.

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Co-operative Societies (Amendment) Act, 1989
metadata.long_title: An Act to amend the Sindh Co-operative Societies Act, 1925.
metadata.one_line: Amends the Sindh Co-operative Societies Act, 1925 regarding membership transfer in housing societies.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the Sindh Co-operative Societies Act, 1925 to regulate membership changes when interests in a co-operative housing society are transferred. It stipulates that a member ceases to be a member upon transferring all immovable property interests via sale, inheritance, or gift, while the acquirer becomes a new member subject to specific rules. The Act further details voting rights for multiple acquirers and provisions for admitting guardians of minors or mentally disabled persons as members.

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Co-operative Societies Act, 2020
metadata.long_title: An Act to consolidate and amend the law relating to cooperative societies in the Province of Sindh.
metadata.territorial_extent: the whole of the Province of Sindh
repeals: The Cooperative Societies Act, 1925 (Act VII of 1925), in its application to the Province of Sindh
metadata.max_penalty: fine not exceeding rupees five hundred thousand
metadata.one_line: This Act consolidates and amends the law relating to cooperative societies in Sindh, repealing the 1925 Act.
metadata.summary: The Sindh Co-operative Societies Act, 2020 consolidates and amends laws regarding cooperative societies in the Province of Sindh. It facilitates the formation of societies for thrift, self-help, and mutual aid among agriculturists and others with common economic needs. The Act defines various types of societies, establishes a Registrar, outlines registration procedures, and grants powers to make rules.

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Coal Act, 2012
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for regulation and development of coal in the Province of Sindh.
metadata.territorial_extent: the whole of Province of Sindh
metadata.administering_body: Coal and Energy Mines Development Department
metadata.one_line: Regulates and develops coal activities in Sindh through licensing, safety standards, and environmental assessments.
metadata.summary: This Act regulates the exploration, exploitation, and development of coal within the Province of Sindh. It establishes an Inspectorate of Coal Mines and a Mining Committee to oversee safety and operations. The legislation mandates environmental impact assessments, health and safety plans, and corporate social responsibility for all entities engaged in coal activities.

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Coal Authority (Amendment) Act, 1994
metadata.long_title: An Act to amend the Sindh Coal Authority Act, 1994.
repeals: The Sindh Coal Authority (Amendment) Ordinance, 1994
metadata.one_line: Amends the Sindh Coal Authority Act, 1994 regarding its composition and repeals a related Ordinance.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the Sindh Coal Authority Act, 1994 to alter the composition of the Authority's members. Specifically, it substitutes clauses in section 7 to define the number of National Assembly members, Provincial Assembly members, and non-official members nominated by the Government or Assembly. The Act also repeals the Sindh Coal Authority (Amendment) Ordinance, 1994.

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Coal Authority (Amendment) Act, 2017
metadata.long_title: An Act to amend the Sindh Coal Authority Act, 1993.
metadata.one_line: Amends the Sindh Coal Authority Act, 1993 regarding board composition, funds, and appointment validation.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the Sindh Coal Authority Act, 1993 to update the composition of the Board, substitute references to the Authority with Government in specific sections, and establish gratuity and provident fund schemes. It also validates appointments made after May 11, 2002, and provides mechanisms for removing difficulties in implementing the Act. The amendments include new provisions for meeting quorums, notice periods, and casting votes.

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Coal Authority Act, 1993
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the establishment of the Sindh Coal Authority.
repeals: Sindh Ordinance No.XXII of 1993
establishes: Board of the Sindh Coal Authority
metadata.one_line: Establishes the Sindh Coal Authority to manage coal exploration, development, and utilization in Sindh.
metadata.summary: This Act establishes the Sindh Coal Authority as a body corporate responsible for the exploration, development, processing, exploitation, mining, and utilization of coal in the Province of Sindh. The Authority is empowered to plan projects, promote joint ventures with foreign investors, and manage regional offices. It operates under the direction of the Government of Sindh and its accounts are audited by the Auditor General of Pakistan.

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Coastal Development Authority (Amendment) Act, 2015
metadata.long_title: An Act to amend the Sindh Coastal Development Authority Act, 1994.
amends: The Sindh Coastal Development Authority Act, 1994
metadata.one_line: Amends the Sindh Coastal Development Authority Act, 1994 to redefine coastal areas and update authority composition.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the Sindh Coastal Development Authority Act, 1994 to redefine 'coastal areas' to include Districts Thatta, Sujawal, and Badin. It also updates Section 5 of the said Act to specify Deputy Commissioners from these districts and three nominated Members of the Provincial Assembly of Sindh as part of the authority structure. The amendments come into force immediately upon enactment.

name: SINDH COMMISSION ON THE STATUS OF WOMEN ACT, 2015

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Commission on the Status of Women Act, 2015
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the setting up Provincial Commission on the Status of Women.
metadata.territorial_extent: the whole of the Province of Sindh
establishes: Sindh Commission on the Status of Women (SPCSW)
metadata.one_line: Establishes the Sindh Commission on the Status of Women to promote women's rights in Sindh.
metadata.summary: This Act establishes the Sindh Commission on the Status of Women (SPCSW) to promote social, economic, political, and legal rights of women in the Province of Sindh. The Commission consists of twenty-one members, including a Chairperson and various representatives appointed based on specific qualifications and experience. The Act outlines procedures for appointment, removal, resignation, and functioning of the Commission, along with provisions for financial management, annual reporting to the Assembly, and legal protections for its members.

name: SINDH COMMISSION ON THE STATUS OF WOMEN ACT, 2015

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Information of Temporary Residents Act, 2015
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for sharing of information of tenants and other temporary residents in the Province of Sindh.
metadata.territorial_extent: the whole of Province of Sindh
repeals: The Sindh Information of Temporary Residents Ordinance, 2015
metadata.max_penalty: imprisonment up to six months and fine between ten thousand and forty five thousand rupees
metadata.one_line: This Act mandates information sharing between landlords, hotels, and police to combat terrorism and track temporary residents.
metadata.summary: The Act requires property dealers, landlords, and hotel managers to provide information about tenants and guests to the police within specific timeframes. It establishes a police database for analyzing data related to terrorism and other offences under the Pakistan Penal Code. The legislation also mandates identification checks using national identity cards or passports and regulates the possession of firearms in rented premises.

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Companies Profits (Workers' Participation) Act, 2015
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for participation of workers in the profits of companies and for matters ancillary thereto.
metadata.territorial_extent: the whole of Province of Sindh
metadata.commencement: at once and deemed to have been taken effect from 1st July, 2011
repeals: The Companies Profits (Workers Participation) Act, 1968
metadata.one_line: This Act establishes a Workers' Participation Fund in Sindh companies to allow workers to share in profits.
metadata.summary: The Act provides for the participation of workers in the profits of companies operating in the Province of Sindh. It mandates the establishment of a Workers' Participation Fund and a Board of Trustees consisting of elected worker representatives and management nominees. Companies are required to contribute five percent of their net profits to this fund, which is then distributed to eligible workers according to a specific scheme.

name: SINDH COMPULSORY IODIZATION OF SALT ACT, 2013

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Compulsory Iodization of Salt Act, 2013
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for compulsory iodization of salt, in the Province.
metadata.territorial_extent: the whole of the Province of Sindh
metadata.max_penalty: fine extending to rupees one hundred thousand
metadata.one_line: This Act mandates compulsory iodization of salt in Sindh to prevent iodine deficiency disorders.
metadata.summary: The Sindh Compulsory Iodization of Salt Act, 2013 establishes a legal framework for the mandatory iodization of edible salt within the Province of Sindh. It defines specific obligations for manufacturers, processors, and importers regarding hygiene, labeling, and adherence to food standards. The Act empowers appointed Inspectors to monitor compliance, seize sub-standard salt, and imposes penalties including fines and license cancellation for violations.

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Condominium Act, 2014
metadata.long_title: An Act to make provision for the regulation of maintenance of public sale projects in the Province of Sindh;
metadata.territorial_extent: the whole of the province of Sindh except to the cantonment areas and the projects of National Security declared by the Federal Government
metadata.one_line: Regulates maintenance of public sale projects in Sindh through registered maintenance companies and resident societies.
metadata.summary: This Act regulates the maintenance of services, amenities, and common areas in public sale projects within the Province of Sindh. It establishes Residents Cooperative Maintenance Societies to manage these projects alongside registered maintenance companies. The legislation defines key terms such as allottee, amenity, and unit, while outlining responsibilities for builders, societies, and maintenance companies regarding repairs, insurance, and utility bill payments.

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Consumer Protection Act, 2014
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide and protect the rights and interests of consumers in the Province of Sindh.
metadata.territorial_extent: whole of the Province of Sindh
metadata.max_penalty: imprisonment up to two years or fine up to hundred thousand rupees for manufacturer infringement; imprisonment up to three years or fine up to two hundred thousand rupees for non-compliance with Consumer Court orders
metadata.one_line: An Act to protect consumer rights in Sindh regarding defective products, services, and unfair practices.
metadata.summary: This Act provides for the protection of consumer rights and interests within the Province of Sindh. It establishes mechanisms for speedy redress of complaints through Consumer Courts and defines liabilities arising from defective products and services. The legislation also outlines obligations for manufacturers, prohibits unfair practices like false advertising, and sets penalties for non-compliance.

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Control of Narcotic Substances (Amendment) Act, 2025
metadata.long_title: An Act to amend the Sindh Control of Narcotic Substances Act, 2024.
amends: Sindh Control of Narcotic Substances Act, 2024
metadata.one_line: Amends the Sindh Control of Narcotic Substances Act, 2024 regarding police roles, bail, and drug schedules.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the Sindh Control of Narcotic Substances Act, 2024 to update definitions of police officers involved in narcotics control. It modifies provisions related to bail conditions, confiscation of seized items, and the appointment of judges for special courts. Additionally, it updates schedules to include new narcotic substances and chemical precursors while clarifying operational procedures for law enforcement agencies.

name: SINDH CONTROL OF NARCOTIC SUBSTANCES ACT, 2024

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Control of Narcotic Substances Act, 2024
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the laws relating to narcotic drugs and psychotropic substances.
metadata.territorial_extent: the whole of the Province of Sindh
repeals: The Control of Narcotic Substances Act, 1997
metadata.one_line: This Act regulates narcotic drugs and psychotropic substances in Sindh by prohibiting cultivation, possession, trafficking, and establishing special courts.
metadata.summary: The Sindh Control of Narcotic Substances Act, 2024 provides a comprehensive legal framework for regulating narcotic drugs, psychotropic substances, precursor chemicals, and control substances within the Province of Sindh. It prohibits the cultivation, possession, import/export, and trafficking of these substances while empowering law enforcement agencies with specific search, seizure, and arrest powers. The Act establishes special courts to try offences under this legislation and repeals the previous Control of Narcotic Substances Act, 1997 for the province.

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Covid-19 Emergency Relief (Amendment) Act, 2020
metadata.long_title: An Act to amend the Sindh Covid-19 Emergency Relief Act, 2020.
amends: The Sindh Covid-19 Emergency Relief Act, 2020
subjects: financial assistance for daily wage workers
metadata.one_line: Amends the Sindh Covid-19 Emergency Relief Act, 2020 to mandate masks and provide paid leave for infected workers.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the Sindh Covid-19 Emergency Relief Act, 2020 to introduce new provisions regarding public health measures. It mandates that persons visiting public places must wear face masks to mitigate infection spread. Additionally, it grants paid leave to employees testing positive for Covid-19 and requires financial assistance for daily wage workers during isolation. The Health Department is tasked with encouraging free testing through awareness campaigns.

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Covid-19 Emergency Relief Act, 2020
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide relief to the people of Sindh in an emergency situation arising due to widespread pandemic of Corona Virus (Covid-19) disease, which has badly hit, hurt or affected the population of the Province, directly or indirectly by the measures adopted or taken by Government to stop the spread of the disease for the general welfare of the public and to mitigate challenges emanating from the ban/lockdown imposed by the Government of Sindh throughout the Province.
metadata.territorial_extent: the whole of the Province of Sindh
metadata.commencement: at once and shall be deemed to have taken effect on and from the 1st of April, 2020
repeals: The Sindh COVID-19 Emergency Relief Ordinance, 2020
metadata.one_line: Provides emergency relief to people in Sindh regarding fees, salaries, rent, and utilities during the COVID-19 pandemic.
metadata.summary: This Act provides relief measures to the people of Sindh affected by the widespread COVID-19 pandemic. It limits educational institution fees to 80% of the total monthly amount, protects employees from termination during establishment closures, suspends 50% of rent recovery for landlords, and waives water and sewerage bills based on consumption area. The Act also empowers the Chief Minister to authorize departments and officers to perform functions under this legislation.

name: SINDH CRIMINAL PROSECUTION SERVICE (CONSTITUTION, FUNCTIONS AND POWERS) (AMENDMENT) ACT, 2015

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Criminal Prosecution Service (Constitution, Functions and Powers) (Amendment) Act, 2015
metadata.long_title: An Act to amend the Sindh Criminal Prosecution Service (Constitution, Functions and Powers) Act, 2009.
amends: The Sindh Criminal Prosecution Service (Constitution, Functions and Powers) Act, 2009
metadata.one_line: Amends the 2009 Act to update powers, supervision, and functions of the Sindh Criminal Prosecution Service.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the Sindh Criminal Prosecution Service (Constitution, Functions and Powers) Act, 2009 to enhance the service's constitution and powers. It updates provisions regarding the supervision by the Prosecutor General, the distribution of work across various courts, and the authority to withdraw from prosecution with court consent. The amendment also inserts new sections to allow for general guidelines on investigation and disciplinary actions against public servants involved in prosecution.

name: SINDH CRIMINAL PROSECUTION SERVICE (CONSTITUTION, FUNCTIONS AND POWERS) (AMENDMENT) ACT, 2011

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Criminal Prosecution Service (Constitution, Functions and Powers) (Amendment) Act, 2011
metadata.long_title: An Act to amend the Sindh Criminal Prosecution Service (Constitution, Functions and Powers) Act, 2009.
amends: The Sindh Criminal Prosecution Service (Constitution, Functions and Powers) Act, 2009
metadata.one_line: Amends the 2009 Act regarding the constitution, functions, and powers of the Sindh Criminal Prosecution Service.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the Sindh Criminal Prosecution Service (Constitution, Functions and Powers) Act, 2009 to clarify government superintendence over the service. It establishes that the administration vests in the Government and defines the appointment terms for the Prosecutor General. The Act also specifies a non-extendable three-year tenure for the Prosecutor General and updates qualification requirements for High Court judges.

name: SINDH CRIMINAL PROSECUTION SERVICE (CONSTITUTION, FUNCTIONS AND POWERS)(AMENDMENT) ACT, 2014

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Criminal Prosecution Service (Constitution, Functions & Powers) (Amendment) Act, 2014
metadata.long_title: An Act to amend the Sindh Criminal Prosecution Service (Constitution, Functions & Powers) Act, 2009.
metadata.territorial_extent: the whole of Province of Sindh
metadata.parent_law: The Sindh Criminal Prosecution Service (Constitution, Functions & Powers) Act, 2009
amends: The Sindh Criminal Prosecution Service (Constitution, Functions & Powers) Act, 2009
metadata.one_line: Amends the 2009 Act regarding Prosecutor General tenure, appointment criteria, and terminology.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the Sindh Criminal Prosecution Service (Constitution, Functions & Powers) Act, 2009 to alter provisions concerning the Prosecutor General. It substitutes text in section 6 regarding tenure at the pleasure of the Government and changes the term 'delegate' to 'assign'. Additionally, it revises section 7 to specify citizenship, age, and experience requirements for appointing a Prosecutor General.

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Cultural Heritage (Preservation) Act, 1994
metadata.long_title: An Act to preserve and protect ancient places and objects of architectural, historical, archaeological, artistic, ethnological anthropological and national interest in the Province of Sindh.
metadata.territorial_extent: the whole Province of Sindh including its coastal areas
metadata.max_penalty: fine extending to one lakh rupees or imprisonment extending to three years or both
metadata.one_line: This Act preserves ancient places in Sindh by establishing an Advisory Committee and defining protected heritage.
metadata.summary: The Sindh Cultural Heritage (Preservation) Act, 1994 was enacted to preserve and protect ancient places and objects of architectural, historical, archaeological, artistic, ethnological, anthropological, and national interest within the Province of Sindh. It establishes an Advisory Committee consisting of a Chairman and six members, including experts in architecture and archaeology, to oversee preservation efforts. The Act empowers the Government to declare premises as protected heritage, acquire custody or guardianship, regulate public access, and impose penalties for destruction or damage to such sites.

name: SINDH DEVELOPMENT AND MAINTENANCE OF INFRASTRUCTURE CESS (AMENDMENT) ACT, 2018.

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Development and Maintenance of Infrastructure Cess (Amendment) Act, 2018
