amends: Sindh Development and Maintenance of Infrastructure Cess Act, 2017
repeals: section 9 of the Sindh Finance Act, 1994
metadata.one_line: Amends the Sindh Development and Maintenance of Infrastructure Cess Act, 2017 by adding a section to repeal specific provisions.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the Sindh Development and Maintenance of Infrastructure Cess Act, 2017. It adds a new section that repeals the provisions of section 9 of the Sindh Finance Act, 1994. The Act came into force immediately upon enactment.

name: SINDH DEVELOPMENT AND MAINTENANCE OF INFRASTRUCTURE CESS ACT, 2017

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Development and Maintenance of Infrastructure Cess Act, 2017
metadata.long_title: An Act to consolidate the law relating to the levy of a cess on goods entering into and leaving the Province from or for outside the country through air or sea.
metadata.territorial_extent: the whole of the Province of Sindh
metadata.commencement: at once and shall be deemed to have taken effect on and from 1st July, 1994
repeals: section 9 of the Sindh Finance Act, 1994
key_definitions: District Excise, Taxation and Narcotics Control Officer
metadata.administering_body: Excise, Taxation and Narcotics Control Department, Government of Sindh
metadata.one_line: This Act consolidates the law for levying a cess on goods entering or leaving Sindh via air or sea to fund infrastructure.
metadata.summary: The Act consolidates laws regarding the levy of a cess on goods entering or leaving the Province of Sindh through air or sea. The collected funds are designated for the development and maintenance of provincial infrastructure, including roads, public facilities, and traffic control. It defines the liable persons, payment procedures, exemptions for specific categories like re-exported goods, and penalties for non-compliance.

name: SINDH DEVELOPMENT AND MAINTENANCE OF INFRASTRUCTURE CESS (AMENDMENT) ACT, 2026

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Development and Maintenance of Infrastructure Cess (Amendment) Act, 2026
metadata.long_title: An Act to amend the Sindh Development and maintenance of Infrastructure Cess Act 2017.
amends: Sindh Development and Maintenance of Infrastructure Cess Act, 2017
metadata.administering_body: Excise, Taxation and Narcotics Control Department, Government of Sindh
metadata.one_line: Amends the 2017 Cess Act to introduce settlement agreements, payment installments, reduced rates, and export exemptions.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the Sindh Development and Maintenance of Infrastructure Cess Act, 2017 to facilitate the settlement of cess liabilities through new agreements. It establishes a framework for installment payments, conditions for withdrawing pending litigation, and specific reduced cess rates for compliant owners. Additionally, it grants exemptions for goods imported solely for re-export under the Export Facilitation Scheme.

name: SINDH DIFFERENTLY ABLE PERSONS (EMPLOYMENT, REHABILITATION AND WELFARE) (AMENDMENT) ACT, 2017

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Differently Able Persons (Employment, Rehabilitation and Welfare) (Amendment) Act, 2017
metadata.long_title: An Act to amend the Sindh Differently Able Persons (Employment, Rehabilitation and Welfare) Act, 2014.
amends: The Sindh Differently Able Persons (Employment, Rehabilitation and Welfare) Act, 2014
metadata.one_line: Amends the 2014 Sindh Differently Able Persons Act to increase employment quota from two percent to five percent.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the Sindh Differently Able Persons (Employment, Rehabilitation and Welfare) Act, 2014. Specifically, it substitutes the words 'two percent' with 'five percent' in subsection (1) of section 8 of the parent Act. The amendment applies to the Province of Sindh and came into force immediately upon enactment.

name: SINDH DIFFERENTLY ABLE PERSONS (EMPLOYMENT, REHABILITATION AND WELFARE) ACT, 2014

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Differently able persons (Employment, Rehabilitation and Welfare) Act, 2014
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the employment, rehabilitation and welfare of differently able persons.
establishes: Council for the Rehabilitation of Differently able persons
metadata.max_penalty: fine which may extend to one hundred thousand rupees and, in the case of non-payment of fine, with an additional fine which may extend to five thousand rupees for every day during which the payment of fine is not made
metadata.one_line: This Act provides for the employment, rehabilitation, and welfare of differently able persons in Sindh.
metadata.summary: The Act establishes a Council to execute policies for the employment and welfare of differently able persons. It creates a Fund to support training centers, financial assistance, and medical treatment for these individuals. The legislation defines key terms such as 'differently able persons' and sets penalties for establishments failing to comply with payment requirements.

name: SINDH DISPOSAL OF URBAN LAND (REPEAL) ACT, 2005

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Disposal of Urban Land (Repeal) Act, 2005
metadata.long_title: An act to repeal the Sindh Disposal of Urban Land Ordinance, 2002.
repeals: Sindh Ordinance X of 2002
metadata.one_line: This Act repeals the Sindh Disposal of Urban Land Ordinance, 2002.
metadata.summary: The Sindh Disposal of Urban Land (Repeal) Act, 2005 was enacted by the Provincial Assembly of Sindh to repeal the Sindh Disposal of Urban Land Ordinance, 2002. The Act came into force immediately upon enactment on December 27, 2006. It serves solely to remove the earlier ordinance from the statute book.

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Education Foundation Act, 1992
metadata.long_title: An Act to Provide for the establishment of an Education Foundation in the Province of Sindh.
metadata.territorial_extent: the whole of the Province of Sindh
repeals: Sindh Ordinance No.III of 1992
subjects: research and survey of education system
metadata.one_line: Establishes the Sindh Education Foundation to promote and develop education in Sindh through a corporate body.
metadata.summary: This Act establishes the Sindh Education Foundation as a body corporate with perpetual succession to promote and develop education in the Province of Sindh. The Foundation is managed by a Board consisting of the Chief Minister, the Minister for Education, and other appointed members, headed by a Managing Director. Its aims include expanding educational facilities, providing financial grants and loans to non-commercial institutions, conducting research on the education system, and improving literacy rates.

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Emergency Procurement Act, 2014
metadata.long_title: An Act to make provision for emergency procurement for the law enforcement agency in the Province of Sindh.
metadata.territorial_extent: the whole of the Province of Sindh
metadata.status_evidence: It shall come into force at once and shall remain in force for one year from the date of its commencement.
metadata.one_line: Provides for urgent procurement of security items for law enforcement agencies in Sindh for one year.
metadata.summary: This Act facilitates emergency procurement specifically for the law enforcement agencies in the Province of Sindh. It applies to the Sindh Police, Sindh Prisons Police, Pakistan Rangers, and Frontier Constabulary deployed in the province. The legislation allows these agencies to procure urgent security items like armored vehicles and bulletproof gear without following standard regulatory procedures, valid for one year from commencement.

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Emergency Rescue Service Act, 2023
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the establishment of the Sindh Emergency Rescue Service to deal with emergencies in the Province of Sindh.
metadata.territorial_extent: the whole of the Province of Sindh
metadata.max_penalty: simple imprisonment for six months or with fine not exceeding rupees fifty thousand or with both
metadata.one_line: Establishes the Sindh Emergency Rescue Service to handle emergencies, medical treatment, and rescue operations in Sindh.
metadata.summary: This Act establishes the Sindh Emergency Rescue Service (Rescue 1122) as a body corporate to manage emergencies in the Province of Sindh. It defines the functions of the service, including providing timely rescue, evacuation, and medical treatment, as well as managing fire fighting and urban search and rescue services. The Act creates various governing bodies like the Sindh Emergency Council and District Emergency Board, outlines the appointment of officers, and prescribes offences for false calls or disobedience to the Act.

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Employees Special Allowance (Payment) (Amendment) Act, 1991
metadata.long_title: An Act further to amend the Sind Employees Special Allowance (Payment) Act, 1986.
metadata.commencement: at once and deemed to have taken effect on 1st day of December, 1990
repeals: The Sindh, Employees Special Allowance (Payment) (Amendment) Ordinance, 1991
metadata.one_line: Amends the 1986 Sindh Employees Special Allowance Act to add an additional allowance and repeals a 1991 Ordinance.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the Sind Employees Special Allowance (Payment) Act, 1986 to include an additional special allowance for employees. It mandates that every employee be paid an additional special allowance of two hundred rupees per month starting from December 1, 1990. The Act also repeals the Sindh, Employees Special Allowance (Payment) (Amendment) Ordinance, 1991.

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Employees Special Allowance (Payment) (Amendment) Act, 1995
metadata.long_title: An Act Further to amend the Sind Employees Special Allowance (Payment) Act, 1986.
amends: The Sind Employees Special Allowance (Payment) Act, 1986
repeals: The Sindh Employees Special Allowance (Payment) (Amendment) Ordinance, 1995
metadata.one_line: Amends the 1986 Act to add a special allowance of one hundred rupees per month for Sindh employees from May 1, 1995.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the Sind Employees Special Allowance (Payment) Act, 1986 to introduce an additional special allowance. The new provision mandates that every employee in Sindh shall receive an extra payment of one hundred rupees per month starting from May 1, 1995. This applies regardless of whether wages are paid to the employee. The Act also repeals a previous amendment ordinance from 1995.

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Employees' Old-Age Benefits (Amendment) Act, 2016
metadata.long_title: An Act to amend the Sindh Employees' Old-Age Benefits Act, 2014.
metadata.commencement: at once and deemed to have taken effect on and from 1st day of July, 2014
metadata.administering_body: Employees Old-age Benefits Institution / Sindh Employees' Old-age Benefits Institution
metadata.one_line: Amends the Sindh Employees' Old-Age Benefits Act, 2014 regarding contributions, definitions, and pension eligibility.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the Sindh Employees' Old-Age Benefits Act, 2014 to update contribution rates, expand coverage to include contractors' employees, and adjust age limits for women. It substitutes various clauses to redefine terms like 'wages' and 'year', while also adding protections against discrimination based on sex or other grounds. The legislation ensures the continuation of benefit claims processing by the existing institution until assets are transferred.

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Employees' Old-Age Benefits Act, 2014
metadata.long_title: An Act to repeal and re-enact the law relating to old-age benefits for the persons employed in industrial, commercial and other organizations in the Province of Sindh.
metadata.territorial_extent: the whole of the Province of Sindh
repeals: The Employees Old-age Benefit Act, 1976 (Act No.XIV of 1976)
metadata.one_line: This Act establishes an old-age benefits scheme for employees in Sindh's industrial and commercial organizations.
metadata.summary: The Sindh Employees' Old-Age Benefits Act, 2014 repeals and re-enacts the previous law regarding old-age benefits for persons employed in industrial, commercial, and other organizations within the Province of Sindh. It mandates compulsory insurance contributions from employers and the Government to fund pensions for employees, invalidity survivors, and grants. The Act defines insured persons, establishes a Board of Trustees for management, outlines contribution rates, and specifies offences and penalties for non-compliance while exempting certain state servants.

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Employees' Social Security Act, 2016
metadata.long_title: An Act to introduce a scheme of Social Security for providing benefits to certain employees or their dependents in the event of sickness, maternity, employment, injury or death and for matters ancillary thereto.
metadata.territorial_extent: the whole of the Province of Sindh
metadata.commencement: at once, but shall apply only to such areas, classes of persons, industries or establishments, from such date or dates, and with regard to the provision of such benefits as Government may, by notification, specify in this behalf.
repeals: The Employees Social Securities Ordinance, 1965 (relating to the Province of Sindh)
Workmen's Compensation Act, 1923
Employers' Liability Act, 1938
Mines Maternity Benefit Act, 1941
West Pakistan Maternity Benefit Ordinance, 1958
metadata.one_line: Establishes a social security scheme for employees in Sindh providing benefits for sickness, maternity, injury, and death.
metadata.summary: This Act introduces a social security scheme to provide benefits to employees or their dependents in Sindh facing sickness, maternity, employment issues, injury, or death. It establishes the Employees' Social Security Institution with a Governing Body to manage contributions, funds, and medical care. The Act also creates a Social Security Court to handle disputes and repeals previous conflicting laws regarding workmen's compensation and maternity benefits.

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Enquiries and Anti-Corruption Act, 1991
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the constitution of a special agency for the investigation of certain offences relating to corruption by, or enquiry into mis-conduct of, public servants and for holding preliminary enquiries against such servants in Sindh.
repeals: The Sindh Anti-Corruption Establishment Ordinance, 1961
The Sindh Enquiries and Anti-Corruption Ordinance, 1991
metadata.one_line: Constitutes a special agency in Sindh to investigate corruption offences and misconduct of public servants.
metadata.summary: This Act establishes the Enquiries and Anti-Corruption Establishment within the Province of Sindh. It grants the Director and officers powers of search, arrest, and seizure similar to police officers for investigating specific corruption offences listed in the Schedule. The Act also defines key terms such as 'mis-conduct' and provides legal protections against suits filed against the establishment acting in good faith.

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Entertainments Duty (Amendment) Act, 1992
metadata.long_title: An Act to amend the Sind Entertainments Duty Act, 1958.
metadata.commencement: at once and be deemed to have taken effect on and from 17th May, 1992
metadata.one_line: Amends the Sind Entertainments Duty Act, 1958 by changing duty rates and adding cinema owners to specific clauses.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the Sind Entertainments Duty Act, 1958 to adjust financial provisions and expand the scope of certain sections. Specifically, it substitutes the word 'seventy five' with 'fifty five' in section 3 and adds references to cinema owners and film exhibitors in section 11. The amendments apply immediately but are deemed effective from May 17, 1992.

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Environmental Protection Act, 2014
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the protection, conservation, rehabilitation and improvement of the environment, for the prevention and control of pollution, and promotion of sustainable development.
metadata.territorial_extent: the whole of the Province of Sindh
metadata.one_line: An Act to protect the environment in Sindh, control pollution, and promote sustainable development through specific agencies and funds.
metadata.summary: This Act establishes the Sindh Environmental Protection Council and Agency to oversee environmental protection and pollution control within the province. It creates a Sustainable Development Fund for eligible projects and sets strict prohibitions on hazardous waste and emissions. The legislation also provides for environmental impact assessments, the establishment of tribunals for disputes, and penalties for non-compliance.

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Epidemic Diseases Act, 2014
metadata.long_title: An Act to consolidate the law relating to the prevention of the spread of dangerous epidemic disease in the Province of Sindh.
metadata.territorial_extent: the whole of the Province of Sindh
repeals: The West Pakistan Epidemic Diseases Act, 1958
metadata.max_penalty: punishable under section 188 of the Pakistan Penal Code
metadata.one_line: Consolidates laws to prevent the spread of dangerous epidemic diseases in Sindh and empowers the Government to take special measures.
metadata.summary: This Act consolidates existing laws regarding the prevention of dangerous epidemic diseases within the Province of Sindh. It grants the Government power to prescribe temporary regulations, inspect travelers, and segregate suspected infected persons when ordinary laws are insufficient. The Act also defines key terms like 'disease' and 'Government', establishes penalties for non-compliance under the Pakistan Penal Code, and repeals previous legislation applicable to Sindh.

name: SINDH ESSENTIAL COMMODITIES PRICE CONTROL AND PREVENTION OF PROFITEERING AND HOARDING (AMENDMENT) ACT, 2008

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Essential Commodities Price Control and Prevention of Profiteering and hoarding (Amendment) Act, 2008
metadata.long_title: An Act to further amend the Sindh Essential Commodities Price Control and Prevention of Profiteering and hoarding Act, 2005.
amends: The Sindh Essential Commodities Price Control and Prevention of Profiteering and hoarding Act, 2005
metadata.one_line: Amends the 2005 Sindh Essential Commodities Act by extending time limits and increasing fines.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the Sindh Essential Commodities Price Control and Prevention of Profiteering and hoarding Act, 2005. It substitutes 'six months' for 'three months' and increases the fine from 'ten thousand rupees' to 'thirty thousand rupees' in section 8 of the parent Act. The amendment came into force immediately upon enactment.

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Eye Surgery (Restriction) Act, 2014
metadata.long_title: An Act to prevent the surgery of eye by the persons other than registered medical practioners.
metadata.territorial_extent: the whole of Province of Sindh
metadata.max_penalty: seven years imprisonment and fine up to five hundred thousand rupees
metadata.one_line: This Act prevents non-registered persons from performing eye surgery in Sindh and prescribes punishments for such acts.
metadata.summary: The Sindh Eye Surgery (Restriction) Act, 2014 prohibits any person who is not a registered medical practitioner from performing eye surgery. It defines terms like complete blindness, partial blindness, and eye surgery to clarify the scope of the restriction. The Act prescribes imprisonment and fines for performing unauthorized surgery or holding oneself out as practicing it, with heavier penalties if the act results in blindness.

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Factories (Second Amendment) Act, 2021
metadata.long_title: An Act to further amend the Sindh Factories Act, 2015.
metadata.max_penalty: five hundred thousand rupees or imprisonment of six months or both
metadata.one_line: Amends the Sindh Factories Act, 2015 regarding registration requirements and penalties.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the Sindh Factories Act, 2015 to update registration document requirements and increase penalties for non-compliance. It mandates approval from the Sindh Building Control Authority and utility agencies for factory registration. Additionally, it introduces new sections imposing higher fines and imprisonment terms for failing to register a factory or violating specific provisions.

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Factories Act, 2015
metadata.long_title: An Act to consolidate and amend the law regulating labour in factories.
metadata.territorial_extent: the whole of the Province of Sindh
metadata.commencement: on such date as Government may notify in the official gazette
repeals: The Factories Act, 1934 (Act XXV of 1934), in its application to the Province of Sindh
metadata.one_line: Consolidates and amends laws regulating labour in factories within the Province of Sindh.
metadata.summary: This Act consolidates and amends the law regulating labour in factories and related matters. It applies to the whole of the Province of Sindh, including government and federal factories within its limits. The legislation establishes standards for health, safety, working hours, and welfare, while defining specific terms like 'factory' and 'adolescent'. It repeals the previous Factories Act, 1934, as it applied to Sindh.

name: SINDH FACULTY OF PARAMEDICAL AND ALLIED HEALTH SCIENCES ACT, 2023

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Faculty of Paramedical and Allied Health Sciences Act, 2023
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide and establishment of the Sindh Medical Faculty Paramedical and Allied Health Sciences.
metadata.territorial_extent: the whole of the Province of Sindh
repeals: Notification No.SO (DC&MS)1-54/70 dated 19.05.1971 under section 3 of the Medical Degree Act, 1916
establishes: Sindh Faculty of Para-Medical and Allied Health Sciences
metadata.one_line: Establishes the Sindh Faculty of Paramedical and Allied Health Sciences to regulate paramedic training and registration in Sindh.
metadata.summary: This Act establishes the Sindh Faculty of Paramedical and Allied Health Sciences with necessary autonomy to improve training standards and administration. It regulates the education, training, examination, and registration of paramedics and allied health professionals across various health sectors in the Province. The Faculty is constituted as a body corporate with powers to manage funds, appoint staff, grant affiliations to institutions, and oversee academic quality.

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Fertilizer (Control) Act, 1994
metadata.long_title: An Act to regulate the sale, distribution and use of fertilizer and fertilizer material.
metadata.one_line: Regulates the sale, distribution, and use of fertilizers in Sindh through labeling, testing, and committee oversight.
metadata.summary: This Act regulates the sale, distribution, and use of fertilizer and fertilizer material within the Province of Sindh. It establishes a Fertilizer Control Committee and a Fertilizer Testing Laboratory to oversee quality and administration. The legislation prohibits the sale of adulterated fertilizers, mandates specific labelling requirements, and grants powers to Government Analysts and Inspectors for testing and enforcement.

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Finance Act, 1977
metadata.long_title: An Act to rationalize, levy and enhance certain taxes and duties in the Province of Sind and to amend certain laws.
metadata.commencement: 1977-07-01, except section 3 sub-sections (3) and (6) and section 5 which came into force on 1977-01-01
repeals: West Pakistan Act XXXVIII of 1958
Sind Tabacco Vend Act, 1958
Sind Finance Act, 1965 (Sections 12, 14 and clause (ii) of sub-section (2) of section 18)
metadata.max_penalty: penalty not exceeding the amount of the tax due or surcharge not exceeding ten percent of the tax due
metadata.one_line: This Act rationalizes and enhances taxes in Sindh, amends existing laws, and establishes penalties for non-payment.
metadata.summary: The Sindh Finance Act, 1977 was enacted to rationalize, levy, and enhance certain taxes and duties within the Province of Sind. It amends several previous acts regarding stamp duties, immovable property tax, and energy consumption charges. The Act also introduces specific provisions for hotel taxation, including powers to inspect accounts and impose penalties for defaults.

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Finance (Amendment) Act, 1991
metadata.long_title: An Act to amend the Sind Finance Act, 1964, and the Sind Finance Act, 1975.
repeals: The Sindh Finance (Amendment) Ordinance, 1991
metadata.administering_body: Councils constituted under the Sind Local Government Ordinance, 1979
metadata.one_line: Amends the Sind Finance Acts of 1964 and 1975 to levy surcharges for water supply and drainage schemes.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the Sind Finance Act, 1964, and the Sind Finance Act, 1975. It introduces new sub-sections to levy a surcharge on cess and fees payable by local councils. The collected funds are designated to meet expenses for water supply and drainage schemes undertaken by councils constituted under the Sind Local Government Ordinance, 1979. The Act also repeals the Sindh Finance (Amendment) Ordinance, 1991.

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Finance (Amendment) Act, 1995
metadata.long_title: An act to amend the Sind Finance Preamble.
metadata.commencement: at once and deemed to have taken effect on and from the 27th day of October, 1994
repeals: The Sindh Finance (Amendment) Ordinance, 1995
metadata.one_line: Amends the Sindh Finance Act, 1964 regarding sugar cess rates and repeals a related Ordinance.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the Sindh Finance Act, 1964 to update monetary values and redefine the sharing of sugar cess between mills and cane sellers. It substitutes specific amounts in Section 12 and clarifies payment obligations for sugar-cane obtained from mill farms. The Act also repeals the Sindh Finance (Amendment) Ordinance, 1995.

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Finance (Amendment) Act, 2007
metadata.long_title: An Act to amend the Sindh Finance Act, 1994 to rationalize cess for special maintenance and development of infrastructure for smooth and safer movement of goods entering or leaving the Province from or for outside the country through air or sea.
repeals: The Sindh Finance (Amendment) Ordinance, 2006
metadata.one_line: Amends the Sindh Finance Act, 1994 to rationalize cess on goods moving through air or sea.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the Sindh Finance Act, 1994 to adjust the rates of cess levied on goods entering or leaving the Province via air or sea. The amendment rationalizes these charges to fund the maintenance and development of infrastructure required for the smooth and safer movement of such goods. It substitutes specific subsections in the parent Act and adds a new Schedule detailing cess rates based on net weight, distance, and C&F value.

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Finance (Amendment) Act, 2009
metadata.long_title: An Act to further amend the Sindh Finance (Amendment) Act, 2007.
metadata.one_line: Amends the Sindh Finance (Amendment) Act, 2007 to give it retrospective effect and add provisions on cess utilization and refunds.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the Sindh Finance (Amendment) Act, 2007 to provide it with retrospective effect dating back to July 1, 1994. It modifies Section 1 of the said Act regarding its deemed commencement date. Additionally, it adds provisions to Section 2 concerning the utilization of cess proceeds for infrastructure maintenance and restricts refunds of over-paid cess to claims made within three months.

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Finance (Amendment) Act, 2013
metadata.long_title: An Act to amend the Sindh Finance Act, 1964.
metadata.one_line: Amends the Sindh Finance Act, 1964 to levy Electricity Duty and define exemptions and recovery mechanisms.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the Sindh Finance Act, 1964 to introduce a new Electricity Duty on energy consumption effective April 1, 2013. It defines specific terms such as 'consumer', 'energy', 'licensee', and 'non-licensee' while listing exemptions for government bodies, religious places, and small domestic users. The Act outlines the assessment and collection process through licensees, scheduled banks, and post offices, and establishes recovery procedures for unpaid duties via land revenue laws.

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Finance (Amendment) Act, 2015
metadata.long_title: An Act to further the Sindh Finance Act, 2014.
metadata.one_line: Amends the Sindh Finance Act, 2014 and Stamp Act, 1899 to adjust stamp duty rates for REITs and EITS.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the Sindh Finance Act, 2014 and the Stamp Act, 1899 to update stamp duty rates applicable in Sindh. It specifically introduces new clauses for Real Estate Investment Trusts (REITs) and Lease or sub-lease of Real Estate Investment Trusts (EITS). The amendments substitute specific percentage rates based on valuation tables or market values, whichever is higher.

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Finance (Amendment) Act, 2015
metadata.long_title: An Act to amend the Sindh Finance Act, 1993.
metadata.one_line: Amends the Sindh Finance Act, 1993 by changing truck trip fees to a per metric ton rate.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the Sindh Finance Act, 1993 to alter specific fee structures related to transport. It substitutes the phrase 'fifty rupees per truck per trip' with 'ten rupees per metric ton' in section 10 of the parent Act. The legislation came into force immediately upon enactment on May 18, 2015.

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Finance (Amendment) Act, 2020
metadata.long_title: An Act to amend the Sindh Finance Act, 2010.
metadata.one_line: Amends the Sindh Finance Act, 2010 by omitting section 4.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the Sindh Finance Act, 2010 by omitting section 4. It was passed by the Provincial Assembly of Sindh on August 24, 2020, and assented to by the Governor on September 3, 2020. The Act came into force immediately upon publication.

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Finance (Second Amendment) Act, 1995
metadata.long_title: An Act to amend the Sind Finance Act, 1964.
repeals: The Sindh Finance (Second Amendment) Ordinance, 1995
metadata.one_line: Amends the Sind Finance Act, 1964 by deleting specific words in its fifth Schedule and repeals a related Ordinance.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the Sind Finance Act, 1964 by deleting the terms 'industrial undertakings' and 'one and a half paisa per unit energy' from serial No. 2 of the fifth Schedule. It also explicitly repeals The Sindh Finance (Second Amendment) Ordinance, 1995. The legislation came into force immediately upon enactment.

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Finance Act, 1989
metadata.long_title: An Act to rationalize, enhance and levy certain taxes, duties and fees in the Province of Sindh;
metadata.max_penalty: penalty not exceeding the amount of such fee
metadata.one_line: This Act rationalizes and enhances taxes, duties, and fees in Sindh while regulating motor vehicle dealers.
metadata.summary: The Sindh Finance Act, 1989 was enacted to rationalize, enhance, and levy specific taxes, duties, and fees within the Province of Sindh. It amends several existing laws regarding stamp duties and motor vehicle taxation, including the Stamp Act of 1899 and the Sind Motor Vehicles Taxation Act of 1958. The Act also establishes a licensing regime for motor vehicle dealers, prescribing specific fees for metropolitan cities and other areas, and bars suits in civil courts against tax assessments made under the Act.

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Finance Act, 1990
metadata.long_title: An Act to rationalize, enhance and levy certain duties and fees in the Province of Sindh.
repeals: Sind Ordinance XVII of 1977
metadata.max_penalty: a penalty not exceeding the amount of such fees
metadata.one_line: This Act rationalizes and enhances duties/fees in Sindh, amends existing laws, and regulates video film dealers.
metadata.summary: The Sindh Finance Act, 1990 was enacted to rationalize, enhance, and levy certain duties and fees within the Province of Sindh. It amends several existing statutes including the Societies Registration Act, Court-Fees Act, and Stamp Act by substituting specific monetary values and clauses. Additionally, the Act regulates the business of video film dealers by requiring a licence and imposes penalties for contravention, while also repealing an earlier ordinance.

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Finance Act, 1993
metadata.long_title: An Act to rationalize, levy and enhance certain taxes and duties in the Province of Sindh.
amends: Sindh Urban Immovable Property Tax Act, 1958
metadata.one_line: This Act rationalizes and enhances various taxes and duties within the Province of Sindh.
metadata.summary: The Sindh Finance Act, 1993 was enacted to rationalize, levy, and enhance specific taxes and duties in the Province of Sindh. It amends existing legislation regarding stamp duties, immovable property tax, motor vehicle taxation, and company levies while introducing new cesses like the Coal Development Cess and Non-utilization Tax. The Act also establishes rules for the assessment and collection of these financial obligations.

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Finance Act, 1994
metadata.long_title: An Act to rationalize, levy and enhance certain taxes, duties and fees in the Province of Sindh;
metadata.one_line: This Act rationalizes and enhances taxes, duties, and fees in Sindh, including bed tax on hospitals and fees for marriage halls.
metadata.summary: The Sindh Finance Act, 1994 was enacted to rationalize, levy, and enhance certain taxes, duties, and fees within the Province of Sindh. It amends existing stamp duty rates and introduces specific levies such as a bed tax on private hospitals and annual licence fees for marriage halls, hotels, clubs, and community halls. The Act also empowers the Government to make rules regarding the assessment, collection, and payment of these taxes.

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Finance Act, 1995
metadata.long_title: An Act to rationalize, levy and enhance certain taxes and duties in the Province of Sindh.
metadata.one_line: This Act rationalizes, levies, and enhances various taxes and duties in the Province of Sindh.
metadata.summary: The Sindh Finance Act, 1995 was enacted to rationalize, levy, and enhance specific taxes and duties within the Province of Sindh. It amends several existing laws, including the Stamp Act, Urban Immovable Property Tax Act, Motor Vehicles Taxation Act, and previous Finance Acts, to adjust tax rates and introduce new levies such as a surcharge on property tax and a tax on ceremonial parties. The Act also establishes rules for assessment, collection, and payment of these taxes while defining key terms like 'Government' and 'developer'.

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Finance Act, 1996
metadata.long_title: An Act to rationalize, levy enhance certain taxes and duties in the Province of Sindh.
metadata.one_line: An Act to rationalize, levy and enhance certain taxes and duties in the Province of Sindh.
metadata.summary: This Act provides for the rationalization and enhancement of various taxes and duties within the Province of Sindh. It amends existing legislation regarding stamp duties on documents like debt acknowledgements, allotment orders, and contracts. The Act also establishes new tax regimes for land ownership based on acreage and location, as well as a tax on the sale of services by various professionals and entities.

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Finance Act, 2003
metadata.long_title: An Act to rationalize and provide relief in certain taxes and duties in the province of Sindh and to amendment certain laws.
amends: Section 8 of Sindh Act VII of 1977
First Schedule to Ordinance XII of 2000
metadata.one_line: Rationalizes taxes in Sindh and amends various provincial laws regarding duties, property tax, and salaries.
metadata.summary: This Act rationalizes and provides relief on certain taxes and duties within the Province of Sindh. It amends several existing laws, including the Stamp Act, Urban Immovable Property Tax Act, Assembly Members Salaries Act, and previous Finance Acts. The legislation substitutes specific figures and clauses to adjust tax rates, exemptions, and salary allowances.

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Finance Act, 2004
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide relief in certain duties and taxes in the Province of Sindh and to amend certain laws.
metadata.one_line: Provides tax relief in Sindh and amends the Stamp Act of 1899 and West Pakistan Finance Act of 1964.
metadata.summary: This Act provides relief from certain duties and taxes within the Province of Sindh. It also amends specific sections of the Stamp Act, 1899, as applied to Sindh. Additionally, it substitutes a serial number in the Seventh Schedule of the Sind Finance Act, 1964.

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Finance Act, 2005
metadata.long_title: An Act to rationalize certain taxes and provide relief in certain taxes and fee in the Province of Sindh and to amend certain laws.
metadata.one_line: This Act rationalizes taxes in Sindh and amends various finance acts and ordinances.
metadata.summary: The Sindh Finance Act, 2005 was enacted to rationalize certain taxes and provide relief on fees within the Province of Sindh. It also serves to amend specific sections and schedules of existing laws, including the West Pakistan Act of 1964, various Sindh Acts from 1977 and 1994, and Ordinances from 2000 and 2001. The Act came into force on July 1st, 2005, shortly after its promulgation on July 6th, 2005.

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Finance Act, 2006
metadata.long_title: An Act to rationalize certain taxes and duties and amend certain laws in the Province of Sindh.
metadata.commencement: 1st day of July, 2006 (except sections 4, 5 and 7 which came into force on 1st day of July, 2005)
amends: Schedule to Sindh Ordinance VIII of 2000
repeals: Sindh Ordinance XVII of 2006
metadata.one_line: This Act rationalizes taxes and duties in Sindh while amending various provincial laws regarding salaries and stamp duties.
metadata.summary: The Sindh Finance Act, 2006 was enacted to rationalize certain taxes and duties within the Province of Sindh. It amends the Stamp Act of 1899 to include digital media formats and updates schedules regarding duty payments for various instruments like leases and bills of entry. Additionally, the Act revises salaries and allowances for Assembly members, Ministers, and Special Assistants in several existing Acts from 1974, 1975, and 2003, while repealing a specific amending ordinance from 2006.

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Finance Act, 2007
metadata.long_title: An Act to rationalize certain taxes in the Province of Sindh and to amend relevant laws.
metadata.one_line: Rationalizes certain taxes in Sindh and amends the Sind Motor Vehicle Taxation Act, 1958 and Sind Finance Act, 1977.
metadata.summary: This Act aims to rationalize specific taxes within the Province of Sindh by amending existing relevant laws. It modifies the Sind Motor Vehicle Taxation Act, 1958 regarding truck and trailer taxation based on laden weight. Additionally, it substitutes a new provision in section 8 of the Sind Finance Act, 1977 to establish a hotel tax levied on an advalorem basis at a specified rate per lodging unit.

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Finance Act, 2008
metadata.long_title: An Act to rationalize certain duties and cess in the Province of Sindh and to amend relevant laws.
amends: West Pakistan Act No. XXXII of 1958
metadata.one_line: This Act rationalizes duties and cess in Sindh and amends relevant laws including stamp, sales tax, and motor vehicle acts.
metadata.summary: The Sindh Finance Act, 2008 was enacted to rationalize certain duties and cess within the Province of Sindh. It amends several existing laws, including the Stamp Act, 1899, the Sindh Finance Act, 1994, the Sindh Sales Tax Ordinance, 2000, and the Sind Motor Vehicles Taxation Act, 1958. The Act introduces specific changes such as adjusting cess rates on gold, modifying sales tax percentages, and establishing a one-time luxury tax on imported or locally manufactured motor cars registered in Sindh.

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Finance Act, 2009
metadata.long_title: An Act to rationalize certain duties and taxes, in the Province of Sindh and to amend relevant laws.
metadata.one_line: This Act rationalizes duties and taxes in Sindh and amends several relevant provincial laws.
metadata.summary: The Sindh Finance Act, 2009 aims to rationalize certain duties and taxes within the Province of Sindh. It amends existing legislation including the Stamp Act, 1899, the Sind Finance Act, 1977, and others to update tax rates and definitions. The Act also introduces new penalties for motor vehicle registration defaults and adjusts electricity duty categories.

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Finance Act, 2010
metadata.long_title: An Act to rationalize certain duties and taxes and provide for levy of Capital Value Tax on immovable property, in the Province of Sindh and to amend relevant laws.
metadata.one_line: This Act levies Capital Value Tax on immovable property in Sindh and amends relevant stamp and property tax laws.
metadata.summary: The Sindh Finance Act, 2010 rationalizes existing duties and taxes within the Province of Sindh. It introduces a new Capital Value Tax on the acquisition of immovable property by individuals, firms, companies, and development authorities, excluding specific family transfers and inheritances. The Act also amends the Stamp Act, 1899 and the Sind Urban Immovable Property Tax Act, 1958 to update rates and definitions for real estate transactions.

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Finance Act, 2013
metadata.long_title: An Act to rationalize, levy and enhance certain taxes, duties and cess and amend certain laws in the Province of Sindh.
amends: Sindh Urban Immovable Property Tax Act, 1958
metadata.one_line: This Act rationalizes, levies, and enhances taxes in Sindh while amending several existing provincial laws.
metadata.summary: The Sindh Finance Act, 2013 was enacted to rationalize, levy, and enhance certain taxes, duties, and cess within the Province of Sindh. It also amends specific sections of previous acts, including the Sindh Urban Immovable Property Tax Act, 1958, and the Sindh Sales Tax on Services Act, 2011. The Act introduces new tariff headings for various service providers and adjusts tax rates for goods and services.

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Finance Act, 2014
metadata.long_title: An Act to rationalize, levy and enhance certain taxes and duties in the Province of Sindh and to amend certain laws in the Province of Sindh;
amends: Sindh Sales Tax on Services Act, 2011
key_definitions: car or automobile washing or similar service station
metadata.one_line: This Act rationalizes and enhances taxes in Sindh while amending the Finance Act 2010, Stamp Act 1899, and Sales Tax on Services Act 2011.
metadata.summary: The Sindh Finance Act, 2014 aims to rationalize, levy, and enhance certain taxes and duties within the Province of Sindh. It amends existing legislation including the Sindh Finance Act of 2010, the Stamp Act of 1899, the Sindh Act of 2011, and the Sindh Sales Tax on Services Act of 2011. The Act introduces specific definitions for market value and real estate investment trusts, adjusts stamp duty rates, and updates service tax classifications.

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Finance Act, 2015
metadata.long_title: An Act to rationalize, levy and enhance certain taxes and duties in the Province of Sindh and to amend certain laws in the Provinces of Sindh;
amends: The Sindh Urban Immovable Property Tax Act, 1958
The Sindh Sales Tax on Services Act, 2011
metadata.one_line: This Act rationalizes and enhances taxes in Sindh while amending several existing provincial laws.
metadata.summary: The Sindh Finance Act, 2015 was enacted to rationalize, levy, and enhance certain taxes and duties within the Province of Sindh. It also aims to amend specific existing laws in the province to align them with new fiscal policies. The Act modifies the Stamp Act, Urban Immovable Property Tax Act, previous Finance Acts, and the Sales Tax on Services Act by substituting values, adding new clauses, and updating tariff headings for various services.

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Finance Act, 2017
metadata.long_title: An Act to rationalize certain taxes in the Province of Sindh and to amend certain laws in the Province of Sindh.
amends: Sindh Sales Tax on Services Act, 2011
metadata.max_penalty: 100,000 rupees or imprisonment up to one year or both
metadata.one_line: This Act rationalizes taxes in Sindh and amends the Sales Tax on Services Act, 2011 regarding input tax, penalties, and electronic monitoring.
metadata.summary: The Sindh Finance Act, 2017 aims to rationalize certain taxes within the Province of Sindh and amend existing provincial laws. It specifically targets the Sindh Sales Tax on Services Act, 2011 by introducing new clauses for input tax adjustment, stricter penalties for non-compliance, and provisions for electronic monitoring of transactions. The Act also establishes mechanisms for recovering short-paid tax amounts without prior notice and mandates the use of electronic means like fiscal cash registers for issuing tax invoices.

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Finance Act, 2026
metadata.long_title: An Act to rationalize, levy and enhance certain taxes and duties in the Province of Sindh and to amend certain laws in the Province of Sindh;
amends: Sindh Sales Tax on Services Act, 2011
metadata.max_penalty: one hundred million rupees
metadata.one_line: This Act rationalizes taxes in Sindh and amends the Sales Tax on Services Act, 2011 regarding invoicing software penalties and tax exemptions.
metadata.summary: The Sindh Finance Act, 2026 is an amendment act designed to rationalize and enhance certain taxes and duties within the Province of Sindh. It specifically amends the Sindh Sales Tax on Services Act, 2011 by increasing time limits for de-registration, imposing penalties for non-compliant invoicing software, and updating tax exemptions for education and reinsurance services. The Act also introduces new provisions regarding the display of tax notices, confidentiality of information held by the Board of Revenue, and the maintenance of records by owners.

name: SINDH FINANCIAL MANAGEMENT AND ACCOUNTABILITY ACT, 2011

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Financial Management and Accountability Act, 2011
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for efficient and transparent management of the Provincial Consolidated Fund and Public Account of the Province and proper accountability of all transactions in relation thereto.
metadata.territorial_extent: the whole of the Province of Sindh
metadata.max_penalty: imprisonment up to three years or fine up to one million rupees or both
metadata.one_line: This Act ensures efficient, transparent management of Sindh's funds and accountability for financial transactions.
metadata.summary: The Sindh Financial Management and Accountability Act, 2011 establishes a legal framework for the efficient and transparent management of the Provincial Consolidated Fund and Public Account of Sindh. It defines key terms such as 'financial transaction' and 'public servant', and outlines principles for proper financial conduct including authorization, recording, and efficiency. The Act creates offences for breaches of its provisions, prescribing penalties of up to three years imprisonment or a fine of one million rupees, and empowers the Government to make necessary rules.

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Fisheries (Amendment) Act, 2003
metadata.long_title: An Act to amend the Sindh Fisheries Ordinance, 1980.
repeals: The Sindh Fisheries (Amendment) Ordinance, 2003
metadata.max_penalty: imprisonment for one year or fine of fifty thousand rupees or both
metadata.one_line: Amends the Sindh Fisheries Ordinance, 1980 regarding net definitions and penalties, repealing a 2003 Ordinance.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the Sindh Fisheries Ordinance, 1980 to include specific government-declared nets in its definition. It also substitutes provisions in Section 21 to establish new offences and penalties for contravening sections 4, 5, 7, or 8 of the Ordinance. The Act repeals the earlier Sindh Fisheries (Amendment) Ordinance, 2003 and comes into force immediately.

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Fisheries (Amendment) Act, 2011
metadata.long_title: An Act to amend the Sind Fisheries Ordinance, 1980.
metadata.one_line: Amends the Sind Fisheries Ordinance, 1980 to update terminology and licensing provisions.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the Sind Fisheries Ordinance, 1980 to replace references to 'Sind' with 'Sindh'. It updates the definition of a fisherman and expands the scope of fishing water bodies. The Act also cancels prior leases and modifies sections regarding licensing and penalties.

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Food Fortification Act, 2021
metadata.long_title: An Act to address and alleviate nutritional deficiencies through food fortification.
metadata.territorial_extent: whole of the Province of Sindh
metadata.one_line: This Act mandates the fortification of staple foods like wheat flour and ghee to combat nutritional deficiencies in Sindh.
metadata.summary: The Sindh Food Fortification Act, 2021 aims to alleviate severe micronutrient malnutrition among women and children in the province. It mandates that importers, manufacturers, and commercial users fortify specific staple foods such as wheat flour, ghee, and edible oil with essential micronutrients like iron, zinc, and vitamins. The Act establishes quality assurance requirements, labeling standards, and registration processes enforced by the Sindh Food Authority to ensure food safety and nutritional adequacy.

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Freedom of Information Act, 2006
metadata.long_title: An act to provide for transparency and Freedom of Information.
establishes: Ombudsman (under section 3 of the Establishment of Office for the Province of Sindh Act, 1991)
metadata.max_penalty: imprisonment for a term not exceeding two years, or with fine, or with both
metadata.one_line: An Act to provide for transparency and freedom of information in the Province of Sindh.
metadata.summary: This Act ensures citizens of Sindh have improved access to public records to make the Provincial Government more accountable. It mandates that all official records be maintained, indexed, published, and computerized while defining specific exemptions for sensitive data like national security or personal privacy. The Act establishes a procedure for requesters to file complaints with the Ombudsman if information is wrongfully denied or unduly delayed.

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Fund Management House Act, 2013
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the establishment and regulation of the Sindh Fund Management House.
metadata.territorial_extent: the whole of the Province of Sindh
metadata.one_line: Establishes and regulates the Sindh Fund Management House for managing government investment funds in Sindh.
metadata.summary: This Act provides for the establishment and regulation of the Sindh Fund Management House to efficiently manage investment funds of the Government and its entities in the Province of Sindh. It defines the structure, functions, and powers of the House, including the Board, Investment Committee, and various officers. The legislation also outlines financial management procedures, designated fund policies, secrecy obligations, and provisions for making rules and regulations.

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Goth-Abad (Housing Scheme) (Amendment) Act, 2008
metadata.long_title: An Act to amend the Sind Goth-Abad (Housing Scheme) Act, 1987.
metadata.one_line: Amends the Sind Goth-Abad (Housing Scheme) Act, 1987 regarding rural area definitions and local government ordinances.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the Sind Goth-Abad (Housing Scheme) Act, 1987 to update references to local government ordinances and redefine rural areas. It substitutes specific clauses in sections 1, 2, and 3 of the original Act to reflect changes from the 1979 to the 2001 Sind Local Government Ordinance. Additionally, it inserts a new section allowing the Government to declare dehs or towns as rural areas via notification.

name: SINDH GOVERNMENT SERVANTS BENEVOLENT FUND (AMENDMENT) ACT, 1989

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Government Servants Benevolent Fund (Amendment) Act, 1989
metadata.long_title: An Act to amend the Sindh Government Servants Benevolent Fund Ordinance, 1960.
amends: The Sindh Government Servants Benevolent Fund Ordinance, 1960
metadata.one_line: Amends the Sindh Government Servants Benevolent Fund Ordinance, 1960 regarding family definitions and fund management.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the Sindh Government Servants Benevolent Fund Ordinance, 1960 to update the definition of 'family' for government servants. It omits certain clauses from previous sections and adds provisions for housing schemes for serving servants and their families. The Act also establishes specific Boards of Management at provincial, divisional, and secretariat levels to manage fund investments, allocate expenditures, and provide relief to eligible government servants.

name: SINDH GOVERNMENT SERVANTS BENEVOLENT FUND (AMENDMENT) ACT, 2012

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Government Servants Benevolent Fund (Amendment) Act, 2012
metadata.long_title: An Act to amend the Sind Government Servants Benevolent Fund Ordinance, 1960.
amends: Sind Government Servants Benevolent Fund Ordinance, 1960
metadata.one_line: Amends the Sind Government Servants Benevolent Fund Ordinance, 1960 by substituting 'District' for 'Division'.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the Sind Government Servants Benevolent Fund Ordinance, 1960. It specifically substitutes the word 'District' for 'Divisional' and 'Division' in section 6 of the original Ordinance. The amendment came into force immediately upon enactment.

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Health Foundation Act, 1992
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the establishment of the Health Foundation in the Province of Sindh.
establishes: Board of the Sindh Health Foundation
metadata.one_line: Establishes the Sindh Health Foundation to promote, develop and finance health services in Sindh.
metadata.summary: This Act establishes the Sindh Health Foundation as a body corporate to promote and finance health services, particularly in less developed and rural areas of Sindh. The Foundation is administered by a Board appointed by the Government of Sindh and has powers to establish health institutions, provide grants and loans, and assist the private sector. It includes provisions for a dedicated Fund, annual audits, and an indemnity clause protecting officials acting in good faith.

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Healthcare Commission Act, 2013
metadata.long_title: An Act to improve the quality of healthcare services and banning quackery in the Province of Sindh in all its forms and manifestations;
metadata.territorial_extent: the whole of the Province of Sindh
metadata.one_line: This Act establishes the Sindh Healthcare Commission to improve healthcare quality and ban quackery in Sindh.
metadata.summary: The Sindh Healthcare Commission Act, 2013 was enacted to improve access, equity, and quality of healthcare services while banning quackery in Sindh. It establishes a Commission with a Board, Technical Advisory Committee, and Chief Executive Officer to regulate healthcare establishments. The Act provides for registration, licensing, accreditation, inspection, and enforcement mechanisms to ensure standards of care.

name: SINDH HEALTHCARE SERVICE PROVIDERS AND FACILITIES (PREVENTION OF VIOLENCE AND DAMAGE TO PROPERTY) ACT, 2021

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Healthcare Service Providers and Facilities (Prevention of Violence and Damage to Property) Act, 2021
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide protection to and prohibit violence against healthcare service providers and to prevent damage or loss to property in healthcare service facilities or to those mandated for the provision of healthcare services and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
metadata.one_line: This Act protects healthcare providers from violence and prevents damage to property in healthcare facilities within Sindh.
metadata.summary: The Act provides legal protection against violence directed at healthcare service providers and prohibits damage to property within healthcare facilities. It defines key terms such as 'healthcare', 'healthcare service providers', and 'medical supplies' to ensure comprehensive coverage of the sector. The legislation applies to the entire Province of Sindh and comes into force immediately upon enactment.

metadata.short_title: The Sindh High Density Development Board (Amendment) Act, 2013
metadata.long_title: An Act to amend the Sindh High Density Development Board Act, 2010.
amends: Sindh High Density Development Board Act, 2010
metadata.one_line: Amends the constitution of the Sindh High Density Development Board by substituting Section 3.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the Sindh High Density Development Board Act, 2010 to update the composition of the Board. It substitutes Section 3 to list specific members including the Chief Minister, Minister for Local Government and Housing Town Planning Department, Chief Secretary, Secretary for Local Government, Mayor or Chairman of respective Council, Chief Controller of Buildings, Head of Buildings Control, and Head of Master Plan of the Respective Council.

name: SINDH HIGH DENSITY DEVELOPMENT BOARD (AMENDMENT) ACT, 2011

metadata.short_title: The Sindh High Density Development Board (Amendment) Act, 2011
metadata.long_title: An Act to amend the Sindh High Density Development Board Act, 2010.
amends: Sindh High Density Development Board Act, 2010
metadata.one_line: Amends the Sindh High Density Development Board Act, 2010 to allow co-option of local civil agency heads and professional body representatives.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the Sindh High Density Development Board Act, 2010 by modifying Section 4. The amendment adds a proviso allowing the Board to co-opt heads of local civil agencies, other persons, or representatives of professional bodies as members. It also changes the punctuation at the end of Section 4 from a full stop to a colon.

name: SINDH HIGH DENSITY DEVELOPMENT BOARD ACT, 2010

metadata.short_title: The Sindh High Density Development Board Act, 2010
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for creation of High Density Development Board to ensure coordinated and integrated development of the High Density Zones in the urban centers of the Province.
metadata.territorial_extent: the whole of Province of Sindh
metadata.one_line: Establishes the High Density Development Board for coordinated urban development in Sindh.
metadata.summary: This Act creates the High Density Development Board to ensure integrated development of high density zones in Sindh's urban centers. The Board is constituted by key provincial officials including the Governor and Chief Minister. It empowers the Board to identify high-density zones and allows the Government to make rules for its implementation.

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Higher Education Commission Act, 2013
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the establishment of Sindh Higher Education Commission.
repeals: The Higher Education Commission Ordinance, 2002
metadata.one_line: Establishes the Sindh Higher Education Commission and defines its functions, composition, and powers within Sindh.
metadata.summary: This Act establishes the Sindh Higher Education Commission as a body corporate to promote higher education, research, and development in the Province of Sindh. The Commission is headed by a Chairperson appointed by the Controlling Authority (Chief Minister) and includes various secretaries and other members representing different sectors. It outlines the Commission's powers to acquire property, set up sub-offices, make rules, and submit annual reports and audited accounts to the Controlling Authority.

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Hindus Marriage Act, 2016
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for law relating to marriage amongst Hindus.
metadata.territorial_extent: all Hindus in the Province of Sindh
metadata.one_line: Provides a formal process for registering Hindu marriages in Sindh, including conditions, ceremonies, and registration procedures.
metadata.summary: This Act establishes a uniform mechanism for the registration of marriages among Hindus in the Province of Sindh. It sets out specific conditions for solemnizing a marriage, such as age requirements, free consent, and the presence of witnesses. The Act mandates that every marriage be registered with the Union Council or Municipal Authority within 45 days of the ceremony and provides for the issuance of a Certificate of Marriage.

name: SINDH HIV AND AIDS CONTROL TREATMENT AND PROTECTION ACT, 2013

metadata.short_title: The Sindh HIV and AIDS Control Treatment and Protection Act, 2013
metadata.long_title: An Act to control the transmission and spread of HIV in the Province of Sindh and to provide measures for the treatment, care and support of the People Living With HIV and AIDS.
metadata.territorial_extent: the whole of the Province of Sindh
metadata.max_penalty: imprisonment of five years and fine which may extend to two hundred thousand rupees
metadata.one_line: This Act controls HIV transmission in Sindh, provides treatment support, establishes the Sindh AIDS Commission, and prohibits discrimination.
metadata.summary: The Sindh HIV and AIDS Control Treatment and Protection Act, 2013 aims to control HIV transmission and provide care for people living with HIV/AIDS within the Province of Sindh. It establishes the Sindh AIDS Commission to oversee implementation and monitoring of these measures. The Act prohibits discrimination based on HIV status, mandates confidentiality of health information, and outlines penalties for negligence or unauthorized disclosure.

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Home-Based Workers Act, 2018
metadata.long_title: An Act to formulate the law relating to the persons who work in the informal or unorganized sector carrying out remunerative work within their homes or in the surrounding, grounds, and protection for their rights.
metadata.territorial_extent: the whole Province of the Sindh
establishes: Provincial Council for the Home Based Workers
metadata.one_line: This Act provides social protection and legal mechanisms for home-based workers in Sindh.
metadata.summary: The Sindh Home-Based Workers Act, 2018 establishes a legal framework to protect persons working in the informal sector within their homes. It creates a Provincial Council and a Fund to support these workers and settle disputes through an Arbitration Committee. The Act defines key terms such as 'home-based worker' and 'contractor', mandates record-keeping by employers, and ensures the payment of wages.

metadata.short_title: The Sind Incumbered Estates Act, 1896
metadata.long_title: An act to amend the law providing for the relief of zamindars in Sind.
metadata.one_line: This Act provides relief to zamindars in Sindh by allowing for the inquiry, management, and liquidation of their incumbered estates.
metadata.summary: The Sind Incumbered Estates Act, 1896 amends the law to provide relief to zamindars in Sindh who are subject to significant debts or liabilities. It establishes a framework where a Zamindar can apply for an inquiry into their debts and property sufficiency. Upon approval, a manager is appointed to take charge of the estate, collect rents, pay debts, and formulate a liquidation scheme sanctioned by the Board of Revenue. The Act outlines the powers of the manager, procedures for appealing decisions, and provisions regarding the validity of mortgages and leases made during management.

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Industrial Relations Act, 2013
metadata.long_title: An Act to regulate formation of trade unions, regulation and improvement of relations between employers and workmen.
metadata.territorial_extent: the whole of the Province of Sindh
repeals: the repealed Act
metadata.one_line: Regulates trade unions and industrial relations in Sindh, establishing courts for dispute resolution.
metadata.summary: This Act regulates the formation of trade unions and improves relations between employers and workmen in Sindh. It establishes mechanisms for collective bargaining, defines unfair labour practices, and sets procedures for strikes, lock-outs, and arbitration. The Act creates Labour Courts and Tribunals to adjudicate industrial disputes and provides penalties for contraventions.

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Information Technology Board (Amendment) Act, 2004
metadata.long_title: An Act to amend the Sindh Information Technology Board Ordinance, 2002.
amends: The Sindh Information Technology Board Ordinance, 2002
repeals: The Sindh Information Technology Board (Amendment) Ordinance, 2003
metadata.one_line: Amends the Sindh Information Technology Board Ordinance, 2002 regarding board composition and powers.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the Sindh Information Technology Board Ordinance, 2002 to update definitions for 'Member' and 'Vice Chairperson'. It revises the board's composition to include a Governor as Chairperson, a Minister as Vice-Chairperson, and eleven members including private sector representatives. The Act also substitutes provisions regarding the promotion of information technology strategies and allows the Chairperson to delegate powers to officers.

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Injured Persons (Medical Aid) Act, 2014
metadata.long_title: An Act to make provisions for medical aid and treatment of injured persons.
metadata.territorial_extent: the whole of the Province of Sindh
metadata.max_penalty: imprisonment which may extend to three years, or with fine which shall not be less than twenty thousand rupees, or with both
metadata.one_line: This Act provides for medical aid and treatment of injured persons in Sindh, prioritizing their care over police formalities.
metadata.summary: The Sindh Injured Persons (Medical Aid) Act, 2014 establishes provisions to ensure immediate medical aid and treatment for injured persons in the Province of Sindh. It mandates that injured persons be treated on a priority basis without delay, even before medico-legal formalities are completed. The Act restricts police interference during treatment, prohibits shifting stabilized patients, and requires hospitals to be notified by the Government. It also outlines penalties for contravention and mechanisms for public awareness.

name: SINDH INJURED PERSONS COMPULSORY MEDICAL TREATMENT (AMAL UMER) ACT, 2019

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Injured Persons Compulsory Medical Treatment (Amal Umer) Act, 2019
metadata.long_title: An Act to make provisions for medical aid and treatment of injured persons in an emergency.
metadata.territorial_extent: the whole of the Province of Sindh
repeals: The Sindh Injured Persons (Medical Aid) Act, 2014
metadata.one_line: This Act mandates immediate medical treatment for injured persons in Sindh without payment or medico-legal formalities.
metadata.summary: The Act ensures that injured persons in Sindh receive compulsory medical treatment immediately upon arrival at a hospital, regardless of their ability to pay or the completion of medico-legal formalities. It prohibits hospitals and doctors from demanding payment before stabilizing an injured person and forbids police officers from interrupting treatment or interrogating patients while they are in danger. The Act defines key terms such as 'ambulance' and 'emergency medical condition', mandates the maintenance of specific records by hospitals, and repeals the previous Sindh Injured Persons (Medical Aid) Act, 2014.

name: SINDH INSTITUTE OF MANAGEMENT AND TECHNOLOGY ACT, 2015

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Institute of Management and Technology Act, 2015
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the establishment of an Institute at Karachi and other places in Sindh Province known as the Sindh Institute of Management and Technology.
metadata.territorial_extent: Karachi and other places in Sindh Province
establishes: Sindh Institute of Management and Technology
Board of Advanced Studies and Research
metadata.one_line: Establishes the Sindh Institute of Management and Technology in Karachi with defined powers, governance, and academic functions.
metadata.summary: This Act establishes the Sindh Institute of Management and Technology at Karachi and other places in Sindh Province. It defines the institute's powers to conduct education, research, and examinations while ensuring openness to all classes and creeds. The legislation outlines the structure of governing bodies including the Board, Academic Council, and various committees responsible for finance, faculty selection, and academic planning.

name: SINDH INSTITUTE OF MEDICAL SCIENCES, KARACHI ACT, 2009

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Institute of Medical Sciences, Karachi Act, 2009
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the establishment of an Institute known as the Sindh Institute of Medical Sciences, Karachi.
establishes: Sindh Institute of Medical Sciences, Karachi
metadata.one_line: Establishes the Sindh Institute of Medical Sciences, Karachi as a degree-awarding body with perpetual succession.
metadata.summary: This Act establishes the Sindh Institute of Medical Sciences, Karachi as a corporate body with powers to award degrees and conduct research. It defines the structure including the Patron, Rector, Board, and various councils responsible for academics and administration. The Institute is authorized to prescribe courses, hold examinations, engage staff, and maintain linkages with other institutions both inside and outside Pakistan.

name: SINDH INSTITUTE OF OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISUAL SCIENCES ACT, 2013

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Institute of Ophthalmology and Visual Sciences Act, 2013
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the establishment of an Institute known as the Sindh Institute of Ophthalmology and Visual Sciences at Hyderabad.
repeals: The Liaquat University of Medical Health Sciences Ordinance., 2000 (Ordinance No.VIII of 2001) relating to the Ophthalmology Department of Liaquat University of Medical and Health Sciences, Jamshoro
establishes: Sindh Institute of Ophthalmology and Visual Sciences
metadata.one_line: Establishes the Sindh Institute of Ophthalmology and Visual Sciences at Hyderabad to treat eye diseases, teach, and conduct research.
metadata.summary: This Act establishes the Sindh Institute of Ophthalmology and Visual Sciences at Hyderabad by reconstituting the Liaquat University Eye Hospital. It defines the Institute as a body corporate with perpetual succession, transferring its property and staff from the previous hospital. The Act outlines the functions of the Institute, including treatment, teaching, research, and fund management, while also repealing relevant provisions of the 2001 Ordinance.

name: SINDH INSTITUTE OF UROLOGY AND TRANSPLANTATION ACT, 1991

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Institute of Urology and Transplantation Act, 1991
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the establishment of an Institute of Urology and Transplantation.
repeals: Sindh Ordinance VII of 1990
establishes: Sindh Institute of Urology and Transplantation
metadata.one_line: Establishes the Sindh Institute of Urology and Transplantation to treat urological diseases, conduct research, and teach.
metadata.summary: This Act establishes the Sindh Institute of Urology and Transplantation by reconstituting the Urology Department of Dow Medical College. The Institute functions as a body corporate with powers to acquire property, undertake treatment, develop medical techniques, and run postgraduate teaching programs. It is administered by a Board of Governors comprising government officials, medical experts, and representatives from various organizations.

name: SINDH INSURANCE OF PUBLIC PROPERTY ACT 2015

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Insurance of Public Property Act, 2015
metadata.long_title: An Act to regulate and direct the procurement of non-life insurance with respect to public property pertaining to the Province of Sindh.
metadata.territorial_extent: the whole of the Province of Sindh
metadata.max_penalty: fine extending to one percent of the sum assured or an amount not exceeding two million rupees, whichever is lower
metadata.one_line: This Act mandates that all non-life insurance for public property in Sindh must be procured from Sindh Insurance Limited.
metadata.summary: The Sindh Insurance of Public Property Act, 2015 was enacted to regulate the procurement of non-life insurance for public property within the Province of Sindh. It mandates that such insurance must be placed with and procured exclusively from Sindh Insurance Limited, unless exempted by government notification or due to the company's inability to provide coverage. The Act establishes a Committee to determine insurance tariff rates based on market trends and outlines penalties for contravention, including fines up to two million rupees.

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Irrigation (Amendment) Act, 2011
metadata.long_title: An Act to amend the Sind Preamble. Irrigation Act,1879, in the manner hereinafter appearing;
metadata.max_penalty: imprisonment which may extend to ten years and fine which may extend to rupees one million
metadata.one_line: Amends the Sindh Irrigation Act, 1879 to resume natural depression courses for flood discharge.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the Sind Irrigation Act, 1879 by adding a new section regarding the resumption of land used for natural or artificial depression courses meant for flood or rain waters. It mandates that such land shall be exclusively used for its intended purpose and requires persons in possession to vacate within seven days of commencement. Failure to comply results in imprisonment up to ten years and a fine up to one million rupees, with the offence being non-bailable.

name: SINDH IRRIGATION AND DRAINAGE AUTHORITY ACT, 1997

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Irrigation and Drainage Authority Act, 1997
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the establishment of the Irrigation and Drainage Authority in the Province of Sindh.
metadata.territorial_extent: the whole of Province of Sindh
repeals: Sindh Ordinance No.III of 1997
metadata.one_line: Establishes the Sindh Irrigation and Drainage Authority for equitable water distribution and flood control in Sindh.
metadata.summary: This Act establishes the Sindh Irrigation and Drainage Authority as a body corporate to manage irrigation water distribution, drainage, and flood control. It defines the composition of the Authority's board, including representatives from various government departments and farmer organizations. The Act also provides for the transfer of assets and liabilities from the existing Irrigation Wing to the new Authority and repeals a previous ordinance.

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Judicial Academy Act, 1993
metadata.long_title: An Act to establish a Provincial Judicial Academy in the Province of Sindh.
repeals: Sindh Ordinance No.XVIII of 1993
establishes: Board of Governors of the Academy
metadata.one_line: Establishes the Sindh Judicial Academy to provide legal training and education for the subordinate judiciary and bar.
metadata.summary: This Act establishes the Sindh Judicial Academy as a body corporate with its headquarters in Karachi. The Academy is tasked with providing legal orientation, continuing education, and conducting seminars for members of the subordinate judiciary, law officers, and the bar. It creates a Board of Governors comprising high-ranking judicial officials, the Attorney General, and other members to oversee the Academy's functions and budget.

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Katchi Abadis (Amendment) Act, 2009
metadata.long_title: An Act to amend the Sindh Katchi Abadis Act, 1987 and the Prosecution Service (Constitution, Functions and Powers) Act, 2009 in the manner hereinafter appearing.
amends: Prosecution Service (Constitution, Functions and Powers) Act, 2009
metadata.one_line: Amends the Sindh Katchi Abadis Act, 1987 and Prosecution Service Act, 2009 by substituting specific dates.
metadata.summary: This Act amends two existing laws: the Sindh Katchi Abadis Act, 1987 and the Prosecution Service (Constitution, Functions and Powers) Act, 2009. It specifically substitutes the date '30th day of June, 1997' for '23rd day of March, 1985' in section 19, subsection 1 of the Katchi Abadis Act. The legislation came into force immediately upon enactment.

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Katchi Abadis (Amendment) Act, 2022
