metadata.summary: This Act amends the Sindh Katchi Abadis Act, 1987. It specifically substitutes the words '30th day of June, 1997' with '31st day of December, 2011' in section 19, subsection (1) of the parent Act. The legislation was passed by the Provincial Assembly of Sindh and assented to by the Governor on July 19, 2022.

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Land Revenue (Amendment) Act, 2013
metadata.long_title: An Act to amend the Sindh Land Revenue Act, 1967.
metadata.one_line: Amends the Sindh Land Revenue Act, 1967 to define Service Centers and computerized records.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the Sindh Land Revenue Act, 1967 to introduce new definitions regarding Service Centers and computerized records of rights. It establishes a Service Center for maintaining computerized records and providing services for mutation and registration. The Act also updates provisions in sections 39 and 40 to recognize electronic documents and authenticated computerized records as official records of rights.

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Land Revenue (Amendment) Act, 2008
metadata.long_title: An Act to amend the Sind Land Revenue Act, 1967.
metadata.one_line: Amends the Sindh Land Revenue Act, 1967 to allow renaming of districts or talukas via provincial resolution.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the Sindh Land Revenue Act, 1967 by inserting a new section 6-A. The amendment empowers the Government to rename a District or Taluka if the Provincial Assembly passes a resolution for such renaming. It overrides provisions in sections 5 and 6 of the parent Act regarding these names.

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Land Revenue (Amendment) Act, 2011
metadata.long_title: An Act to amend the Sind Land Revenue Act, 1967.
repeals: The Sindh Land Revenue (Amendment) Ordinance, 2011
metadata.one_line: Amends the Sind Land Revenue Act, 1967 by updating terms and administrative structure.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the Sind Land Revenue Act, 1967 to update terminology and administrative structures within Sindh. It substitutes specific words such as 'Sind' with 'Sindh' and revives original nomenclatures like 'Division' and 'Sub-Division'. The legislation also revises sections regarding revenue officers, their appointments, and the division of the province into districts and sub-divisions.

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Land Revenue (Amendment) Act, 2019
metadata.long_title: An Act to amend the Sindh Land Revenue Act, 1967.
key_definitions: law for the time being in force
metadata.one_line: Amends the Sindh Land Revenue Act, 1967 by substituting section 52 regarding the presumption of correctness of records.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the Sindh Land Revenue Act, 1967 to update the provisions concerning the presumption of correctness in records of rights. It substitutes the existing text of section 52 with a new version that clarifies when entries are presumed true until contrary proof or lawful substitution occurs. The legislation was passed by the Provincial Assembly of Sindh and received assent from the Governor on August 15, 2022.

metadata.summary: This Act amends several existing laws applicable to the Province of Sindh by deleting specific words, substituting figures or names, and removing sections that are no longer necessary. It also repeals a series of older Acts and Ordinances listed in the Schedule, including those related to elections, agriculture, drugs, and corruption. The legislation comes into force immediately upon enactment.

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Laws (Amendment) Act, 2012
metadata.long_title: An Act to correct the spelling of the name of the province in all legal documents prior to the 18th Amendment.

metadata.one_line: Amends all legal instruments in Sindh to substitute 'Sind' with 'Sindh' following the 18th Amendment.
metadata.summary: This Act corrects the spelling of the province's name from 'Sind' to 'Sindh' in all existing legal documents. It applies to Acts, Ordinances, rules, regulations, notifications, orders, bye-laws, and other legal instruments having force of law in the Province of Sindh. The amendment requires substituting the word 'Sind' with 'Sindh' in titles, preambles, sections, and throughout the text of these instruments.

metadata.summary: This Act amends twenty-two specific laws currently in force in the Province of Sindh. The primary mechanism involves substituting the titles 'District Officer (Revenue)' with 'Collector' and 'Executive District Officer (Revenue)' with 'Commissioner' throughout the specified Acts. Additionally, it updates references to Deputy District Officers and other revenue-related designations across various statutes governing land, irrigation, tenancy, and local administration.

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Lepers (Repeal) Act, 1989
metadata.long_title: An Act to repeal the Sind Lepers Act, 1947.
repeals: Sind Lepers Act, 1947

metadata.summary: The Sindh Lepers (Repeal) Act, 1989 is a short provincial statute enacted by the Provincial Assembly of Sindh. Its sole purpose is to repeal the earlier Sind Lepers Act, 1947. The legislation was promulgated on May 4, 1989 and commenced immediately upon enactment.

name: SINDH LETTERS OF ADMINISTRATION AND SUCCESSION CERTIFICATES ACT, 2021

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Letters of Administration and Succession Certificates Act, 2021
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for an efficacious and speedy mechanism for issuance of Letters of Administration and Succession Certificates.
metadata.territorial_extent: the whole of the Province of Sindh
metadata.commencement: on such dates as Government may, by notification in the official Gazette, appoint
metadata.one_line: Establishes a mechanism for NADRA to issue Letters of Administration and Succession Certificates in Sindh.
metadata.summary: This Act empowers the National Database and Registration Authority (NADRA) to issue Letters of Administration and Succession Certificates for movable or immovable property within Sindh. It establishes a Succession Facilitation Unit to process applications, publish public notices, and maintain an online record of issued certificates. The Act outlines the required documents for application, fees, objection procedures, and penalties for offences, aiming to provide expeditious relief to legal heirs.

name: SINDH LOCAL GOVERNMENT (AMENDMENT AND RAWANGI MAHSOOL VALIDATING) ACT, 1989

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Local Government (Amendment and Rawangi Mahsool Validating) Act, 1989
metadata.long_title: An Act to amend the Sind Local Government Ordinance, 1979 and to validate the levy of Rawangi Mahsool on certain commodities by the District Councils in the Province.
metadata.commencement: on and from the 1st day of September, 1983 (for District Council Hyderabad), the 19th day of May, 1984 (for District Council Nawabshah), and the 12th day of June, 1986 (for other District Councils)
repeals: The Sindh Local Government (Amendment and Rwangi Mahsool Validating) Ordinance, 1989
metadata.administering_body: Government of Sindh, Housing, Town Planning, Local Government and Rural Development Department
metadata.one_line: Amends the 1979 Ordinance to validate Rawangi Mahsool levies on specific commodities by District Councils in Sindh.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the Sind Local Government Ordinance, 1979 to validate the levy of Rawangi Mahsool on various commodities by District Councils in the Province. It specifically validates a government notification issued in June 1986 regarding these levies and deems past collections as valid. The Act applies to fire wood, timber, wheat, rice, cotton, rectified spirit, molasses, bagasse, sugar, and sugar products exported from urban or rural limits.

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Local Government (Amendment) Act, 2015
metadata.long_title: An Act to amend the Sindh Local Government Act, 2013.
metadata.one_line: Amends the Sindh Local Government Act, 2013 regarding council composition, delimitation, and reserved seats.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the Sindh Local Government Act, 2013 to update provisions related to Union Committees and Wards. It modifies sections concerning delimitation processes, council composition including reserved seats for women, non-Muslims, laborers, and peasants, and the powers of the Election Commission. The legislation also addresses the extension or alteration of council areas and the appointment of administrators during election gaps.

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Local Government (Amendment) Act, 1991
metadata.long_title: An Act to amend the Sind Local Government Ordinance, 1979.
repeals: The Sindh Local Government (Amendment) Ordinance, 1991
metadata.one_line: Amends the Sind Local Government Ordinance, 1979 by adding a sub-section allowing government extension of a period.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the Sind Local Government Ordinance, 1979 by inserting a new sub-section into section 58. The amendment allows the Government to extend the period mentioned in sub-section (1) via official Gazette notification, provided the extension does not exceed six months. Additionally, the Act repeals the Sindh Local Government (Amendment) Ordinance, 1991.

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Local Government (Amendment) Act, 1996
metadata.long_title: An Act to amend The Sindh Local Government Ordinance, 1979.
metadata.one_line: Amends the 1979 Ordinance to establish metropolitan and district municipal corporations in Karachi.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the Sindh Local Government Ordinance, 1979, to restructure local governance in Karachi. It establishes a Metropolitan Corporation and District Municipal Corporations, defining their respective powers, tax levies, and electoral units. The legislation also creates a unified Municipal Service for employees of these new bodies and outlines the delegation of controlling authority powers.

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Local Government (Amendment) Act, 2010
metadata.long_title: An Act further to amend the Preamble. Sindh Local Government Ordinance, 2001, in the manner hereinafter appearing;
metadata.one_line: Amends the Sindh Local Government Ordinance, 2001 regarding party-based elections and council dissolution procedures.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the Sindh Local Government Ordinance, 2001 to mandate that local government elections be held on a party basis while allowing independent candidates. It introduces provisions for the dissolution of all local governments upon the call for next elections, leading to the cessation of Nazims and Naib Nazims' offices. The Act empowers the Government to appoint civil servants as Administrators to perform functions until newly elected officials take office and sets a timeline for holding elections within 120 days.

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Local Government (Amendment) Act, 2013
metadata.long_title: An Act to amend the Sindh Local Government Act, 2013.
metadata.one_line: Amends the Sindh Local Government Act, 2013 regarding definitions, election procedures, and local body structures.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the Sindh Local Government Act, 2013 to update definitions for labourers and peasants, modify election rules for Union Committees and Councils, and adjust population thresholds for various local bodies. It also revises schedules concerning functions, town planning entries, and offences under the Act. The amendments aim to streamline governance structures and ensure representation through reserved seats.

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Local Government (Amendment) Act, 2016
metadata.long_title: An Act to amend the Sindh Local Government Act, 2013.
metadata.one_line: Amends the Sindh Local Government Act, 2013 by substituting 'show of hands' for 'secret ballot' in section 18.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the Sindh Local Government Act, 2013 to change the voting method specified in section 18. Specifically, it substitutes the words 'show of hands' for the words 'secret ballot' in sub-sections (3), (4), (6), (7), (8), and (9) and clause (c) of that section. The amendment came into force immediately upon enactment.

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Local Government (Amendment) Act, 2017
metadata.long_title: An Act to amend the Sindh Local Government Act, 2013.
metadata.one_line: Amends Section 27 of the Sindh Local Government Act, 2013 regarding Union Committee/Vice Chairman exceptions.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the Sindh Local Government Act, 2013 by modifying Section 27. The amendment inserts specific words to exclude the Chairman or Vice Chairman of a Union Committee or Union Council from certain provisions. It came into force immediately upon enactment.

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Local Government (Amendment) Act, 2021
metadata.long_title: An Act to amend the Sindh Local Government Act, 2013.
metadata.one_line: Amends the Sindh Local Government Act, 2013 by substituting 'Elections Act, 2017' for 'Representation of Peoples Act, 1976' in section 71.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the Sindh Local Government Act, 2013 to update a reference within Section 71. Specifically, it substitutes the words 'Elections Act, 2017' for the previous reference to the 'Representation of Peoples Act, 1976'. The amendment came into force immediately upon enactment.

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Local Government (Amendment) Act, 2021
metadata.long_title: An Act to amend the Sindh Local Government Act, 2013.
subjects: reserved seats for minorities and persons with disabilities
metadata.one_line: Amends the Sindh Local Government Act, 2013 to introduce Town Municipal Corporations and update reserved seat definitions.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the Sindh Local Government Act, 2013 to replace references to 'District' with 'Town' in specific contexts and introduces the concept of 'Town Municipal Corporation'. It updates the definitions for persons with disabilities and transgender persons by referencing existing empowerment acts. The legislation also modifies provisions regarding reserved seats for various groups and mandates quarterly reporting on specific social issues.

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Local Government (Fifth Amendment) Act, 2010
metadata.long_title: An Act further to amend the Preamble and section 179-A of the Sindh Local Government Ordinance, 2001.
repeals: The Sindh Local Government (Fifth Amendment) Ordinance, 2010
metadata.one_line: Amends the Sindh Local Government Ordinance, 2001 regarding elections after dissolution and repeals a 2010 Ordinance.
metadata.summary: This Act further amends the Preamble and section 179-A of the Sindh Local Government Ordinance, 2001. It specifically substitutes subsection (5) of section 179-A to mandate that the Government request the Chief Election Commissioner for holding local government elections after a dissolution. The Act also repeals the Sindh Local Government (Fifth Amendment) Ordinance, 2010 and comes into force immediately.

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Local Government (Fourth Amendment) Act, 2010
metadata.long_title: An Act further to amend the Sindh Local Government Ordinance, 2001.
repeals: The Sindh Local Government (Fourth Amendment) Ordinance, 2010
metadata.one_line: Amends the Sindh Local Government Ordinance, 2001 by extending time limits and repeals a previous amendment ordinance.
metadata.summary: This Act further amends the Sindh Local Government Ordinance, 2001. It substitutes specific time periods in section 179-A of the Ordinance, changing seventy-five days to six months and 165 days to nine months. The Act also repeals the Sindh Local Government (Fourth Amendment) Ordinance, 2010.

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Local Government (Fourth Amendment) Act, 2016
metadata.long_title: An Act to amend the Sindh Local Government Act, 2013.
metadata.one_line: Amends the Sindh Local Government Act, 2013 by reviving Section 18-A and inserting 'youth' alongside 'women'.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the Sindh Local Government Act, 2013 to revive Section 18-A, which was previously omitted. It further modifies the revived section by inserting the word 'youth' after the word 'women' wherever it appears in that section. The Act comes into force immediately upon enactment.

metadata.short_title: The Sind Local Government (Second Amendment) Act, 1987
metadata.long_title: An Act to amend the Sind Local Government Ordinance, 1979.
repeals: The Sind Local Government (Second Amendment) Ordinance, 1987
metadata.one_line: Amends the Sind Local Government Ordinance, 1979 regarding Karachi Corporation appointments and validates past actions.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the Sind Local Government Ordinance, 1979 to allow the Government to appoint an authority if the Mayor and members of the Karachi Metropolitan Corporation cease their functions. It also validates actions taken under specific sections during a transitional period in early 1987. Finally, it repeals the previous Second Amendment Ordinance from 1987.

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Local Government (Second Amendment) Act, 1989
metadata.long_title: An Act to amend the Sind Local Government Ordinance, 1979.
metadata.one_line: Amends the Sind Local Government Ordinance, 1979 regarding election eligibility and authority structure.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the Sind Local Government Ordinance, 1979 to modify provisions concerning election eligibility and the composition of the Election Authority. It restricts eligibility for certain general seats based on previous contestation outcomes and updates criteria regarding physical incapacity and moral turpitude in section 37.

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Local Government (Second Amendment) Act, 1996
metadata.long_title: An Act to amend the Sindh Local Government Ordinance, 1979.
metadata.one_line: Amends the Sindh Local Government Ordinance, 1979 to include deh panchayats and adjust council composition.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the Sindh Local Government Ordinance, 1979 to incorporate 'deh panchayats' into the local government structure alongside union councils. It substitutes various clauses to define new roles for deh panchayats, adjusts member representation including women, and modifies election procedures and penalties. The Act also grants the Government power to dissolve councils early and appoint administrators.

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Local Government (Second Amendment) Act, 2010
metadata.long_title: An Act further to amend the Preamble. Sindh Local Government Ordinance, 2001, in the manner hereinafter appearing;
repeals: The Sindh Local Government (Second Amendment) Ordinance, 2010
metadata.one_line: Amends the Sindh Local Government Ordinance, 2001 regarding Administrator appointments and repeals a previous amendment ordinance.
metadata.summary: This Act further amends the Preamble and Section 179-A of the Sindh Local Government Ordinance, 2001. It specifies criteria for appointing Administrators from Civil Servants to perform Nazim functions until newly elected officials take office. The Act also repeals the Sindh Local Government (Second Amendment) Ordinance, 2010.

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Local Government (Second Amendment) Act, 2015
metadata.long_title: An Act to amend the Sindh Local Government Act, 2013.
metadata.one_line: Amends the Sindh Local Government Act, 2013 by reviving omitted clauses and substituting provisions regarding town committees.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the Sindh Local Government Act, 2013 to revive a proviso in section 15 that was previously omitted. It also substitutes a new proviso in Schedule-I concerning Town Committees, Municipal Committees, and Municipal Corporations, ensuring their existence regardless of population size if they existed prior to or were notified after the 2001 Ordinance.

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Local Government (Second Amendment) Act, 2016
metadata.long_title: An Act to amend the Sindh Local Government Act, 2013.
metadata.one_line: Amends the Sindh Local Government Act, 2013 regarding reserved seats for women, youth, non-Muslims, and labourers.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the Sindh Local Government Act, 2013 to modify the composition of reserved seats. Specifically, it substitutes clause (b) of section 18(9) to define the extent of reserved seats for women members at 33%, youth members at 5%, non-Muslim members at 5%, and labourer or peasant members at 5%. The amendment applies to elections conducted in the manner prescribed by law.

metadata.short_title: The Sind Local Government (Third Amendment) Act, 1994
metadata.long_title: An Act to amend the Sindh Local Government Ordinance, 1979
repeals: The Sindh Local Government (Third Amendment) Ordinance, 1994
metadata.one_line: Amends the Sindh Local Government Ordinance, 1979 to delete references to Zonal Municipal Committees and transfer their assets to the Karachi Metropolitan Corporation.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the Sindh Local Government Ordinance, 1979 by deleting specific clauses and provisions related to Zonal Municipal Committees. It substitutes references to district councils in place of metropolitan corporations or zonal committees where applicable. The Act also transfers all assets and liabilities of Zonal Municipal Committees to the Karachi Metropolitan Corporation upon its commencement.

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Local Government (Third Amendment) Act, 2010
metadata.long_title: An Act further to amend the Sindh Local Government Ordinance, 2001.
repeals: The Sindh Local Government (Third Amendment) Ordinance, 2010
metadata.one_line: Amends the Sindh Local Government Ordinance, 2001 regarding council elections and repeals a 2010 Ordinance.
metadata.summary: This Act further amends the Sindh Local Government Ordinance, 2001 to include 'and Councils' in specific sections and define election timelines following dissolution. It mandates that elections be conducted within 75 days of a request by the Government or within 165 days if no new law is passed. The Act also explicitly repeals the Sindh Local Government (Third Amendment) Ordinance, 2010.

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Local Government (Third Amendment) Act, 2016
metadata.long_title: An Act to amend the Sindh Local Government Act, 2013.
metadata.one_line: Amends the Sindh Local Government Act, 2013 regarding council supervision, inspections, and public garden maintenance.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the Sindh Local Government Act, 2013 to strengthen government supervision over local councils. It mandates that councils be inspected at least once a financial year by the Government or designated officers. Additionally, it updates provisions regarding the laying out and maintenance of public gardens through various partnerships.

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Local Government Act, 2013
metadata.long_title: An Act to rationalise local government institutions and provide for their constitution, powers, functions, finance, administration and other matters connected therewith.
repeals: The Sindh Local Government Act, 1979
metadata.one_line: This Act establishes the framework for local government councils in Sindh, defining their constitution, powers, elections, and finances.
metadata.summary: The Sindh Local Government Act, 2013 provides a comprehensive legal framework for local government institutions within the province of Sindh. It details the constitution, composition, and functions of various councils, including ward committees, municipalities, and corporations. The Act also establishes mechanisms for local taxation, financial management through the Provincial Finance Commission, and outlines procedures for elections and the conduct of office bearers.

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Madressatul Islam University Act, 2011
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the establishment of Sindh Madressatul Islam University at Karachi.
repeals: notifications and legislative instruments constituting the Sindh Madressatul Islam Karachi
metadata.one_line: Establishes Sindh Madressatul Islam University at Karachi and defines its structure, authorities, and functions.
metadata.summary: This Act establishes the Sindh Madressatul Islam University at Karachi and outlines its constitution, officers, and governing bodies. It defines various academic and administrative terms, sets up committees for finance, affiliation, and discipline, and provides for the university fund and audit procedures. The Act also repeals previous notifications and legislative instruments related to the institution.

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Mass Transit Authority Act, 2014
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the establishment of an Authority known as the Sindh Mass Transit Authority in the Province of Sindh.
metadata.territorial_extent: the whole of the Province of Sindh
establishes: Board of the Sindh Mass Transit Authority
metadata.one_line: Establishes the Sindh Mass Transit Authority to regulate and operate mass transit systems in Sindh.
metadata.summary: This Act establishes the Sindh Mass Transit Authority (SMTA) within the Province of Sindh. The Authority is empowered to plan, coordinate, construct, develop, operate, maintain, monitor, and regulate various forms of mass transit systems. It provides for the constitution of a Board, appointment of officers, financial management, and mechanisms for grievance redressal and enforcement.

metadata.short_title: The Sind Medical Colleges Act, 1987
metadata.long_title: An Act to regulate admissions in the medical colleges in Sind and other ancillary matters including the conduct and discipline of the students of such colleges.
repeals: Sind Ordinance II of 1987
metadata.one_line: Regulates admissions and student discipline in medical colleges in Sindh.
metadata.summary: This Act regulates admissions into medical colleges in Sindh and addresses ancillary matters such as student conduct and discipline. It empowers the Government to make rules regarding seat allocation, application forms, admission conditions, migration procedures, and hostel management. The Act also defines key terms including 'medical college' (which includes dental colleges) and grants the Government authority to institute halls of residence.

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Mental Health (Amendment) Act, 2015
metadata.long_title: An Act to amend the Sindh Mental Health Act, 2013.
metadata.one_line: Amends the Sindh Mental Health Act, 2013 regarding suicide assessment for accused of blasphemy.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the Sindh Mental Health Act, 2013 to include specific provisions regarding suicide attempts. It mandates that a person attempting suicide, including an accused of blasphemy, must be assessed by an approved physiatrist. If found to suffer from a mental disorder, the individual shall be treated appropriately under the provisions of the Act.

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Mental Health Act, 2013
metadata.long_title: An Act to regulate the matters relating to the mentally disordered persons with respect to their care, treatment, management of their property and other related matters.
metadata.territorial_extent: whole of the Province of Sindh
metadata.commencement: at once and deemed to have taken effect on and from 7th August, 2013
repeals: Mental Health Ordinance, 2001
metadata.one_line: Regulates care, treatment, and property management for mentally disordered persons in Sindh.
metadata.summary: This Act regulates matters relating to the care, treatment, and management of property for mentally disordered persons within the Province of Sindh. It establishes the Sindh Mental Health Authority and a Board of Visitors to oversee psychiatric facilities in both public and private sectors. The legislation outlines procedures for admission, discharge, guardianship, and includes provisions for human rights protection and offences related to false statements.

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Metalliferous Mines Act, 2021
metadata.long_title: An Act to consolidate the law relating to the regulation and inspection of Metalliferous other than coal mines and matters ancillary thereto in the Province of Sindh.
metadata.territorial_extent: the whole of the Province of Sindh
repeals: Mines Act, 1923 (Act IV of 1923)
metadata.administering_body: Mines and Mineral Development Department, Government of Sindh
metadata.one_line: Consolidates laws regulating metalliferous mines (excluding coal) in Sindh, establishing a Board and repealing the 1923 Act.
metadata.summary: This Act consolidates legislation regarding the regulation and inspection of metalliferous mines in the Province of Sindh, excluding coal mines. It establishes the Metalliferous Mining Board and defines key terms related to mine operations, safety, and management. The Act applies to all metalliferous mines within Sindh and repeals the relevant provisions of the Mines Act, 1923.

name: SINDH MINES AND MINERALS GOVERNANCE ACT, 2021

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Mines and Minerals Governance Act, 2021
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for an effective regulation of minerals, mines, mining and mineral dressing in the Province of Sindh.
metadata.territorial_extent: whole of the Province of Sindh
repeals: The Regulation of Mines and Oil field and Mineral Development (Government Control) Act, 1948 (XXIV of 1948)
The Sindh Prohibition of Taking Minerals including Reti (Sand) and Bajri from any Land Act, 2003
metadata.administering_body: Mines & Mineral Development Department of Government of Sindh
metadata.one_line: This Act regulates minerals, mines, mining and mineral dressing in Sindh to create a transparent business environment.
metadata.summary: The Sindh Mines and Minerals Governance Act, 2021 provides for the effective regulation of minerals, mines, mining, and mineral dressing within the Province of Sindh. It aims to establish a transparent, competitive, and enabling business environment for investment in the mining sector while providing institutional oversight. The Act regulates grants of mineral titles, permits, and dressing operations, defines key terms related to exploration and licensing, and establishes authorities such as the Licensing Authority and Appellate Authority.

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Minimum Wages (Amendment) Act, 2018
metadata.long_title: An Act to amend the Sindh Minimum Wages Act, 2015.
metadata.one_line: Amends the Sindh Minimum Wages Act, 2015 by substituting specific clauses regarding wage board composition.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the Sindh Minimum Wages Act, 2015 to alter the composition of wage boards. Specifically, it substitutes the word 'one' with 'four' in certain clauses and adds an independent coopted member after clause (e). The legislation was passed by the Provincial Assembly of Sindh and assented to by the Governor on May 12, 2018, coming into force immediately upon publication.

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Minimum Wages Act, 2015
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the regulation of minimum rates of wages and various allowances for different categories of workers employed in certain industrial and commercial undertakings and establishments.
metadata.territorial_extent: the whole of the Province of Sindh
repeals: Minimum Wages Ordinance, 1961 (Ordinance No.XXXIX of 1961)
the Minimum Wages for Unskilled Workers Ordinance, 1969 (W.P.Ord.No.XX of 1969)
the Employees Cost of Living Allowance (Relief) Act, 1973
The Sindh Employees Special Relief Allowance 1986
the Sindh (Payment of Dearness Allowance to Certain Employees) Act, 1991 (Sindh Act No.II of 1991)
metadata.max_penalty: fine which may extend to seventy five thousand rupees but shall not be less than fifty thousand rupees
metadata.one_line: Regulates minimum wages and allowances for workers in industrial and commercial establishments across Sindh.
metadata.summary: This Act regulates minimum rates of wages and various allowances for different categories of workers employed in specific industrial and commercial undertakings within Sindh. It establishes a Minimum Wages Board to recommend and declare these rates, which include basic pay, cost of living allowance, dearness allowance, and adhoc relief. The legislation applies to all industrial and commercial establishments in the province and repeals previous enactments related to minimum wages.

name: SINDH MINISTERS (SALARIES, ALLOWANCES AND PRIVILEGES) (AMENDMENT) ACT, 1991

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Ministers (Salaries, Allowances and Privileges) (Amendment) Act, 1991
metadata.long_title: An Act to amend the Sind Ministers (Salaries, Allowances and Privileges) Act, 1975.
amends: The Sind Ministers (Salaries, Allowances and Privileges) Act, 1975
metadata.one_line: Amends the 1975 Act regarding ministerial salaries, allowances, and travel expense reimbursements.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the Sind Ministers (Salaries, Allowances and Privileges) Act, 1975 to adjust financial provisions for provincial ministers. It substitutes a specific grant limit in section 6-A and updates daily allowance figures in section 10. Additionally, it introduces a new section allowing reimbursement of actual single room rent for ministers staying outside the province on duty.

name: SINDH MINISTERS (SALARIES, ALLOWANCES AND PRIVILEGES) (AMENDMENT) ACT, 2013

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Ministers (Salaries, Allowances and Privileges) (Amendment) Act, 2013
metadata.long_title: An Act to amend the Sind Ministers (Salaries, Allowances and Privileges) Act,1975.
amends: The Sind Ministers (Salaries, Allowances and Privileges) Act, 1975
metadata.one_line: Amends the 1975 Act to grant lifetime perks and privileges to Chief Ministers serving at least four years.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the Sind Ministers (Salaries, Allowances and Privileges) Act, 1975. It adds a new section granting specific perks and privileges to a person who has served as Chief Minister for not less than four years. The benefits include a percentage of salary, private staff, lifetime police security, communication facilities, and temporary bulletproof car usage.

name: SINDH MINISTERS (SALARIES, ALLOWANCES AND PRIVILEGES) (AMENDMENT) ACT, 1996

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Ministers (Salaries, Allowances and Privileges) (Amendment) Act, 1996
metadata.long_title: An Act further to amend the Sindh Ministers (Salaries, Allowances and Privileges) Act, 1975.
amends: The Sindh Ministers (Salaries, Allowances and Privileges) Act, 1975
repeals: The Sindh Ministers (Salaries, Allowances and Privileges) (Amendment) Ordinance, 1996
metadata.one_line: Amends the 1975 Act to exempt the Chief Minister from customs/sales tax on a specific car and repeals the 1996 Ordinance.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the Sindh Ministers (Salaries, Allowances and Privileges) Act, 1975 by inserting a new section regarding tax exemptions for the Chief Minister. Specifically, it exempts the Chief Minister from custom duties or sales tax on one Mercedes Benz 280 SEL or equivalent car imported or purchased out of bond for personal use upon appointment or during tenure. The Act also re-numbers the existing Section 8-A to 8-AA and repeals the corresponding Amendment Ordinance of 1996.

name: SINDH MINISTERS (SALARIES, ALLOWANCES AND PRIVILEGES) (AMENDMENT) ACT, 2008

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Ministers (Salaries, Allowances and Privileges) (Amendment) Act, 2008
metadata.long_title: An Act to amend the Sind Ministers (Salaries, Allowances and Privileges) Act, 1975.
metadata.commencement: at once and shall be deemed to have taken effect on and from 1st July, 2011
amends: The Sind Ministers (Salaries, Allowances and Privileges) Act, 1975
metadata.one_line: Amends the 1975 Act by substituting a salary figure in section 7(2) and applies from July 1, 2011.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the Sind Ministers (Salaries, Allowances and Privileges) Act, 1975. It specifically substitutes the words 'fifty four thousand six hundred' for 'thirty nine thousand' in section 7, subsection (2) of the 1975 Act. The amendment came into force immediately but is deemed to have taken effect from July 1, 2011.

name: SINDH MINISTERS (SALARIES, ALLOWANCES AND PRIVILEGES) (SECOND AMENDMENT) ACT, 1996

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Ministers (Salaries, Allowances and Privileges) (Second Amendment) Act, 1996
metadata.long_title: An Act further to amend the Sind Ministers (Salaries, Allowances And Privileges) Act, 1975 in the manner hereinafter appearing
amends: The Sind Ministers (Salaries, Allowances and Privileges) Act, 1975
metadata.one_line: Amends the 1975 Act to change the authorized car specification for Sindh Ministers.
metadata.summary: This Act further amends the Sind Ministers (Salaries, Allowances and Privileges) Act, 1975. It specifically substitutes the description of an authorized motor car in section 8-A of the 1975 Act. The change replaces 'Car Marcedes Benz 280 SEL or equivalent' with 'motor car with engine capacity upto 3200 CC'. The Act came into force immediately upon enactment.

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Motion Pictures Act, 2011
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide of the censorship of films and the regulation of exhibition of films by means of cinematographs.
metadata.territorial_extent: the whole of the Province of Sindh
repeals: The Motion Pictures Ordinance, 1979
The Sindh Motion Pictures Ordinance, 2011
metadata.one_line: This Act establishes a Board to censor films and regulate their exhibition in Sindh.
metadata.summary: The Sindh Motion Pictures Act, 2011 provides for the censorship of films and the regulation of their exhibition by means of cinematographs within the Province of Sindh. It establishes a Board consisting of a Chairman and members appointed by the Government to examine and certify films for public exhibition. The Act outlines procedures for certification, including principles of guidance, appeals to the Government, and penalties for unauthorized exhibition or violation of licensing conditions.

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Motor Vehicles Taxation (Amendment) Act, 2021
metadata.long_title: An Act to amend the Sindh Motor Vehicles Taxation Act, 1958.
amends: The Sindh Motor Vehicles Taxation Act, 1958
metadata.one_line: Amends the Sindh Motor Vehicles Taxation Act, 1958 to update engine power classifications and tax rates.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the Sindh Motor Vehicles Taxation Act, 1958 by updating engine power classifications in its Schedule. It introduces specific kilowatt equivalents for various cubic centimeter ranges and adjusts tax rates for commercial vehicles after ten and fifteen years of registration. The legislation also provides a formula for converting between horsepower, watts, and cubic centimeters.

name: SINDH NATIONAL INSTITUTE OF CARDIOVASCULAR DISEASES (SINDH ADMINISTRATION) ACT 2014 Act, 2015

metadata.short_title: The National Institute of Cardiovascular Diseases (Sindh Administration) Act, 2014
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the proper administration of the affairs of the National Institute of Cardiovascular Diseases Sindh, Karachi.
metadata.territorial_extent: the whole of the Province of Sindh
metadata.one_line: This Act provides for the proper administration of the National Institute of Cardiovascular Diseases in Sindh.
metadata.summary: This Act establishes the National Institute of Cardiovascular Diseases as a body corporate with perpetual succession. It vests the powers of the Board of Trustees in a Governing Body comprising government officials, medical professionals, and social workers. The Institute is authorized to undertake treatment, research, training, and international cooperation regarding cardiovascular diseases.

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Newborn Screening Act, 2013
metadata.long_title: An Act to establish and integrate a sustainable newborn screening system within the public health delivery system.
metadata.one_line: Establishes a sustainable newborn screening system in Sindh to detect heritable conditions and hearing impairments.
metadata.summary: This Act establishes an integrated newborn screening system within the public health delivery system of Sindh. It mandates protocols for screening all newborns for heritable conditions and hearing impairment, typically within the first three days of life. The legislation creates an Advisory Committee to oversee the program and defines key terms such as 'health institution' and 'heritable condition'. It also outlines procedures for parental education, follow-up care, and the management of identified cases.

name: SINDH PARLIAMENTARY SECRETARIES (SALARIES, ALLOWANCES AND PRIVILEGES) (AMENDMENT) ACT, 1996

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Parliamentary Secretaries (Salaries, Allowances and Privileges) (Amendment) Act, 1996
metadata.long_title: An Act to amend the Sind Parliamentary Secretaries (Salaries, Allowances and Privileges) Act, 1974
amends: The Sind Parliamentary Secretaries (Salaries, Allowances and Privileges) Act, 1974
metadata.one_line: Amends the 1974 Act to update salaries, allowances, privileges, and medical facilities for Parliamentary Secretaries in Sindh.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the Sind Parliamentary Secretaries (Salaries, Allowances and Privileges) Act, 1974 to revise financial benefits for Parliamentary Secretaries. It updates salary amounts, orderly allowances, official car specifications, telephone facilities, and medical reimbursement scales effective from September 1, 1995. The Act also substitutes references to Assembly members with officers of BS-21 scale in specific sections and deletes the original section 5.

name: SINDH PARLIAMENTARY SECRETARIES (SALARIES, ALLOWANCES, AND PRIVILEGES) (AMENDMENT) ACT, 2021

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Parliamentary Secretaries (Salaries, Allowances and Privileges) (Amendment) Act, 2021
metadata.long_title: An Act to amend the Sindh Parliamentary Secretaries (Salaries, Allowances and Privileges) Act, 1974.
metadata.commencement: at once and deemed to have taken effect on and from 13th August, 2018
amends: The Sindh Parliamentary Secretaries (Salaries, Allowances and Privileges) Act, 1974
metadata.administering_body: Secretariat of Provincial Assembly of Sindh / Law Department, Government of Sindh
metadata.one_line: Amends the 1974 Act regarding salaries, allowances, and travel privileges for Sindh Parliamentary Secretaries.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the Sindh Parliamentary Secretaries (Salaries, Allowances and Privileges) Act, 1974 to update financial benefits for Parliamentary Secretaries. It substitutes existing sections to increase special allowances, house rent, and airfare rates while adding new provisions for sumptuary allowances and specific travel entitlements by air, train, road, or abroad.

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Payment of Wages Act, 2015
metadata.long_title: An Act to regulate the payment of wages to certain classes of persons employed in factories, Industrial and commercial establishments in the Province of Sindh; and to provide for matters ancillary thereto.
metadata.territorial_extent: the whole of the Province of Sindh
repeals: Payment of Wages Act, 1936
metadata.max_penalty: fine which may extend to twenty thousand rupees
metadata.one_line: Regulates wage payment, deductions, and penalties for factories and commercial establishments in Sindh.
metadata.summary: This Act regulates the payment of wages to workers in factories, industrial, and commercial establishments within the Province of Sindh. It defines key terms such as 'Employer', 'wages', and 'commercial establishment' and sets rules regarding wage periods, time of payment, and permissible deductions. The legislation also establishes an Authority and Inspectors to oversee compliance, imposes penalties for offences, and repeals the previous Payment of Wages Act, 1936 in Sindh.

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Peoples Local Government Act, 2012
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for and regulate the affairs of the local councils in the Province of Sindh
metadata.one_line: An Act to provide for and regulate the affairs of local councils in the Province of Sindh.
metadata.summary: This Act establishes a comprehensive framework for local governance in Sindh, creating Metropolitan Corporations, District Councils, Taluka Municipal Administrations, Town Municipal Administrations, Union Administrations, Village Councils, and Neighbourhood Councils. It defines their composition, functions, powers, financial structures, and administrative procedures while ensuring they work under the overall superintendence of the Provincial Government. The legislation also outlines mechanisms for dispute resolution through Musalihat Anjuman and regulates local finance, including budget preparation and tax collection.

name: SINDH PREVENTION AND CONTROL OF THALASSEMIA ACT, 2013

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Prevention and Control of Thalassemia Act, 2013
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for prevention and control of thalassemia.
metadata.territorial_extent: the whole of the Province of Sindh
metadata.commencement: at once and shall be deemed to have taken effect on and from 8th August, 2013
metadata.max_penalty: rupees one hundred thousand or punishment under section 337E of the Pakistan Penal Code
metadata.one_line: This Act establishes a framework for preventing and controlling thalassemia in Sindh through screening, counselling, and penalties.
metadata.summary: The Sindh Prevention and Control of Thalassemia Act, 2013 aims to prevent and control thalassemia within the Province of Sindh. It mandates pre-marital blood screening for relatives of patients, requires health care facilities to provide genetic counselling and diagnostic services, and establishes a dedicated foundation to manage funds and promote treatment centers. The Act also imposes penalties on facilities that fail to conduct necessary screenings or obtain proper consent for testing.

name: SINDH PREVENTION OF DEFACEMENT OF PROPERTY ACT 2013

metadata.short_title: The Prevention of Defacement of Property Act, 2013
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for prevention of defacement of property and prohibition of expression of matters on walls in the Province of Sindh.
metadata.territorial_extent: the whole of the Province of Sindh
metadata.commencement: at once and deemed to have taken effect on 25th July, 2014
metadata.max_penalty: imprisonment up to six months or fine up to five thousand rupees or both
metadata.one_line: This Act prevents property defacement and prohibits unauthorized writing or material on walls in Sindh.
metadata.summary: The Prevention of Defacement of Property Act, 2013 aims to prevent the impairment of property appearance and prohibit unauthorized expressions on walls in Sindh. It defines specific acts like writing or affixing material without permission as defacement and prescribes penalties including imprisonment and fines for offenders. The Act also mandates the creation of an Anti-Property Defacement Task Force within fifteen days to assess the issue and propose enforcement programs, while requiring local councils to remove existing defacement within thirty days.

name: SINDH PRIVATE EDUCATIONAL INSTITUTIONS (REGULATION AND CONTROL) (AMENDMENT) ACT, 2003

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Private Educational Institutions (Regulation and Control) (Amendment) Act, 2003
metadata.long_title: An Act to amend the Sindh Private Educational Institutions (Regulation and Control) Ordinance, 2001.
amends: The Sindh Private Educational Institutions (Regulation and Control) Ordinance, 2001
metadata.administering_body: Government of Sindh / Secretary Education and Literacy Department
metadata.one_line: Amends the 2001 Ordinance to update registration authority powers, infrastructure standards, and curriculum requirements for private schools.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the Sindh Private Educational Institutions (Regulation and Control) Ordinance, 2001 to redefine the Registering Authority as an officer notified by the Government. It mandates specific infrastructure standards, requires fee structures to have prior government approval, and ensures curriculum parity with government schools while teaching Sindhi language. The amendment also expands dispute settlement procedures and clarifies the roles of the Secretary Education and Literacy Department in monitoring institutions.

name: SINDH PRIVATE TEACHERS TRAINING INSTITUTIONS (REGISTRATION AND CONTROL) ACT, 1994

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Private Teachers' Training Institutions (Registration and Control) Act, 1994
metadata.long_title: An Act to regulate the functioning of private teachers' training institutions in the Province of Sindh.
metadata.commencement: at once for section 1; on such date as may be notified by Government for remaining provisions
repeals: The Sindh Private Teacher's Training Institutions (Registration and Control) Ordinance, 1994
establishes: Registration Authority (Director, Bureau of Curriculum and Extension Wing, Sindh Jamshoro)
metadata.max_penalty: imprisonment up to one year or fine up to fifty thousand rupees or both
metadata.one_line: This Act regulates private teachers' training institutions in Sindh through a registration and control system.
metadata.summary: The Act establishes a regulatory framework for private teachers' training institutions within the Province of Sindh. It mandates that no institution be established or continued without a certificate granted by the Registration Authority after an enquiry process. The legislation outlines procedures for application, suspension or cancellation of certificates, appeals to the Government, and penalties for operating without registration.

name: SINDH PROHIBITION OF CORPORAL PUNISHMENT ACT, 2016

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Prohibition of Corporal Punishment Act, 2016
metadata.long_title: An Act to make provisions of prohibition of corporal punishment against children.
metadata.max_penalty: punishments prescribed in the Pakistan Penal Code, 1860 and other respective laws; minor penalties include censure, withholding promotion/increment, stoppage from promotion, recovery of pecuniary loss; major penalties include demotion, compulsory retirement, removal from service, and dismissal from service.
metadata.one_line: This Act prohibits all forms of corporal punishment against children in Sindh educational, care, and workplace settings.
metadata.summary: The Sindh Prohibition of Corporal Punishment Act, 2016 establishes a legal framework to protect children from physical and humiliating treatment. It applies to all types of institutions including schools, orphanages, foster care centers, and workplaces within the province of Sindh. The Act defines corporal punishment broadly to include physical force causing pain or discomfort, as well as cruel non-physical forms like humiliation. Violations attract penalties under the Pakistan Penal Code and specific administrative sanctions ranging from censure to dismissal from service.

name: SINDH PROHIBITION OF EMPLOYMENT OF CHILDREN ACT, 2017

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Prohibition of Employment of Children Act, 2017
metadata.long_title: An Act to prohibit the employment of children and to regulate employment of adolescents in certain occupations and work.
metadata.territorial_extent: the whole of the Province of Sindh
repeals: The Employment of Children Act, 1991
establishes: Sindh Coordination Committee on Child Labour
metadata.one_line: Prohibits child employment and regulates adolescent work in hazardous occupations within Sindh.
metadata.summary: This Act prohibits the employment of children under fourteen years of age in any establishment. It also regulates the employment of adolescents (aged fourteen to seventeen) by restricting them from hazardous work listed in the Schedule and limiting their working hours to ensure rest periods. The legislation establishes a Sindh Coordination Committee on Child Labour to advise on legislative and administrative measures for eradicating child labour. Additionally, it repeals the previous Employment of Children Act, 1991, as it applies to the Province of Sindh.

name: SINDH PROHIBITION ON MANUFACTURE, SALE AND USE OF POLYTHENE BAGS ACT, 2006

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Prohibition on Manufacture, Sale and use of Polythene Bags Act, 2006
metadata.long_title: An act to prohibit, manufacture, sale and use of black polythene bangs in including polythene bags below thirty micron thickness in the Province.
metadata.max_penalty: Imprisonment for six months or fine of one lac rupees or both
metadata.one_line: This Act prohibits the manufacture, sale, and use of black polythene bags under thirty microns in Sindh.
metadata.summary: The Sindh Prohibition on Manufacture, Sale and Use of Polythene Bags Act, 2006 was enacted to prohibit the manufacture, sale, and use of black polythene bags with a thickness below thirty microns in the Province. It defines key terms such as 'factory', 'person', and 'polythene bags' and imposes strict penalties for contravention, including imprisonment and fines. The Act empowers the Director General of the Provincial Environmental Agency to initiate legal proceedings against offenders.

name: SINDH PROTECTION AND PROMOTION OF BREAST-FEEDING AND CHILD NUTRITION ACT, 2013

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Protection and Promotion of Breast-Feeding and Child Nutrition Act, 2013
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for protection of breast-feeding and nutrition for infants and young children.
metadata.territorial_extent: the whole of the Province of Sindh
metadata.max_penalty: imprisonment for a term which may extend to two years, or with fine which shall not be less than fifty thousand rupees or more than five hundred thousand rupees, or both
metadata.one_line: This Act protects breast-feeding and child nutrition in Sindh by regulating designated products and establishing an Infant Feeding Board.
metadata.summary: The Sindh Protection and Promotion of Breast-Feeding and Child Nutrition Act, 2013 aims to ensure safe and adequate nutrition for infants by promoting breast-feeding. It regulates the marketing of designated products like milk substitutes and feeding bottles within the Province of Sindh. The Act establishes an Infant Feeding Board to oversee implementation, prohibits certain advertising practices, and prescribes penalties for contraventions.

name: SINDH PROTECTION OF COMMUNAL PROPERTIES OF MINORITIES ACT, 2013

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Protection of Communal Properties of Minorities Act, 2013
metadata.long_title: An Act to protect the properties of minority communities of the Province of Sindh meant for their communal use.
metadata.territorial_extent: the whole of Province of Sindh
metadata.max_penalty: Imprisonment up to seven years and fine not less than one hundred thousand rupees
key_definitions: Property (places of worship, monasteries, seminaries, vicarages, dharamsalas, goashalas, burial places, community centers, social welfare, education, health and recreational Institutions meant for communal use)
metadata.one_line: This Act protects minority communal properties in Sindh by banning their sale or transfer without a No Objection Certificate.
metadata.summary: The Sindh Protection of Communal Properties of Minorities Act, 2013 aims to safeguard properties belonging to minority communities meant for their communal use within the Province of Sindh. It prohibits the buying, selling, or transferring of such properties without obtaining a No Objection Certificate (NOC) from the Provincial Government, which may be issued based on the recommendation of the Provincial Commission for Minorities. The Act explicitly excludes evacuee trust properties and housing schemes approved by the government from its provisions. Violations are punishable by imprisonment up to seven years and a fine of at least one hundred thousand rupees, rendering any unauthorized transaction legally void.

name: SINDH PROTECTION OF HUMAN RIGHTS ACT, 2011

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Protection of Human Rights Act, 2011
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for protection of the human rights in the Province of Sindh.
metadata.commencement: on such date as Government may, by notification in the official gazette, specify
metadata.one_line: Establishes the Sindh Human Rights Commission to protect human rights within the Province of Sindh.
metadata.summary: This Act establishes the Sindh Human Rights Commission to protect human rights in the Province of Sindh. The Commission consists of a Chairperson, members with judicial or human rights experience, and representatives from the Provincial Assembly. It outlines the Commission's powers, functions, meeting procedures, funding mechanisms, and provides immunity for its officers acting in good faith.

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Province Pension Fund (Amendment) Act, 2006
metadata.long_title: An Act to amend the Sindh Province Pension Fund Ordinance, 2002.
metadata.commencement: at once and deemed to have taken effect on 10th April, 2005
metadata.administering_body: Board consisting of Minister Finance as Chairman and other members including Secretary Finance
metadata.one_line: Amends the Sindh Province Pension Fund Ordinance, 2002 regarding fund management, board composition, and insurance contracts.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the Sindh Province Pension Fund Ordinance, 2002 to allow investment returns in calculations and permit the Board to enter into contracts with insurance companies for pensionary benefits. It also modifies the composition of the Board, substituting specific members and clarifying the roles of the Secretary Finance and Chief Secretary. Additionally, the Act removes remuneration eligibility for Board members and specifies the signature requirements for fund withdrawals.

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Provincial Assembly (Members) Privileges (Amendment) Act, 2013
metadata.long_title: An Act to amend the Sindh Provincial Assembly (Members) Privileges Act, 1975.
amends: The Sindh Provincial Assembly (Members) Privileges Act, 1975
metadata.one_line: Amends the 1975 Act to grant former members and spouses specific facilities like guest house access and lifetime passes.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the Sindh Provincial Assembly (Members) Privileges Act, 1975 to align member privileges with those of Senate and National Assembly members. It inserts a new section granting former members and their deceased spouses entitlements including access to government guest houses, lifetime entry passes for the Assembly Secretariat, VIP lounge usage, official passports, and weapons licenses. The provisions apply to the Province of Sindh and come into force immediately upon enactment.

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Public Finance Administration Act, 2020
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for efficient and transparent management of the Provincial Consolidated Fund and Public Account of the Province, and proper accountability of all transactions in relation thereto.
metadata.territorial_extent: the whole of the Province of Sindh
repeals: The Sindh Financial Management and Accountability Act, 2011 (No. XVIII of 2011)
metadata.one_line: This Act ensures efficient management of the Provincial Consolidated Fund and Public Account in Sindh.
metadata.summary: The Sindh Public Finance Administration Act, 2020 establishes a framework for the efficient and transparent management of the Provincial Consolidated Fund and Public Account. It defines key financial terms such as appropriation, budget grants, and charged expenditure to ensure proper accountability of all transactions. The Act applies to the whole of the Province of Sindh and repeals the previous Sindh Financial Management and Accountability Act, 2011.

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Public Private Partnership (Amendment) Act, 2014
metadata.long_title: An Act to amend the Sindh Public Private Partnership Act, 2010.
metadata.one_line: Amends the Sindh Public Private Partnership Act, 2010 to expand definitions and include new sectors.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the Sindh Public Private Partnership Act, 2010 to update definitions regarding agreements and services. It expands the scope of eligible partners to include civil society organizations and allows for voluntary contributions. Additionally, it adds health, education, and social welfare sectors to the list of permissible public private partnership modes.

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Public Private Partnership (Amendment) Act, 2011
metadata.long_title: An Act to amend the Sindh Public Private Partnership Act, 2010.
amends: The Sindh Public Private Partnership Act, 2010
metadata.one_line: Amends the Sindh Public Private Partnership Act, 2010 regarding ministerial composition and assembly nominations.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the Sindh Public Private Partnership Act, 2010 to update the composition of a specific committee. It substitutes clauses related to the Minister for Finance, Minister for Law and Parliamentary Affairs, and Minister for Planning and Development. Additionally, it modifies the clause regarding members from the Provincial Assembly of Sindh nominated by the Chief Minister.

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Public Procurement (Amendment) Act, 2013
metadata.long_title: An Act to amend the Sindh Public Procurement Act,2009.
metadata.one_line: Amends the Sindh Public Procurement Act, 2009 to grant government power for national interest exemptions.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the Sindh Public Procurement Act, 2009 to empower the Government to grant exemptions from procurement regulations. These exemptions apply to objects or classes of objects deemed necessary in the national interest. The Authority is also empowered to recommend such exemptions to the Government for recording reasons in writing.

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Public Procurement (Amendment) Act, 2021
metadata.long_title: An Act to amend the Sindh Public Procurement Act, 2009.
metadata.one_line: Amends the Sindh Public Procurement Act, 2009 by omitting a specific clause in Section 6.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the Sindh Public Procurement Act, 2009. It was passed by the Provincial Assembly of Sindh and assented to by the Governor on August 15, 2022. The amendment specifically omits clause (xvii) from subsection (2) of Section 6 of the original Act. The legislation comes into force immediately upon enactment.

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Public Procurement (Amendment) Act, 2025
metadata.long_title: An Act to amend the Sindh Public Procurement Act, 2009.
metadata.one_line: Amends the Sindh Public Procurement Act, 2009 regarding public assets and disposal methods.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the Sindh Public Procurement Act, 2009 to include the disposal of public assets within its scope. It defines 'disposal' to include auction, rental, lease, donation, destruction, and recycling of public assets. Additionally, it inserts a new definition for 'public asset' as all goods owned by a procuring agency and updates section 6 to substitute 'Science & Information Technology'.

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Public Procurement Act, 2009
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for establishment of Public Procurement Regulatory Authority for regulating public procurement of goods, services and works in the public sector.
metadata.commencement: at once and shall be deemed to have taken effect on and from 22nd August, 2007
repeals: Public Procurement Rules, 2004
metadata.one_line: Establishes the Public Procurement Regulatory Authority to regulate public procurement of goods, services, and works in Sindh.
metadata.summary: This Act establishes the Sindh Public Procurement Regulatory Authority as a body corporate to regulate public procurement. It defines key terms such as goods, services, and works, and outlines the financial provisions including the establishment of a fund. The Act also empowers the Government to issue directives and grants exemptions, while repealing previous rules from 2004.

name: SINDH PUBLIC PROPERTY (REMOVAL OF ENCROACHMENT) (AMENDMENT) ACT, 2008

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Public Property (Removal of Encroachment) (Amendment) Act, 2008
metadata.long_title: An Act to further amend the Sind Public Property (Removal of Encroachment) Act, 1975.
amends: The Sind Public Property (Removal of Encroachment) Act, 1975
metadata.one_line: Amends the 1975 Act to update definitions, time limits, penalties, and establish an Anti-Encroachment Force.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the Sind Public Property (Removal of Encroachment) Act, 1975 to update various provisions. It substitutes specific terms like 'Council' and reduces certain time limits from seven or three days to two or three days respectively. The Act also increases penalties for encroachment and establishes a new Anti-Encroachment Force to enforce the law.

name: SINDH PUBLIC PROPERTY (REMOVAL OF ENCROACHMENT) (AMENDMENT) ACT, 2010

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Public Property (Removal of Encroachment) (Amendment) Act, 2011
metadata.long_title: An Act to amend the Sindh Public Property (Removal of Encroachment) Act, 2010.
amends: Sindh Public Property (Removal of Encroachment) Act, 2010
repeals: The Sindh Public Property (Removal of Encroachment) (Amendment) Ordinance, 2010
metadata.one_line: Amends the Sindh Public Property (Removal of Encroachment) Act, 2010 and repeals a related Ordinance.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the Sindh Public Property (Removal of Encroachment) Act, 2010 to add a definition for 'Special Court' and specify its composition. It substitutes section 26 of the amended Act to define the Special Court as consisting of a retired Sessions Judge appointed by the Government. Additionally, the Act repeals the Sindh Public Property (Removal of Encroachment) (Amendment) Ordinance, 2010.

name: SINDH PUBLIC PROPERTY (REMOVAL OF ENCROACHMENT) (SECOND AMENDMENT) ACT, 2011

amends: The Sindh Public Property (Removal of Encroachment) Act, 2010
repeals: The Sindh Public Property (Removal of Encroachment) (Second Amendment) Ordinance, 2011
