metadata.summary: This Act further amends the Sindh Public Property (Removal of Encroachment) Act, 2010 to update provisions on tribunals and special courts. It substitutes sections detailing the composition, appointment, tenure, and removal of Presiding Officers for Tribunals and Special Courts. Additionally, it omits a subsection from section 23 of the parent Act and repeals the corresponding Second Amendment Ordinance of 2011.

name: SINDH PUBLIC PROPERTY (REMOVAL OF ENCROACHMENT) ACT, 1975

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Public Property (Removal of Encroachment) Act, 1975
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide measure for removal of encroachment from public property.
repeals: The West Pakistan Government Lands and Buildings (Recovery of Possession) Ordinance, 1966
The West Pakistan Autonomous Bodies Immovable Property (Ejectment of Unauthorized Occupants) Ordinance, 1965
metadata.max_penalty: imprisonment up to six months or fine up to three thousand rupees or both
metadata.one_line: This Act provides measures for the removal of encroachment from public property in Sindh.
metadata.summary: The Sindh Public Property (Removal of Encroachment) Act, 1975 establishes a legal framework to remove unauthorized structures and occupants from public property. It defines key terms such as 'encroachment' and 'public property', authorizes the government to order removal within three days, and provides for eviction by force if orders are not followed. The Act creates a Tribunal with exclusive jurisdiction to adjudicate disputes regarding the status of property or lease determination, while also outlining penalties for offenders and procedures for recovering demolition costs and rent arrears.

name: SINDH PUBLIC PROPERTY (REMOVAL OF ENCROACHMENT) ACT, 2010

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Public Property (Removal of Encroachment) Act, 2010
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide measures for removal of encroachment from public property and to retrieve possession
metadata.commencement: at once and deemed to have taken effect on 8th September, 2010
repeals: The Sindh Public Property (Removal of Encroachment) Act, 1975
metadata.max_penalty: imprisonment for six months or fine not less than fifty thousand rupees or both
metadata.one_line: This Act provides measures to remove encroachments from public property, establish tribunals and special courts, and create an Anti-Encroachment Force.
metadata.summary: The Act empowers the Government or authorized officers to order the removal of unauthorized structures on public property within a specified period. It establishes Tribunals and Special Courts to handle eviction cases and creates the Anti-Encroachment Force to assist in enforcement. The legislation also outlines penalties for disobedience, procedures for appeals, and repeals the previous 1975 Act.

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Public Service Commission (Amendment) Act, 1994
metadata.long_title: An Act to amend the Sindh Public Service Commission Act, 1989.
amends: The Sindh Public Service Commission Act, 1989
metadata.one_line: Amends the Sindh Public Service Commission Act, 1989 to allow curtailing office terms.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the Sindh Public Service Commission Act, 1989. It authorizes the Government to curtail the term of office for the Chairman or Members appointed before July 31, 1994. The amendment comes into force immediately upon enactment.

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Public Service Commission (Amendment) Act, 2008
metadata.long_title: An Act to further amend the Sindh Public Service Commission Act, 1989.
amends: The Sindh Public Service Commission Act, 1989
metadata.one_line: Amends the Sindh Public Service Commission Act, 1989 by omitting a clause, substituting 'Government' for 'Governor', and altering tenure terms.
metadata.summary: This Act further amends the Sindh Public Service Commission Act, 1989 to update specific provisions regarding the commission's composition and operation. It omits Clause (bb) of Section 2 and substitutes the word 'Government' for 'Governor' throughout the parent Act. Additionally, it modifies Section 4 to define a single non-renewable five-year term for the Chairman and Members, with provisions for reconstitution by the Government within thirty days.

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Public Service Commission Act, 1973
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for a Public Service Commission for Sind.
repeals: Sind Ordinance XII of 1973
metadata.one_line: Establishes the Sindh Public Service Commission to conduct recruitment exams and advise on civil service terms.
metadata.summary: This Act establishes a Public Service Commission for the Province of Sindh consisting of three Members appointed by the Government. The Commission is empowered to conduct tests and examinations for recruitment to Provincial Civil Service posts and other civil positions, as well as to advise the Government on terms and conditions of service. The Act also grants the Government power to make rules for carrying out the purposes of the Act and repeals the earlier Sind Ordinance XII of 1973.

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Public Service Commission Act, 1989
metadata.long_title: An Act to repeal and with certain modifications, re-enact the Sindh Public Service Commission Ordinance (Sind Ordinance VI of 1978).
amends: Sindh Public Service Commission Ordinance (Sind Ordinance VI of 1978)
repeals: Sindh Public Service Commission Ordinance, 1978
metadata.one_line: This Act establishes the Sindh Public Service Commission and outlines its composition, functions, and terms of service.
metadata.summary: The Sindh Public Service Commission Act, 1989 repeals and re-enacts the previous ordinance with modifications to establish a Public Service Commission for the Province of Sindh. The Commission consists of a Chairman and Members appointed by the Government, who conduct recruitment tests, advise on qualifications, and hold examinations. The Act defines terms such as 'misconduct' and outlines procedures for removing members due to incapacity or misconduct, while requiring annual reports to be presented to the Provincial Assembly.

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Public-Private Partnership Act, 2010
metadata.long_title: An Act to create an enabling environment for private sector participation in infrastructure development projects in the province of Sindh through public-private partnership projects.
metadata.territorial_extent: the whole of the Province of Sindh
metadata.one_line: This Act enables private sector participation in Sindh's infrastructure projects via public-private partnerships.
metadata.summary: The Sindh Public-Private Partnership Act, 2010 creates an enabling environment for private sector involvement in infrastructure development within the province. It establishes a Policy Board and a Unit to manage project identification, prioritization, and implementation through various partnership models like BOT and DBFO. The Act outlines procedures for bidding, financing, dispute resolution, and termination of agreements while ensuring transparency and fairness.

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Pure Food (Amendment) Act, 1995
metadata.long_title: An Act to amend the Sind Pure Food Ordinance, 1960.
metadata.commencement: on such date as Government may, by notification in the official Gazette, specify
metadata.one_line: Amends the Sind Pure Food Ordinance, 1960 to include iodized salt in definitions and regulations.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the Sind Pure Food Ordinance, 1960 to explicitly define 'iodized salt' as food for the purposes of the law. It adds a new explanation regarding iodized salt and modifies Section 37 to include iodized salt in prohibitions or regulations concerning food ingredients. The amendments ensure that iodized salt is considered food whether consumed alone or as an ingredient, aiming to prevent iodine deficiency.

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Race-Courses Licensing (Amendment) Act, 2013
metadata.long_title: An Act to amend the Sindh Race-Courses Licensing Act, 1912.
repeals: The Sindh Race-Courses Licensing (Amendment) Ordinance, 2003
metadata.one_line: Amends the 1912 Race-Courses Licensing Act by adding new sections and repealing a 2003 Ordinance.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the Sindh Race-Courses Licensing Act, 1912, to insert new sections regarding government rule-making powers. It explicitly repeals the Sindh Race-Courses Licensing (Amendment) Ordinance, 2003. The legislation comes into force immediately upon enactment.

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Regional Plan Organization (Repeal) Act, 2006
metadata.long_title: An act to repeal the Sind Regional Plan Organization Act, 1976.
repeals: The Sind Regional Plan Organization Act, 1976
metadata.status_evidence: An act to repeal the Sind Regional Plan Organization Act, 1976.
metadata.one_line: This Act repeals the Sind Regional Plan Organization Act, 1976.
metadata.summary: The Sindh Regional Plan Organization (Repeal) Act, 2006 is a short legislative instrument enacted by the Provincial Assembly of Sindh. Its sole purpose is to repeal the Sind Regional Plan Organization Act, 1976. The Act came into force immediately upon enactment on December 27, 2006.

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Registration of Godowns Act, 1995
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the registration of godowns in the Province of Sindh.
metadata.territorial_extent: the whole of the Province of Sindh
repeals: Sindh Ordinance X of 1995
metadata.max_penalty: imprisonment for a term which may extend to one year or with fine which may extend to one thousand rupees
metadata.administering_body: Director General Bureau of supply and Prices or any other officer appointed as such by Government
metadata.one_line: This Act provides for the registration, maintenance, and inspection of godowns storing essential articles in Sindh.
metadata.summary: The Act establishes a system for registering godowns used to store essential articles within the Province of Sindh. It mandates owners to apply for registration within specific timeframes and maintain accurate records for inspection by the Registering Authority. The legislation also grants powers for search, defines penalties for contraventions, and repeals the previous Sindh Registration of Godowns Ordinance, 1995.

name: SINDH REGULARIZATION OF DOCTORS APPOINTED ON CONTRACT BASIS ACT, 2003

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Regularization of Doctors Appointed on Contract Basis Act, 2003
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for regularization of the services of certain doctors appointed on contract basis.
key_definitions: appointment of a Doctor on contract
metadata.one_line: This Act regularizes doctors appointed on contract basis in Sindh as civil servants if they held the post for over a year.
metadata.summary: The Sindh Regularization of Doctors Appointed on Contract Basis Act, 2003 provides for the regularization of services of certain doctors appointed on a contract basis. It applies to doctors who have held such appointments for more than a year and are in employment at the commencement of the Act. Such doctors are deemed to have been validly appointed as civil servants on a regular basis from the date of the Act's commencement, provided they possess the prescribed qualifications.

name: SINDH REGULATION AND CONTROL OF DISPOSABLE SYRINGES ACT, 2010

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Regulation and Control of Disposable Syringes Act, 2010
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for regulation of and control on the use of disposable syringes; and for matters connected therewith or incidental thereto.
metadata.max_penalty: imprisonment for a term which may extend to three years or with fine which may extend to one million rupees or with both
metadata.one_line: Regulates and controls the manufacture, sale, and use of disposable syringes in Sindh to prevent reuse.
metadata.summary: This Act regulates and controls the use of disposable syringes within the Province of Sindh. It mandates that only auto lock, auto destruct, or auto break syringes can be manufactured, sold, or used for injection or drawing blood. The legislation establishes specific offences for contravention, prescribing penalties including imprisonment up to three years and fines up to one million rupees for repeat offenders.

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Reproductive Healthcare Rights (Amendment) Act, 2022
metadata.long_title: An Act to amend the Sindh Reproductive Healthcare Rights Act, 2019.
amends: The Sindh Reproductive Healthcare Rights Act, 2019
establishes: maternal, perinatal death surveillance response and review (MPDSRR) system
key_definitions: maternal and perinatal death surveillance and response (MPDSR)
metadata.one_line: Amends the Sindh Reproductive Healthcare Rights Act, 2019 to include marital counseling, telehealth, and maternal death surveillance.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the Sindh Reproductive Healthcare Rights Act, 2019 to incorporate new definitions related to counselors, marital counseling, and maternal death surveillance. It establishes mechanisms for providing reproductive healthcare information through telehealth and self-care, particularly in remote areas. The legislation also mandates the creation of a maternal and perinatal death surveillance response system, including provincial task forces and district committees to investigate causes of deaths and prevent future occurrences.

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Revenue Board (Amendment) Act, 2012
metadata.long_title: An Act to amend the Sindh Revenue Board Act, 2010.
metadata.one_line: Amends the Sindh Revenue Board Act, 2010 regarding appointments, employee regularization, and departmental support.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the Sindh Revenue Board Act, 2010 to alter appointment procedures for the Chairman and members. It empowers the Board to regularize existing contract employees without consulting the Sindh Public Service Commission. Additionally, it modifies the composition of certain committees and mandates government departments to assist the Board in its functions.

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Revenue Board Act, 2010
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the establishment of the Sindh Revenue Board in the Province of Sindh.
metadata.territorial_extent: the whole of the Province of Sindh
metadata.one_line: Establishes the Sindh Revenue Board to regulate fiscal policies and tax collection in Sindh.
metadata.summary: This Act establishes the Sindh Revenue Board (SRB) within the Province of Sindh to manage fiscal and economic policies. It defines the Board's powers for imposing, levying, and collecting taxes using modern automated techniques. The legislation outlines the Board's structure, including its Chairman, members, and committees, while also detailing human resource management, budgeting, and the authority to make rules and regulations.

name: SINDH REVISION OF EMOLUMENTS OF PUBLIC REPRESENTATIVES ACT, 1995

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Revision of Emoluments of Public Representatives Act, 1995
metadata.long_title: An Act to revise the salaries and other emoluments of the holders of representative offices in the Province of Sindh.
metadata.one_line: This Act revises salaries and emoluments for public representatives in Sindh and amends related laws.
metadata.summary: The Sindh Revision of Emoluments of Public Representatives Act, 1995 was enacted to revise the salaries and other emoluments of holders of representative offices in the Province of Sindh. It amends several existing Acts, including the Sind Assembly Members (Salaries and Allowances) Act, 1974, by updating figures for allowances, travel, accommodation, and telephone charges. The Act applies to members of the Provincial Assembly, the Chief Minister, and Ministers within the province.

name: SINDH RIGHT OF CHILDREN TO FREE AND COMPULSORY EDUCATION ACT, 2013

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Right of Children to Free and Compulsory Education Act, 2013
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for free and compulsory education to all children of the age of five to sixteen years.
repeals: The Sindh Compulsory Primary Education Ordinance, 2001
metadata.one_line: This Act guarantees free and compulsory education for children aged five to sixteen in the Province of Sindh.
metadata.summary: The Sindh Right of Children to Free and Compulsory Education Act, 2013 establishes a fundamental right for all children between the ages of five and sixteen to receive free and compulsory education. It mandates that both government and private schools provide this education without charging fees that could prevent attendance, while also setting norms for school management, teacher duties, and curriculum evaluation. The Act repeals the previous Sindh Compulsory Primary Education Ordinance, 2001, and creates an Education Advisory Council to oversee implementation.

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Sacked Employees' (Reinstatement) Act, 2016
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide relief to persons in corporation service or autonomous or semi-autonomous bodies or in Government service who were dismissed, removed or terminated from service.
metadata.territorial_extent: the whole of the Province of Sindh
metadata.one_line: This Act reinstates employees dismissed between 1997 and 2008 due to political victimization in Sindh government or autonomous bodies.
metadata.summary: The Act provides relief to persons employed in corporation, autonomous, semi-autonomous bodies, or Government service in Sindh who were dismissed, removed, or terminated between February 3, 1997 and February 18, 2008 due to political victimization. It deems such employees validly reinstated in their original scale, grade, and post as held at the time of dismissal. The provisions override any conflicting laws, judgments, or terms of appointment and entitle sacked employees to all applicable service benefits under prevailing Sindh Civil Servants laws.

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Safe Blood Transfusion (Amendment) Act, 2026
metadata.long_title: An Act to amend the Sindh Blood Transfusion Act, 2017.
metadata.one_line: Amends section 5 of the Sindh Blood Transfusion Act, 2017 regarding the appointment and qualifications of the Authority's Secretary.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the Sindh Blood Transfusion Act, 2017 to update the requirements for appointing the Secretary of the Authority. The amendment specifies that the Secretary must possess an MBBS degree with significant experience in the health sector and blood banking, or be a Hematologist with substantial administrative experience. The appointment is made by the Government on the recommendation of the Authority for a renewable term determined by the Board.

name: SINDH SALES TAX ON SERVICES (AMENDMENT) ACT, 2011

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Sales Tax on Services (Amendment) Act, 2011
metadata.long_title: An Act to amend the Sindh Sales Tax on Services Act, 2011.

repeals: The Sindh Sales Tax on Services (Amendment) Ordinance, 2011
metadata.one_line: Amends the Sindh Sales Tax on Services Act, 2011 regarding tax rates, definitions, and repeals a 2011 Ordinance.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the Sindh Sales Tax on Services Act, 2011 to update tax classifications and rates for various services. It specifically adds new tariff headings for financial leasing, construction, and airport/port services while modifying existing entries for insurance and non-banking finance companies. The legislation also omits certain clauses regarding tax rate adjustments and substitutes specific words in the schedules to reflect updated service categories.

name: SINDH SALES TAX ON SERVICES (AMENDMENT) ACT, 2015

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Sales Tax on Services (Amendment) Act, 2015
metadata.long_title: An Act to amend the Sindh Sales Tax on Services Act, 2011.
metadata.commencement: at once and deemed to have taken effect on 1st day of July, 2015
amends: Sindh Sales Tax on Services Act, 2011
repeals: The Sindh Sales Tax on Services (Amendment) Ordinance, 2015
