metadata.summary: This Act amends the Sindh Sales Tax on Services Act, 2011 to define 'renting of immovable property services' for taxation purposes. It inserts a new validation section to deem certain past notifications and orders regarding these services as validly issued. Additionally, it repeals the corresponding Amendment Ordinance from 2015.

name: SINDH SALES TAX ON SERVICES (AMENDMENT) ACT, 2021

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Sales Tax on Services (Amendment) Act, 2021
metadata.long_title: An Act to amend the Sindh Sales Tax on Services Act, 2011.
amends: The Sindh Sales Tax on Services Act, 2011
key_definitions: software or IT based system development consultant
metadata.one_line: Amends the Sindh Sales Tax on Services Act, 2011 to include new definitions and tariff headings for specific services.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the Sindh Sales Tax on Services Act, 2011 by inserting new clauses defining terms such as 'active taxpayer' and 'truck aggregator'. It updates references from the Companies Ordinance, 1984 to the Companies Act, 2017 and adds specific services related to guarantees and truck aggregators to the tax schedules. The amendments apply to services provided within Sindh in the course of an economic activity.

name: SINDH SALES TAX ON SERVICES ACT, 2011 (codified)

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Sales Tax on Services Act, 2011
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the levy of a tax on services provided, rendered, initiated, received, originated, executed or consumed in the Province of Sindh.
metadata.territorial_extent: the whole of the Province of Sindh
metadata.max_penalty: 100,000 rupees
metadata.one_line: This Act levies sales tax on services provided, rendered, initiated, received, originated, executed or consumed in Sindh.
metadata.summary: The Sindh Sales Tax on Services Act, 2011 establishes a framework for levying and collecting sales tax on various services within the Province of Sindh. It defines taxable services, outlines registration requirements for providers, and sets rules for payment, record-keeping, and audit proceedings. The Act also details penalties for non-compliance, procedures for appeals, and specific tax rates for different service categories.

name: SINDH SCHOOL EDUCATION STANDARS AND CIRRICULUM ACT, 2014

metadata.short_title: The Sindh School Education Standards and Curriculum Act, 2014
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for maintenance of school education standards and supervision of curriculum, textbooks, and assessment processes for improving quality of education from early years to grade twelve in the Province of Sindh.
metadata.territorial_extent: the whole of the Province of Sindh
repeals: Federal Supervision of Curricula, Textbooks and Maintenance of Standards of Education Act, 1976 (X of 1976)
establishes: Directorate of Curriculum, Research and Assessment
metadata.max_penalty: imprisonment up to six months or fine not less than forty five thousand rupees or both
metadata.one_line: This Act establishes standards and supervision for school education, curriculum, and textbooks in Sindh.
metadata.summary: The Act provides for the maintenance of school education standards and the supervision of curriculum, textbooks, and assessment processes in Sindh. It establishes a Curriculum Wing and a Provincial Curriculum Council to oversee these functions. The legislation repeals the Federal Supervision of Curricula, Textbooks and Maintenance of Standards of Education Act, 1976 to the extent it applies to Sindh.

name: SINDH SECURITY OF VULNERABLE ESTABLISHMENTS ACT, 2015

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Security of Vulnerable Establishments Act, 2015
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for effective security arrangements of vulnerable establishments.
metadata.territorial_extent: the whole of Province of Sindh
repeals: The Sindh Security of Vulnerable Establishment Ordinance, 2015
metadata.max_penalty: imprisonment which may extend to six months and fine which shall not be less than forty five thousand rupees
metadata.one_line: This Act establishes security arrangements for vulnerable establishments in Sindh to prevent terrorism and facilitate investigations.
metadata.summary: The Act provides for effective security arrangements at vulnerable establishments such as hospitals, banks, and places of worship to prevent acts of terrorism. It establishes a Security Advisory Committee to identify these establishments, inspect them quarterly, and issue security advice to managers. Managers must comply with the committee's advice regarding physical and technical security measures. The Act also outlines penalties for non-compliance and provides mechanisms for appeals and evidence collection.

name: SINDH SEIZED AND FREEZED FACILITIES (HOSPITALS AND DISPENSARIES) ACT, 2020

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Seized and Freezed Facilities (Hospitals and Dispensaries) Act, 2020
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the establishment of the Hospitals and Dispensaries Management Board in the Province of Sindh to manage the seized and freezed Facilities and to ensure mainstreaming of employees of such Facilities.
metadata.territorial_extent: the whole of the Province of Sindh
metadata.commencement: on such date as the Government may, by notification in the official Gazette, specify
metadata.one_line: Establishes a Board to manage seized UN facilities and mainstream employees in Sindh.
metadata.summary: This Act establishes the Hospitals and Dispensaries Management Board in the Province of Sindh. The Board is tasked with managing facilities that were seized and frozen under United Nations Security Council orders and ensuring the mainstreaming of their employees. It grants the Board powers to acquire property, recruit staff, formulate budgets, and frame regulations necessary for its operations.

name: SINDH SEIZED AND FREEZED INSTITUTIONS (MADAARIS AND SCHOOLS) ACT, 2020

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Seized and Freezed Institutions (Madaaris and Schools) Act, 2020
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the establishment of the Madaaris and Schools Management Board in the Province of Sindh to manage the seized and freezed Institutions, to ensure mainstreaming of students and employees of such Institutions.
metadata.territorial_extent: the whole of the Province of Sindh
metadata.commencement: on such date as the Government may, by notification in the official Gazette, specify
metadata.one_line: Establishes a Board to manage seized Madaaris and schools in Sindh and mainstream their students.
metadata.summary: This Act establishes the Madaaris and Schools Management Board in the Province of Sindh. The Board is empowered to manage institutions that have been seized or frozen under United Nations Security Council orders. Its primary objectives include ensuring the mainstreaming of students and employees from these institutions, managing their properties, and recruiting staff.

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Senior Citizens Welfare Act, 2014
metadata.long_title: An Act to make provisions for the welfare of senior citizens of the Province of Sindh.
metadata.territorial_extent: the whole of the Province of Sindh
metadata.max_penalty: rigorous imprisonment not less than one year but not more than three years or fine which may extend to thirty thousand rupees or with both
metadata.one_line: This Act establishes a council and fund to provide welfare, medical care, and support for senior citizens in Sindh.
metadata.summary: The Sindh Senior Citizens Welfare Act, 2014 aims to improve the well-being of senior citizens aged sixty or above residing in Sindh. It establishes a Senior Citizens Council comprising government officials, NGO representatives, and retired officers to formulate policies and oversee welfare measures. The Act also creates a Senior Citizens Welfare Fund for financial support and mandates provisions for medical care, old age homes, and special facilities like tax exemptions and fare concessions.

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Service Tribunals (Amendment) Act, 2014
metadata.long_title: An Act to amend the Sindh Service Tribunals Act, 1973.
metadata.commencement: at once and deemed to have taken effect on and from 7th August, 2013
metadata.one_line: Amends the composition and appointment criteria for members of Sindh Service Tribunals.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the Sindh Service Tribunals Act, 1973 to update the composition of Service Tribunals. It specifies that a Tribunal shall consist of a Chairman and two Members appointed by the Government in consultation with the Chief Justice of the High Court of Sindh. The amendment details eligibility criteria for the Chairman (qualified High Court Judge) and the two members (one practicing Advocate with seven years experience and one sitting civil servant with legal background).

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Service Tribunals (Amendment) Act, 1991
metadata.long_title: An Act to amend the Sind Service Tribunals Act, 1973.
repeals: The Sindh Service Tribunals (Amendment) Ordinance, 1991
establishes: Tribunal consisting of three Judges of the High Court for members of the subordinate judiciary
metadata.one_line: Amends the Sind Service Tribunals Act, 1973 to establish a new tribunal for subordinate judiciary matters and repeals an Ordinance.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the Sind Service Tribunals Act, 1973 to empower the Chief Justice of the High Court to establish a Tribunal consisting of three judges for the subordinate judiciary. It grants this new Tribunal exclusive jurisdiction over terms, conditions of service, and disciplinary matters for subordinate judiciary members. The Act also transfers pending cases from the previous tribunal to the newly established one and repeals the Sindh Service Tribunals (Amendment) Ordinance, 1991.

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Service Tribunals (Amendment) Act, 1994
metadata.long_title: An Act to amend the Sind Service Tribunals Act, 1973.
metadata.one_line: Amends the Sind Service Tribunals Act, 1973 to include corporations in service definitions and abate pending cases.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the Sind Service Tribunals Act, 1973 to expand the definition of 'Corporation' to include those established by provincial enactments. It declares that service in such corporations is deemed to be the service of the Province, treating employees as civil servants for the purposes of the Act. Additionally, it provides for the abatement of pending suits or appeals regarding these employees immediately before the Act's commencement, allowing appeals within ninety days.

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Service Tribunals (Amendment) Act, 2011
metadata.long_title: An Act to amend the Sind Service Tribunals Act, 1973.
metadata.one_line: Amends the Sind Service Tribunals Act, 1973 to add execution of decisions as a function.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the Sind Service Tribunals Act, 1973 by modifying section 5. Specifically, it changes punctuation in subsection (2) and adds a new clause (d) regarding the execution of its decisions.

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Service Tribunals (Amendment) Act, 2016
metadata.long_title: An Act to amend the Sindh Service Tribunals Act, 1973.
metadata.one_line: Amends the Sindh Service Tribunals Act, 1973 by updating section numbers and terminology.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the Sindh Service Tribunals Act, 1973 to update specific section references from '5-(A)' and '5-(B)' to '5-A' and '5-B'. It also substitutes the word 'Provincial' with 'Principal' within the said Act. The legislation came into force immediately upon enactment.

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Service Tribunals (Fourth Amendment) Act, 2015
metadata.long_title: An Act to amend the Sindh Service Tribunals Act, 1973.
metadata.one_line: Amends the composition of members in Sindh Service Tribunals by specifying qualifications for District Judges and civil servants.
metadata.summary: This Act amends section 3 of the Sindh Service Tribunals Act, 1973 to update the requirements for tribunal members. It stipulates that one member must be a sitting District and Sessions Judge while another must be a civil servant in BS-20 with a legal background. The provision allows for the appointment of a qualified Advocate as a substitute if the primary candidates are unavailable, subject to consultation with the Chief Justice of the High Court of Sindh.

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Service Tribunals (Second Amendment) Act, 1994
metadata.long_title: An Act to amend the Sind Service Tribunals Act, 1973.
metadata.one_line: Amends the Sind Service Tribunals Act, 1973 to define members of the subordinate judiciary.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the Sind Service Tribunals Act, 1973 by inserting a new definition into section 2. The amendment expands the meaning of 'member of the subordinate judiciary' to include various judicial officers and employees under the administrative control of the District and Sessions Judge. It came into force immediately upon enactment.

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Service Tribunals (Third Amendment) Act, 2015
metadata.long_title: An Act to amend the Sindh Service Tribunals Act, 1973.
metadata.one_line: Amends the Sindh Service Tribunals Act, 1973 to grant financial and administrative powers to the Tribunal Chairman.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the Sindh Service Tribunals Act, 1973 to enhance the administrative and financial autonomy of the Sindh Service Tribunal. It designates the Chairman as the Provincial Accounting Officer and grants powers to re-appropriate funds without Government approval. Additionally, it empowers the Chairman to create new posts or abolish old posts within the allocated budget, also without requiring Government approval.

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Service Tribunals Act, 1973
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the establishment of Service Tribunal to exercise jurisdiction in respect of matters relating to the terms and conditions of service of civil servants.
metadata.territorial_extent: all civil servants wherever they may be
repeals: Sindh Service Tribunal Ordinance, 1973 (Sindh Ordinance XI of 1973)
establishes: Tribunal for members of the subordinate judiciary
metadata.one_line: Establishes Service Tribunals in Sindh to adjudicate matters regarding the terms and conditions of service for civil servants.
metadata.summary: This Act establishes Service Tribunals within the Province of Sindh to exercise exclusive jurisdiction over disputes concerning the terms and conditions of service of civil servants. It defines the composition of these tribunals, including chairmen and members drawn from High Court judges and senior civil servants. The legislation also provides for specific tribunals for subordinate judiciary members and declares that employees of provincial corporations are deemed civil servants for the purposes of this Act.

name: SINDH SHAHEED RECOGNITION AND COMPENSATION ACT, 2014.

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Shaheed Recognition and Compensation Act, 2014
metadata.long_title: An Act to honor and recognize the services of persons who sacrifice their lives in act of terrorism while performing duty and to provide compensation to their legal heirs in the Province of Sindh;
metadata.one_line: This Act honors terrorism victims in Sindh and provides compensation and welfare benefits to their families.
metadata.summary: The Sindh Shaheed Recognition and Compensation Act, 2014 aims to honor individuals who sacrificed their lives while performing duty during acts of terrorism. It empowers the Government of Sindh to award monetary compensation to the legal heirs of these individuals and grants posthumous promotions. Additionally, the Act allows for further welfare measures such as scholarships, medical coverage, and land allotment for the families of Shaheeds.

name: SINDH SHAHEED RECONGNOTION AND COMPENSATION (AMENDMENT) ACT, 2017

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Shaheed Recognition and Compensation (Amendment) Act, 2017
metadata.long_title: An Act to amend the Sindh Shaheed Recognition and Compensation Act, 2014.
amends: Sindh Shaheed Recognition and Compensation Act, 2014
metadata.one_line: Amends the 2014 Act to allow appointing two legal heirs of Shaheeds to government service with relaxed qualifications.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the Sindh Shaheed Recognition and Compensation Act, 2014 to provide additional benefits for the families of Shaheeds. Specifically, it substitutes Section 3(5) to authorize the Government to appoint two legal heirs of a Shaheed person into government service ranging from BS-01 to BS-15. These appointments are made in relaxation of standard conditions regarding qualifications and age, at the discretion of the Government.

name: SINDH SHOPS AND COMMERCIAL ESTABLISHMENT ACT, 2015

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Shops and Commercial Establishment Act, 2015
metadata.long_title: An Act to amend and consolidate the law relating to the hours and other conditions of work and employment of persons employed in shops and commercial, industrial and other establishments in the Province of Sindh and matters connected therewith and ancillary thereto.
metadata.territorial_extent: the whole of the Province of Sindh
repeals: Shops and Establishments Ordinance, 1969
metadata.max_penalty: one thousand rupees and a further fine of three hundred rupees for every day during which the breach continues
metadata.one_line: This Act consolidates laws regarding working hours, wages, and conditions for employees in shops and commercial establishments in Sindh.
metadata.summary: The Sindh Shops and Commercial Establishment Act, 2015 amends and consolidates legislation governing the hours and conditions of work for employees in various establishments within the Province of Sindh. It defines key terms such as 'employee', 'employer', and 'commercial establishment' while setting rules for weekly holidays, working hours, overtime wages, and leave entitlements. The Act also establishes penalties for breaches, outlines the powers of inspectors, and repeals the previous Shops and Establishments Ordinance, 1969.

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Small Industries Corporation (Amendment) Act, 1989
metadata.long_title: An Act to amend the Sind Small Industries Corporation Act, 1972.
metadata.one_line: Amends the Sind Small Industries Corporation Act, 1972 by substituting the composition of its Board.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the Sind Small Industries Corporation Act, 1972 to update the composition of the Corporation's Board. It specifies new members including representatives from the Government of Sindh, Provincial Assembly, Industrial Development Bank of Pakistan, and other industrial bodies. The changes also include provisions for appointing persons domiciled in Sindh and representatives from women's associations.

metadata.short_title: The Sind Smoke-nuisances Act, 1912
metadata.long_title: An Act for the abatement of nuisances arising from the smoke of furnaces in Sind.
metadata.max_penalty: fine which may extend to twenty rupees for every day thereafter during which such failure continues
metadata.one_line: This Act regulates smoke emissions from furnaces in Sind, establishes a commission, and defines penalties for nuisances.
metadata.summary: The Sind Smoke-nuisances Act, 1912 was enacted to abate nuisances caused by smoke from furnaces in the province of Sind. It establishes a Commission supervised by the Provincial Government to control furnace operations and appoints Inspectors as public servants to enforce the law. The Act prohibits the erection of kilns or furnaces without approval, mandates plans for new installations, and imposes fines for excessive smoke emission or failure to comply with regulations.

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Solid Waste Management Act, 2021
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the collection and disposal of solid waste, arrange effective delivery of sanitation services and provide for pollution free environment and matters ancillary thereto, and for the purpose establish the Solid Waste Management Boards in the Province of Sindh.
metadata.territorial_extent: the whole of the Province of Sindh
repeals: The Sindh Solid Waste Management Board Act, 2014
metadata.administering_body: Local Government and Housing Town Planning Department, Government of Sindh
metadata.one_line: Establishes Solid Waste Management Boards in Sindh to manage waste collection, disposal, and sanitation services.
metadata.summary: This Act provides for the collection and disposal of solid waste and the delivery of effective sanitation services in the Province of Sindh. It establishes Solid Waste Management Boards at every Divisional Headquarters to oversee these operations. The legislation also defines key terms related to waste, buildings, and local authorities, and repeals the previous 2014 Board Act.

name: SINDH SOLID WASTE MANAGEMENT BOARD ACT, 2014

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Solid Waste Management Board Act, 2013
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the establishment of a Board called as the Sindh Solid Waste Management Board for the collection and disposal of solid and other waste in the Province of Sindh.
metadata.territorial_extent: the whole of the Province of Sindh
repeals: The Sindh Solid Waste Management Board Ordinance
metadata.one_line: Establishes the Sindh Solid Waste Management Board to manage solid waste collection and disposal in Sindh.
metadata.summary: This Act establishes the Sindh Solid Waste Management Board as a body corporate responsible for collecting and disposing of solid waste in the Province of Sindh. The Board is empowered to arrange sanitation services, ensure a pollution-free environment, and manage finances through a dedicated fund. It defines various terms related to waste, local authorities, and infrastructure, and repeals the previous Ordinance on the same subject.

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Sound System (Regulation) Act, 2015
metadata.long_title: An Act to regulate and control use of sound systems in the Province of Sindh.
metadata.territorial_extent: the whole of Province of Sindh
repeals: The Sindh Sound System (regulation) Ordinance, 2015
metadata.max_penalty: imprisonment up to six months and fine between twenty five thousand rupees and fifty thousand rupees
metadata.one_line: This Act regulates sound systems in Sindh to prevent public nuisance and protect public order.
metadata.summary: The Sindh Sound System (Regulation) Act, 2015 was enacted to regulate and control the use of sound systems within the Province of Sindh. It aims to prevent public nuisance, maintain public order, ensure decency, and prevent incitement to terrorism or offences. The Act prohibits the use of sound systems that generate unnecessary noise, particularly near places of worship during prayer times, hospitals, educational institutions, and residential areas. It empowers police officers to inspect sound systems, seize those used in offences, and imposes penalties including imprisonment and fines for violations.

name: SINDH SPEAKER AND DEPUTY SPEAKER (SALAIRES, ALLOWANCES AND PRIVILEGES) ACT, 2007

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Speaker's and Deputy Speaker's (Salaries, Allowances and Privileges) Act, 2007
metadata.long_title: An Act to amend the Sindh Speaker's and Deputy Speaker's (Salaries, Allowances and Privileges) Act, 1975.
amends: The Sindh Speaker's and Deputy Speaker's (Salaries, Allowances and Privileges) Act, 1975
repeals: The Sindh Speaker's and Deputy Speaker's (Salaries, Allowances and Privileges) Ordinance, 2006
metadata.one_line: Amends the 1975 Act regarding official cars for the Speaker and Deputy Speaker and repeals a 2006 Ordinance.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the Sindh Speaker's and Deputy Speaker's (Salaries, Allowances and Privileges) Act, 1975 to grant entitlements for official cars. It substitutes Section 7 of the 1975 Act to specify that the Speaker is entitled to official cars maintained at Government expense, while the Deputy Speaker is entitled to an official car maintained at Government expense. Additionally, the Act repeals the Sindh Speaker's and Deputy Speaker's (Salaries, Allowances and Privileges) Ordinance, 2006.

name: SINDH SPEAKER’S AND DEPUTY SPEAKER’S (SALARIES, ALLOWANCES AND PRIVILEGES) (AMENDMENT) ACT, 1989

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Speaker's and Deputy Speaker's (Salaries, Allowances and Privileges) (Amendment) Act, 1989
metadata.long_title: An Act to amend the Sind Speaker's and Deputy Speaker's (Salaries, Allowances and Privileges) Act, 1975
amends: The Sind Speaker's and Deputy Speaker's (Salaries, Allowances and Privileges) Act, 1975
metadata.administering_body: Speaker of the Provincial Assembly of Sindh
metadata.one_line: Amends the 1975 Act to grant discretionary funds and telephone privileges to the Speaker.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the Sind Speaker's and Deputy Speaker's (Salaries, Allowances and Privileges) Act, 1975. It inserts a new section granting the Speaker discretionary annual grants up to fifty thousand rupees subject to annual audit by the Accountant General, Sindh. Additionally, it entitles the Speaker to use two telephones at his office and two at his residence at government expense.

name: SINDH SPEAKER’S AND DEPUTY SPEAKER’S (SALARIES, ALLOWANCES AND PIVILEGES) (SECOND AMENDMENT) ACT, 1995

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Speaker's and Deputy Speaker's (Salaries, Allowances and Privileges) (Second Amendment) Act, 1995
metadata.long_title: An Act to amend the Sindh Speaker's and Deputy Speaker's (Salaries, Allowances and Privileges) Act, 1975.
amends: The Sindh Speaker's and Deputy Speaker's (Salaries, Allowances and Privileges) Act, 1975
metadata.one_line: Amends Section 13 of the 1975 Act regarding the duration of Speaker's and Deputy Speaker's allowances.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the Sindh Speaker's and Deputy Speaker's (Salaries, Allowances and Privileges) Act, 1975. It specifically alters Section 13 to change the wording regarding the period for which allowances are payable. The amendment substitutes 'for an aggregate period not exceeding three months during the whole term of his office' with 'for a period not exceeding three months in a year'. The Act came into force immediately upon enactment.

name: SINDH SPEAKER’S AND DEPUTY SPEAKER’S (SALARIES, ALLOWANCES AND PRIVILEGES) (AMENDMENT) ACT, 2009

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Speaker's and Deputy Speaker's (Salaries, Allowances and Privileges) (Amendment) Act, 2009
metadata.long_title: An Act to amend the Sind Speaker's and Deputy Speaker's (Salaries, Allowances and Privileges) Act, 1975.
metadata.commencement: at once and deemed to have taken effect on and from 1 July, 2011
amends: The Sind Speaker's and Deputy Speaker's (Salaries, Allowances and Privileges) Act, 1975
metadata.one_line: Amends the 1975 Act to increase salaries, allowances, and privileges for the Speaker and Deputy Speaker of Sindh.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the Sind Speaker's and Deputy Speaker's (Salaries, Allowances and Privileges) Act, 1975. It updates salary figures, introduces automatic increases linked to civil servant pay, and enhances official perks like cars and mobile phones. The changes apply specifically to the Speaker and Deputy Speaker of the Provincial Assembly of Sindh.

name: SINDH SPEAKER’S AND DEPUTY SPEAKER’S (SALARIES, ALLOWANCES AND PRIVILEGES) (AMENDMENT) ACT, 2013

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Speaker's and Deputy Speaker's (Salaries, Allowances and Privileges) (Amendment) Act, 2013
metadata.long_title: An Act to amend the Sind Speaker's and Deputy Speaker's (Salaries, Allowances and Privileges) Act,1975.
amends: The Sind Speaker's and Deputy Speaker's (Salaries, Allowances and Privileges) Act, 1975
metadata.one_line: Amends the 1975 Act to grant post-retirement perks and privileges to Sindh Speakers serving at least four years.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the Sind Speaker's and Deputy Speaker's (Salaries, Allowances and Privileges) Act, 1975. It adds a new section granting specific perks and privileges to individuals who have served as Speaker for not less than four years upon expiry of their term. The benefits include a percentage of salary, private staff, lifetime police security, communication facilities, and a car for six months.

name: SINDH SPEAKER’S AND DEPUTY SPEAKER’S (SALARIES, ALLOWNCES AND PRIVILEGES) (AMENDMENT) ACT, 1989

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Speaker's and Deputy Speaker's (Salaries, Allowances and Privileges) (Amendment) Act, 1989
metadata.long_title: An Act to amend the Sindh Speaker's and Deputy Speaker's (Salaries, Allowances and Privileges) Act, 1975.
amends: The Sindh Speaker's and Deputy Speaker's (Salaries, Allowances and Privileges) Act, 1975
metadata.one_line: Amends the 1975 Act regarding salaries and allowances for Sindh's Speaker and Deputy Speaker.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the Sindh Speaker's and Deputy Speaker's (Salaries, Allowances and Privileges) Act, 1975. It specifically modifies Section 6 of the parent Act to delete certain words and insert references to the Deputy Speaker alongside the Speaker regarding allowances. The amendment came into force immediately upon enactment.

name: SINDH SPECIAL ASSISTANTS (APPOINTMENT, POWERS, FUNCTIONS, SALARIES, ALLOWANCES AND PRIVILEGES) (AMENDMENT) ACT, 2008

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Special Assistants (Appointment, Powers, Functions, Salaries Allowances and Privileges) Act, 2008
metadata.long_title: An Act to further amend the Sindh Special Assistants (Appointment, Powers, Functions, Salaries Allowances and Privileges) Act, 2003.
metadata.commencement: at once and deemed to have taken effect on and from 1st July, 2011
amends: The Sindh Special Assistants (Appointment, Powers, Functions, Salaries Allowances and Privileges) Act, 2003
metadata.one_line: Amends the 2003 Act regarding special assistants' salaries and allowances.
metadata.summary: This Act further amends the Sindh Special Assistants (Appointment, Powers, Functions, Salaries Allowances and Privileges) Act, 2003. It specifically substitutes the figure 'eleven thousand' with 'fifteen thousand four hundred' in section 8, subsection (2) of the 2003 Act. The amendment applies to special assistants within the Province of Sindh and came into force immediately upon enactment.

name: SINDH SPECIAL ASSISTANTS (APPOINTMENT, POWERS, FUNCTIONS, SALARIES, ALLOWANCES AND PRIVILEGES) ACT, 2003

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Special Assistants (Appointment, Powers, Functions, Salaries, Allowances and Privileges) Act, 2003
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for appointments, powers, functions, salaries, allowances and privileges of Special Assistants to the Chief Minister of Sindh.
metadata.commencement: at once and be deemed to have taken effect on and from January 1, 2003
metadata.one_line: This Act regulates the appointment, powers, salaries, allowances, and privileges of Special Assistants to the Chief Minister of Sindh.
metadata.summary: This Act provides for the appointment, powers, functions, salaries, allowances, and privileges of Special Assistants to the Chief Minister of Sindh. It defines key terms such as 'Special Assistant' and 'official residence', and outlines specific entitlements including salary, sumptuary allowance, transport, official residence, travelling allowance, leave, and personal staff. The provisions override any contrary laws or judgments currently in force.

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Special Development Board Act, 2014
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for establishment of a Board to be known as the Sindh Special Development Board; to facilitate and undertake low cost housing schemes, rehabilitation of katchi abadis, slums areas, gothabad schemes, mutli-stories and high rise buildings in the Province of Sindh, and to provide for matters connected therewith or ancillary thereto.
metadata.territorial_extent: the whole of Province of Sindh
metadata.one_line: Establishes the Sindh Special Development Board to facilitate low-cost housing and rehabilitation schemes in Sindh.
metadata.summary: This Act establishes the Sindh Special Development Board to facilitate and undertake low-cost housing schemes, rehabilitation of katchi abadis, slum areas, gothabad schemes, multi-stories, and high-rise buildings in the Province of Sindh. The Board is a body corporate with perpetual succession, headquartered in Karachi, and acts on sound principles guided by the Government of Sindh. It defines various terms including 'Katchi Abadi' and 'slum structure', outlines the composition of the Board consisting of government officials and representatives from utility agencies, and empowers the Board to make rules and regulations for its functioning.

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Sports Board (Amendment) Act, 1993
metadata.long_title: An Act to amend the Sindh Sports Board Ordinance, 1980.
repeals: The Sindh Sports Board (Amendment) Ordinance, 1993
metadata.one_line: Amends the Sindh Sports Board Ordinance, 1980 by adding the Secretary to Government of Sindh, Culture Department to the Board.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the Sindh Sports Board Ordinance, 1980 to include the Secretary to the Government of Sindh (Culture Department) in the Board's composition. It substitutes the existing sub-section regarding the roles of the Secretary and Director of Sports within the Board. The Act also repeals the earlier Sindh Sports Board (Amendment) Ordinance, 1993.

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Steam-Vessels Act, 1864
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the periodical survey of steam-vessels in the ports, harbours, rivers or waters of [* * Sind].
metadata.status_evidence: [Rep. Act VI of 1884.] ... Rep. Act VI of 1884.
metadata.one_line: Provides for the periodical survey of steam-vessels in Sind ports and waters.
metadata.summary: This Act establishes a framework for the periodic survey of steam-vessels operating in the ports, harbours, rivers, or waters of Sind. It declares that specific sections of the Merchant Shipping Act apply to these vessels and sets an exchange rate for penalty calculations. The entire Act, including its schedules and preamble, was repealed by Act VI of 1884.

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Students Union Act, 2019
metadata.long_title: An Act to activate an effective system to provide for the establishment of Students Unions and regulating them in the Province of Sindh.
metadata.territorial_extent: the whole of the Province of Sindh
establishes: Student Union in every Educational Institution
metadata.administering_body: College Education Department, Government of Sindh
metadata.one_line: Establishes and regulates Students Unions in educational institutions across the Province of Sindh.
metadata.summary: This Act provides for the establishment and regulation of Students Unions within all educational institutions in the Province of Sindh. It defines key terms such as 'Student', 'Educational Institution', and 'prejudicial activity' to ensure a safe and disciplined academic environment. The Act mandates the formation of Student Unions with elected representatives, outlines their functions including promoting student welfare and organizing cultural events, and requires institutions to maintain committees for protection against harassment.

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Tax Evasion (Punishment) (Amendment) Act, 2004
metadata.long_title: An Act to amend the Sind Tax Evasion Preamble (Punishment) Act, 1974.
metadata.one_line: Amends the Sindh Tax Evasion (Punishment) Act, 1974 to add imprisonment provisions for contravention of specific sections.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the Sindh Tax Evasion (Punishment) Act, 1974 by modifying Section 3 and adding a new entry to the Schedule. It specifically addresses imprisonment terms for contraventions of Sections 9 and 10 of the Sindh Finance Act, 1994. The amendment came into force immediately upon enactment.

name: SINDH TECHNICAL EDUCATION AND VOCATIONAL TRAINING AUTHORITY (AMENDMENT) ACT, 2010

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Technical Education and Vocational Training Authority (Amendment) Act, 2010
metadata.long_title: An Act to amend the Sindh Technical Education and Vocational Training Authority Act, 2009.
amends: The Sindh Technical Education and Vocational Training Authority Act, 2009
metadata.one_line: Amends the Sindh Technical Education and Vocational Training Authority Act, 2009 by omitting specific subsections of section 15.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the Sindh Technical Education and Vocational Training Authority Act, 2009. It specifically directs the omission of sub-sections (4), (5), and (6) from section 15 of the 2009 Act. The amendment also references Sindh Act No. VIII of 2010 in relation to these changes. The Act comes into force immediately upon enactment.

name: SINDH TECHNICAL EDUCATION AND VOCATIONAL TRAINING AUTHORITY (AMENDMENT) ACT, 2016

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Technical Education and Vocational Training Authority (Amendment) Act, 2016
metadata.long_title: An Act to amend the Sindh Technical Education and Vocational Training Authority Act, 2009.
amends: The Sindh Technical Education and Vocational Training Authority Act, 2009
subjects: National Vocational and Technical Training Commission
key_definitions: Commission (National Vocational and Technical Training Commission)
NVTTC (National Vocational and Technical Training Commission)
metadata.administering_body: Minister or Advisor or Special Chairperson Assistant to Chief Minister
metadata.one_line: Amends the Sindh Technical Education and Vocational Training Authority Act, 2009 regarding definitions and authority composition.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the Sindh Technical Education and Vocational Training Authority Act, 2009 to update specific clauses within it. The primary changes involve substituting references to the National Vocational and Technical Training Commission (NVTTC) in section 2 and updating abbreviations in section 4. Additionally, the Act modifies the composition of the authority by changing a numerical value in section 5 from two to five.

name: SINDH TECHNICAL EDUCATION AND VOCATIONAL TRAINING AUTHORITY ACT, 2009

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Technical Education and Vocational Training Authority Act, 2009
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the establishment of an Authority known as the Sindh Technical Education and Vocational Training Authority to manage and regulate technical education and vocational training in the Province.
metadata.territorial_extent: the whole of Province of Sindh
establishes: Sindh Technical Education and Vocational Training Authority (STEVTA)
metadata.one_line: Establishes the STEVTA to manage and regulate technical education and vocational training in Sindh.
metadata.summary: This Act establishes the Sindh Technical Education and Vocational Training Authority (STEVTA) to manage and regulate technical education and vocational training in the Province of Sindh. The Authority is empowered to formulate policies, align programs with industry requirements, evolve curriculum standards, and oversee institutional restructuring. It functions as a body corporate with perpetual succession, responsible for managing resources and ensuring skilled manpower development in coordination with the industry.

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Telemedicine and Telehealth Act, 2021
metadata.long_title: An Act to facilitate, enhance and improve access to healthcare through distant health platform and to ease the shortage of healthcare professionals.
metadata.territorial_extent: the whole of the Province of Sindh
metadata.one_line: This Act facilitates access to healthcare via telemedicine platforms in Sindh while regulating practitioners and patient data.
metadata.summary: The Sindh Telemedicine and Telehealth Act, 2021 aims to improve healthcare access through distant health platforms and address shortages of professionals. It defines key terms like telemedicine, telehealth, and registered medical practitioners, establishing a registry for qualified providers. The Act outlines protocols for consultations, emergency situations, and data privacy, empowering the government to make necessary rules.

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Tenancy (Amendment) Act, 2013
metadata.long_title: An Act to amend the Sind Tenancy Act, 1950.
metadata.one_line: Amends the Sind Tenancy Act, 1950 by updating titles and expanding tenant rights regarding labor and crop expenses.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the Sind Tenancy Act, 1950 to update administrative titles from District Officers to Commissioners and Assistant Commissioners. It expands the definition of crop expenditure to include water course maintenance and clarifies that harvesting and transport charges are borne equally by landlords and tenants. Additionally, it modifies provisions regarding animal labor requirements and omits clauses allowing landlords to take free labor against a tenant's will.

name: SINDH TERMS OF EMPLOYMENT (STANDING ORDERS) ACT, 2015

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Terms of Employment (Standing Orders) Act, 2015
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for regulation of industrial and commercial employment in the Province of the Sindh and for matters connected therewith or ancillary thereto.
metadata.territorial_extent: whole of the Province of the Sindh
repeals: The Industrial and Commercial Employment (Standing Orders) Ordinance, 1968 (W.P. Ordinance No.VI of 1969)
metadata.one_line: Regulates terms of employment, standing orders, and worker classification for industrial and commercial establishments in Sindh.
metadata.summary: This Act regulates industrial and commercial employment within the Province of Sindh by establishing specific standing orders regarding terms of service, wages, and termination. It applies to establishments employing ten or more workers, excluding those under Federal Government authority. The legislation repeals the previous Standing Orders Ordinance of 1968 in its application to Sindh and provides mechanisms for enforcement, penalties, and eviction procedures.

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Textbook Board (Amendment) Act, 2022
metadata.long_title: An Act to amend the Sindh Textbook Board Ordinance, 1970.
metadata.one_line: Amends the Sindh Textbook Board Ordinance, 1970 by substituting 'Chief Minister' for 'Government' in specific sections.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the Sindh Textbook Board Ordinance, 1970 to replace references to the 'Government' with the 'Chief Minister' or 'Chief Secretary, Sindh' in designated sections. The amendments specifically target sections 4, 5, and 13 of the parent Ordinance. It came into force immediately upon enactment.

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Tourist Guides Act, 2011
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the regulation and control of the profession of tourist guides.
metadata.territorial_extent: the whole of Province of Sindh
metadata.max_penalty: fine which may extend to five thousand rupees
metadata.one_line: This Act regulates and controls the profession of tourist guides in Sindh through licensing and a code of conduct.
metadata.summary: The Sindh Tourist Guides Act, 2011 establishes a regulatory framework for tourist guides within the Province of Sindh. It creates a Tourist Guide Regulatory Committee to advise the government and assist in preparing codes of conduct. The Act mandates that all tourist guides must obtain a license from the Government after passing prescribed tests and paying fees, with licenses valid for three years. It also sets maximum service charges, outlines penalties for unlicensed practice or code violations, and empowers the government to make rules regarding fees and procedures.

name: SINDH TRANSFUSION OF SAFE BLOOD ACT, 1997

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Transfusion of Safe Blood Act, 1997
metadata.long_title: An Act to regulate Transfusion of Safe Blood and Blood Products.
metadata.territorial_extent: the whole of the Province of Sindh
metadata.max_penalty: imprisonment up to two years or fine up to five hundred thousand rupees or both
metadata.one_line: Regulates safe blood transfusion, establishes an Authority, and mandates registration for blood banks in Sindh.
metadata.summary: This Act regulates the transfusion of safe and healthy blood free from viruses and infective agents within the Province of Sindh. It establishes the Provincial Blood Transfusion Authority to oversee policy, licensing, and monitoring of blood banks. The legislation imposes strict responsibilities on blood banks regarding donor selection, screening procedures, and equipment standards, while prescribing penalties for contravention.

name: SINDH TRANSPLANTATION OF HUMAN ORGANS AND TISSUES ACT, 2013

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Transplantation of Human Organs and Tissues Act, 2013
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for regulation removal, storage and transplantation of human organs and tissues for therapeutic purposes.
metadata.territorial_extent: the whole of Province of Sindh
metadata.one_line: Regulates the removal, storage, and transplantation of human organs and tissues in Sindh for therapeutic purposes.
metadata.summary: This Act regulates the removal, storage, and transplantation of human organs and tissues within the Province of Sindh specifically for therapeutic purposes. It establishes Evaluation Committees at recognized medical institutions to oversee donations from living relatives or non-relatives after verification, as well as a Monitoring Authority to supervise the process. The legislation defines critical terms such as 'brain dead' and 'death', prohibits commercial dealings in organs, and outlines penalties for unauthorized removal or transplantation.

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Travel Agencies Act, 2011
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the development, regulation and control of the profession of travel agencies in the Province.
metadata.territorial_extent: the whole of the Province of Sindh
metadata.max_penalty: fine which may extend to twenty-five thousand rupees
metadata.one_line: This Act regulates and controls travel agencies in Sindh through licensing, a regulatory committee, and penalties.
metadata.summary: The Sindh Travel Agencies Act, 2011 provides for the development, regulation, and control of travel agencies within the Province of Sindh. It establishes a Travel Agencies Regulatory Committee to advise the government, approve service charges, and assist in preparing a code of conduct. The Act mandates licensing for operators, defines specific exemptions for government enterprises and airlines, and prescribes penalties for non-compliance.

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Trusts (Amendment) Act, 2021
metadata.long_title: An Act to amend the Sindh Trusts Act, 2020.
metadata.one_line: Amends the Sindh Trusts Act, 2020 to regulate specialized trusts and modify registration requirements.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the Sindh Trusts Act, 2020 to introduce new definitions for 'regulator' and 'Specialized Trust'. It modifies registration procedures, requiring No Objection Certifications from relevant regulators for specialized trusts. The Act also updates penalties for non-compliance and allows the government to delegate powers to regulators regarding specialized trusts.

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Trusts Act, 2020
metadata.long_title: An Act to define and amend the law relating to Trusts.
metadata.territorial_extent: the whole of the Province of Sindh
repeals: Trust Act 1882 (to the extent of the Province of Sindh)
establishes: Department of Industries and Commerce Directorate
metadata.administering_body: Industries and Commerce Department, Government of Sindh
metadata.one_line: This Act defines and amends the law relating to trusts in Sindh, regulating their creation, administration, and monitoring.
metadata.summary: The Sindh Trusts Act, 2020 was enacted to define and amend the law relating to trusts in the Province of Sindh. It addresses gaps in the existing Trust Act 1882 regarding monitoring and evaluation purposes and provides for better administrative control following the 18th Constitutional Amendment. The Act applies to both immovable and movable property, outlining requirements for validity, creation, and the duties of trustees while safeguarding the rights of bona fide purchasers.

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Tuberculosis Notification Act, 2014
metadata.long_title: An Act to develop Tuberculosis Notification Forms and distribute copies of the relevant TB Notification Forms to every registered medical practitioner, private clinic, private hospital, registered practitioner, community leader and Incharge of a covered premises operating within the jurisdiction and to provide for matters ancillary thereto
metadata.territorial_extent: the whole of the Province of Sindh
metadata.one_line: This Act establishes a system for developing and distributing TB notification forms to medical practitioners and facilities in Sindh.
metadata.summary: The Sindh Tuberculosis Notification Act, 2014 aims to develop specific notification forms and distribute them to registered medical practitioners, private clinics, hospitals, community leaders, and those in charge of covered premises within the province. It outlines the duties of various stakeholders, including medical practitioners, laboratories, and community representatives, regarding the notification of tuberculosis cases. The Act provides mechanisms for online notification via a Universal Access Number and establishes penalties for breaches of confidentiality or failure to comply with notification requirements.

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Universities and Institutes Laws (Amendment) Act, 2014
metadata.long_title: An Act to amend the certain laws relating to the Universities and Institutes in force in the Province of Sindh.
amends: The Mehran University of Engineering and Technology Act, 1977
The Shah Abdul Latif University Act, 1986
The Institute of Business Administration Act, 1994
The Quaid-e-Awam University of Engineering, Science and Technology, Nawabshah Act, 1996
The Liaquat University of Medical and Health Sciences Ordinance, 2000
The Dow University of Health Sciences Act, 2004
The Sukkur Institute of Business Administration Act, 2006
The Sindh Madressatul Islam University Act, 2012
The Shaheed Benazir Bhutto University of Veterinary and Animal Sciences Sakrand Act, 2012
The Shaheed Zulfiqar Ali Bhutto University of Law, Karachi Act, 2012
The Jinnah Sindh Medical University Act, 2013
metadata.one_line: Amends various Sindh university and institute acts regarding Vice Chancellor appointments and tenure.
metadata.summary: This Act amends several existing laws relating to universities and institutes in the Province of Sindh. The primary purpose is to standardize the appointment process for Vice Chancellors and Directors, requiring them to be eminent academics or distinguished administrators appointed by the Chancellor or Patron on the advice of the Government. It also specifies a four-year tenure with the possibility of extension for one more term under conditions determined by the Government.

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Universities Laws (Amendment) Act, 1997
metadata.long_title: An Act further to amend Sind Universities Laws.
amends: Amendment of University of Karachi Act, 1972
N.E.D. University of Engineering and Technology Act, 1977
Mehran University of Engineering and Technology Act, 1977
metadata.one_line: Amends specific sections of various Sindh university acts to insert a proviso regarding employee retirement procedures.
metadata.summary: This Act further amends the Sind Universities Laws by inserting a new proviso into section 43 of the Shah Abdul Latif University Act, 1986. The amendment requires that no employee be retired without written notice of the grounds for action and a reasonable opportunity to show cause. It also references amendments to sections 40-A of the University of Sindh and Karachi Acts, as well as section 37 of other university acts.

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Universities Laws (Amendment) Act, 2013
metadata.long_title: An Act to amend certain laws relating to the Universities in force in the Province of Sindh.
amends: The Sindh University Act, 1972 (Sind Ordinance No.XVI of 1972)
The University of Karachi Act, 1972 (Sind Act No.XXV of 1972)
The Shaheed Benazir Bhutto University Lyari Act, 2009 (Sindh Act No.I of 2010)
metadata.one_line: Amends laws governing universities in Sindh regarding appointments and administration.
metadata.summary: This Act amends various university laws in the Province of Sindh to ensure uniformity in organization and management. It specifically alters appointment procedures for Vice-Chancellors and Pro-Vice-Chancellors, requiring recommendations from the Government. The Act also updates roles for Registrars, Controllers of Examinations, and other officers, while inserting provisions for equal admission opportunities.

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Vocational Training Council Act, 2006
metadata.long_title: An act to provide for the establishment of a vocational training council in the Province of Sindh.
repeals: The Sindh Vocational Training Council Ordinance, 2006
metadata.one_line: Establishes the Sindh Vocational Training Council to administer vocational training institutes in Sindh.
metadata.summary: This Act establishes the Sindh Vocational Training Council as a body corporate within the Province of Sindh. The Council is empowered to establish and administer vocational training institutes and perform related functions. It outlines the constitution of the Council, including ex-officio members from government departments and private sector representatives, and provides for the creation of a Council Fund.

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Waqaf Properties Act, 2020
metadata.long_title: An Act to make provisions relating to the proper management and administration of Waqf Properties in the Province of Sindh.
metadata.commencement: at once as may be notified by the Government
repeals: The Sindh Waqf Properties Ordinance, 1979 (IX of 1979)
metadata.one_line: This Act regulates the management and administration of Waqf properties in Sindh through appointed administrators.
metadata.summary: The Sindh Waqaf Properties Act, 2020 establishes a framework for the proper management and administration of Waqf properties within the Province of Sindh. It creates the office of the Chief Administrator Auqaf and allows for the appointment of Administrators and Deputy Administrators to assist in these duties. The Act defines key terms related to Waqf, including beneficiaries, waqif, and waqf property, while also incorporating provisions from the Anti-Money Laundering Act, 2010 regarding competent authorities. It repeals the Sindh Waqf Properties Ordinance, 1979, upon its commencement.

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Water Management (Amendment) Act, 2005
metadata.long_title: An Act to amend the Sindh Water Management Ordinance, 2002.
repeals: The Sindh Water Management (Amendment) Ordinance, 2005
metadata.one_line: Amends the Sindh Water Management Ordinance, 2002 regarding appointments and tenure, repealing the 2005 Amendment Ordinance.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the Sindh Water Management Ordinance, 2002 to clarify the appointment of the Chairman and restrictions on holding political office. It also modifies the terms of service for the Chairman and Members of the SIDA. Finally, the Act repeals the Sindh Water Management (Amendment) Ordinance, 2005.

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Water Management (Amendment) Act, 2018
metadata.long_title: An Act to further amend the Sindh Water Management Ordinance, 2002.
metadata.one_line: Amends the Sindh Water Management Ordinance, 2002 to increase women representation in water management boards.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the Sindh Water Management Ordinance, 2002 to enhance female participation in water management structures. It mandates the inclusion of two prominent women members in specific command areas and ensures one woman member is landless in certain sections. The legislation also requires that Board of Watercourses include share croppers among its elected members.

name: SINDH WHOLESALE AGRICULTURAL PRODUCE MARKETS (DEVELOPMENT AND REGULATION) ACT, 2010

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Wholesale Agricultural Produce Markets (Development and Regulation) Act, 2010
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for development and regulation of competitive and transparent wholesale agricultural produce markets in the Province of Sindh.
metadata.territorial_extent: the whole of the Province of Sindh
repeals: The Agricultural Produce Markets Act, 1939
establishes: Board of Directors for notified markets
metadata.max_penalty: fine extending to one hundred thousand rupees, plus a continuing fine of one thousand rupees per day
metadata.one_line: This Act regulates wholesale agricultural produce markets in Sindh by establishing private markets and transferring existing committees to market companies.
metadata.summary: The Act provides for the development and regulation of competitive and transparent wholesale agricultural produce markets in the Province of Sindh. It enables the establishment of private sector markets, promotes private investment, and mandates the transfer of existing notified markets to newly incorporated market companies. The legislation regulates trading modes through open auctions, defines key terms like 'dealer' and 'grower', and establishes penalties for contraventions while repealing the Agricultural Produce Markets Act, 1939 after three years.

metadata.short_title: The Sind Wildlife Protection (Amendment) Act, 1990
metadata.long_title: An Act to amend the Sind Wildlife Protection Ordinance, 1972.
repeals: Sindh Wildlife Protection (Amendment) Ordinance, 1990
metadata.one_line: Amends the Sind Wildlife Protection Ordinance, 1972 and repeals a related 1990 Ordinance.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the Sind Wildlife Protection Ordinance, 1972 by substituting Section 4 to designate the Chief Minister or their nominee as the Chief Game Warden. It also explicitly repeals the Sindh Wildlife Protection (Amendment) Ordinance, 1990. The legislation came into force immediately upon enactment.

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Wildlife Protection (Amendment) Act, 1993
metadata.long_title: An Act to amend the Sind Wildlife Protection Ordinance, 1972.
repeals: The Sindh Wildlife Protection (Amendment) Ordinance, 1993
metadata.one_line: Amends the 1972 Ordinance to include fish in protected species and ban commercial fishing in sanctuaries.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the Sind Wildlife Protection Ordinance, 1972, to substitute 'birds, fish' for 'birds' in section 2. It adds a new sub-section to section 14 prohibiting the leasing or use of wildlife sanctuary waters for commercial fishing or lotus collection. Additionally, it annuls any leases or agreements executed before the coming into force of the 1992 Amendment Ordinance regarding these activities.

metadata.short_title: Sindh Wildlife Protection (Amendment) Act, 2008
metadata.long_title: An Act to amend the Sind Wildlife Protection Ordinance, 1972.
metadata.max_penalty: imprisonment of either description for a term which shall not be less than two months or more than twelve months and with a fine upto four hundred thousand rupees
metadata.one_line: Amends the Sind Wildlife Protection Ordinance, 1972 to increase penalties for illegal hunting of specific game animals.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the Sind Wildlife Protection Ordinance, 1972 to substitute stricter punishments for illegally hunting various game animals. It specifically increases imprisonment terms and fines for hunting rabbits, deer, ibex, urial, and other game birds like sandgrouse. The amendments apply throughout the Province of Sindh and came into force immediately upon enactment.

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Witness Protection Act, 2013
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for protection of witnesses to enable them to give evidence in criminal proceedings in the Province of Sindh.
metadata.territorial_extent: the whole of the Province of Sindh
establishes: Committee to Assist the Head of the Unit
metadata.one_line: This Act establishes a witness protection programme in Sindh to protect witnesses giving evidence in criminal proceedings.
metadata.summary: The Sindh Witness Protection Act, 2013 provides for the protection of witnesses enabling them to give evidence in criminal proceedings within the Province of Sindh. It establishes a Witness Protection Board and a Witness Protection Unit headed by a Chief Witness Protection Officer to manage these protections. The Act outlines various measures including identity changes, relocation, financial assistance, and court orders to ensure witness safety during investigations and trials.

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Workers Welfare Fund (Amendment) Act, 2018
metadata.long_title: An Act to amend the Sindh Workers Welfare Fund Act, 2014.
amends: The Sindh Workers Welfare Fund Act, 2014
metadata.one_line: Amends the Sindh Workers Welfare Fund Act, 2014 regarding committee composition and secretary appointment.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the Sindh Workers Welfare Fund Act, 2014 to update the Standing Committee on Labour and Human Resources membership. It substitutes specific clauses in Section 3, changes the number of members from three to four, replaces 'Health' with 'Finance', and omits certain clauses. Additionally, it modifies Section 9 to specify that the Secretary must be appointed from the PAS, ex-PCS, or PSS group at a rank not below BPS-20.

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Workers Welfare Fund (Amendment) Act, 2021
metadata.long_title: An Act to amend the Sindh Workers Welfare Fund Act, 2014.
key_definitions: Taxation Officer or Officer of Inland Revenue
metadata.one_line: Amends the Sindh Workers Welfare Fund Act, 2014 to align with the Sindh Sales Tax on Services Act, 2011 and update definitions.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the Sindh Workers Welfare Fund Act, 2014 to incorporate provisions from the Sindh Sales Tax on Services Act, 2011 regarding assessment, payment, and recovery. It updates specific clauses in sections 2, 4, 5, and 6 of the parent Act, substitutes references to older acts with newer ones like the Sindh Companies Profits (Workers' Participation) Act, 2015, and introduces new definitions for officers involved in tax administration. The Act also omits certain subsections and adds provisions for provisional payment where income returns are not filed.

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Workers' Compensation Act, 2015
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the payment by certain classes of employers to their workers or their legal heirs of compensation for injury or death by accident.
metadata.territorial_extent: the whole of the Province of Sindh
metadata.one_line: This Act provides for employer payment of compensation to workers or their heirs for injury or death by accident in Sindh.
metadata.summary: The Sindh Workers' Compensation Act, 2015 establishes a legal framework for employers to pay compensation to workers or their legal heirs who suffer injury or death due to accidents. It defines key terms such as 'worker', 'employer', and 'compensation', and outlines the method for calculating wages and determining the amount of compensation payable. The Act also empowers a Commissioner to handle proceedings, register agreements, and recover payments, while specifying penalties for non-compliance.

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Zakat and Ushr Act, 2011
metadata.long_title: An Act to make provisions relating to the assessment, collection and disbursement of Zakat and Ushr.
repeals: The Sindh Zakat and Ushr Act, 2003
metadata.one_line: This Act regulates the assessment, collection, and disbursement of Zakat and Ushr in Sindh.
metadata.summary: The Sindh Zakat and Ushr Act, 2011 establishes a legal framework for the compulsory collection and voluntary disbursement of Zakat and Ushr within the Province of Sindh. It creates specific administrative bodies, including the Sindh Zakat Council and various District, Taluka, Town, and Local Committees, to manage these funds. The Act outlines detailed rules for assessing liabilities on assets such as livestock, minerals, and financial holdings, while also providing exemptions for non-Muslim citizens who declare their faith.

name: SIR COWASJEE JAHANGIR INSTITUTE OF PSYCHIATRY AND BEHAVIORAL SCIENCES, HYDERABAD ACT, 2019

metadata.short_title: The Sir Cowasjee Jahangir Institute of Psychiatry and Behavioral Sciences, Hyderabad Act, 2019
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the establishment of an Institute known as the Sir Cowasjee Jahangir Institute of Psychiatry and Behavioral Sciences at Hyderabad.
establishes: Sir Cowasjee Jahangir Institute of Psychiatry and Behavioral Sciences at Hyderabad
metadata.one_line: Establishes the Sir Cowasjee Jahangir Institute of Psychiatry and Behavioral Sciences at Hyderabad for mental health treatment and education.
metadata.summary: This Act establishes the Sir Cowasjee Jahangir Institute of Psychiatry and Behavioral Sciences at Hyderabad by reconstituting an existing mental hospital. The Institute is empowered to treat mental disorders, manage drug addicts, and provide rehabilitation services throughout Sindh. It also functions as an educational hub affiliated with local universities for training medical professionals in psychiatry and behavioral sciences.

name: SIR SYED UNIVERSITY OF ENGINEERING AND TECHNOLOGY ACT, 1995

metadata.short_title: The Sir Syed University of Engineering and Technology Act, 1995
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for establishment of Sir Syed University of Engineering and Technology at Karachi.
establishes: Sir Syed University of Engineering and Technology
metadata.one_line: Establishes the Sir Syed University of Engineering and Technology in Karachi as an autonomous body.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance establishes the Sir Syed University of Engineering and Technology at Karachi as a body corporate with perpetual succession. It defines the university's powers to provide engineering instruction, admit students regardless of background, and confer degrees. The Act creates various authorities including the Board of Governors, Academic Council, and committees for finance, affiliation, and faculty selection.

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Social Protection Authority (Amendment) Act, 2023
metadata.long_title: An Act to amend the Sindh Social Protection Authority Act, 2022.
metadata.one_line: Amends the Sindh Social Protection Authority Act, 2022 regarding board composition, recruitment terms, and officer grades.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the Sindh Social Protection Authority Act, 2022 to update provisions concerning the appointment of Vice-Chairpersons and additional members. It modifies the tenure of officers from a fixed four-year period to an extendable term and adjusts the required grade for certain officers from BPS-20 to BPS-19/20. Additionally, it increases financial limits and changes the title of the Director General to Chief Executive Officer.

metadata.short_title: The Sohail University Act, 2017
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the establishment of a University known as Sohail University at Karachi and to provide for matters ancillary thereto.
metadata.one_line: Establishes Sohail University at Karachi and defines its powers, structure, and governing bodies.
metadata.summary: This Act establishes the Sohail University at Karachi as a body corporate with perpetual succession. It outlines the composition of the university's leadership, including the Patron, Chancellor, Vice-Chancellor, and Board of Governors. The legislation grants the university powers to confer degrees, prescribe curricula, conduct research, and affiliate with other educational institutions while adhering to moral codes derived from Islamic principles.

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Sports Board (Amendment) Act, 2018
metadata.long_title: An Act to amend the Sindh Sports Board Ordinance, 1980.
metadata.one_line: Amends the Sindh Sports Board Ordinance, 1980 to update the composition and administrative structure of the Board.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the Sindh Sports Board Ordinance, 1980 to redefine the composition of the Sports Board. It substitutes the list of members to include specific government officials, divisional commissioners, and representatives from sports associations. The Act also inserts provisions regarding who presides over meetings and designates the Secretary and Director Sports as the Board's administrative officers.

metadata.short_title: The Stamp (Sind Amendment) Act, 1985
metadata.long_title: An Act to amend the Stamp Act, 1899, in its application to the Province of Sind.
metadata.one_line: Amends the Stamp Act, 1899 to expand definitions of public office and public officer in Sindh.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the application of the Stamp Act, 1899 specifically to the Province of Sind. It inserts new clauses into Section 2 of the 1899 Act to broaden the definition of 'public office' and 'public officer'. The amendments include government offices, local authorities, statutory corporations, commercial concerns with over twenty employees, companies registered under Company Law, and co-operative societies.

metadata.short_title: The Stamp (Sindh Amendment) Act, 1994
metadata.long_title: An Act to amend the Stamp Act, 1899 in its application to the Province of Sindh.
repeals: The Stamp (Sindh Amendment) Ordinance, 1994
metadata.one_line: Amends the Stamp Act, 1899 for Sindh by deleting an exemption clause and repealing a prior Ordinance.
metadata.summary: This Act amends the application of the Stamp Act, 1899 to the Province of Sindh. Specifically, it deletes clause (a) under the 'Exemptions' heading in Article 5 of Schedule-I of the 1899 Act. The Act also repeals the earlier Stamp (Sindh Amendment) Ordinance, 1994.

metadata.summary: This Act amends the Stamp Act 1899 specifically for its application within the Province of Sindh. It substitutes references to 'Provincial Government' with 'Government' and limits the jurisdiction from 'Pakistan' to 'Sindh'. The legislation updates definitions to include electronic technologies and clarifies the roles of the Board of Revenue and Commissioners under Sindh-specific acts.

metadata.short_title: The Stamp (Sindh Amendment) Act, 2020
metadata.long_title: An Act to amend the Stamp Act 1899, in its application to the Province of Sindh.

metadata.summary: This Act amends the Stamp Act 1899 as it applies to the Province of Sindh. It introduces new definitions for 'e-stamp' and 'duly stamped' to accommodate electronic instruments. The legislation also inserts a new section regarding certificates for e-stamps, modifies penalty amounts for unpaid duties, and expands inspection powers to include electronic data.

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Street Children Shelter Home Act, 2018
metadata.long_title: An Act to provide for the welfare and protection of the rights of street children.
metadata.territorial_extent: the whole of Province of Sindh

metadata.one_line: This Act establishes Hamara Ghar to provide welfare, education, and protection for street children in Sindh.
metadata.summary: The Sindh Street Children Shelter Home Act, 2018 provides for the establishment of 'Hamara Ghar' facilities across the province to care for orphaned or abandoned street children until age 18. It creates a Board of Directors comprising government officials, experts, and community representatives to manage the facility's administration, budgeting, and policy. The Act outlines provisions for education, health insurance, scholarships, and funding through government grants and donations, while also defining offences related to discrimination or harm against residents.

metadata.short_title: The Sugar Factories Control (Sindh Amendment) Act, 1993

metadata.summary: This Act amends the Sugar Factories Control Act, 1950 as it applies to Sindh. It removes references to Cane Growers Cooperative Societies from various sections and substitutes specific dates and authorities. The Act also repeals a previous Ordinance on the same subject.

metadata.summary: This Act amends the Sugar Factories Control Act, 1950 as it applies to the province of Sindh. It was enacted on October 25, 1995, and came into force immediately. The primary mechanism is the insertion of a new section (17-A) requiring factories established after the Act's commencement to install a core sampler of specified standards.

It establishes a Board with specific members including government officials and industry representatives to oversee sugar factory operations. The legislation updates sections related to the appointment of an Additional Cane Commissioner, prohibition of certain sugarcane varieties, sale and purchase rules, minimum price fixation mechanisms, and requirements for installing core samplers.

It substitutes sections defining the Vice Chancellor's duties, emergency powers, and authority over staff appointments and examinations. Additionally, it modifies financial reporting requirements by substituting 'Treasurer' with 'Director Finance' and inserting new clauses for account submission timelines.

The Institute is created as a body corporate with perpetual succession, endowed with powers to acquire property, sue, and be sued. It outlines the functions of the Institute, including medical treatment, teaching, research, and publishing, while defining the composition and powers of its governing bodies such as the Board, Academic Council, and Selection Board.

metadata.short_title: The SZABIST University Act, 2023

It establishes the Board of Governors, Academic Council, various committees, and defines the powers and functions of the university authorities. The Act also incorporates existing assets and liabilities, sets out the first statutes in Schedule-I, and repeals the previous Sindh Act No. XI of 1995.

metadata.summary: This Act amends the Sindh Civil Courts Ordinance, 1962 to remove value limits on the original jurisdiction of District Judges. It mandates the transfer of specific pending suits from the High Court to concerned District Judges. It substitutes sections 13 and 20 of the 1973 Act to introduce Defined Contribution Pension Schemes for civil servants appointed after its commencement. The legislation also outlines rules for compassionate allowances upon dismissal and provisional payment of pensions in cases of delayed determination.

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Finance Act, 2024

amends: West Pakistan Act No. XXXII of 1958
metadata.one_line: This Act rationalizes and enhances taxes in Sindh while amending various existing provincial laws.
metadata.summary: The Sindh Finance Act, 2024 is an amendment act designed to rationalize, levy, and enhance specific taxes and duties within the Province of Sindh. It achieves this by substituting, inserting, or omitting clauses in several pre-existing Acts, including the Stamp Act, 1899, and the Sindh Development and Maintenance of Infrastructure Cess Act, 2017. The legislation updates duty rates for items such as immovable property, air tickets, insurance policies, and education services, while also adjusting cess rates based on the weight of goods transported.

It establishes the Sindh Blood Transfusion Authority to oversee these operations and ensure health protection against transfusion-transmissible diseases. The Act defines key terms related to blood products and establishments, sets up committees for safety, and outlines penalties for contraventions while repealing the previous 1997 Act.

The Authority is empowered to formulate policies, manage funds, and oversee services such as cemetery, funeral, and crematorium operations. It defines key terms related to poverty thresholds, grievance redressal, and public servants, while ensuring immunity for officials acting in good faith.

It creates the Sindh Information Commission to oversee these processes and ensures proactive disclosure of organizational details by public authorities. The Act defines various terms such as 'Public Body' and 'Information', sets out procedures for complaints and internal reviews, and prescribes penalties for obstructing access to information.
