The document also provides powers to dissolve market committees and adds a schedule listing various types of agricultural produce.

metadata.short_title: The Agricultural Produce Markets (Amendment) Ordinance, 1981
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to amend the Agricultural Produce Markets Act, 1939.
metadata.one_line: Amends the Agricultural Produce Markets Act, 1939 by substituting and omitting specific words in sections 16 and 19-A.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance amends the Agricultural Produce Markets Act, 1939 to update references from 'Government' to 'such authority' or empowered officers. It also omits references to 'leave salary' in specific subsections of sections 16 and 19-A. The changes apply to the Province of Sindh and came into force immediately upon promulgation.

metadata.short_title: The Sind Agricultural Supplies Organization (Amendment) Ordinance, 1981
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to amend the Sind Agricultural Supplies Organization Act, 1973.
metadata.parent_law: The Sind Agricultural Supplies Organization Act, 1973
amends: The Sind Agricultural Supplies Organization Act, 1973
metadata.one_line: Amends the Sind Agricultural Supplies Organization Act, 1973 regarding the Board and Operational Director.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance amends the Sind Agricultural Supplies Organization Act, 1973 to update provisions concerning the composition and appointment of the Board. It specifically revises section 5 to define the responsibilities of the Operational Director, including administrative duties, procurement, handling, and distribution of improved seeds and fertilizers. The changes are effective immediately upon promulgation by the Governor of Sindh.

metadata.short_title: The Sind Board of Technical Education (Amendment) Ordinance, 1981
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to amend the Sind Board Technical Education Ordinance, 1970.
amends: The Sind Board of Technical Education Ordinance, 1970
metadata.administering_body: Minister for Education, Sind or in his absence the Education Secretary, Government of Sind
metadata.one_line: Amends section 10 of the Sind Board of Technical Education Ordinance, 1970 regarding the designation of the head of the department.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance amends the Sind Board of Technical Education Ordinance, 1970 by updating the title in section 10. The amendment substitutes 'The Minister for Education, Sind or in his absence the Education Secretary, Government of Sind' for the previous reference to 'The Secretary, Government of Sind'. It was promulgated by the Governor of Sindh on August 27, 1981, and came into force immediately.

metadata.short_title: The Sind Building Control (Amendment) Ordinance, 1982
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to amend the Sind Building Control Ordinance, 1979.
metadata.one_line: Amends the Sind Building Control Ordinance, 1979 by defining terms, appointing an Authority, and regulating building licences.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance amends the Sind Building Control Ordinance, 1979 to update definitions regarding architects, builders, and other professionals. It establishes a mechanism for appointing an 'Authority' to oversee building activities within specified areas and creates a fund for that Authority. The document also grants powers to order repairs or demolition of dangerous buildings and outlines the framework for framing regulations concerning fees, licences, and occupancy certificates.

metadata.short_title: The Sind Civil Courts (Amendment) Ordinance, 1981
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to amend the Sind Civil Courts Ordinance, 1962 and to repeal the Sind Court Act, 1926 and the Karachi Courts Order, 1956.
repeals: Sind Court Act, 1926
Karachi Courts Order, 1956
metadata.one_line: Amends the Sind Civil Courts Ordinance, 1962 regarding jurisdiction limits and repeals earlier court acts.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance amends the Sind Civil Courts Ordinance, 1962 to adjust the original jurisdiction of District Judges in civil suits based on value. It specifically addresses jurisdictional limits in the Karachi District and transfers pending suits from the High Court to the District Judge of Karachi. Additionally, it repeals the Sind Court Act, 1926 and the Karachi Courts Order, 1956.

metadata.short_title: The Sind Civil Courts (Second Amendment) Ordinance, 1981
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to amend the Civil courts Ordinance, 1962 and the Sind Civil Courts (Amendment) Ordinance, 1981.
metadata.one_line: Amends the Civil Courts Ordinance, 1962 and the Sind Civil Courts (Amendment) Ordinance, 1981 regarding jurisdiction and fees.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance amends two existing laws: the Civil Courts Ordinance, 1962, and the Sind Civil Courts (Amendment) Ordinance, 1981. It adjusts the jurisdictional limits for civil suits in Karachi Districts by specifying which cases remain with the High Court versus those transferred to the District Court. Additionally, it substitutes the court fee limit from twenty-five thousand rupees to fifty thousand rupees and omits section 4 of the previous amendment ordinance.

metadata.short_title: The Sind Cotton Control (Amendment) Ordinance, 1981
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to amend the Sindh Cotton Control Ordinance, 1966.
metadata.one_line: Amends the Sindh Cotton Control Ordinance, 1966 by substituting terms and inserting a new definition.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance amends the Sindh Cotton Control Ordinance, 1966 to update terminology within the legislation. It substitutes 'Advisory Committees' with 'Cotton Committees', changes 'Extra Assistant Director of Agriculture' to 'Assistant Director of Agriculture', and replaces 'Cotton Control Board' with 'Sind Cotton Board'. Additionally, it omits clause (b) of section 2 and inserts a new definition for 'Cotton Committee'.

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Disposal of Plots Ordinance, 1980
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to regulate the disposal of residential plots and flat sites in the Province of Sindh.
metadata.commencement: at once for this section; remaining provisions on such date as Government may by notification specify
metadata.one_line: Regulates the disposal, size, and eligibility for residential plots and flat sites in Sindh.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance regulates the disposal of residential plots and flat sites within the Province of Sindh. It establishes categories for plot sizes, sets maximum area limits, and defines eligibility criteria for various groups including civil servants, defence personnel, and professionals. The document outlines procedures for auctioning plots, allotting flat sites to construction companies or government organizations, and provides for rules and relaxations by the Government.

metadata.short_title: The Sind Finance (Amendment) Ordinance, 1980
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to amend the Sind Finance Act, 1964.
metadata.commencement: at once and deemed to have taken effect on the 1st day of November, 1980
key_definitions: Industrial undertaking (deemed usage based on Factories Act, 1934)
metadata.one_line: Amends the Sind Finance Act, 1964 to update energy charge rates and schedules.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance amends the Sind Finance Act, 1964 to revise energy charges for various categories of consumers. It substitutes the Fifth Schedule with new rates for domestic, office, commercial, industrial, irrigation, and agricultural machinery uses. The amendment also specifies different charges for energy supplied by a licensee versus other sources and includes an explanation regarding the definition of industrial undertakings.

metadata.short_title: The Sind Finance (Amendment) Ordinance, 1981
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to amend the Sind Finance Act, 1964.
metadata.commencement: at once and be deemed to have taken effect on and from the first day of July, 1980
metadata.one_line: Amends the Sindh Finance Act, 1964 regarding share capital definitions and minimum subscription limits.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance amends the Sindh Finance Act, 1964 to update terminology in its seventh Schedule. Specifically, it substitutes 'paid up share capital' for 'share capital' and reduces a monetary figure from Rs.5,000 to Rs.2,500. The changes are deemed effective from July 1, 1980.

metadata.short_title: The Sind Finance Ordinance, 1980
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to rationalize and enhance certain taxes and duties in the Province of Sind and to amend certain laws.
metadata.one_line: This Ordinance rationalizes taxes in Sindh and amends various Stamp, Entertainments, Motor Vehicle, and Finance Acts.
metadata.summary: The Sind Finance Ordinance, 1980 was promulgated by the Governor to rationalize and enhance specific taxes and duties within the Province of Sind. It amends several existing laws, including the Stamp Act, Entertainments Duty Act, and Motor Vehicles Taxation Act, by updating duty rates and schedules. The document also introduces new tax categories for professions, companies, and factories while omitting certain sections from previous ordinances.

metadata.short_title: The Karachi Development Authority (Sindh Amendment) Ordinance, 1994
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to further amend the Karachi Development Authority Order, 1957.
metadata.one_line: Amends the Karachi Development Authority Order, 1957 to restrict conversion of amenity plots.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance amends the Karachi Development Authority Order, 1957 by substituting clauses in Article 52-A. The amendment prohibits the conversion or utilization of amenity plots reserved for specific purposes for any other use. It was promulgated by the Governor of Sindh under Article 128 of the Constitution because the Provincial Assembly was not in session.

metadata.short_title: The Karachi Water Management Board Ordinance, 1981
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to provide for the establishment of a Board for supply of water in Karachi Division.
metadata.max_penalty: double the amount due for recovery
metadata.one_line: Establishes the Karachi Water Management Board to supply water in Karachi Division.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance establishes the Karachi Water Management Board to manage and distribute water within the Karachi Division. The Board is a body corporate with powers to levy charges, impose penalties for non-payment, and maintain water supply works. It operates under the supervision of the Government of Sind, which appoints its members and approves its rules and regulations.

metadata.short_title: The Land Acquisition (Sindh Amendment) Ordinance, 1992
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to amend the Land Acquisition Act, 1894, in its application to the Province of Sindh.
metadata.administering_body: The Federal Government, the Provincial Government, a Company or a local authority
metadata.one_line: Amends the Land Acquisition Act, 1894 to include Federal and Local authorities in Sindh.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance amends the Land Acquisition Act, 1894 specifically for its application to the Province of Sindh. It substitutes references to 'the Provincial Government' with broader terms including 'The Federal Government', 'the Provincial Government', 'a Company' or 'a local authority'. The amendments affect sections 18, 20, 22-A, 31, and 50 of the said Act. The Ordinance was promulgated by the Governor of Sindh under Article 128 of the Constitution because the Provincial Assembly was not in session.

metadata.short_title: The Sind Land Revenue (Amendment) Ordinance, 1980
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to amend the Sind Land Revenue Act, 1967
metadata.one_line: Amends the Sind Land Revenue Act, 1967 regarding record of rights, mutation registers, and appeal procedures.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance amends the Sind Land Revenue Act, 1967 to update provisions concerning the record of rights and register of mutation. It establishes cells in Mukhtiarkar offices for maintaining land records and mandates notification procedures for acquired rights or interests. The text also modifies sections related to appeals, revisions, and the powers of revenue officers regarding case remand.

metadata.short_title: The Sind Local Government (Amendment) Ordinance, 1980
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to amend the Sind Local Government Ordinance, 1979.
establishes: panchayats for each electoral unit of a council other than a district council or Taluka council
metadata.one_line: Amends the Sind Local Government Ordinance, 1979 regarding panchayats, councils, accounts committees, and complaint procedures.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance amends the Sind Local Government Ordinance, 1979 to establish panchayats for specific electoral units and modify provisions related to council membership and conduct. It introduces new sections detailing the procedure for investigating complaints regarding weights and measures by panchayats, including summoning accused persons and handling appeals. Additionally, it establishes an Accounts committee and adjusts rules concerning council service members and the disposal of pending cases.

metadata.short_title: The Sind Local Government (Amendment) Ordinance, 1981
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to amend the Sind Local Government Ordinance, 1979.
metadata.one_line: Amends the Sind Local Government Ordinance, 1979 regarding elections, honoraria, and place naming.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance amends the Sind Local Government Ordinance, 1979 to address various administrative and structural changes. It clarifies the tenure of council members following a declaration, mandates separate panchayats for minority communities, and regulates honoraria for local leaders. Additionally, it introduces strict guidelines for naming or renaming cities and towns, establishes committees for public consultation on such names, and inserts provisions regarding disciplinary actions for employees of local government boards.

metadata.short_title: The Sind Local Government (Fourth Amendment) Ordinance, 1981
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to amend the Sind Local Government Ordinance, 1979.
metadata.one_line: Amends the Sind Local Government Ordinance, 1979 regarding Taluka Council composition and optional functions.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance amends the Sind Local Government Ordinance, 1979 to alter the composition of Taluka Councils by specifying members from Union Councils and District Councils. It also modifies provisions in sections 37 and 60 regarding legal references and government orders, and updates Schedule II and V concerning optional functions and tolls on goods.

metadata.short_title: The Sind Local Government (Second Amendment) Ordinance, 1980
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to amend the Sind Local Government Ordinance, 1979.
metadata.one_line: Amends the Sind Local Government Ordinance, 1979 regarding member disqualification procedures.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance amends the Sind Local Government Ordinance, 1979 to modify provisions concerning the disqualification of council members. It allows the Government to disqualify a member who acted in contravention of specific subsections without prior notice or hearing. The disqualified member is given sixty days to make a representation for review, after which the Government may issue an order as deemed fit.

metadata.short_title: The Sind Local Government (Second Amendment) Ordinance, 1981
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to amend the Sind Local Government Ordinance, 1979.
metadata.one_line: Amends section 62 of the Sind Local Government Ordinance, 1979 regarding Chief Executive notifications.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance amends the Sind Local Government Ordinance, 1979 by substituting sub-section (2) of section 62. The amendment mandates that if a direction is issued under sub-section (1), the Chief Executive must issue a notification to give effect to it within the specified date. This power applies notwithstanding anything contained in the existing Ordinance.

metadata.short_title: The Sind Local Government (Third Amendment) Ordinance, 1981
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to amend the Sind Local Government Ordinance, 1979.
metadata.one_line: Amends the Sind Local Government Ordinance, 1979 by adding a disqualification clause for council members associated with groups.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance amends the Sind Local Government Ordinance, 1979 to add specific disqualifications for council members. It prohibits members who are associated with any group or association formed before or after their election from working in connection with council activities. Additionally, it disqualifies members who style themselves as leaders of the House or the Opposition in the Council.

metadata.short_title: The Sind Local Government (Third Amendment) Ordinance, 1980
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to amend the Sind Local Government Ordinance, 1979.
metadata.one_line: Amends the Sind Local Government Ordinance, 1979 regarding presiding officers for specific meetings.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance amends the Sind Local Government Ordinance, 1979 by modifying section 51. It adds a proviso specifying that certain meetings involving confidence motions or elections for Mayor, Chairman, Deputy Mayor, or Vice-Chairman shall be presided over by a prescribed person or officer.

name: MEHRAN UNIVERSITY OF ENGINEERING AND TECHNOLOGY (AMENDMENT) ORDINANCE, 1980

metadata.short_title: The Mehran University of Engineering and Technology (Amendment) Ordinance, 1980
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to amend the Mehran University of Engineering and Technology Act, 1977.
amends: The Mehran University of Engineering and Technology Act, 1977
metadata.one_line: Amends the Mehran University of Engineering and Technology Act, 1977 to include a university college at Nawabshah.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance amends the Mehran University of Engineering and Technology Act, 1977 to formally establish a University College at Nawabshah. It modifies sections 3, 13, 15, and 17 of the said Act to incorporate the University College into the university's structure and administration. The Ordinance was promulgated by the Governor of Sindh on June 21, 1980, and came into force immediately.

metadata.short_title: The Military Courts (Validation of Orders) Ordinance, 1980
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to validate certain orders passed by Military Courts under Martial Law Order No.20.
metadata.one_line: Validates orders passed by Military Courts under Martial Law Order No.20 in Sindh and allows appeals to the High Court.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance validates certain orders passed by Military Courts operating under Martial Law Order No.20 made by the Martial Law Administrator Zone 'C'. It deems these orders as having been passed under the Sindh Rented Premises Ordinance, 1979, effective from August 16, 1977. The document grants aggrieved persons the right to prefer an appeal to the High Court within thirty days of the Ordinance's commencement.

metadata.short_title: The Muhammad Ali Jinnah University Ordinance, 1999
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to provide for the establishment of a University at Karachi known as Muhammad Ali Jinnah University.
metadata.one_line: Establishes the Muhammad Ali Jinnah University in Karachi and defines its structure, authorities, and functions.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance establishes the Muhammad Ali Jinnah University at Karachi as a body corporate with perpetual succession. It creates various governing bodies including the Board of Governors, Academic Council, and Finance and Planning Committee to manage academic, administrative, and financial affairs. The document outlines the powers to admit students, confer degrees, affiliate colleges, and prescribe courses of study while ensuring open access regardless of sex, religion, or race.

metadata.short_title: The Pakistan Institute of Management Ordinance, 2008
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to provide for the establishment of an Institute at Karachi known as the Pakistan Institute of Management.
establishes: Board of Advanced Studies and Research
metadata.one_line: Establishes the Pakistan Institute of Management at Karachi and defines its powers, structure, and functions.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance establishes the Pakistan Institute of Management in Karachi as a body corporate with perpetual succession. It outlines the institute's powers to conduct education, research, and confer degrees while remaining under the general control of the Government of Sindh. The document creates various governing bodies including the Board, Academic Council, and Selection Board to manage academic and administrative affairs.

metadata.short_title: The Sind Rented Premises (Amendment) Ordinance, 1980
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to amend the Sindh Rented Premises Ordinance, 1979.
metadata.commencement: at once and deemed to have taken effect on and from the 21st day of November, 1979
metadata.max_penalty: fine which shall not exceed one year's rent of the building or the premises
key_definitions: said Ordinance (refers to Sindh Rented Premises Ordinance, 1979)
metadata.one_line: Amends the 1979 Ordinance regarding landlord possession and reletting restrictions with penalties.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance amends the Sindh Rented Premises Ordinance, 1979 to address issues related to landlord possession of buildings. It omits a specific subsection from section 14, adds words to section 15 regarding applications to the Controller, and inserts a new section 15-A imposing fines on landlords who relet premises or use them for non-personal purposes within one year of obtaining possession. Additionally, it modifies section 27 to ensure pending cases continue under the new provisions and deems prior orders effective under this Ordinance.

metadata.short_title: The Sind Rented Premises (Second Amendment) Ordinance, 1980
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to amend the Sindh Rented Premises Ordinance, 1979.
metadata.one_line: Amends the Sind Rented Premises Ordinance, 1979 regarding landlord age and status exemptions.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance amends the Sind Rented Premises Ordinance, 1979 by substituting a proviso in section 14. The amendment exempts landlords who have retired or attained the age of sixty years, or who are widows or orphans, from certain provisions when renting out buildings. It came into force immediately upon promulgation on September 1, 1980.

metadata.short_title: The Sindh People's Local Government (Amendment) Ordinance, 1974
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to further amend the Sind People's Local Government Ordinance, 1972.
amends: The Sind People's Local Government Ordinance, 1972
metadata.one_line: Amends the Sind People's Local Government Ordinance, 1972 to allow councils to enter contracts without auctions.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance was promulgated by the Governor of Sindh on February 12, 1974, to further amend the Sind People's Local Government Ordinance, 1972. It specifically modifies Section 42 of the parent Ordinance regarding council contracts. The amendment allows a Council to enter into a contract without inviting offers in an auction, provided they have the approval of the Government.

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Agricultural Income Tax (Amendment) Ordinance, 1997
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to amend the Sindh Agricultural Income Tax Act, 1994 and Act II of 1899.
metadata.commencement: on the date of its promulgation
metadata.one_line: Amends the Sindh Agricultural Income Tax Act, 1994 and Act II of 1899 regarding tax rates and assessment procedures.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance amends the Sindh Agricultural Income Tax Act, 1994 and Act II of 1899 to update tax rates and definitions. It modifies sections related to taxable income, agricultural land classification, and the powers of the Collector. The document also introduces provisions to protect taxpayers from harassment during assessment proceedings.

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Agricultural Income Tax (Amendment) Ordinance, 1997
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to amend the Sindh Agricultural Income Tax Act, 1994.
amends: The Sindh Agricultural Income Tax Act, 1994
metadata.max_penalty: two and a half times the amount of tax evaded (or not less than that amount)
metadata.one_line: Amends the Sindh Agricultural Income Tax Act, 1994 by defining terms, setting tax rates, and imposing penalties.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance amends the Sindh Agricultural Income Tax Act, 1994 to update definitions of 'cropped area' and 'tax year'. It establishes specific tax rates for various crops like cotton, wheat, and rice, distinguishing between barrage and non-barrage areas. The document also introduces new penalties for failing to furnish declarations or complying with notices, and mandates a shift to net income assessment starting July 1, 1998.

name: SINDH ARID ZONE DEVELOPMENT AUTHORITY (AMENDMENT) ORDINANCE, 1997

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Arid Zone Development Authority (Amendment) Ordinance, 1997
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to amend the Sindh Arid Zone Development Authority Act, 1985.
metadata.parent_law: The Sindh Arid Zone Development Authority Act, 1985
amends: The Sindh Arid Zone Development Authority Act, 1985
metadata.one_line: Amends the Sindh Arid Zone Development Authority Act, 1985 to add a Vice Chairman role and define its functions.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance amends the Sindh Arid Zone Development Authority Act, 1985 to introduce the position of Vice Chairman. It adds 'Vice Chairman' to the definition of office holders and specifies that this role must be held by a Member of the Provincial Assembly. The Ordinance also establishes that the Vice Chairman's office is not a whole-time remunerated position and defines their duties as assigned by the Chairman.

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Healthcare Commission Ordinance, 2013
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to improve the quality of healthcare services and banning quackery in the Province of Sindh in all its forms and manifestations
metadata.territorial_extent: the whole of the Province of Sindh
metadata.one_line: Establishes the Sindh Healthcare Commission to improve healthcare quality and ban quackery in Sindh.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance establishes the Sindh Healthcare Commission to regulate healthcare services and ban quackery within the Province of Sindh. It defines the composition, functions, and powers of the Commission and its Board, including the authority to issue licenses, set standards, conduct inspections, and investigate medical negligence. The legislation also empowers the Commission to make regulations regarding fees, staff qualifications, equipment standards, and price controls for healthcare services.

metadata.short_title: The Sindh (Textile Institute of Pakistan) Ordinance, 1999
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to provide for the establishment of a Textile Institute in the Province of Sindh.
metadata.one_line: Establishes the Textile Institute of Pakistan in Sindh with powers for education, research, and examinations.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance establishes the Textile Institute of Pakistan as a body corporate within the Province of Sindh. It defines the institute's structure, including the Patron, Chancellor, President, Board of Governors, and various councils. The document outlines the institute's functions such as providing instruction in textile sciences, admitting students, conducting examinations, and managing funds. It also grants legal immunity to officers acting in good faith under the Ordinance.

name: SINDH BOARD OF INTERMEDIATE AND SECONDARY EDUCATION (AMENDMENT) ORDINANCE, 1995

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Board of Intermediate and Secondary Education (Amendment) Ordinance, 1995
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to amend the Sind Boards of Intermediate and Secondary Education Ordinance, 1972.
metadata.parent_law: The Sind Boards of Intermediate and Secondary Education Ordinance, 1972
amends: The Sind Boards of Intermediate and Secondary Education Ordinance, 1972
subjects: Boards of Intermediate and Secondary Education
establishes: Board of Intermediate and Secondary Education Larkana
metadata.one_line: Amends the 1972 Ordinance to establish a new Board in Larkana and update references.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance amends the Sind Boards of Intermediate and Secondary Education Ordinance, 1972. It substitutes 'Boards at Sukkur and Larkana' for 'Board at Sukkur' and adds a new clause establishing the Board of Intermediate and Secondary Education Larkana. The amendments also update references in sections 3, 4, and the Schedule to include Larkana.

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Buildings Control (Amendment) Ordinance, 1997
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to amend the Sind Buildings Control Ordinance, 1979.
metadata.one_line: Amends the Sind Buildings Control Ordinance, 1979 regarding compounding of building work offences.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance amends the Sind Buildings Control Ordinance, 1979 to prohibit the compounding of certain offences. Specifically, it substitutes a proviso in section 19, sub-section (1-A) of the parent Ordinance. The amendment states that no offence relating to building works commenced or carried out in violation of regulations under section 21-A shall be compounded. It was promulgated by the Governor of Sindh because the Provincial Assembly was not in session.

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Civil Courts (Amendment) Ordinance, 1994
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to further amend the Sind Civil Courts Ordinance, 1962.
metadata.one_line: Amends the Sind Civil Courts Ordinance, 1962 by increasing a monetary limit in section 18.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance amends the Sind Civil Courts Ordinance, 1962 to update a specific monetary figure within Section 18. It was promulgated by the Governor of Sindh under Article 128 of the Constitution because the Provincial Assembly was not in session. The amendment substitutes 'five hundred thousand' for 'two lacs and fifty thousand' in the relevant clause.

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Civil Servants (Amendment) Ordinance, 2008
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to amend the Sind Civil Servants Act, 1973.
metadata.one_line: Amends the Sind Civil Servants Act, 1973 by omitting section 9-A.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance amends the Sind Civil Servants Act, 1973. It was promulgated by the Governor of Sindh because the Provincial Assembly was not in session and immediate action was deemed necessary. The primary mechanism is the omission of section 9-A from the existing Act.

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Compulsory Primary Education Ordinance, 2001
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to provide for compulsory education in the Province of Sindh.
metadata.commencement: at once; other provisions as notified; enforced in all Districts by June, 2004
repeals: The Sindh Primary Education Ordinance, 1962
metadata.max_penalty: fine extending to fifty hundred rupees with a further fine of twenty five rupees for every day after conviction
metadata.one_line: This Ordinance makes primary education compulsory for children in Sindh and establishes authorities to enforce attendance.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance provides for compulsory primary education for every child in the Province of Sindh. It defines key terms such as 'child', 'parent', and 'primary school', and mandates that parents ensure their children attend school unless there is a reasonable excuse. The Ordinance establishes Authorities to oversee attendance and issue orders against non-compliant parents, with specific penalties for offences including employing children who should be in school.

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Development Authority (Amendment) Ordinance, 1997
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to amend certain laws relating to development authorities in force in certain areas of the Province of Sindh.
amends: The Badin Amendment of Sindh Act V of 1994
metadata.one_line: Amends development authority acts in Sindh to replace Chairman references with Commissioner of the Chairman.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance amends specific laws relating to development authorities within certain areas of the Province of Sindh. It was promulgated by the Governor because the Provincial Assembly was not in session and immediate action was deemed necessary under Article 128 of the Constitution. The primary mechanism involves substituting references to the 'Chairman' with the 'Commissioner of the Chairman' in specific sections of acts governing the Sehwan, Badin, Lyari, and Malir development authorities.

name: SINDH DISPOSAL OF URBAN LAND ORDINANCE, 1999

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Disposal of Urban Land Ordinance, 1999
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to regulate the disposal of urban land in the Province of Sindh and to provide for matters ancillary thereto.
repeals: The Sindh Disposal of Plots Ordinance, 1980
metadata.one_line: Regulates the disposal of urban land in Sindh through auctions, schemes, and specific plot types.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance regulates the disposal of urban land within the Province of Sindh to ensure transparency and adherence to market prices. It mandates that land be disposed of primarily through open auction, with specific provisions for amenity plots, residential plots, and incremental housing. The document also outlines procedures for laying out land, sanctioning schemes, renewing existing leases, and repealing previous conflicting legislation.

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Finance (Second Amendment) Ordinance, 1995
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to amend the Sind Finance Act, 1964.
metadata.one_line: Amends the Sind Finance Act, 1964 by deleting specific words regarding industrial undertakings and energy charges in its Fifth Schedule.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance amends the Sind Finance Act, 1964 to delete specific references to 'industrial under-takings' and energy rates in the Fifth Schedule. It was promulgated by the Governor of Sindh because the Provincial Assembly was not in session. The changes take effect immediately upon promulgation.

name: SINDH HEALTH INSTITUTIONS (ESTABLISHMENT AND MANAGEMENT) ORDINANCE, 2008

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Health Institutions (Establishment and Management) Ordinance, 2008
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to provide for the establishment and management of health institutions in the Province of Sindh.
metadata.commencement: at once and deemed to have taken effect on 24th October, 2007
metadata.one_line: Establishes health institutions in Sindh as autonomous bodies corporate managed by a Board of Governors.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance provides for the establishment and management of health institutions in the Province of Sindh, granting them autonomy to provide quality healthcare. It creates a Board of Governors consisting of official and non-official members to oversee administration and management. The document outlines provisions for appointing officers, managing funds, auditing accounts, and making rules and regulations necessary for the Ordinance's implementation.

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Information Technology Board Ordinance, 1999
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to provide for the establishment of a Board of Information Technology in the Province of Sindh.
metadata.one_line: Establishes the Sindh Information Technology Board to promote and develop information technology in Sindh.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance establishes the Sindh Information Technology Board as a body corporate within the Province of Sindh. The Board is empowered to promote information technology use, formulate schemes, procure equipment, and engage in research and consultancy. It consists of a Chairman and members appointed by the Government, with powers to make rules and regulations for its functioning.

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Laws (Amendment) Ordinance, 2001
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to amend certain laws in force in the Province of Sindh.
metadata.commencement: at once and be deemed always to have taken effect from 14th August, 2001
amends: The Charitable Funds (Regulation and Collections) Act, 1953
The Sind Court of Wards Act, 1905
The Sind Prevention of Gambling Ordinance, 1978
The Sind Land Tax and Agriculture Ordinance, 2000
The Colonization of Government Lands Acts, 1912
metadata.one_line: Amends various Sindh and Federal laws applicable to Sindh by substituting revenue officer titles.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance amends a wide range of existing laws in force in the Province of Sindh to update terminology related to revenue administration. It substitutes terms like 'Collector' with 'District Officer (Revenue)' and 'Commissioner' with 'Executive District Officer (Revenue)' across various Acts from 1883 to 2000. The amendments also introduce new designations such as 'Chief Inspector of Stamps' and 'District Co-ordination Officer' in specific contexts. The Ordinance comes into force immediately and is deemed effective from August 14, 2001.

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Local Government (Second Amendment) Ordinance, 1994
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to amend the Sind Local Government Ordinance, 1979.
metadata.one_line: Amends the Sind Local Government Ordinance, 1979 by adding provisions for an Advisory Council in Panchayats.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance amends the Sind Local Government Ordinance, 1979 to introduce new sub-sections regarding an Advisory Council. It allows the Government to appoint such a council to perform assigned functions within Panchayats. The text defines the tenure and resignation process for council members and specifies that the Chairman's powers may be exercised by a designated member if no council is appointed.

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Local Government (Third Amendment) Ordinance, 1994
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to amend the Sind Local Government Ordinance, 1979.
metadata.one_line: Amends the Sind Local Government Ordinance, 1979 to transfer functions and assets from Zonal Municipal Committees to the Karachi Metropolitan Corporation.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance amends the Sind Local Government Ordinance, 1979 to restructure local governance in Sindh. It deletes specific clauses and provisions related to Zonal Municipal Committees while substituting references to district councils. The document transfers assets, liabilities, and employees of Zonal Municipal Committees to the Karachi Metropolitan Corporation and updates schedules regarding functions and taxes levied by municipal bodies.

name: SINDH MINISTERS (SALARIES, ALLOWANCES AND PRIVILEGES) (AMENDMENT) ORDINANCE, 2008

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Ministers (Salaries, Allowances and Privileges) (Amendment) Ordinance, 2008
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to amend the Sind Ministers (Salaries, Allowances and Privileges) Act, 1975.
metadata.parent_law: The Sind Ministers (Salaries, Allowances and Privileges) Act, 1975
amends: The Sind Ministers (Salaries, Allowances and Privileges) Act, 1975
metadata.one_line: Amends the 1975 Act to grant Ministers facilities including government guest houses and transport.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance amends the Sind Ministers (Salaries, Allowances and Privileges) Act, 1975 by adding a new subsection to section 19. It grants Chief Ministers and Ministers entitlement to facilities such as Government guest houses, rest houses, circuit houses, and Sindh House at Islamabad and Murree. The amendment also includes provisions for pick and drop facilities via car during their stay on payment of usual charges.

name: SINDH PRIVATE TEACHERS’ TRAINING INSTITUTIONS (REGISTRATION AND CONTROL) ORDINANCE, 1994

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Private Teachers' Training Institutions (Registration and Control) Ordinance, 1994
metadata.long_title: An Act to regulate the functioning of private teachers' training institutions in the Province of Sindh.
metadata.commencement: at once for this section; on such date as may be notified by Government in the Official Gazette for remaining provisions
metadata.max_penalty: imprisonment up to one year or fine up to fifty thousand rupees or both
metadata.administering_body: Government of Sindh (via the Registration Authority, Director, Bureau of Curriculum and Extension Wing, Sindh)
metadata.one_line: This Ordinance regulates private teachers' training institutions in Sindh by mandating registration, setting standards, and imposing penalties for non-compliance.
metadata.summary: The Sindh Private Teachers' Training Institutions (Registration and Control) Ordinance, 1994 was promulgated by the Governor of Sindh to regulate private institutions providing teacher training. It establishes a mandatory registration process where applications are reviewed by a Registration Authority based on criteria such as building hygiene, staff qualifications, and fee structures. The Ordinance outlines procedures for granting certificates, suspending or cancelling them upon contravention, and provides for appeals to the Government. It also defines offences for running unregistered institutions, prescribing penalties of imprisonment up to one year or fines up to fifty thousand rupees.

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Public Service Commission (Amendment) Ordinance, 1999
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to amend the Sindh Public Service Commission Act, 1989.
metadata.parent_law: The Sindh Public Service Commission Act, 1989
metadata.one_line: Amends the Sindh Public Service Commission Act, 1989 regarding the term of office for Chairman and members.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance amends the Sindh Public Service Commission Act, 1989 to allow the Government to curtail the term of office for the Chairman and members appointed before its enactment. It was promulgated by the Governor of Sindh because the Provincial Assembly was not in session. The amendment specifically targets section 5-A of the parent Act.

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Registration (Amendment) Ordinance, 1997
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to amend the Registration Act, 1908, in its application to the Province of Sindh.
metadata.one_line: Amends the Registration Act, 1908 in Sindh to include power of attorney for selling immovable property.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance amends the Registration Act, 1908 specifically for its application to the Province of Sindh. It was promulgated by the Governor because the Provincial Assembly was not in session. The amendment adds a new clause (f) to Section 17, sub-section (1), clause (e) of the Registration Act, 1908. This addition explicitly includes 'power of attorney when authorizing the attorney to sell any immovable property' within the scope of registration requirements.

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Registration of Godowns Ordinance, 1995
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to provide for the registration of godowns in the Province of Sindh.
metadata.territorial_extent: the whole of the Province of Sindh
metadata.max_penalty: imprisonment for a term which may extend to one year or with fine which may extend to one thousand rupees
metadata.one_line: This Ordinance provides for the registration, maintenance, and inspection of godowns storing essential articles in Sindh.
metadata.summary: The Sindh Registration of Godowns Ordinance, 1995 was promulgated by the Governor to regulate the storage of essential articles in the Province of Sindh. It mandates the registration of existing and new godowns within specific timeframes and requires owners to maintain records for inspection. The Ordinance grants the Registering Authority powers to search premises and imposes penalties for non-compliance or false information.

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Sports Board (Amendment) Ordinance, 1992
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to amend the Sind Sports Board Ordinance, 1980.
metadata.one_line: Amends the Sind Sports Board Ordinance, 1980 by adding a new secretary post and substituting section 4.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance amends the Sind Sports Board Ordinance, 1980 to update its administrative structure. It inserts a new item regarding the Secretary to the Government of Sindh in the Culture and Tourism Department. Additionally, it substitutes Section 4(2) to clarify that the Secretary and Director of Sports serve as the Joint Secretary and Secretary of the Board respectively.

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Wildlife Protection (Amendment) Ordinance, 1992
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to amend the Sind Wildlife Protection Ordinance, 1972.
metadata.one_line: Amends the 1972 Ordinance to restrict commercial fishing and leases in wildlife sanctuaries.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance amends the Sind Wildlife Protection Ordinance, 1972, to update definitions of protected species and restrict commercial activities. It specifically prohibits leasing or using fishing waters within wildlife sanctuaries for fishing or collecting lotus/roots for commercial purposes. Additionally, any leases or agreements executed before this Ordinance came into force regarding these prohibited activities are declared void.

metadata.short_title: The Sind Sports Board (Amendment) Ordinance, 1982
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to amend the Sind Sports Board Ordinance, 1980.
metadata.one_line: Amends the Sind Sports Board Ordinance, 1980 by substituting 'affiliate' for 'register'.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance amends the Sind Sports Board Ordinance, 1980 to replace the term 'register' with 'affiliate' in specific sections. It was promulgated by the Governor of Sindh on January 30, 1982, and comes into force immediately. The changes affect clauses regarding registration and affiliation within the said Ordinance.

metadata.short_title: The Stamp (Sind Amendment) Ordinance, 1981
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to amend the Stamp Act, 1899, in its application to the Province of Sind.
metadata.one_line: Amends the Stamp Act, 1899 regarding duty on shares and debentures in Sindh.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance amends the application of the Stamp Act, 1899 to the Province of Sind. It specifically substitutes clauses in Schedule I, Article 62 to define the face value thresholds for shares and debentures liable to duty. The changes adjust the minimum face values for shares and debentures subject to stamp duty.

metadata.short_title: The Stamp (Sindh Amendment) Ordinance, 1997
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to amend the Stamp Act, 1899, in its application to the Province of Sindh.
metadata.max_penalty: ten thousand rupees
metadata.one_line: Amends the Stamp Act, 1899 in Sindh regarding power of attorney registration and penalties for obstruction.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance amends the Stamp Act, 1899 to apply specifically to the Province of Sindh. It adds provisions requiring registering authorities to verify that sale consideration has been paid before registering deeds executed under a power of attorney. The text also introduces new sections regarding reporting unstamped instruments and imposes penalties for obstructing the Collector or concealing information.

metadata.short_title: The Stamp (Sindh Amendment) Ordinance, 1994
metadata.long_title: An Act to amend the Stamp Act, 1899, in its application to the Province of Sindh.
metadata.one_line: Amends the Stamp Act, 1899 in Sindh by deleting a specific exemption clause.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance amends the application of the Stamp Act, 1899 to the Province of Sindh. It was promulgated by the Governor because the Provincial Assembly was not in session and immediate action was deemed necessary. The primary mechanism is the deletion of clause (a) under the heading 'Exemptions' in Article 5 of the Schedule-I of the Stamp Act, 1899.

metadata.short_title: The Sugar Factories Control (Amendment) Ordinance, 1980
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to amend the Sugar Factories Control Act, 1950.
metadata.one_line: Amends the Sugar Factories Control Act, 1950 by substituting board names.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance amends the Sugar Factories Control Act, 1950 to update specific terminology within sections 2 and 3. It replaces references to the 'Sugarcane Control Board' with the 'Sugar Factories Control Board'. The document was promulgated by the Governor of Sindh on November 15, 1980, and comes into force immediately.

metadata.short_title: The Sind Finance (Amendment) Ordinance, 1979
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to amend the Sind Finance Act, 1963.
metadata.one_line: Amends the Sind Finance Act, 1963 by modifying Section 16 regarding officer authorization and sub-sections.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance amends the Sind Finance Act, 1963 specifically within Section 16. It substitutes references to sub-sections (2-b) and (2-c) and inserts provisions allowing other officers authorized by Government or subordinate authorities to act alongside the Director-General.

metadata.short_title: The Sind Universities Laws (Amendment) Ordinance, 1982
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to amend the enactments relating to Universities in Sind.
amends: The N.E.D. University of Engineering and Technology Act, 1977
The Mehran University of Engineering and Technology Act, 1997
subjects: Sindh Acts XXIV and XXV of 1972
Sind Acts II and IV of 1977
metadata.one_line: Amends university acts in Sindh regarding appointment pay scales and selection board recommendations.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance amends several enactments relating to universities in Sind to update provisions concerning appointment pay scales. Specifically, it substitutes clauses in the University of Sind Act, 1972, and the University of Karachi Act, 1972 regarding appointments to National Scales of pay up to grade 16 and grades 17 and above. It also amends the N.E.D. University of Engineering and Technology Act, 1977, the Mehran University of Engineering and Technology Act, 1997, and the Sind Agriculture University Act, 1977 with similar substitutions regarding pay scales and selection board recommendations.

metadata.short_title: The Sindh University Laws (Amendment) Ordinance, 1980
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to amend the University Laws.
amends: The N.E.D. University of Engineering and Technology Act, 1977
The Mehran University of Engineering and Technology Act, 1977
metadata.one_line: Amends university acts to update syndicate composition, add Islamic studies, and adjust auditing requirements.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance amends several University Acts in Sindh to modernize their structures and requirements. It updates the composition of university Syndicates by adding specific members like representatives from student unions and provincial assemblies while reducing certain other seats. The legislation mandates a compulsory 'Islamic and Pakistan Studies' discipline for Muslim students and offers an alternative Ethics course for non-Muslims. Additionally, it changes auditing procedures to require approval by a Resident Auditor appointed by the Provincial Audit Department before university expenditures can be made.

metadata.short_title: The Sind University Laws (Amendment) Ordinance, 1981
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to amend the University Laws.
amends: The N.E.D. University of Engineering and Technology Act, 1977
The Mehran University of Engineering and Technology Act, 1977
metadata.one_line: Amends university laws regarding appointments, Senate composition, and employee service conditions in Sindh.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance amends the University Laws of Sindh to update provisions for appointing Pro-Vice-Chancellors and modifying Senate membership rules. It alters appointment procedures for Deans and Department Chairmen while ensuring favorable terms for transferred employees. The legislation also updates statutes regarding faculty appointments and adds clauses concerning member attendance and resignation.

metadata.short_title: The Sind Waqf Properties (Amendment) Ordinance, 1981
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to amend the Sindh Waqf Properties Ordinance, 1979.
metadata.one_line: Amends the 1979 Ordinance to allow transfer of waqf properties to local councils.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance amends the Sindh Waqf Properties Ordinance, 1979. It authorizes the Government to transfer waqf properties taken over under section 7(1) to any Council constituted under the Sind Local Government Ordinance, 1979. Upon such transfer, the Council or its authorized members exercise the powers of the Chief Administrator, while authorized persons with Government approval exercise the powers of the Administrator regarding the transferred property.

metadata.short_title: The Sind Abkari (Amendment) Ordinance, 1984
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to amend the Sind Abkari Act, 1878.
metadata.one_line: Amends the Sind Abkari Act, 1878 to restrict licenses for Muslims and ensure hearing opportunities.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance amends the Sind Abkari Act, 1878 in response to directions from the Federal Shariat Court. It inserts a new section restricting the issuance of licenses, permits, or passes to Muslims except for specific purposes defined under the Prohibition (Enforcement of Hadd) Order, 1979. Additionally, it ensures that no appeal or revision order is passed without giving the affected person an opportunity to be heard.

metadata.short_title: The Abkari Laws (Sind Amendment) Ordinance, 1977
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to further amend the Sind Abkari Act, 1878, the Sind Consumption of Intoxicants Restriction Act, 1940 and the West Pakistan Prohibition of Opium Smoking Ordinance, 1960.
amends: Sind Consumption of Intoxicants Restriction Act, 1940
West Pakistan Prohibition of Opium Smoking Ordinance, 1960
metadata.one_line: Amends three specific Acts and an Ordinance regarding abkari laws, intoxicants, and opium smoking in Sindh.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance amends the Sind Abkari Act, 1878, the Sind Consumption of Intoxicants Restriction Act, 1940, and the West Pakistan Prohibition of Opium Smoking Ordinance, 1960. It was promulgated by the Governor of Sindh because the Provincial Assembly was not in session. The amendments restrict trial jurisdiction to Courts of the Magistrate of the First Class for offences under these laws and transfer pending cases to such courts.

metadata.short_title: The Agricultural Produce Markets (Sind Amendment) Ordinance, 1984
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to amend the Agricultural Produce Markets Act, 1939.
metadata.one_line: Amends the Agricultural Produce Markets Act, 1939 to add procedural safeguards regarding hearings and notices.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance amends the Agricultural Produce Markets Act, 1939 in response to directions from the Federal Shariat Court. It introduces requirements for giving affected persons an opportunity to be heard before orders are passed by the Deputy Commissioner. Additionally, it mandates that market committee members must be given a chance to show cause before action is taken against them.

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Agricultural Income Tax (Amendment) Ordinance, 1997
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to amend the Sindh Agricultural Income Tax Act, 1994.
metadata.parent_law: The Sindh Agricultural Income Tax Act, 1994
amends: The Sindh Agricultural Income Tax Act, 1994
metadata.max_penalty: two and a half times the amount of tax evaded
metadata.one_line: Amends the Sindh Agricultural Income Tax Act, 1994 regarding tax rates, definitions, and penalties.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance amends the Sindh Agricultural Income Tax Act, 1994 to update definitions of cropped area and tax year. It establishes specific tax rates for various crops like cotton, wheat, and orchards, while exempting small holdings in certain areas. The document also introduces penalties for failing to furnish declarations or complying with notices regarding cultivated land.

metadata.short_title: The Agricultural Produce Markets (Amendment) Ordinance, 1983
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to amend the Agricultural Produce Markets Act, 1939.
subjects: Director General, Bureau of Supply and Prices
metadata.administering_body: Director General, Bureau of Supply and Prices, Sind
metadata.one_line: Amends the Agricultural Produce Markets Act, 1939 regarding market committees, fees, land acquisition, and penalties.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance amends the Agricultural Produce Markets Act, 1939 to update provisions concerning market committees, licensing requirements for agricultural produce sales, and fee structures. It also modifies sections related to land acquisition procedures and penalties for non-payment of fines. The changes are administered by the Director General, Bureau of Supply and Prices, Sind.

metadata.short_title: The Agricultural Produce Markets (Amendment) Ordinance, 1993
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to amend the Agricultural Produce Markets Act, 1939.
metadata.one_line: Amends the Agricultural Produce Markets Act, 1939 by substituting the Director General of Agriculture Extension for the Bureau of Supply and Prices.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance amends the Agricultural Produce Markets Act, 1939 to update the designation of the Director General. The change substitutes 'Director General, Agricultural, Extension' for 'Director General, Bureau of Supply and Prices, Sindh'. It was promulgated by the Governor of Sindh because the Provincial Assembly was not in session.

metadata.short_title: The Agricultural Produce Markets (Amendment) Ordinance, 1993
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to amend the Agricultural Produce Markets Act, 1939.
metadata.one_line: Amends the Agricultural Produce Markets Act, 1939 by substituting the Director General of Agriculture for the Director General of Bureau of Supply and Prices.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance amends the Agricultural Produce Markets Act, 1939 to replace references to the Director General, Bureau of Supply and Prices with the Director General, Agriculture. It was promulgated by the Governor of Sindh under Article 128 of the Constitution because the Provincial Assembly was not in session. The amendment takes effect from August 25, 1993, despite being promulgated on September 25, 1993.

metadata.short_title: The Sind Agricultural Supplies Organization (Amendment) Ordinance, 1984
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to amend the Sind Agricultural Supplies Organization Act, 1973.
metadata.parent_law: The Sind Agricultural Supplies Organization Act, 1973
metadata.one_line: Amends the Sind Agricultural Supplies Organization Act, 1973 regarding rent assessment provisions.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance amends the Sind Agricultural Supplies Organization Act, 1973 in response to directions from the Federal Shariat Court. It adds a new sub-section to section 14 of the parent Act concerning rent assessments. The amendment stipulates that assessed rent must not be less than the prevailing area rent and must comply with the Sindh Rented Premises Ordinance, 1979.

metadata.short_title: The Sind Agriculture University (Amendment) Ordinance, 1984
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to amend the Sind Agriculture University Act, 1977.
metadata.one_line: Amends the Sind Agriculture University Act, 1977 regarding appeals and administrative good faith.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance amends the Sind Agriculture University Act, 1977 to address directions from the Federal Shariat Court. It modifies Section 36 to require an opportunity of being heard before making orders in appeal or review. Additionally, it inserts the phrase 'in good faith' into Section 45 of the said Act.

metadata.short_title: The Sind Agriculturists' Loans (Amendment) Ordinance, 1982
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to amend the Sind Agriculturists' Loans Act, 1958.
metadata.commencement: at once and deemed to have taken effect on and from the 1st day of July, 1982
metadata.one_line: Amends the Sind Agriculturists' Loans Act, 1958 to make loans interest-free and introduce Qarz-e-Hasna.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance amends the Sind Agriculturists' Loans Act, 1958 to ensure that all loans made or seed sold on credit are interest-free. It specifically designates loans for small land holders with subsistence holdings as 'Qarz-e-Hasana'. The document also modifies recovery procedures and omits references to interest in specific sections of the parent Act.

name: AO POST GRADUATE INSTITUTE OF ORTHOPAEDIC SCIENCES ORDINANCE, 2013

metadata.short_title: The AO Post Graduate Institute of Orthopaedic Sciences Ordinance, 2013
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to provide for the establishment of an Institute known as the AO Post Graduate Institute of Orthopaedic Sciences and to provide for matters ancillary thereto.
establishes: AO Post Graduate Institute of Orthopaedic Sciences
metadata.one_line: Establishes the AO Post Graduate Institute of Orthopaedic Sciences and defines its powers, functions, and authorities.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance establishes the AO Post Graduate Institute of Orthopaedic Sciences as a body corporate with perpetual succession. It outlines the institute's powers to conduct postgraduate teaching programs in orthopaedics, undertake research, and admit students. The document creates various governing bodies including the Board of Governors, Academic Council, and specific committees for finance, discipline, and affiliation.

metadata.short_title: The Badin Development Authority Ordinance, 1995
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to make provisions for the development improvement and beautification of the areas comprising taluka Badin and other areas of Badin District and to establish an Authority for such purpose.
metadata.territorial_extent: the areas comprising taluka of Badin District and such other areas of Badin District as Government may from time to time specify by notification
metadata.one_line: Establishes the Badin Development Authority to develop, improve, and beautify Badin District areas.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance establishes the Badin Development Authority to oversee the development, improvement, and beautification of Badin District. The Authority is empowered to formulate schemes, manage water supply and drainage, acquire land, and maintain public infrastructure. It also consolidates powers previously held by local councils within its jurisdiction.

metadata.short_title: The Baqai University Ordinance, 1993
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to provide for the establishment of the Baqai University at Karachi.
metadata.one_line: Establishes the Baqai University at Karachi and defines its authorities, officers, and powers.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance establishes the Baqai University at Karachi as a body corporate with perpetual succession. It creates various governing bodies including the Board of Governors, Academic Council, and specific committees for finance, affiliation, and selection. The document outlines the powers of the university to confer degrees, affiliate institutions, and manage its funds, while defining the roles of officers such as the Chancellor, Rector, and Vice-Chancellor.

metadata.short_title: The Sind Board of Technical Education (Amendment) Ordinance, 1982
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to amend the Sind Board of Technical Education Ordinance, 1970.
amends: The Sind Board of Technical Education Ordinance, 1970
subjects: Sindh Board of Intermediate and Secondary Education
metadata.one_line: Amends the Sind Board of Technical Education Ordinance, 1970 by adding a reference to the Chairman of SIBE Sukkur.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance amends the Sind Board of Technical Education Ordinance, 1970. It adds a specific clause regarding the Chairman of the Board of Intermediate and Secondary Education, Sukkur. The amendment was promulgated by the Governor of Sindh on November 6, 1982.

metadata.short_title: The Sind Board of Technical Education (Amendment) Ordinance, 1984
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to amend the Sind Board of Technical Education Ordinance, 1970.
metadata.parent_law: The Sind Board of Technical Education Ordinance, 1970
amends: The Sind Board of Technical Education Ordinance, 1970
metadata.one_line: Amends the Sind Board of Technical Education Ordinance, 1970 regarding member removal procedures.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance amends the Sind Board of Technical Education Ordinance, 1970 to address directions from the Federal Shariat Court. It specifically modifies Section 6 by adding a proviso that ensures no member is removed without being given an opportunity to be heard. The Ordinance was promulgated by the Governor of Sindh on November 18, 1984, and came into force immediately.

name: BOARDS OF INTERMEDIATE AND SECONDARY EDUCATION (AMENDMENT) ORDINANCE, 1984

metadata.short_title: The Sind Boards of Intermediate and Secondary Education (Amendment) Ordinance, 1984
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to amend the Sind Boards of Intermediate and Secondary Education Ordinance, 1972.
amends: The Sind Boards of Intermediate and Secondary Education Ordinance, 1972
subjects: Boards of Intermediate and Secondary Education
metadata.one_line: Amends the 1972 Ordinance to require a hearing before removing members of education boards.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance amends the Sind Boards of Intermediate and Secondary Education Ordinance, 1972 in response to directions from the Federal Shariat Court. It modifies Section 6 of the parent Ordinance by adding a proviso that no member shall be removed unless given an opportunity of being heard. The amendment came into force immediately upon promulgation by the Governor of Sindh on November 4, 1984.

metadata.short_title: The Boilers Act (Sind Amendment) Ordinance, 1971
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to amend the Boilers Act, 1923, in application to the Province of Sind.
metadata.one_line: Amends the Boilers Act, 1923 in Sindh to exclude railways and nuclear facilities from its scope and establish a Sind Boilers Board.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance amends the Boilers Act, 1923 specifically for its application to the Province of Sind. It substitutes provisions regarding boilers and steam-pipes belonging to railways or powered by nuclear energy owned by the Pakistan Atomic Energy Commission, effectively excluding them from the Act's application. Additionally, it establishes the Sind Boilers Board with six specific members and modifies section 28 to require Provincial Government approval for certain notifications.

metadata.short_title: The Sind Buildings Control (Amendment) Ordinance, 1984
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to amend the Sind Buildings Control Ordinance, 1979.
metadata.one_line: Amends the Sind Buildings Control Ordinance, 1979 to ensure opportunity of being heard before action is taken.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance amends the Sind Buildings Control Ordinance, 1979 in response to directions from the Federal Shariat Court. It modifies Section 14 and Section 17 of the parent Ordinance by adding provisos that require giving an opportunity of being heard to affected persons before action is taken or appeals are disposed of. The amendments came into force immediately upon promulgation.

name: CANAL AND DRAINAGE (EXTENSION TO ROHRI CANAL AREA) ORDINANCE, 1990

metadata.short_title: The Canal and Drainage (Extension to Rohri Canal Area) Ordinance, 1990
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to extend the Canal and Drainage Act, 1873, to certain areas irrigated by the Rohri Canal.
metadata.territorial_extent: the area irrigated by the Rohri Canal in Tando Adam Taluka District Sanghar
metadata.commencement: at once and deemed to have taken effect on and from 1st April, 1990
metadata.one_line: Extends the Canal and Drainage Act, 1873 to areas irrigated by the Rohri Canal in Tando Adam Taluka.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance extends the application of the Canal and Drainage Act, 1873 to specific areas irrigated by the Rohri Canal in Tando Adam Taluka, District Sanghar. It explicitly excludes the Sind Irrigation Act, 1879 from applying to these areas while this Ordinance is in force. The measure was promulgated because the Provincial Assembly was not in session and immediate action was deemed necessary.

name: CANAL AND DRAINAGE (EXTENSION TO ROHRI CANAL AREA) (SIND AMENDMENT) ORDINANCE, 1970

metadata.short_title: The Canal and Drainage (Extension to Rohri Canal Area) (Sindh Amendment) Ordinance, 1970
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to amend Canal and Drainage (Extension to Rohri Canal Area) Ordinance, 1970
metadata.parent_law: Canal and Drainage (Extension to Rohri Canal Area) Ordinance, 1970
amends: Canal and Drainage (Extension to Rohri Canal Area) Ordinance, 1970
metadata.one_line: Amends the Canal and Drainage Ordinance, 1970 to extend coverage to Rohri and Ghotki Canals Areas.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance amends the Canal and Drainage (Extension to Rohri Canal Area) Ordinance, 1970. It adds references to the Sukkur Barrage and Ghutki Canal in the long title and preamble of the Principal Ordinance. Additionally, it substitutes 'Rohri and Ghotki Canals Areas' for 'Rohri Canal Area' in section 1 of the Principal Ordinance.

name: CANAL AND DRAINAGE (EXTENSION TO ROHRI CANAL AREA) ORDINANCE, 1991

metadata.short_title: The Canal and Drainage (Extension to Rohri Area) Ordinance, 1991
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to extend the Canal and Drainage Act, 1873, to certain areas irrigated by the Rohri Canal.
metadata.territorial_extent: certain areas irrigated by the Rohri Canal in Tando Adam Taluka District Sanghar
metadata.one_line: Extends the Canal and Drainage Act, 1873 to Rohri Canal areas in Sanghar District.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance extends the application of the Canal and Drainage Act, 1873 to specific areas irrigated by the Rohri Canal. It was promulgated because the Provincial Assembly was not in session at the time. The extension covers areas in Tando Adam Taluka, District Sanghar. metadata.short_title: The Sind Children (Amendment) Ordinance, 1984

It omits section 14 of the said Act and substitutes the word 'state' for 'putative father' in specific subsections of section 90. metadata.short_title: The Civil Courts (Sindh Amendment) Ordinance, 1970

It restricts the original civil jurisdiction of the District Judge of Karachi to cases where the subject matter does not exceed fifty thousand rupees. Additionally, it substitutes the monetary threshold from twenty-five thousand to fifty thousand rupees in specific sections of the West Pakistan Civil Courts Ordinance, 1962.

metadata.short_title: The Sind Civil Servants (Amendment) Ordinance, 1982

It substitutes words such as 'post', 'cadre', and 'service' for 'grade' throughout various sections of the parent Act. Additionally, it modifies provisions concerning seniority calculation and entitlements under specific welfare funds.

It mandates that one percent of such appointments shall be made from amongst disabled persons, subject to availability. The amendment references the definition of disabled persons found in the Disabled Persons (Employment and Rehabilitation) Ordinance, 1981.

It substitutes the term 'grade' with 'basic scale' throughout the Act and its Schedule. metadata.short_title: The Sind Co-operative Housing Authority Ordinance, 1982
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to provide for the establishment of a Sind Co-operative Housing Authority.
metadata.one_line: Establishes the Sind Co-operative Housing Authority to regulate and supervise co-operative housing societies in Sindh.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance establishes the Sind Co-operative Housing Authority to re-organize, regulate, and supervise activities of co-operative societies dealing in housing development within the Province of Sind. The Authority is a body corporate with perpetual succession, consisting of a Chairman and members appointed by the Governor. It possesses powers to acquire property, sue, and be sued, and may appoint officers and staff. The Ordinance also provides for the assignment of functions to the Authority, rules making, indemnity for officials acting in good faith, and mechanisms for winding up the Authority.

metadata.summary: This Ordinance amends the Sind Co-operative Societies Act, 1925 to address the transfer of shares upon a member's death. It mandates that when a deceased member's share is transferred to a nominee or legal representative, the value must be disbursed among all heirs according to the deceased's personal law. The amendment was promulgated by the Governor of Sindh in response to directions from the Federal Shariat Court.

It inserts a new sub-section into section 7 of the parent Ordinance, allowing aggrieved persons to prefer an appeal to the Government within seven days of an order. The decision of the Government on such appeals is final, provided the appellant was afforded an opportunity of being heard.

The Ordinance was promulgated by the Governor of Sind on July 7, 1977, and came into force immediately.

It substitutes the word 'Director' with 'Inspector General' wherever it occurs in those Acts. The Ordinance was promulgated on January 26, 1978, but is deemed to have taken effect from December 26, 1973.

metadata.short_title: The Sind Private Colleges (Management and Control) (Amendment) Ordinance, 1984
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to amend the Sind Private Colleges (Management and Control) Ordinance, 1970.
amends: The Sind Private Colleges (Management and Control) Ordinance, 1970
metadata.one_line: Amends the 1970 Ordinance to allow removal of college officials after giving them an opportunity to be heard.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance amends the Sind Private Colleges (Management and Control) Ordinance, 1970. It inserts a new sub-section into Section 5 regarding the removal of Chairmen or members from office. The amendment mandates that no removal order can be passed unless the official is given an opportunity to be heard.

metadata.short_title: The Sind Private Schools (Management and Control) (Amendment) Ordinance, 1984
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to amend the Sind Private Schools (Management and Control) Act, 1974.
metadata.parent_law: The Sind Private Schools (Management and Control) Act, 1974
amends: The Sind Private Schools (Management and Control) Act, 1974
metadata.one_line: Amends the 1974 Act to require an opportunity to be heard before removing a member from a school management committee.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance amends the Sind Private Schools (Management and Control) Act, 1974 in response to directions from the Federal Shariat Court. It specifically modifies Section 5, Sub-section (2) of the parent Act by adding a proviso regarding the removal of members. The amendment mandates that no member shall be removed unless they are given an opportunity to be heard.

name: PRIVATE UNIVERSITIES AND EDUCATIONAL INSTITUTES LAWS (AMENDMENT) ORDINANCE, 2002

metadata.short_title: The Private Universities and Educational Institutes Laws (Amendment) Ordinance, 2002
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to amend certain laws relating to the Private Universities and Educational Institutes in force in the Province of Sindh.

The Prestion Institute of Management Science and Technology Ordinance, 2001
The Newports Institute of Communications and Economics Ordinance, 2002
metadata.one_line: Amends various private university and institute laws in Sindh regarding inspection, patron powers, and monitoring charges.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance amends specific acts and ordinances governing private universities and educational institutes in the Province of Sindh. It grants Patrons expanded powers to conduct inspections, direct inquiries, and take actions such as withdrawing charters or closing institutions if necessary. The amendments also mandate that these institutions work within the framework of government education policies and pay annual monitoring charges to the Secretary Education Government of Sindh.

metadata.short_title: The Provincial Motor Vehicles (Amendment) Ordinance, 2000
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance further to amend the Provincial Motor Vehicles Ordinance, 1965.
metadata.one_line: Amends the Provincial Motor Vehicles Ordinance, 1965 to update ticket systems and penalties for traffic violations.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance amends the Provincial Motor Vehicles Ordinance, 1965 to introduce a new ticket system for on-the-spot charges of traffic offences. It substitutes specific sections and schedules within the parent Ordinance to define new violations and corresponding fines. The document applies throughout the Province of Sindh and comes into force immediately upon promulgation by the Governor.

metadata.short_title: The Provincial Motor Vehicles (Amendment) Ordinance, 2008
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to amend the Provincial Motor Vehicles Ordinance, 1965.
metadata.one_line: Amends the Provincial Motor Vehicles Ordinance, 1965 by adding penalties for unauthorized use of emergency lights and updating fine schedules.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance amends the Provincial Motor Vehicles Ordinance, 1965 to address specific traffic violations. It introduces new offenses regarding the unauthorized use of revolving or emergency lights and distinctive signs on motor vehicles. The document also substitutes Section 112 and the Twelfth Schedule to update the fines applicable for various traffic infractions in Sindh.

metadata.short_title: The Provincial Motor Vehicles (Sind Amendment) Ordinance, 1976
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance further to amend the Provincial Motor Vehicles Ordinance, 1965, in its application to the Province of Sind.
metadata.one_line: Amends the Provincial Motor Vehicles Ordinance, 1965 regarding compensation for injuries in Sindh.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance amends the Provincial Motor Vehicles Ordinance, 1965 specifically for its application to the Province of Sind. It substitutes higher monetary figures for certain clauses and inserts new text into section 67 regarding carriage ownership by a Corporation. Additionally, it adds a new entry to the Sixth Schedule and substitutes the entire Thirteenth Schedule with a revised scale of compensation payable for injuries to passengers in stage or contract carriages.

name: PROVINCIAL SMALL CAUSES COURTS (SINDH AMENDMENT) ORDINANCE, 1993

metadata.short_title: The Provincial Small Causes Courts (Sindh Amendment) Ordinance, 1993

amends: The Provincial Small Causes Courts Act, 1887
metadata.one_line: Amends the Provincial Small Causes Courts Act, 1887 regarding monetary limits in Sindh.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance amends the Provincial Small Causes Courts Act, 1887 specifically for its application to the Province of Sindh. It was promulgated by the Governor because the Provincial Assembly was not in session and immediate action was deemed necessary under Article 128 of the Constitution. The text substitutes specific monetary figures in sections 15 and 27-A of the said Act, raising jurisdictional limits from two thousand to twenty-five thousand and from five thousand to fifty thousand.

name: PROVINCIAL SMALL CAUSES COURTS (SINDH AMENDMENT) ORDINANCE, 1993

metadata.summary: This Ordinance amends the Provincial Small Causes Courts Act, 1887 specifically for its application to the Province of Sindh. It substitutes higher monetary figures into sections 15 and 27-A of the said Act. The document was promulgated by the Governor of Sindh under Article 128 of the Constitution because the Provincial Assembly was not in session.
