metadata.short_title: The Sindh Public Conveyances (Amendment) Ordinance, 1984
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to amend the Sind Public Conveyances Act, 1920.
metadata.one_line: Amends the Sind Public Conveyances Act, 1920 to add provisions for hearing affected persons before orders are passed.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance amends the Sind Public Conveyances Act, 1920 to ensure procedural fairness in administrative proceedings. It requires that any person likely to be affected by an order under specific sections must be given an opportunity of being heard before the order is passed. The amendments apply to orders made under sections 5, 10, and 12 of the said Act.

metadata.short_title: The Sind Public Service Commission (Amendment) Ordinance, 1984
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to amend the Sind Public Service Commission Ordinance, 1978.
metadata.parent_law: The Sind Public Service Commission Ordinance, 1978
amends: The Sind Public Service Commission Ordinance, 1978
metadata.one_line: Amends the Sind Public Service Commission Ordinance, 1978 regarding appointment and term of members.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance amends the Sind Public Service Commission Ordinance, 1978 to clarify the appointment process for the Chairman and Members by the Governor. It stipulates that a Member's term shall not exceed five years but allows re-appointment for up to three years. Additionally, it permits members to resign their office by writing addressed to the Governor.

metadata.short_title: The Sind Qaumi Razakars (Amendment) Ordinance, 1984
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to amend the Sind Qaumi Razakars Ordinance, 1965.
metadata.one_line: Amends the Sind Qaumi Razakars Ordinance, 1965 to require a hearing before dismissal of members.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance amends the Sind Qaumi Razakars Ordinance, 1965 in response to directions from the Federal Shariat Court. It modifies Section 7 by adding a proviso that mandates an opportunity for any member of the Qaumi Razakars to show cause and be heard before an order of dismissal is passed against them. The amendment ensures adherence to principles of natural justice within the disciplinary framework of the Razakars.

name: QUAID-E-AWAM UNIVERSITY OF ENGINEERING, SCIENCE AND TECHNOLOGY, NAWABSHAH ORDINANCE, 1996

metadata.short_title: The Quaid-e-Awam University of Engineering, Science and Technology, Nawabshah Ordinance, 1996
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to establish Quaid-e-Awam University of Engineering, Science and Technology, Nawabshah.
metadata.territorial_extent: the Province of Sindh excluding the division of Karachi
establishes: Quaid-e-Awam University of Engineering, Science and Technology, Nawabshah
metadata.one_line: Establishes Quaid-e-Awam University of Engineering, Science and Technology, Nawabshah in Sindh.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance establishes the Quaid-e-Awam University of Engineering, Science and Technology, Nawabshah as a corporate body with perpetual succession. It defines the composition of the University, including the Chancellor, Pro-Chancellor, Senate, Syndicate, and Academic Council, outlining their respective powers and duties. The legislation also sets out provisions for the Vice-Chancellor, officers, students, affiliated colleges, and the conduct of examinations and research.

metadata.short_title: The Sind Race-Courses Licensing (Amendment) Ordinance, 1984
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to amend the Sind Race-Courses Licensing Act, 1912.
metadata.one_line: Amends the Sind Race-Courses Licensing Act, 1912 to prohibit betting and wagering terms in licenses.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance amends the Sind Race-Courses Licensing Act, 1912, following a directive from the Federal Shariat Court. It omits specific clauses allowing bets on horses and adds a new sub-section prohibiting any license term that allows betting or wagering. The amendments apply to the Province of Sind and came into force immediately upon promulgation by the Governor.

metadata.short_title: The Reformatory Schools (Sind Amendment) Ordinance, 1984
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to amend the Reformatory Schools Act, 1897.
metadata.one_line: Amends the Reformatory Schools Act, 1897 regarding citizenship requirements in Sindh.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance amends the Reformatory Schools Act, 1897 as directed by the Federal Shariat Court. It specifically applies to the Province of Sind and deletes certain words from section 17, sub-section (2) of the parent Act. The amendment removes a requirement that at least two members be citizens of Pakistan.

metadata.short_title: The Sind Regional Plan Organization (Amendment) Ordinance, 1984
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to amend the Sind Regional Plan Organization Act, 1975.
metadata.parent_law: The Sind Regional Plan Organization Act, 1975
metadata.one_line: Amends the Sind Regional Plan Organization Act, 1975 regarding land acquisition and removal procedures.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance amends the Sind Regional Plan Organization Act, 1975 to address directions from the Federal Shariat Court. It modifies Section 4 to require a hearing for non-official members before an order of removal is passed. Additionally, it substitutes text in Section 16 to specify that property acquisition must follow the Land Acquisition Act, 1984.

name: REGISTRARS OF TRADE UNIONS (VALIDATION OF APPOINTMENTS AND ORDERS) (SIND) ORDINANCE, 1983

metadata.short_title: The Registrars of Trade Unions (Validation of Appointments and Orders) (Sindh) Ordinance, 1983
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to validate appointments of Registrars of Trade Unions and orders passed and actions taken by them as such.
metadata.one_line: Validates appointments and orders of Registrars of Trade Unions in Sindh.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance validates the appointments of Registrars of Trade Unions and the orders passed by them in Sindh. It deems the Director of Labour, Sindh to have continued as the Registrar for the whole province despite any conflicting notifications. Consequently, all actions taken or orders passed by the Director Labour, Sindh are deemed valid and effective.

metadata.short_title: The Registration (Sindh Amendment) Ordinance, 1996
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to amend the Registration Act, 1908, in its application to the Province of Sindh.
metadata.one_line: Amends the Registration Act, 1908 in Sindh to include power of attorney for selling immovable property.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance amends the Registration Act, 1908 specifically for its application to the Province of Sindh. It was promulgated by the Governor because the Provincial Assembly was not in session and immediate action was deemed necessary. The amendment adds a new clause (f) to Section 17 of the Registration Act, 1908, regarding power of attorney authorizing an attorney to sell immovable property.

metadata.short_title: The Sind Relief of Indebtedness (Amendment) Ordinance, 1984
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to amend the Sind Relief of Indebtedness Ordinance, 1960.
metadata.parent_law: The Sind Relief of Indebtedness Ordinance, 1960
metadata.one_line: Amends the Sind Relief of Indebtedness Ordinance, 1960 regarding exemption of milk animals from attachment.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance amends the Sind Relief of Indebtedness Ordinance, 1960 to address directions from the Federal Shariat Court. It specifically substitutes section 8 to exempt certain milk animals and draught animals used for a debtor's maintenance from attachment or sale in execution of decrees. The amendment applies to the Province of Sind and came into force immediately upon promulgation by the Governor.

metadata.short_title: The Removal from Service (Special Powers) (Amendment) Sindh Ordinance, 2005
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to amend Removal from Service (Special Powers) Sindh, Ordinance, 2000.
metadata.commencement: at once and deemed to have taken effect on 25th January, 2005
metadata.parent_law: The Removal from Service (Special Powers) Sindh Ordinance, 2000
amends: The Removal from Service (Special Powers) Sindh Ordinance, 2000
metadata.one_line: Amends the 2000 Sindh Ordinance to substitute 'Chief Minister' for 'Governor' and add procedures for dismissal due to corruption.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance amends the Removal from Service (Special Powers) Sindh Ordinance, 2000. It substitutes the term 'Chief Minister' for 'Governor' throughout the text. The amendment introduces new provisions allowing for dismissal of civil servants convicted of corruption or moral turpitude and establishes a review process involving the Chief Minister. It also inserts sections regarding legal immunity for authorities acting in good faith under the Ordinance.

metadata.short_title: The Removal from Service (Special Powers) (Amendment) Sindh Ordinance, 2004
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to amend the Removal from Service (Special Powers) Sindh Ordinance, 2000.
amends: The Removal from Service (Special Powers) Sindh Ordinance, 2000
metadata.one_line: Amends the 2000 Sindh Ordinance to replace 'Governor' with 'Chief Minister' and add procedures for dismissal due to corruption.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance amends the Removal from Service (Special Powers) Sindh Ordinance, 2000. It substitutes references to the Governor with the Chief Minister throughout the text. The amendment introduces new provisions allowing dismissal for corruption or moral turpitude and establishes a review process before the Chief Minister. It also inserts indemnity clauses protecting authorities acting in good faith and bars judicial review of decisions made under the Ordinance.

name: REMOVAL FROM SERVICE (SPECIAL POWERS) (AMENDMENT) SINDH ORDINANCE, 2001

metadata.short_title: The Removal from Service (Special Powers) (Amendment) Sindh Ordinance, 2001
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to amend the Removal from Service (Special Powers) Sindh Ordinance, 2000.
amends: The Removal from Service (Special Powers) Sindh Ordinance, 2000
metadata.one_line: Amends the Removal from Service (Special Powers) Sindh Ordinance, 2000 regarding dismissal and inquiry procedures.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance amends the Removal from Service (Special Powers) Sindh Ordinance, 2000 to expand grounds for dismissal and removal. It introduces new provisions for plea bargaining involving asset return and modifies inquiry procedures by requiring show cause notices and defining the powers of Inquiry Officers or Committees. The amendments also adjust procedural timelines and conditions under which inquiries may be dispensed with.

name: REMOVAL FROM SERVICE (SPECIAL POWERS) SINDH ORDINANCE, 2000

metadata.short_title: The Removal from Service (Special Powers) Sindh Ordinance, 2000
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to provide for dismissal, removal, compulsory retirement from service and reduction to lower post or pay scale of certain persons from Government service and corporation service.
metadata.one_line: Provides special powers to the Governor for dismissal, removal, or retirement of government and corporation employees due to inefficiency, misconduct, or corruption.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance empowers the competent authority in Sindh to dismiss, remove, compulsorily retire, or reduce certain persons from Government or corporation service. It applies specifically to cases involving inefficiency, misconduct, corruption, subversive activities, or appointment violations. The document establishes procedures for inquiry committees, allows for representation and review petitions to the Governor, and provides a mechanism for appeals to the Sindh Service Tribunal.

metadata.short_title: The Sind Rented Premises (Amendment) Ordinance, 1984
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to amend the Sind Rented Premises Ordinance, 1979.
metadata.max_penalty: fine not exceeding one year's rent
metadata.one_line: Amends the Sind Rented Premises Ordinance, 1979 by omitting specific sections and adding penalties for landlords.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance amends the Sind Rented Premises Ordinance, 1979 to address tenancy issues in Sindh. It omits certain provisos and sections regarding tenant possession and landlord obligations. Additionally, it introduces a new subsection imposing fines on landlords who relet premises or change their use within one year of obtaining possession, while also granting evicted tenants the right to apply for restoration of possession.

name: REPEAL OF THE SINDH LAND REVENUE (AMENDMENT) ACT, 2011 (SINDH ACT NO.XXIII OF 2011) ORDINANCE, 2011

metadata.short_title: The Repeal of the Sindh Land Revenue (Amendment) Act, 2011 (Sindh Act No.XXIII of 2011) Ordinance, 2011
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to repeal the Sindh Land Revenue (Amendment) Act, 2011.
metadata.commencement: at once and deemed to have taken effect on 9th July, 2011
repeals: The Sindh Land Revenue (Amendment) Act, 2011 (Sindh Act No.XXIII of 2011)
metadata.one_line: This Ordinance repeals the Sindh Land Revenue (Amendment) Act, 2011 and revives its substituted provisions.
metadata.summary: This document is an Ordinance promulgated by the Governor of Sindh under Article 128 of the Constitution. Its sole purpose is to repeal the Sindh Land Revenue (Amendment) Act, 2011 because the Provincial Assembly was not in session. The Ordinance also revives all provisions that were substituted by the repealed Act and validates orders made under it.

metadata.short_title: The Sind Requisitioned Land (Continuance) (Amendment) Ordinance, 1984
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to amend the Sind Requisitioned Land (Continuance) Act, 1958.
metadata.one_line: Amends the Sind Requisitioned Land (Continuance) Act, 1958 to add newspaper publication requirements.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance amends the Sind Requisitioned Land (Continuance) Act, 1958 in response to a directive from the Federal Shariat Court. It modifies Section 4 of the parent Act by requiring that notices appear not only in the Gazette but also in two daily newspapers. The Ordinance was promulgated by the Governor of Sind on September 27, 1984, and came into force immediately.

name: REQUISITIONING OF IMMOVABLE PROPERTY (TEMPORARY POWERS) (AMENDMENT) ORDINANCE, 1984

metadata.short_title: The Sind Requisitioning of Immovable Property (Temporary Powers) (Amendment) Ordinance, 1984
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to amend the Sind Requisitioning of Immovable Property (Temporary Powers) Act, 1956.
metadata.parent_law: The Sind Requisitioning of Immovable Property (Temporary Powers) Act, 1956
amends: The Sind Requisitioning of Immovable Property (Temporary Powers) Act, 1956
metadata.one_line: Amends the 1956 Act to adjust compensation interest rates and allow for increases based on new taxes.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance amends the Sind Requisitioning of Immovable Property (Temporary Powers) Act, 1956, following directions from the Federal Shariat Court. It modifies the interest rate applicable to compensation by removing a specific percentage cap and introduces a new provision allowing the Provincial Government to increase compensation after three years if new taxes are imposed. The amendment ensures that compensation is not less than the rent of similar buildings in the same locality and limits any increase to ten percent per annum.

metadata.short_title: The Sind Securities Contracts Control (Amendment) Ordinance, 1984
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to amend the Sind Securities Contracts Control Act, 1925.
metadata.parent_law: The Sind Securities Contracts Control Act, 1925
metadata.one_line: Amends the Sind Securities Contracts Control Act, 1925 to require a hearing before refusing stock-exchange recognition.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance amends the Sind Securities Contracts Control Act, 1925 in response to directions from the Federal Shariat Court. It modifies Section 4 of the parent Act by adding a proviso that mandates an opportunity for a stock-exchange to be heard before any order refusing or withdrawing recognition is made. The Ordinance came into force immediately upon promulgation on October 24, 1984.

metadata.short_title: The Sind Seed Corporation (Amendment) Ordinance, 1984
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to amend the Sind Seed Corporation Act, 1976.
metadata.one_line: Amends the Sind Seed Corporation Act, 1976 to require a hearing before removing the Managing Director.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance amends the Sind Seed Corporation Act, 1976 in response to directions from the Federal Shariat Court. It specifically modifies section 7 of the parent Act regarding the removal of the Managing Director. The amendment ensures that no order of removal is passed unless the Managing Director is given an opportunity to be heard.

metadata.short_title: The Sehwan Development Authority (Amendment) Ordinance, 2001
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to amend the Sehwan Development Authority Act, 1994.
metadata.one_line: Amends the Sehwan Development Authority Act, 1994 regarding Chairman appointment and tenure.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance amends the Sehwan Development Authority Act, 1994 to change the method of appointing the Chairman. It substitutes a clause requiring the Chairman to be appointed by the Government and inserts a new subsection specifying a three-year term of office. The legislation was promulgated by the Governor of Sindh due to the suspension of the Provincial Assembly.

metadata.short_title: The Sehwan Development Authority Ordinance, 1993
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to make provisions for the development, improvement and beautification of the areas comprising taluka Sehwan and other areas of Dadu District and establish an Authority for such purpose.
metadata.territorial_extent: the areas comprising taluka Sehwan and such other areas of Dadu District as Government may from time to time, specify by notification
metadata.one_line: Establishes the Sehwan Development Authority to develop, improve, and beautify Sehwan and Dadu District areas.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance establishes the Sehwan Development Authority to oversee the development, improvement, and beautification of taluka Sehwan and other areas in Dadu District. The Authority is a body corporate with powers to acquire property, formulate schemes, and manage public works including water supply and waste disposal. It was promulgated by the Governor of Sindh because the Provincial Assembly was not in session.

metadata.short_title: The Sind (Amendment of Laws) Ordinance, 1974
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to amend certain laws applicable to the Province of Sind, for conferring powers on Commissioners.
amends: The Karachi Essential Articles (Price Control and Hoarding) Act, 1953
The Sind Court of Wards Act, 1905
repeals: Sind Ordinance III of 1972
metadata.one_line: Amends various Sindh laws to transfer powers from the Provincial Government to the Commissioner.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance amends several Acts and Ordinances applicable to the Province of Sind to confer specific powers on Commissioners. It transfers pending appeals and cases from Revenue Commissioners to Commissioners having jurisdiction. The text also grants Commissioners authority to inspect projects and call for information, while repealing a previous 1972 Ordinance.

metadata.short_title: The Sind (Karachi Development Authority Order, 1957 Amendment) Ordinance, 1973
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to amend the Karachi Development Authority Order, 1957.
metadata.one_line: Amends the Karachi Development Authority Order, 1957 by omitting a clause and inserting 'Chairman and' before Director-General.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance amends the Karachi Development Authority Order, 1957 to address immediate administrative needs while the Provincial Legislature was not in session. It omits Clause (3) of Article 5 and modifies Article 6 by inserting the words 'Chairman and' before 'Director-General'. The amendments take effect immediately upon promulgation by the Governor of Sindh under the Interim Constitution.

name: SIND (TEACHING, PROMOTION AND USE OF SINDHI LANGUAGE) ACT, (APPLICATION) ORDINANCE, 1972

metadata.short_title: The Sind (Teaching, Promotion and Use of Sindhi Language) Act, (Application) Ordinance, 1972
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to make certain provision in relation to the application of the Sind (Teaching, Promotion and Use of Sindhi Language) Act, 1972.
metadata.territorial_extent: the whole of the Province of Sind
amends: Sind (Teaching, Promotion and Use of Sindhi Language) Act, 1972
key_definitions: the Act (referring to the Sind (Teaching, Promotion and Use of Sindhi Language) Act, 1972)
metadata.one_line: This Ordinance clarifies the application of the 1972 Sindhi Language Act to prevent discrimination based on knowledge of Sindhi or Urdu in Sindh civil services.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance was promulgated by the Governor of Sind to clarify and remove doubts regarding the application of the Sind (Teaching, Promotion and Use of Sindhi Language) Act, 1972. It ensures that no person qualified for appointment or promotion in the civil service of the Province of Sind is discriminated against solely due to a lack of knowledge of Sindhi or Urdu languages. The Ordinance also protects existing civil servants from removal based on such linguistic deficiencies and stipulates that these non-discrimination measures apply for twelve years from its commencement.

name: SIND (TOWN COMMITTEE, BHIRYA ROAD) VALIDATION OF OCTROI TAX ORDINANCE, 1971

metadata.short_title: The Sindh (Town Committee, Bhirya Road) Validation of Octroi Tax Ordinance, 1971
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to validate octroi tax charged, collected or realized by the Town Committee, Bhirya Road, District Nawabshah.
metadata.one_line: Validates octroi tax charged by the Town Committee, Bhirya Road, District Nawabshah between 1966 and 1970.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance validates octroi tax charged, collected, or realized by the Town Committee, Bhirya Road, District Nawabshah. It covers the period from March 24, 1966, to August 24, 1970, when such taxes were levied without the sanction of the Commissioner. The validation is enacted under the Martial Law Proclamation of 1969 and the Provisional Constitution Order.

metadata.short_title: The Sind Abkari Act (Amendment) Ordinance, 1970
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to amend the Sind Abkari Act, 1878.
metadata.one_line: Amends the Sind Abkari Act, 1878 by increasing fines and imprisonment terms in specific sections.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance amends the Sind Abkari Act, 1878 to increase monetary penalties and imprisonment terms across several sections. It substitutes higher fine amounts (e.g., from two hundred rupees to one thousand rupees) and longer imprisonment periods (e.g., from three months to one year). The changes apply to the Province of Sind and were promulgated by the Governor under Martial Law.

name: SIND ABOLITION OF LAND REVENUE AND AGRICULTURE INCOME TAX ORDINANCE, 1977

metadata.short_title: The Sind Abolition of Land Revenue and Agriculture Income Tax Ordinance, 1977
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to provide for the abolition of land revenue and agriculture income tax.
repeals: Sind Land Revenue Act, 1967
Sind Finance Act, 1965
metadata.one_line: Abolishes land revenue and agriculture income tax for the Rabi Crop of 1976-77 and thereafter in Sindh.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance provides for the immediate abolition of land revenue and agriculture income tax in the Province of Sind. It applies to land for the Rabi Crop of 1976-77 and all subsequent crops, enacted by the Governor because the Provincial Assembly was not in session. The text specifies that where a flat rate system applies, fifty percent of the total land revenue is deemed payable for perennial canal lands and twenty-five percent for non-perennial canal lands.

metadata.short_title: The Sind Agricultural Supplies Organization Ordinance, 1972
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to establish an Agricultural Supplies Organization in the Province of Sind.
metadata.territorial_extent: the whole of the Province of Sind
metadata.commencement: on such date as may be appointed by Government
metadata.one_line: Establishes the Sindh Agricultural Supplies Organization to procure and distribute agricultural inputs in Sindh.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance establishes the Sindh Agricultural Supplies Organization as a body corporate within the Province of Sind. The organization is tasked with procuring, transporting, storing, and distributing improved seeds and fertilizers on a commercial basis to agriculturists. It creates a Board of Members for general direction, appoints a Chairman as Chief Executive, and outlines procedures for officers, accounts, and dissolution.

metadata.short_title: The Sind Agriculture University (Amendment) Ordinance, 1986
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to amend the Sind Agriculture University Act, 1977.
metadata.one_line: Amends the Sind Agriculture University Act, 1977 to provide for the appointment of a Pro-Vice-Chancellor.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance amends the Sind Agriculture University Act, 1977 to insert provisions regarding the Pro-Vice-Chancellor. It authorizes the Chancellor to appoint a Pro-Vice-Chancellor for the main campus or additional campuses with terms not exceeding four years. The appointed Pro-Vice-Chancellor exercises delegated powers and functions of the Vice-Chancellor as determined by the Chancellor.

metadata.short_title: The Sind Agriculture University Ordinance, 1977

It defines the composition of the university, including the Chancellor, Pro-Chancellor, Senate, Syndicate, and Academic Council, outlining their respective powers and duties. The document also sets out provisions for student admission, discipline, financial management through the University Fund, and legal protections for the university and its officers.

It introduces provisions for superseding governing bodies of societies that fail their duties or act against public interest. Additionally, it modifies regulations concerning privately managed schools and colleges, requiring prior permission for closure or transfer of property and ensuring institutions operate on a genuine non-commercial basis.

metadata.summary: This Ordinance establishes the Sind Arid Zone Development Authority as a body corporate with perpetual succession. The Authority is headed by the Chief Minister as Chairman and includes official and non-official members appointed by the Government of Sind. It empowers the Authority to acquire property, manage funds, implement schemes, and levy betterment fees on properties benefiting from development projects within declared arid zones.

metadata.short_title: The Sind Children (Amendment) Ordinance, 1974
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to amend Sind Children Act, 1955.

metadata.summary: This Ordinance amends the Sind Children Act, 1955 by adding 'including Khairpur District' after the word 'Sind' in section 1. It was promulgated by the Governor of Sind under Article 128 of the Constitution because the Provincial Assembly was not in session. The amendment extends the geographical application of the Children Act to cover Khairpur District immediately upon enactment.

metadata.short_title: The Sind Civil Servants (Amendment) Ordinance, 1976
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to amend the Sind Civil Servants Act, 1973.
metadata.one_line: Amends the Sind Civil Servants Act, 1973 by increasing the age limit for civil servants from fifty-eight to sixty years.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance amends the Sind Civil Servants Act, 1973 to change the retirement age of civil servants. Specifically, it substitutes the words 'fifty-eight years' with 'sixty years' in clause (ii) of section 13 of the parent Act. The Governor of Sindh promulgated this Ordinance because the Provincial Assembly was not in session and immediate action was deemed necessary under Article 128 of the Constitution.

metadata.short_title: The Sind Civil Servants (Amendment) Ordinance, 1978
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to amend the Sind Civil Servants Act, 1973.
metadata.one_line: Amends the Sind Civil Servants Act, 1973 regarding pay for temporary appointments to higher posts.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance amends the Sind Civil Servants Act, 1973 by substituting a proviso in section 18. The amendment addresses pay structures for civil servants appointed to higher posts or grades during exigencies of service. It allows appointing authorities to direct that appointees draw pay from their lower previous post with special pay, except when appointments are made on a current charge basis or additional charge.

metadata.short_title: The Sind Civil Servants (Amendment) Ordinance, 1988
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to amend the Sind Civil Servants Act, 1973.
metadata.one_line: Amends the Sind Civil Servants Act, 1973 to require written grounds and opportunity before retiring a civil servant.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance amends the Sind Civil Servants Act, 1973 to introduce procedural safeguards regarding the retirement of civil servants. It mandates that no civil servant shall be retired unless they are informed in writing of the proposed action's grounds and given a reasonable opportunity to show cause against it. The amendment was promulgated by the Governor of Sindh because the Provincial Assembly was not in session.

metadata.short_title: The Sind Civil Servants Ordinance, 1973

metadata.summary: This Ordinance regulates the appointment and terms of service for civil servants connected with the affairs of the Province of Sind. It defines key terms regarding appointments, probation, promotion, pay, leave, and pension, while establishing mechanisms for appeals and representations against service orders. The document also empowers the Government to make necessary rules and provides for the removal of difficulties arising from its implementation.

metadata.summary: This Ordinance establishes a Welfare Fund to provide financial security and assistance for civil servants and their families in Sindh. The Fund consists of contributions from civil servants, government payments, and investment profits, administered by two separate Provincial Welfare Boards based on pay scales. It also provides for insurance arrangements and outlines the distribution of benefits upon death.

It validates these grants as having been validly made and authorizes the laying down of terms and conditions for them in accordance with the Colonization of Government Lands Act, 1912. The Ordinance came into force immediately upon promulgation on March 2, 1978.

It deems the Council dissolved as of August 25, 1977, and transfers all its assets and liabilities to the Price Stabilization Board. The Ordinance also empowers the Government to replace the Board with another authority in the future and allows for rules regarding asset utilization.

metadata.short_title: The Sind Co-operative Housing Authority (Amendment) Ordinance, 1988

metadata.summary: This Ordinance amends the Sind Co-operative Housing Authority Ordinance, 1982 in response to Supreme Court directions. It mandates that the Government must afford an opportunity of hearing to a society before taking action under section 6(2). An exception allows dispensing with this hearing as an emergent measure if immediate action is necessary, provided the hearing is afforded as soon as possible thereafter. Additionally, it empowers the Government to pass interim orders to prevent mischief or abuse by the society if a hearing was duly afforded before action was taken.

It deems these transfers valid as of February 13, 1971, ensuring that inquiries, trials, penalties, and liabilities incurred are legally recognized despite the Provincial Assembly not being in session. metadata.summary: The Sind Employees Special Allowance (Payment) Ordinance, 1986 was promulgated by the Governor of Sind to provide for the payment of a special allowance to eligible employees. It applies to employees whose wages do not exceed one thousand rupees and mandates that employers pay this allowance alongside regular wages starting from July 1, 1986. The Ordinance defines key terms such as 'employee', 'employer', and 'undertaking' while establishing penalties for non-compliance and mechanisms for the recovery of withheld allowances.

It applies to the entire Province of Sindh as constituted after its dissolution from West Pakistan. The document outlines procedures for tax assessment, collection, and recovery, while barring suits in civil courts regarding these levies. Additionally, it empowers the Provincial Government to make rules necessary for implementing the Ordinance.

It grants specific tax relief to urban property owners by amending the Sind Urban Immovable Property Tax Act, 1958. The Ordinance substitutes a new ratio for tax sharing in section 3-A and adds a definition for residential buildings with limited covered area in section 4 of the said Act.

It applies to a wide range of entities including commercial establishments, factories, video shops, real estate agents, and holders of import/export licenses. The document amends multiple existing laws, including the Societies Registration Act, 1860, the Stamp Act, 1899, and various Sindh Finance Acts, to update tax rates, valuation methods, and fee structures for different categories of businesses and property owners.

metadata.short_title: The Sind Fisheries (Amendment) Ordinance, 1976

The document outlines procedures for granting proprietary rights, cancelling allotments due to false information or breach of conditions, and managing re-entry of resumed lands. key_definitions: Sind Land Revenue Flat Rate Assessment Rules, 1973

metadata.summary: This Ordinance was promulgated by the Governor of Sindh to validate the first draft assessment lists created under the Sind Land Revenue Flat Rate Assessment Rules, 1973. It applies to the Province of Sindh and addresses situations where required public notices were not given as per the said Rules. The document deems these draft lists valid and legally effective despite the lack of such notices, rendering any court orders questioning their validity without legal effect.

metadata.short_title: The Sind Laws (Amendment) Ordinance, 1984
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to amend certain financial laws to facilitate introduction of Islamic economy.
amends: The Sind Cooperative Societies and Cooperative Banks (Repayment of Loans) Ordinance, 1966
metadata.one_line: Amends financial laws in Sindh to facilitate the introduction of an Islamic economy by updating definitions and tax exemptions.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance amends several existing financial laws in Sindh to align them with the principles of an Islamic economy. It introduces new clauses regarding banking instruments, substitutes terms like 'interest' with 'interest or return', and grants powers to exempt certain banking instruments from stamp duties. The amendments specifically update the Stamp Act, Cooperative Societies Act, Finance Act, and the Cooperative Banks Ordinance to include Islamic financial concepts.

name: SIND LOANS FOR AGRICULTURAL PURPOSES ORDINANCE, 1974

metadata.short_title: The Sind Loans for Agricultural Purposes Ordinance, 1974
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to provide for credit facilities to members of the co-operative societies and co-operative banks in Sind for agricultural purposes.
metadata.one_line: Provides credit facilities to members of co-operative societies and banks in Sind for agricultural purposes.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance establishes a framework for granting loans and advances to members of co-operative societies and banks in Sindh specifically for agricultural purposes. It defines key terms such as 'advance', 'borrower', and 'land', and outlines the process for using pass-books as title deeds to secure these loans. The document also details mechanisms for loan repayment, including the delivery of agricultural produce, and provides powers to make rules regarding loan ratios based on land holding sizes.

metadata.short_title: The Sind Local Government (Amendment) Ordinance, 1979
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to amend the Sind Local Government Ordinance, 1979.
metadata.one_line: Amends the Sind Local Government Ordinance, 1979 to ban party-based elections and insert a new section on disqualification.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance amends the Sind Local Government Ordinance, 1979 to prohibit candidates from contesting elections on a party basis. It forbids displaying party insignia, seeking votes based on party manifestos, or receiving financial assistance from political parties during an election. Additionally, it inserts a new section allowing the Election Authority to disqualify any person elected in contravention of these provisions for a period of four years.

metadata.short_title: The Sind Local Government (Amendment) Ordinance, 1979
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to amend the Sind Local Government Ordinance, 1972.
metadata.one_line: Amends the Sind Local Government Ordinance, 1972 regarding public safety powers and utility connections.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance amends the Sind Local Government Ordinance, 1972 to clarify procedures for public safety violations. It grants officers power to seize dangerous articles and seal premises without prior notice in specific cases. Additionally, it mandates that electricity, gas, or water connections must be discontinued if a trade licence is revoked.

metadata.short_title: The Sind Local Government (Amendment) Ordinance, 1986
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to amend the Sind Local Government Ordinance, 1979.
metadata.one_line: Amends the Sind Local Government Ordinance, 1979 by omitting specific clauses and subsections.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance amends the Sind Local Government Ordinance, 1979 by omitting specific clauses from sections 21, 37, 37-A, and 51. It was promulgated by the Governor of Sindh under Article 128 of the Constitution because the Provincial Assembly was not in session. The amendments take effect immediately upon promulgation.

metadata.short_title: The Sind Local Government (Amendment) Ordinance, 1987
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to amend the Sind Local Government Ordinance, 1979.
metadata.one_line: Amends the Sind Local Government Ordinance, 1979 regarding council supersession and minority chairmen.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance amends the Sind Local Government Ordinance, 1979 to address procedures following the supersession of a council. It allows appointed authorities to appoint members of an Advisory Committee or other persons to exercise chairman powers for Panchayats. Additionally, it mandates that chairmen representing minority communities must belong to that community and establishes provisions for an Advisory Committee to advise the appointing authority.

metadata.short_title: The Sind Local Government (Amendment) Ordinance, 1988
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to amend the Sind Local Government Ordinance, 1979, and to validate the levy of Rawangi Mahsool on certain commodities by the District Councils in the Province.
metadata.administering_body: Government of Sind, Housing, Town Planning, Local Government and Rural Development Department
metadata.one_line: Amends the 1979 Ordinance to validate Rawangi Mahsool levies on specific commodities by District Councils in Sindh.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance amends the Sind Local Government Ordinance, 1979, specifically regarding Schedule V. Its primary purpose is to validate the levy of Rawangi Mahsool on various commodities including fire wood, timber, wheat, barley, rice, cotton, and sugar products by District Councils. It applies to the Province of Sindh and deems previous notifications and levies valid from specific dates for certain districts.

metadata.short_title: The Sind Local Government (Fifth Amendment) Ordinance, 1987
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to amend the Sind Local Government Ordinance in the manner hereinafter appearing
metadata.one_line: Amends the Sind Local Government Ordinance, 1979 regarding council dissolution and appointment of authorities.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance amends the Sind Local Government Ordinance, 1979 to allow the Government to dissolve a local council upon the expiry of its term. Upon such dissolution, the functions of the council are to be performed by a person or authority appointed by the Government. The amendment was promulgated because the Provincial Assembly was not in session and immediate action was deemed necessary.

metadata.short_title: The Sind Local Government (Fourth Amendment) Ordinance, 1987
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to amend the Sind Local Government Ordinance, 1979.
metadata.one_line: Amends the Sind Local Government Ordinance, 1979 regarding municipal structures, elections, and taxes.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance amends the Sind Local Government Ordinance, 1979 to establish zonal municipal committees in Karachi and modify existing sections related to offices, elections, and taxation. It introduces restrictions on political party symbols during elections and clarifies the relationship between the metropolitan corporation and zonal committees regarding tax levies. The document also provides transitional provisions for the continuation of the existing metropolitan corporation until new bodies are constituted.

metadata.short_title: The Sind Local Government (Second Amendment) Ordinance, 1979
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to amend the Sind Local Government Ordinance, 1979.
metadata.one_line: Amends the Sind Local Government Ordinance, 1979 by adding powers to the Election Authority regarding judicial enquiries.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance amends the Sind Local Government Ordinance, 1979. It specifically adds a new sub-section to section 37-A of that Ordinance. The amendment empowers the Election Authority to require a Judicial Officer of the rank of District Judge or Additional District Judge to conduct an enquiry and pass orders.

metadata.short_title: The Sind Local Government (Second Amendment) Ordinance, 1987
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to amend the Sind Local Government Ordinance, 1979.
metadata.one_line: Amends the Sind Local Government Ordinance, 1979 regarding appointments when the Karachi Metropolitan Corporation ceases to function.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance amends the Sind Local Government Ordinance, 1979 to address situations where the Mayor, Deputy Mayor, and members of the Karachi Metropolitan Corporation cease to be Chairman and members of the Board. It empowers the Government to appoint any person or authority to perform their functions via notification in the Official Gazette. Additionally, it validates actions taken under Chapter XVI of the 1979 Ordinance during a specific period until such an appointment is made.

metadata.short_title: The Sind Local Government (Second Amendment) Ordinance, 1988
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to amend the Sind Local Government Ordinance, 1979.
metadata.one_line: Amends the Sind Local Government Ordinance, 1979 by omitting subsection (3) of section 26.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance amends the Sind Local Government Ordinance, 1979. It omits sub-section (3) of section 26 of that Ordinance. The Governor of Sindh promulgated this law because the Provincial Assembly was not in session and immediate action was deemed necessary under Article 128 of the Constitution.

metadata.short_title: The Sind Local Government (Sixth Amendment) Ordinance, 1987
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to amend the Sind Local Government Ordinance, 1979.
metadata.one_line: Amends the Sind Local Government Ordinance, 1979 regarding council membership restrictions.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance amends the Sind Local Government Ordinance, 1979 to restrict individuals from holding membership in more than one council or electoral unit of the same council. It specifically exempts members of Zonal municipal Committees from this restriction if they become members of the Karachi Metropolitan Corporation. The Governor promulgated this law under Article 128 of the Constitution because the Provincial Assembly was not in session.

metadata.short_title: The Sind Local Government (Third Amendment) Ordinance, 1979
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to amend the Sind Local Government Ordinance, 1979.
metadata.one_line: Amends the Sind Local Government Ordinance, 1979 regarding council composition, member immunity, and political activities.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance amends the Sind Local Government Ordinance, 1979 to update provisions on council composition and member eligibility. It substitutes sections regarding the number of members for minority communities and local representatives, as well as official nominations without voting rights. The text also modifies financial limits and introduces restrictions on council members' speech and votes to protect national ideology and community harmony, alongside penalties for contravention.

metadata.short_title: The Sind Local Government (Third Amendment) Ordinance, 1987
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to amend the Sind Local Government Ordinance, 1979.
metadata.one_line: Amends the Sind Local Government Ordinance, 1979 regarding council supersession and schedule entries.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance amends the Sind Local Government Ordinance, 1979 to address issues concerning the reconstitution of councils during periods of supersession. It specifically modifies section 58 to prevent reconstitution when a council's term is expiring within four months of its normal expiry date. Additionally, it updates Schedule I by substituting the figure '204' for '202' in entry 1.

metadata.short_title: The Sind Local Government Ordinance, 1979
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to consolidate and amend the law relating to local government in the Province of Sindh.
repeals: Sind Local Government Ordinance, 1972
metadata.one_line: This Ordinance consolidates and amends the law relating to local government, councils, elections, taxation, and functions in Sindh.
metadata.summary: The Sind Local Government Ordinance, 1979 consolidates and amends laws regarding local government in Sindh. It establishes local councils with defined composition, terms, and functions covering public health, sanitation, and town planning. The document outlines procedures for elections, taxation, financial management, and the powers of supervisory authorities like the Local Government Board.

metadata.summary: This Ordinance amends the Sind Maintenance of Public Order Ordinance, 1960 to include acts punishable under the Passports Act, 1974 within its scope. metadata.short_title: The Sind Medical Colleges Ordinance, 1987
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to regulate admissions in the medical colleges in Sind and other ancillary matters including the conduct and discipline of the students of such colleges.
metadata.one_line: Regulates admissions and student discipline in medical colleges in Sindh.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance regulates admissions, conduct, and discipline for students in medical colleges located in the province of Sindh. It empowers the Government of Sind to make rules regarding seat allocation, application forms, admission conditions, migration procedures, and disciplinary actions against students. Additionally, it grants authority to institute and maintain residential halls and hostels for students.

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Mining Concessions (Cancellation) Ordinance, 1978
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to provide for cancellation of mining concessions granted in an irregular manner or, as a political favour.
metadata.one_line: This Ordinance empowers the Government of Sindh to cancel irregular mining concessions and provide compensation.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance provides for the cancellation of mining concessions granted in an irregular manner or as a political favour between January 1, 1972 and July 4, 1977. It establishes a mechanism where the Government appoints an arbitrator to determine and award compensation for losses sustained by concession holders due to cancellation. The Ordinance also grants the arbitrator specific powers of a civil court for conducting summary enquiries and allows the Government to resume possession of the area after cancellation.

metadata.short_title: The Sind Motor Vehicles Taxation (Amendment) Ordinance, 1978

metadata.summary: This Ordinance amends the Sind Motor Vehicles Taxation Act, 1958 to allow tax payments in quarterly or half-yearly installments. It introduces provisions for remitting tax on vehicles that have gone out of use and grants a rebate for early tax payment. The text also specifies requirements for applications regarding non-use, including documentation needed in cases of theft or destruction of registration plates.

metadata.summary: This Ordinance establishes the Sind Orphanages Supervision and Control Board to oversee orphanages in the province. It mandates that no orphanage can operate without a license issued by the Board and requires regular medical examinations for all orphans. The document outlines the Board's composition, its powers to manage funds, and penalties for non-compliance, while repealing previous control acts applicable to Sind.

metadata.summary: This Ordinance amends the Sind Parliamentary Secretaries (Salaries, Allowances and Privileges) Act, 1974. It increases the salary of a Parliamentary Secretary from one hundred twenty five rupees to one hundred and fifty rupees. The Ordinance also inserts new sections providing for official residence, house rent, staff services, leave allowances, travelling allowances, and controlling authority for these benefits.

It specifically prohibits installing new petrol pumps in Karachi or other municipalities without local approval. Additionally, it validates petrol pump fees collected by the Karachi Municipal Corporation between April 16, 1960, and the Ordinance's enactment, allowing recovery of any unpaid amounts as arrears.

metadata.short_title: The Sind Prevention of Gambling (Amendment) Ordinance, 1979

metadata.summary: This Ordinance amends the Sind Prevention of Gambling Ordinance, 1978 to empower police officers. Specifically, it allows a Police Officer not below the rank of Sub-Inspector to arrest without warrant anyone committing an offence under section 5. It also grants powers to search persons and seize instruments of gaming, gaming moneys, securities, articles of value, and other instruments suspected of being used for such offences.

The Ordinance grants specific powers to police officers to arrest suspects, seize instruments of gaming, and search premises, while also providing mechanisms for tendering pardon to accomplices who provide truthful information.

It substitutes a new Schedule listing twelve specific First Information Reports (F.I.R.) related to corruption cases under the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1947, involving various accused persons in Hyderabad City.

metadata.summary: The document is an Ordinance promulgated by the Governor of Sind on February 14, 1972, under Martial Law. Its primary purpose is to repeal the Sind Special Tribunal Ordinance, 1970 (referred to as the Principal Ordinance). The Ordinance ensures that pending cases before the Special Tribunal are transferred to the Court of Special Judge for disposal, while preserving previous operations and penalties incurred under the repealed law.

metadata.one_line: Establishes a Special Tribunal in Sindh to try scheduled anti-corruption cases with expedited procedures.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance establishes a Special Tribunal consisting of a High Court Judge to try specific scheduled cases, primarily involving corruption. The Tribunal operates under exclusive jurisdiction with simplified procedures, including trials without a jury and restricted adjournments. Prosecution is conducted by a Special Public Prosecutor appointed by the Government of Sindh, and convicted persons have the right to appeal to a Bench of the High Court.

metadata.summary: This Ordinance establishes the Sindh Textbook Board as a body corporate to arrange for the production and publication of textbooks and reading material. The Board consists of a Chairman and up to six members appointed by the Chief Minister, with powers delegated to an Advisory Council. It outlines the Board's duties, financial management through rules and regulations, and immunity from legal proceedings for acts done in good faith.

metadata.summary: This Ordinance amends the University of Sind Act, 1972 and the University of Karachi Act, 1972 to facilitate immediate legislative action while the Provincial Assembly is not in session. It introduces the position of Pro-Vice-Chancellor for additional campuses, establishes Boards of Governors for institutions taken over by the University, and modifies retirement ages and jurisdictional bars. The text also substitutes various officer titles and inserts new clauses regarding administrative control and statutory powers.

metadata.one_line: This Ordinance provides for the management and administration of Waqf Properties in Sindh by appointing administrators and framing rules.
metadata.summary: The Sind Waqf Properties Ordinance, 1979 establishes a framework for the proper management and administration of waqf properties within the Province of Sind. It empowers the Government to appoint a Chief Administrator and Deputy Administrators who shall have perpetual succession and official seals. The Ordinance outlines powers regarding the registration, leasing, sale, and income application of waqf properties, while also providing for the recovery of rents as land revenue arrears. Additionally, it retains actions taken under the repealed Auqaf (Federal Control) Act, 1976, to the extent they are not inconsistent with this new legislation.

metadata.summary: The Sind Wild-life Protection Ordinance, 1972 was promulgated to amend and consolidate existing laws regarding the preservation, conservation, and management of wild-life in the Province of Sind. It establishes the Sindh Wild-life Management Board as a corporate body responsible for managing wildlife resources and outlines the appointment of officers, including honorary ones. The Ordinance imposes strict restrictions on hunting protected and game animals, regulates the trade in wildlife products, and defines various terms related to wildlife management.

name: SINDH (ERADICATION AND CURBING THE MENACE OF INVOLUNTARY DONATION OF FORCED CHANDA) ORDINANCE, 2002

metadata.short_title: The Sindh (Eradication and Curbing the menace of involuntary donation of forced Chanda) Ordinance, 2002
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to provide for the eradication and curbing the menace of involuntary donation or forced "Chanda" in the Province of Sindh.
metadata.max_penalty: simple imprisonment up to three months and fine up to ten thousand rupees
metadata.one_line: Prohibits involuntary donations and forced chanda collection in Sindh with penalties for violations.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance aims to eradicate the menace of involuntary donations or forced 'Chanda' within the Province of Sindh. It defines key terms such as donor, door step, fund, and Government, and explicitly prohibits the collection of funds at a donor's doorstep. The law mandates forfeiture of any illegally collected funds and prescribes criminal penalties including imprisonment and fines for contraventions.

metadata.short_title: The Sindh (Poultry Vaccine Centre) Ordinance, 1995
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to provide for the establishment of a Poultry Vaccine Centre in the Province of Sindh.
metadata.one_line: Establishes the Sindh Poultry Vaccine Centre to produce vaccines and conduct research in Sindh.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance establishes the Sindh Poultry Vaccine Centre as a body corporate with its headquarters in Karachi. The Centre is responsible for accelerating poultry vaccine production, undertaking scientific research, and implementing training programs. It is administered by a Board comprising government officials and non-official members, with powers to manage funds, maintain accounts, and make regulations.

name: SINDH (PROHIBITION OF TAKING MINERALS INCLUDING RETI (SAND) AND BAJRI FROM ANY LAND) ORDINANCE, 2003

metadata.short_title: The Sindh (Prohibition of Taking Minerals Including Reti (Sand) and Bajri from Any Land) Ordinance, 2003
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to provides for the prohibition of taking minerals including reti (sand) and bajri from any land by excavation or otherwise, in the Province of Sindh.
metadata.max_penalty: imprisonment which may extend to one year and fine not exceeding twenty thousand rupees
metadata.one_line: Prohibits taking minerals like sand and bajri from land in Sindh without government sanction.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance prohibits the excavation or removal of minerals, specifically reti (sand) and bajri, from any land within the Province of Sindh. It requires prior sanction from the Government or an authorized officer before such activities can take place. The law establishes criminal penalties for contravention, including imprisonment and fines, and outlines procedures for cognizance by courts and the making of rules.

repeals: The Police Order, 2002 (Chief Executive's Order No.XXII of 2002)
metadata.one_line: Revives the Police Act, 1861 and repeals the Police Order, 2002 in Sindh with immediate effect.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance was promulgated by the Governor of Sindh to immediately repeal the Police Order, 2002 and revive the Police Act, 1861 as it stood on August 13, 2002. It applies specifically to the Province of Sindh where the Provincial Assembly was not in session at the time. The document ensures that all orders, proceedings, and appointments made under the repealed Order between August 14, 2002 and the Ordinance's commencement remain valid until altered.

metadata.summary: This Ordinance was promulgated by the Governor of Sindh under Article 128 of the Constitution because the Provincial Assembly was not in session. Specifically, it modifies Section 3 of that Act to ensure that the repeal of the 'Sindh Local Government Ordinance, 2001' does not apply to Karachi and Hyderabad Districts.

The document also substitutes sections regarding penalties for failure to furnish declarations or comply with notices.

It substitutes Section 3 to establish specific tax rates per acre for various crops like cotton, wheat, and orchards, distinguishing between barrage and non-barrage areas. Additionally, it introduces new sections imposing penalties for failure to furnish declarations or comply with notices regarding land cultivation.

It establishes new tax rates based on crop type and land location (barrage vs non-barrage) effective from August 1, 1999. Additionally, it introduces penalties for failing to furnish declarations or complying with notices, as well as for concealing cropped areas.

metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to amend the Sindh Agricultural Income Tax Act, 1994.

The text also establishes specific penalties for failing to furnish declarations or comply with notices, ensuring owners receive a hearing before penalties are imposed.

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Agricultural Income Tax (Amendment) Ordinance, 2000
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to amend the Sindh Agricultural Income Tax Act, 1994.

Additionally, it introduces new sections imposing penalties for failure to furnish declarations or comply with notices, including provisions for concealed cropped areas.

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Agricultural Income Tax Ordinance, 1993
metadata.long_title: An ordinance to provide for imposition of tax on income from agricultural land in the Province of Sindh.
metadata.territorial_extent: the whole of the Province of Sindh
metadata.administering_body: Government of the Province of Sindh
metadata.one_line: Imposes tax on income from agricultural land in Sindh exceeding 4000 produce index units.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance provides for the imposition of tax on income derived from agricultural land situated in the Province of Sindh. It defines key terms such as 'land', 'owner', and 'Collector' and establishes that no tax shall be charged on land not exceeding 4000 produce index units. The tax is levied at a rate of two rupees per index unit on land cultivated in excess of this limit, payable by the land owner. The Ordinance outlines procedures for assessment, collection, exemptions, appeals, and the power to make rules.

metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to amend the Sindh Agricultural Income Tax Act, 1994.

It substitutes sections 3, 6-A, 6-B, 6-C, and 6-D to establish new tax rates based on crop type and acreage, introduce net income assessment from July 1998, and define penalties for failure to furnish declarations or conceal cropped areas.

The substitution changes the title from 'Operational Director' to 'Managing Director'. It was promulgated by the Governor of Sindh on October 24, 1983, and came into force immediately.

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Animals Slaughter Control (Amendment) Ordinance, 2004
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to amend the Sind Animals Slaughter Control Act, 1963.
metadata.one_line: Amends section 3(2)(c) of the Sind Animals Slaughter Control Act, 1963 regarding slaughter days.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance amends the Sind Animals Slaughter Control Act, 1963 to modify the provisions concerning specified days for animal slaughter. It was promulgated by the Governor of Sindh under Article 128 of the Constitution because the Provincial Assembly was not in session and immediate action was deemed necessary. The amendment substitutes a clause allowing the Government to specify slaughter days via notification in the official Gazette.

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Archives Ordinance, 2013
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to provide for the acquisition, custody and preservation of public records of the Province of Sindh and archival materials of historical and national significance to the Province of Sindh.
metadata.territorial_extent: the whole of the Province of Sindh
metadata.max_penalty: imprisonment for a term extending to six months or fine extending to five hundred thousand rupees or both
metadata.one_line: Establishes the Sindh Archives and an Advisory Board to manage, preserve, and provide access to public records in Sindh.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance establishes the Sindh Archives as a department responsible for storing and preserving public records and archival materials of historical significance. It creates an Advisory Board comprising government officials and academicians to oversee the archives' management. The law defines what constitutes a public record, outlines access rules after twenty years, and prescribes penalties for unauthorized destruction or disposal of these records.

name: SINDH ARID ZONE DEVELOPMENT AUTHORITY (AMENDMENT) ORDINANCE, 1998

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Arid Zone Development Authority (Amendment) Ordinance, 1998

metadata.summary: This Ordinance amends the Sind Arid Zone Development Authority Act, 1985 to introduce the office of Vice Chairman. The new position is reserved for a Member of the Provincial Assembly and is designated as a non-whole-time office without salary or fees. Additionally, the Ordinance defines the powers and functions of the Vice Chairman, assigning duties as directed by the Chairman.

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Bank Ordinance, 1995
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to establish a Bank for providing commercial banking and investment banking service in the Province of Sindh.
metadata.territorial_extent: the whole of the Sindh Province
metadata.one_line: Establishes the Sindh Bank to provide commercial and investment banking services in Sindh.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance establishes the Sindh Bank as a body corporate with perpetual succession to carry on banking business. It defines the bank's authorized share capital, the composition of its Board of Directors, and the qualifications for shareholders. The document outlines the powers of the Board, the conduct of meetings, and the authority to make bye-laws for the regulation of the bank's affairs.

It substitutes 'Boards at Hyderabad and Mirpurkhas' for 'Board at Hyderabad' and establishes a new Board at Mirpurkhas. The amendment also updates references in the Schedule and assigns the Executive District Officer Education as an authority for the new Board.

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Buildings Control (Amendment) Ordinance, 1990
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance further to amend the Sind Buildings Control Ordinance, 1979.
metadata.one_line: Amends the Sind Buildings Control Ordinance, 1979 to allow suspension of no objection certificates if construction is not in public interest.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance amends the Sind Buildings Control Ordinance, 1979 to introduce new powers for the Government regarding building construction. It allows the Government to suspend or cancel a no objection certificate issued under section 6 if the construction is deemed not to be in the public interest before the building is completed. The amendment also mandates that any order passed under this power must be re-processed by the Authority following directions given by the Government.

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Buildings Control (Amendment) Ordinance, 1994
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to amend the Sind Buildings Control Ordinance, 1979.
metadata.one_line: Amends the Sindh Buildings Control Ordinance, 1979 to prohibit compounding of offences regarding building works in violation of approved plans.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance amends the Sind Buildings Control Ordinance, 1979 by modifying section 19. Specifically, it alters sub-section (1-A) to add a proviso prohibiting the compounding of any offence related to building works commenced or carried out in violation of approved plans. The amendment changes the punctuation at the end of the existing provision from a full stop to a semi-colon before adding the new text. It was promulgated by the Governor of Sindh on February 2, 1994, as the Provincial Assembly was not in session.

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Buildings Control (Amendment) Ordinance, 1994
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to amend the Sind Buildings Control Ordinance, 1979.
metadata.one_line: Amends the Sind Buildings Control Ordinance, 1979 to prohibit compounding of offences regarding building works done in violation of approved plans.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance amends the Sind Buildings Control Ordinance, 1979 by modifying section 19. Specifically, it adds a proviso stating that no offence relating to building works commenced or carried out in violation of approved plans shall be compounded. The document was promulgated by the Governor of Sindh under Article 128 of the Constitution because the Provincial Assembly was not in session.

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Buildings Control (Amendment) Ordinance, 2001
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to amend the Sindh Buildings Control Ordinance, 1979.
metadata.commencement: on such date as the Government may specify by notification in the official Gazette
metadata.one_line: Amends the Sindh Buildings Control Ordinance, 1979 to allow compounding of offences with enhanced fees.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance amends the Sindh Buildings Control Ordinance, 1979 to facilitate the compounding of offences related to building works. It introduces new subsections allowing authorities to compound offences for approved plans and violations regarding footprints or open spaces upon payment of enhanced composition fees. The text specifies conditions under which offences cannot be compounded, such as environmentally degrading activities or violations of road widening schemes.

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Buildings Control (Second Amendment) Ordinance, 1990
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance further to amend the Sind Buildings Control Ordinance, 1979.
metadata.one_line: Amends the Sind Buildings Control Ordinance, 1979 to allow suspension of no objection certificates if construction is not in public interest.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance amends the Sind Buildings Control Ordinance, 1979 to introduce new provisions regarding the suspension or cancellation of no objection certificates. It empowers the Government to suspend such certificates without notice if satisfied that building construction is not in the public interest. The amendment also mandates re-processing of matters where orders are passed under the new subsections.

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Buildings Control Ordinance, 1979
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to provide for regulation of the planning, construction, control and demolition of buildings and disposal of buildings and plots in the Province of Sindh.
metadata.commencement: from such date and in such area as Government may, by notification, specify
metadata.administering_body: Government of Sindh (via the Authority appointed by notification)
metadata.one_line: This Ordinance regulates building planning, construction, control, demolition, and plot disposal in Sindh through licensing and authority oversight.
metadata.summary: The Sindh Buildings Control Ordinance, 1979 was promulgated to regulate town planning, construction quality, building control, pricing, and the disposal of plots and buildings in Sindh. It establishes an Authority and a Licensing Board to grant licenses to architects, engineers, builders, and developers while setting standards for private and public buildings. The Ordinance also provides mechanisms for inspecting buildings, demolishing dangerous structures, levying interest on unpaid installments, and framing necessary rules and regulations.

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Civil Courts (Amendment) Ordinance, 1991
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to amend the Sind Civil Courts Ordinance, 1962.
metadata.one_line: Amends the Sind Civil Courts Ordinance, 1962 regarding jurisdiction limits and fee structures.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance amends the Sind Civil Courts Ordinance, 1962 to adjust original jurisdiction limits for District Judges in civil suits. It specifically revises monetary thresholds for Karachi districts and updates fee amounts in sections 18 and 24 of the parent law.

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Civil Courts (Amendment) Ordinance, 1994
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to further amend the Sindh Civil Courts Ordinance, 1962.
metadata.one_line: Amends the Sindh Civil Courts Ordinance, 1962 by increasing a monetary limit in section 13.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance amends the Sindh Civil Courts Ordinance, 1962 to increase a specific monetary figure from two lacs and fifty thousand to five hundred thousand. It was promulgated by the Governor of Sindh under Article 128 of the Constitution because the Provincial Assembly was not in session. The amendment specifically targets section 13, sub-section (1), clause (a) of the parent Ordinance.

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Civil Courts (Amendment) Ordinance, 2002
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to amend the Sindh Civil Courts Ordinance, 1962.
metadata.one_line: Amends the Sindh Civil Courts Ordinance, 1962 to adjust jurisdictional limits and transfer pending suits.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance amends the Sindh Civil Courts Ordinance, 1962 to alter the original jurisdiction of District Judges in civil suits. It substitutes specific sections to change pecuniary limits from five lacs to thirty lacs of rupees for certain courts and transfers pending matters from the High Court to District Judges outside Karachi.

metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to repeal the Sindh Civil Servants (Assessment of Suitability of Appointment) Ordinance, 2001.

metadata.one_line: This Ordinance repeals the Sindh Civil Servants (Assessment of Suitability of Appointment) Ordinance, 2001.

Its sole purpose is to repeal the Sindh Civil Servants (Assessment of Suitability of Appointments) Ordinance, 2001. The action was taken pursuant to directions from the Chief Executive and due to the suspension of the Provincial Assembly under Proclamation Order No. 1 of 1999.

name: SINDH CIVIL SERVANTS (REGULARIZATION OF ABSORPTION) ORDINANCE, 2011

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Civil Servants (Regularization of Absorption) Act, 2011
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to provide for regularization of the services of certain employees absorbed as civil servants, in various departments of Government.
metadata.one_line: This Ordinance regularizes the absorption of certain employees as civil servants in Sindh government departments.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance provides for the regularization of services for employees absorbed as civil servants in various Sindh government departments. It deems such employees to have been validly absorbed on a regular basis from their original absorption date if they held the post before the Ordinance commenced. Additionally, it grants seniority benefits based on equivalent posts held prior to absorption.

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Civil Servants (Amendment) Ordinance, 2001
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to amend the Sindh Civil Servants Act, 1973.
metadata.one_line: Amends the Sindh Civil Servants Act, 1973 regarding appointment percentages in lower pay scales.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance amends the Sindh Civil Servants Act, 1973 to change the wording in section 5 regarding appointment percentages. It substitutes 'one percentum' with 'two percentum' for posts in basic pay scale 15 and below. The legislation was promulgated by the Governor of Sindh because the Provincial Assembly was dissolved following the October 1999 proclamation.

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Civil Servants (Amendment) Ordinance, 2002
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to amend the Sindh Civil Servants Act, 1973.
metadata.one_line: Amends the Sindh Civil Servants Act, 1973 to allow out-of-turn promotion for exceptional gallantry or performance.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance amends the Sindh Civil Servants Act, 1973 by inserting a new section 9-A. The amendment allows civil servants who exhibit proven gallantry or very exceptional performance beyond the call of duty to be granted out-of-turn promotion, awards, or rewards. These benefits may be prescribed in such manner as deemed appropriate. The Ordinance was promulgated by the Governor of Sindh on January 22, 2002, and came into force immediately.

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Civil Servants (Amendment) Ordinance, 2012
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to amend the Sind Civil Servants Act, 1973.
metadata.one_line: Amends the Sind Civil Servants Act, 1973 to define absorption and deputation and grant powers for appointments.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance amends the Sind Civil Servants Act, 1973 to insert definitions for 'absorption' and 'deputation'. It grants the Government (Chief Minister) powers to appoint civil servants on deputation or absorption and to award out-of-turn promotions for gallantry. The law also validates appointments made prior to its enactment under the new provisions.

name: SINDH CIVIL SERVANTS (ASSESSMENT OF SUITABILITY OF APPOINTMENTS) ORDINANCE, 2001

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Civil Servants (Assessment of Suitability of Appointments) Ordinance, 2001
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to provide for assessment of suitability of the persons appointed to the specified posts without reference to the Commission and the persons appointed to the service by transfer who were not otherwise eligible for transfer under the Rules
metadata.one_line: This Ordinance mandates suitability assessments for civil servants appointed to specified posts without Commission reference.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance provides a mechanism to assess the suitability of persons appointed to specified posts in Sindh who were appointed without reference to the Sindh Public Service Commission. It applies to individuals appointed between 1985 and 1997 who are still in employment, requiring them to appear for interviews and written tests. If a person fails to comply with directions or is found unsuitable, their service is terminated immediately; otherwise, they retain their seniority. The Ordinance also bars courts from entertaining proceedings related to its provisions.

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Civil Servants (Second Amendment) Ordinance, 2001
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to amend this Sindh Civil Servants Act, 1973.
metadata.one_line: Amends the Sindh Civil Servants Act, 1973 by substituting 'twenty' for 'twenty-five' in section 13(i).
metadata.summary: This Ordinance amends the Sindh Civil Servants Act, 1973 following the dissolution of the Provincial Assembly. It substitutes the word 'twenty' for 'twenty-five' in clause (i) of section 13 of the said Act. The amendment was promulgated by the Governor of Sindh under emergency powers due to the dissolved assembly status.

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Civil Servants (Second Amendment) Ordinance, 2002
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to amend the Sindh Civil Servants Act, 1973.
metadata.one_line: Amends the Sindh Civil Servants Act, 1973 by granting indemnity to civil servants and barring legal proceedings against them.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance amends the Sindh Civil Servants Act, 1973 to provide immunity for civil servants acting in good faith within their official capacity. It inserts new sections that bar suits or prosecutions against such officials and prevents courts from questioning orders made by the Governor under the Act. The legislation was promulgated because the Provincial Assembly was dissolved following the October 1999 proclamation.

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Civil Servants (Second Amendment) Ordinance, 2012
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to further amend the Sind Civil Servants Act, 1973.
metadata.one_line: Amends the Sind Civil Servants Act, 1973 regarding out-of-turn promotions for gallantry.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance amends the Sind Civil Servants Act, 1973 to clarify provisions on out-of-turn promotions. It grants awards or rewards to civil servants exhibiting gallantry or exceptional performance beyond duty calls. The amendment also deems previous out-of-turn promotions made under section 9-A as having been made on a regular basis.

name: SINDH CIVIL SERVANTS HOUSING FOUNDATION ORDINANCE, 2005

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Civil Servants Housing Foundation Ordinance, 2005
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to provide for the establishment of a Housing Foundation for providing houses on no profit no loss basis to the civil servants and the retired civil servants in the Province of Sindh.
metadata.commencement: at once for this section; remaining provisions on such date as may be notified by Government
metadata.one_line: Establishes a Housing Foundation to provide houses on no profit no loss basis to civil servants and retired civil servants in Sindh.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance establishes the Sindh Civil Servants Housing Foundation to provide housing for civil servants and retired civil servants in Sindh on a no-profit, no-loss basis. It creates a body corporate with a Board of Directors comprising government officials and appointed members to manage the foundation's functions. The foundation is empowered to acquire land, hold properties, allocate residential units based on seniority or special circumstances, and maintain accounts audited as prescribed.

The document was promulgated by the Governor of Sindh under Article 128 of the Constitution because the Provincial Assembly was not in session.

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Coal Authority Ordinance, 1993
