metadata.summary: This Ordinance establishes the Sindh Coal Authority as a body corporate responsible for the exploration, development, processing, exploitation, mining, and utilization of coal in the Province of Sindh. The Authority is empowered to acquire property, enter into contracts, promote joint ventures with foreign investors, and formulate schemes for coal resources. It operates under the general direction of the Board, which acts on commercial considerations and follows directions from the Government of Sindh.

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Coal Authority Ordinance, 1993

establishes: Board of the Sindh Coal Authority

The Authority is empowered to acquire property, formulate schemes, promote joint ventures with foreign investors, and manage its finances under the supervision of the Government of Sindh. It defines key terms such as 'Coal' and 'Board', outlines the powers of its officers including the Chairman and Director General, and mandates annual audits by the Auditor General of Pakistan.

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Coal Authority Ordinance, 1993
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to provide for the establishment of the Sindh Coal Authority.
establishes: Board of the Sindh Coal Authority

The Authority is headed by a Board and includes functionaries such as a Director General to oversee operations. It possesses powers to acquire property, formulate schemes, promote joint ventures, and manage its own funds and accounts under the supervision of the Government of Sindh.

metadata.one_line: Amends the 2009 Act to extend the Prosecutor General's term by three years.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance amends the Sindh Criminal Prosecution Service (Constitution, Functions and Powers) Act, 2009. It was promulgated by the Governor of Sindh because the Provincial Assembly was not in session. The amendment substitutes Section 6(3) to allow the Government to extend the Prosecutor General's term for a further period of three years.

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Development Authorities Laws (Repeal) Ordinance, 2002
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to repeal the enactments relating to the Development Authorities in the Province of Sindh.
repeals: The Karachi Development Authority Order, 1957
The Hyderabad Development Authority Act, 1976
The Sehwan Development Authority Act, 1993
The Lyari Development Authority Act, 1993
The Malir Development Authority Act, 1993
The Larkana Development Authority Act, 1994
metadata.one_line: This Ordinance repeals all Sindh enactments relating to Development Authorities effective July 1, 2002.
metadata.summary: The Sindh Development Authorities Laws (Repeal) Ordinance, 2002 was promulgated by the Governor of Sindh on July 3, 2002. It was issued because the Provincial Assembly was dissolved following the October 1999 Proclamation and circumstances required immediate action. The Ordinance repeals six specific laws enacted between 1957 and 1994 that governed various Development Authorities in the Province of Sindh.

name: SINDH DISPOSAL OF URBAN LAND (REPEAL) ORDINANCE, 2005

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Disposal of Urban Land (Repeal) Ordinance, 2005
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to repeal the Sindh Disposal of Urban Land Ordinance, 2002.
repeals: Sindh Disposal of Urban Land Ordinance, 2002
metadata.status_evidence: The Sindh Disposal of Urban Land Ordinance, 2002, is hereby repealed.
metadata.one_line: This Ordinance repeals the Sindh Disposal of Urban Land Ordinance, 2002.
metadata.summary: The Governor of Sindh promulgated this Ordinance to immediately repeal the Sindh Disposal of Urban Land Ordinance, 2002. It was issued under Article 128 of the Constitution because the Provincial Assembly was not in session and immediate action was deemed necessary. The entire Ordinance came into force at once upon its promulgation on November 11, 2005.

name: SINDH DISPOSAL OF URBAN LAND ORDINANCE, 2002

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Disposal of Urban Land Ordinance, 2002
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to regulate the disposal of urban land in the Province of Sindh.
metadata.one_line: Regulates the disposal of urban land in Sindh through public auctions, market pricing, and specific provisions for amenity and residential plots.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance regulates the disposal of urban land within the Province of Sindh to ensure transparency and fair pricing. It mandates that most plots be sold via open public auction at a price not less than the determined market price, while allowing exceptions for amenity plots and specific government agreements. The document defines various land categories such as residential, industrial, and commercial plots, establishes procedures for determining reserve prices, and provides for the continuation of existing leases with renewal conditions based on occupancy value.

name: SINDH DOW UNIVERSITY OF HEALTH SCIENCES (AMENDMENT) ORDINANCE, 2004

metadata.short_title: The Dow University of Health Sciences (Amendment) Ordinance, 2004
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to amend the Dow University of Health Sciences Ordinance, 2003.
metadata.territorial_extent: the territorial limits and in respect of the institutions as specified by the Governor
metadata.commencement: at once and be deemed to have taken effect on and from 29th December, 2003
metadata.one_line: Amends the Dow University of Health Sciences Ordinance, 2003 regarding jurisdiction, faculties, and personnel.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance amends the Dow University of Health Sciences Ordinance, 2003 to update its provisions on jurisdiction, faculty composition, and personnel management. It inserts new sections defining the university's territorial limits and powers while adding specific roles like Research Officers and modifying clauses related to government appointments and constituent colleges. The amendments also update the list of faculties included in the university's schedule.

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Education Foundation Ordinance, 1992
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to Provide for the establishment of an Education Foundation in the Province of Sindh.
metadata.territorial_extent: the whole of the Province of Sindh
metadata.one_line: Establishes the Sindh Education Foundation to promote and develop education in Sindh through grants, loans, and institutional support.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance establishes the Sindh Education Foundation as a body corporate with perpetual succession to promote and develop education in the Province of Sindh. The Foundation is managed by a Board headed by the Chief Minister as Chairman and includes a Managing Director appointed by the Government. It aims to expand educational facilities, prepare projects for less developed areas, provide financial grants and interest-free loans to institutions, and manage a fund derived from government contributions, investments, and donations.

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Employees Special Allowance (Payment) (Amendment) Ordinance, 1991
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance further to amend the Sind Employees Special Allowance (Payment) Act, 1986.
metadata.commencement: at once and deemed to have taken effect on 1st day of December, 1990
metadata.parent_law: The Sind Employees Special Allowance (Payment) Act, 1986
repeals: The Sindh Employees Special Allowance (Payment) (Amendment) Ordinance, 1990
metadata.one_line: Amends the 1986 Act to mandate an additional special allowance of 200 rupees per month for employees in Sindh.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance amends the Sind Employees Special Allowance (Payment) Act, 1986 to introduce a new provision for an additional special allowance. It mandates that every employee in Sindh be paid an extra two hundred rupees per month starting from December 1, 1990. The legislation was promulgated by the Governor of Sindh under Article 128 of the Constitution because the Provincial Assembly was not in session.

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Employees Special Allowance (Payment) (Amendment) Ordinance, 1995
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance further to amend the Sindh Employees Special Allowance (Payment) Act, 1986.
metadata.parent_law: The Sindh Employees Special Allowance (Payment) Act, 1986
amends: The Sindh Employees Special Allowance (Payment) Act, 1986
metadata.one_line: Amends the 1986 Act to add a Rs. 100 monthly special allowance for employees starting May 1, 1995.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance amends the Sindh Employees Special Allowance (Payment) Act, 1986 to introduce an additional special allowance. It applies to every employee regardless of their wage status. The new provision mandates that employers pay an extra one hundred rupees per month for employment on or after May 1, 1995.

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Employees Special Allowance (Payment) Ordinance, 1990
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance further TO amend the Sind Employees Special Allowance (Payment) Act, 1986.
metadata.commencement: at once and deemed to have taken effect on 1st day of December, 1990
key_definitions: relief due to rise in the cost of living
metadata.one_line: Amends the 1986 Act to add an additional special allowance for employees in Sindh based on wage levels.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance amends the Sind Employees Special Allowance (Payment) Act, 1986 to introduce an additional special allowance for employees. It applies to employees whose wages do not exceed a specific threshold and sets out rates for those with higher wages. The allowance is intended to provide relief against the rise in the cost of living and can be set off against existing relief amounts.

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Enquiries and Anti-Corruption Ordinance, 1991
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to provide for the constitution of a special agency for the investigation of certain offences relating to corruption by, or enquiry into mis-conduct of, public servants and for holding preliminary enquiries against such servants in Sindh.
repeals: The Sind Anti-Corruption Establishment Ordinance, 1961
metadata.one_line: Constitutes a special agency in Sindh to investigate corruption and misconduct of public servants.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance establishes the Enquiries and Anti-Corruption Establishment within the Government of Sindh. It grants the Director and officers powers of search, arrest, and seizure similar to police officers for investigating specific offences listed in the Schedule. The law defines key terms such as 'mis-conduct' and 'public servant' and repeals the previous 1961 Ordinance.

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Entertainments Duty (Amendment) Ordinance, 1992
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to amend the Sindh Entertainments Duty Act, 1958.
metadata.one_line: Amends the Sindh Entertainments Duty Act, 1958 by changing duty amounts and adding cinema owners to specific clauses.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance amends the Sindh Entertainments Duty Act, 1958 to adjust financial figures and expand the scope of certain clauses. It substitutes the word 'seventy five' with 'fifty five' in section 3 and adds references to cinema owners and film exhibitors in section 11. The Ordinance was promulgated by the Governor of Sindh because the Provincial Assembly was not in session.

name: SINDH ESSENTIAL COMMODITIES PRICE CONTROL AND PREVENTION OF PROFITEERING AND HOARDING ORDINANCE, 2005

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Essential Commodities Price Control and Prevention of Profiteering and Hoarding Ordinance, 2005
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to provide for price control and prevention of profiteering on and hoarding of essential commodities.
metadata.max_penalty: Rs. 500/- for wholesalers and Rs. 200/- for retailers (or seizure of goods)
metadata.one_line: This Ordinance establishes price controls and penalties for profiteering and hoarding of essential commodities in Sindh.
metadata.summary: The Sindh Essential Commodities Price Control and Prevention of Profiteering and Hoarding Ordinance, 2005 was promulgated by the Governor to regulate prices and prevent unfair trade practices regarding essential goods. It empowers the Government to issue orders fixing maximum prices, limiting stock possession, and requiring dealers to maintain records and display price lists. The Ordinance defines key terms such as 'dealer' and 'essential commodity', outlines specific offences with associated fines ranging from Rs. 100 to Rs. 500, and provides for police support to inspectors in enforcing these regulations.

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Eye Surgery (Restriction) Ordinance, 2013
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to prevent the surgery of eye by the persons other than registered medical practioners.
metadata.territorial_extent: the whole of Province of Sindh
metadata.max_penalty: seven years imprisonment and fine up to five hundred thousand rupees
metadata.one_line: Restricts eye surgery to registered medical practitioners in Sindh with penalties for violations.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance prevents non-registered persons from performing eye surgery in the Province of Sindh. It defines terms like complete blindness and eye surgery, and prescribes imprisonment and fines for unauthorized practice or holding oneself out as a practitioner. Offences are cognizable and triable by Magistrates of the First Class.

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Finance (Amendment) Ordinance, 1991
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to amend the Sind Finance Act, 1964 and the Sind Finance Act, 1975.
metadata.one_line: Amends the Sind Finance Acts of 1964 and 1975 to levy surcharges for water supply and drainage schemes.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance amends the Sind Finance Act, 1964 and the Sind Finance Act, 1975 to introduce new surcharges on existing cess and fees. The amendments are designed to fund expenses related to water supply and drainage schemes undertaken by local councils in Sindh. It was promulgated by the Governor of Sindh because the Provincial Assembly was not in session.

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Finance (Amendment) Ordinance, 1995
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to amend the Sind Finance Act, 1964.
metadata.commencement: at once and deemed to have taken effect on and from the 27th day of October, 1994
metadata.one_line: Amends the Sindh Finance Act, 1964 by substituting fees in Section 12 via Governor's Ordinance.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance amends the Sindh Finance Act, 1964 to update fee structures within Section 12. It substitutes 'eighteen paisa' with 'one rupee' and replaces sub-section (2) entirely. The measure was promulgated by the Governor of Sindh under Article 128 of the Constitution because the Provincial Assembly was not in session.

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Finance (Amendment) Ordinance, 2001
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to amend the Sindh Finance Act, 1994 to levy cess for special maintenance and development of infrastructure for smooth and safer movement of goods entering or leaving the Province from or out side the country through air or sea;
metadata.one_line: Amends the Sindh Finance Act, 1994 to levy a cess for infrastructure maintenance related to goods movement via air or sea.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance amends the Sindh Finance Act, 1994 to introduce a new cess for the special maintenance and development of infrastructure. The levy applies specifically to the smooth and safer movement of goods entering or leaving the Province of Sindh through air or sea routes. It defines 'infrastructure' broadly to include roads, ports, public facilities, and security measures necessary for goods transport. The proceeds are designated for infrastructure development and ancillary activities as prescribed.

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Finance (Second Amendment) Ordinance, 2001
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to amend the Sindh Finance Act, 1994.
metadata.commencement: at once and deemed to have taken effect on 24th February, 2001
metadata.one_line: Amends the Sindh Finance Act, 1994 to levy a cess on goods for infrastructure maintenance.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance amends the Sindh Finance Act, 1994 to introduce a new cess for the maintenance and development of infrastructure. The cess applies to goods entering or leaving the Province by road, air, or sea at a rate of 0.5 percent of their value. It also adds restrictions on refund claims, limiting them to three months from the date of payment.

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Financial Laws (Amendment) Ordinance, 2001
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to rationalize and abolish certain taxes and fees in the Province of Sindh
amends: The Sindh Urban Immovable Property Tax Act, 1958
The Sindh Motor Vehicles Taxation Act, 1958
key_definitions: seating capacity (excluding driver and conductor seats)
tax payment rates after ten/fifteen years
metadata.one_line: Amends four Sindh financial acts to rationalize taxes and fees following the suspension of the Provincial Assembly.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance was promulgated by the Governor of Sindh to rationalize and abolish certain taxes and fees while the Provincial Assembly was suspended. It amends the Sindh Urban Immovable Property Tax Act, 1958, and the Sindh Motor Vehicles Taxation Act, 1958 by substituting specific monetary figures and inserting explanations regarding seating capacity and tax rates for older vehicles. Additionally, it omits sections from the Sindh Finance Act, 1990, and the Sindh Finance Act, 1994 to effectuate these financial changes.

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Fisheries (Amendment) Ordinance, 2003
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to amend the Sindh Fisheries Ordinance, 1980.
metadata.max_penalty: imprisonment for a term which may extend to one year or with a fine which may extend to fifty thousand rupees or with both
metadata.one_line: Amends the Sindh Fisheries Ordinance, 1980 by adding definitions and increasing penalties for contraventions.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance amends the Sindh Fisheries Ordinance, 1980 to include a new definition of 'net' in section 2. It also substitutes subsection (1) of section 21 with enhanced penalties for contraventions, including imprisonment up to one year or fines up to fifty thousand rupees.

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Fisheries Ordinance, 1980
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to amend and consolidate the law relating to fisheries in the Province of Sindh.
repeals: The Sindh Fisheries Ordinance, 1961
metadata.max_penalty: One hundred thousand rupees plus cost of fish caught
metadata.one_line: This Ordinance consolidates and amends laws regarding fisheries, licensing, and penalties in Sindh.
metadata.summary: The Sindh Fisheries Ordinance, 1980 was promulgated by the Governor to amend and consolidate existing laws on fisheries in the Province of Sindh. It establishes a regulatory framework for fishing licenses, prohibited gear, fish sanctuaries, and waste discharge. The document defines key terms such as 'fisherman' and 'fishing craft', outlines penalties for illegal activities like unlicensed fishing or discharging factory effluent, and repeals the previous 1961 Ordinance.

metadata.short_title: The Sindh General Clauses (Amendment) Ordinance, 2002
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to further amend the Sindh General Clauses Act, 1956.
metadata.one_line: Amends the Sindh General Clauses Act, 1956 by inserting a new section regarding the publication of rules and orders.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance amends the Sindh General Clauses Act, 1956 to insert a new section requiring that all rules, notifications, orders, regulations, and circulars having the effect of law be published in the official Gazette. It was promulgated by the Governor of Sindh after the dissolution of the Provincial Assembly in October 1999, exercising powers under the Provisional Constitution Order No. 1 of 1999 and Provisional Constitution (Amendment) Order No. 9 of 1999. The Ordinance comes into force immediately upon promulgation.

name: SINDH GENERAL PROVIDENT INVESTMENT FUND ORDINANCE, 2008

metadata.short_title: The Sindh General Provident Investment Fund Ordinance, 2008
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to provide for the establishment of a General Provident Investment Fund in the Sindh Province.
metadata.commencement: at once and deemed to have taken effect on 1st July, 2007
establishes: Sindh General Provident Investment Fund Board
metadata.one_line: Establishes the Sindh General Provident Investment Fund and sets up a Board to manage it for government employees.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance establishes the Sindh General Provident Investment Fund in the Province of Sindh. The Fund is managed by a Board comprising senior government officials and a private sector representative. It utilizes seed money from the Provincial Consolidated Fund and invests returns to clear G.P. Fund liabilities for employees.

name: Sindh Government Educational and Training Institutions Ordinance, 1960

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Government Educational and Training Institutions Ordinance, 1960
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to establish Boards of Governors or Government Educational and training institutions in Sindh.
metadata.commencement: on such date as may be notified by Government
metadata.one_line: Establishes Boards of Governors to manage Government educational and training institutions in Sindh.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance establishes Boards of Governors for the efficient management and control of Government educational and training institutions in Sindh. It defines the composition, tenure, and powers of these boards, including their authority to acquire property, recruit staff, and frame regulations. The legislation also provides for a Board Fund, audit procedures, and stipulates that board members and employees are deemed public servants.

name: SINDH GOVERNMENT LAND (CANCELLATION OF ALLOTMENTS, CONVERSIONS AND EXCHANGES) (AMENDMENT) ORDINANCE, 2002

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Government Land (Cancellation of Allotments, Conversions and Exchanges) (Amendment) Ordinance, 2002
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to amend the Sindh Government Land (Cancellation of Allotments, Conversions and Exchanges) Ordinance, 2001.

amends: The Sindh Government Land (Cancellation of Allotments, Conversions and Exchanges) Ordinance, 2001
metadata.one_line: Amends the 2001 Sindh Government Land Ordinance to include autonomous bodies and development authorities in government land definitions.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance amends the Sindh Government Land (Cancellation of Allotments, Conversions and Exchanges) Ordinance, 2001. It expands the definition of 'Government land' to include land vesting in autonomous bodies and development authorities established by law. The amendment also inserts a specific word into Section 3 of the parent Ordinance.

name: SINDH GOVERNMENT SERVANTS BENEVOLENT FUND (AMENDMENT) ORDINANCE, 2008

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Government Servants Benevolent Fund (Amendment) Ordinance, 2008
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to amend the Sind Government Servants Benevolent Fund Ordinance, 1960.

amends: Sind Government Servants Benevolent Fund Ordinance, 1960

metadata.summary: This Ordinance amends the Sind Government Servants Benevolent Fund Ordinance, 1960 to update administrative terminology. Specifically, it substitutes the word 'District' for 'Divisional' and 'Division' in section 6 of the parent Act. The legislation was promulgated by the Governor of Sindh under Article 128 of the Constitution because the Provincial Assembly was not in session.

name: SINDH HEALTH INSTITUTIONS (ESTABLISHMENT AND MANGEMENT) ORDINANCE, 2005

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Health Institutions (Establishment and Management) Ordinance, 2005
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to provide for the establishment and management of health institutions in the Province of Sindh.
metadata.one_line: Establishes health institutions in Sindh with autonomous management by a Board of Governors.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance provides for the establishment and management of health institutions in the Province of Sindh. It creates a body corporate known as the Board of Governors to administer these institutions, granting them autonomy to provide quality healthcare. The Ordinance outlines the composition of the Board, appointment of officers, financial management through a specific fund, and the power to make rules and regulations.

name: SINDH HIGH DENSITY DEVELOPMENT BOARD (AMENDMENT) ORDINANCE, 2013

metadata.short_title: The Sindh High Density Development Board (Amendment) Act, 2013
metadata.long_title: An Act to amend the Sindh High Density Development Board Act, 2010.
amends: Sindh High Density Development Board Act, 2010
metadata.one_line: Amends the Sindh High Density Development Board Act, 2010 to substitute the composition of the Board.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance amends the Sindh High Density Development Board Act, 2010 by substituting Section 3. The amendment defines the new constitution of the Board for cities in the Province. It lists specific members including the Chief Minister, Ministers, Secretaries, Mayors, and District officials.

name: SINDH HIV AND AIDS CONTROL TREATMENT AND PROTECTION ORDINANCE, 2013

metadata.short_title: The Sindh HIV and AIDS Control Treatment and Protection Ordinance, 2013
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to control the transmission and spread of HIV in the Province of Sindh and to provide measures for the treatment, care and support of the People Living With HIV and AIDS.
metadata.territorial_extent: the whole of the Province of Sindh
metadata.max_penalty: imprisonment of not less than two years and fine which may extend to ten hundred thousand rupees
metadata.one_line: This Ordinance controls HIV transmission in Sindh, provides treatment support, establishes the Sindh AIDS Commission, and prohibits discrimination.
metadata.summary: The Sindh HIV and AIDS Control Treatment and Protection Ordinance, 2013 aims to control the spread of HIV within the Province of Sindh. It establishes the Sindh AIDS Commission to oversee implementation, treatment, care, and support for people living with HIV/AIDS. The document defines key terms, prohibits discrimination based on HIV status, outlines prevention measures, and prescribes penalties for negligence or unauthorized disclosure of confidential information.

name: SINDH INFORMATION OF TEMPORARY RESIDENTS ORDINANCE 2015

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Information of Temporary Residents Ordinance, 2015
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to provide for sharing of information of tenants and other temporary residents in the Province of Sindh.
metadata.territorial_extent: the whole of Province of Sindh
metadata.max_penalty: imprisonment up to six months and fine between ten thousand and forty five thousand rupees
metadata.one_line: This Ordinance mandates information sharing between landlords, hotels, and police to combat terrorism in Sindh.
metadata.summary: The Sindh Information of Temporary Residents Ordinance, 2015 establishes a legal framework for collecting and sharing data on tenants and guests with the police. It requires property dealers, landlords, and hotel managers to provide identification details within specific timeframes to prevent terrorism and other crimes. The ordinance defines various terms related to lodging, mandates database maintenance by the police, and prescribes penalties for non-compliance.

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Information Technology Board (Amendment) Ordinance, 2004
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to amend the Sindh Information Technology Board Ordinance, 2002.
metadata.parent_law: The Sindh Information Technology Board Ordinance, 2002
amends: The Sindh Information Technology Board Ordinance, 2002
metadata.one_line: Amends the Sindh Information Technology Board Ordinance, 2002 regarding board composition and powers.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance amends the Sindh Information Technology Board Ordinance, 2002 to update definitions and board structure. It modifies Section 2 to define 'Member' and 'Vice-Chairperson', and revises Section 4 to specify the Governor as Chairperson and include private sector members. Additionally, it updates Section 5 regarding the promotion of information technology strategy and Section 7 concerning the delegation of powers by the Chairperson.

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Information Technology Board Ordinance, 2002
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to provide for the establishment of a Board of Information Technology in the Province of Sindh.
metadata.one_line: Establishes the Sindh Information Technology Board to promote IT development and establish an Accreditation Council.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance establishes the Sindh Information Technology Board as a corporate body within the Province of Sindh. The Board is empowered to promote information technology use, facilitate investment, and establish an accreditation council for education standardization. It outlines the Board's constitution, functions, funding mechanisms, and powers to make rules and regulations.

name: SINDH INSTITUTE OF UROLOGY AND TRANSPLANTATION ORDINANCE, 1990

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Institute of Urology and Transplantation Ordinance, 1990
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to provide for the establishment of an Institute of Urology and Transplantation.
establishes: Sindh Institute of Urology and Transplantation
metadata.one_line: Establishes the Sindh Institute of Urology and Transplantation to treat urological diseases, conduct research, and provide medical education.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance establishes the Sindh Institute of Urology and Transplantation by reconstituting the Urology Department of Dow Medical College. The Institute is empowered to treat patients, develop surgical techniques, teach students, conduct research, and train medical staff. It is administered by a Board of Governors comprising government officials, medical experts, and representatives from various organizations.

name: SINDH INSTITUTE OF UROLOGY AND TRANSPLANTATION ORDINANCE, 1990

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Institute of Urology and Transplantation Ordinance, 1990
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to provide for the establishment of an Institute of Urology and Transplantation.
establishes: Sindh Institute of Urology and Transplantation
metadata.one_line: Establishes the Sindh Institute of Urology and Transplantation to treat urological diseases, conduct research, and provide medical education.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance establishes the Sindh Institute of Urology and Transplantation by reconstituting the Urology Department of Dow Medical College. The Institute functions as a body corporate with powers to acquire property, sue, and be sued. Its primary objectives include treating urological diseases, developing medical techniques, conducting postgraduate teaching programs, training nursing staff, and promoting research in urology and transplantation. The affairs of the Institute are administered by a Board of Governors comprising government officials, medical experts, and representatives from various organizations.

metadata.short_title: The Sind Irrigation (Amendment) Ordinance, 1983
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to amend the Sind Irrigation Act, 1879.
metadata.commencement: at once; deemed to have taken effect on 1st day of April, 1983
metadata.one_line: Amends the Sind Irrigation Act, 1879 to allow levying drainage rates on cultivated land with tube well facilities.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance amends the Sind Irrigation Act, 1879 to authorize the Government to levy drainage rates on actually cultivated land under the command of Salinity Control and Reclamation Project. The rate applies where drainage facilities have been provided by tube wells or open surface drains, excluding the first two seasonal crops immediately following the notification of such facilities. Additionally, it empowers the Government to provide rules for recovering amounts payable under this section as arrears of land revenue.

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Irrigation (Amendment) Ordinance, 1999
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to amend the Sind Irrigation Act, 1879 and to provide for the abatement of certain orders relating to distribution of irrigation water in the Province.
metadata.max_penalty: three thousand rupees (fine) or imprisonment terms implied by 'Non-bailable offence' context
metadata.one_line: Amends the Sind Irrigation Act, 1879 and annuls specific irrigation water distribution orders in Sindh.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance amends the Sind Irrigation Act, 1879 to adjust time limits for penalties and fine amounts. It also abrogates specific orders granting irrigation water to listed applicants in the Sukkur, Kotri, and Gudu Barrage regions. Additionally, it establishes a new non-bailable offence for violations of sections 61 or 62 of the amended Act.

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Irrigation (Amendment) Ordinance, 2000
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to amend the Sindh Irrigation Act, 1879.
metadata.max_penalty: twenty thousand rupees
metadata.one_line: Amends the Sindh Irrigation Act, 1879 by increasing penalties and declaring certain offences non-bailable.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance amends the Sindh Irrigation Act, 1879 to increase fines and imprisonment terms for specific violations. It substitutes higher monetary penalties and longer durations in sections 61 and 62 of the original Act. Additionally, it inserts a new section declaring offences under these amended sections as non-bailable. The Ordinance was promulgated by the Governor of Sindh due to the suspension of the Provincial Assembly.

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Irrigation (Amendment) Ordinance, 2011
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to amend the Sind Irrigation Act, 1879.
metadata.max_penalty: imprisonment up to ten years and fine up to one million rupees
metadata.one_line: Amends the Sind Irrigation Act, 1879 to resume government land for flood discharge.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance amends the Sind Irrigation Act, 1879 to ensure that government land used for natural or artificial depression courses is exclusively reserved for flood and rain water discharge. It mandates that any person in possession of such land must vacate within seven days of the Ordinance's commencement. Failure to comply results in imprisonment up to ten years and a fine of up to one million rupees.

name: SINDH IRRIGATION AND DRAINAGE AUTHORITY (AMENDMENT) ORDINANCE, 2002

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Irrigation and Drainage Authority (Amendment) Ordinance, 2002
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to amend the Sindh Irrigation and Drainage Authority Act, 1997.
metadata.parent_law: The Sindh Irrigation and Drainage Authority Act, 1997
amends: The Sindh Irrigation and Drainage Authority Act, 1997
metadata.one_line: Amends the Sindh Irrigation and Drainage Authority Act, 1997 regarding authority composition and bye-laws.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance amends the Sindh Irrigation and Drainage Authority Act, 1997 to alter the composition of the Authority's members representing farmers from specific barrage commands. It also substitutes the number of representatives in a specific clause and omits references to Bye-Laws in the parent Act. The legislation was promulgated by the Governor of Sindh due to the dissolution of the Provincial Assembly.

name: SINDH IRRIGATION AND DRAINAGE AUTHORITY ORDINANCE, 1997

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Irrigation and Drainage Authority Ordinance, 1997
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to provide for the establishment of the Irrigation and Drainage Authority in the Province of Sindh.
metadata.territorial_extent: the whole of Province of Sindh
metadata.one_line: Establishes the Sindh Irrigation and Drainage Authority to manage water distribution, drainage, and flood control in Sindh.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance establishes the Sindh Irrigation and Drainage Authority as a body corporate within the Province of Sindh. It defines the authority's constitution, powers, and duties regarding equitable water distribution, effective drainage, and flood control. The document also sets up Area Water Boards and Farmers Organizations to facilitate beneficiary participation in managing irrigation networks.

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Judicial Academy Ordinance, 1993
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to establish a Provincial the Judicial Academy in the Province of Sindh.
metadata.one_line: Establishes the Sindh Judicial Academy to provide legal training and education for the judiciary and bar in Sindh.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance establishes the Sindh Judicial Academy as a body corporate headquartered in Karachi. The Academy is tasked with providing legal orientation, continuing education, and conducting seminars for members of the subordinate judiciary, law officers, and the bar. A Board of Governors, including the Chief Justice and Attorney General, will oversee its administration and policy.

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Land Revenue (Abolition) Ordinance, 2000
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to abolish the land revenue in the Province of Sindh.
metadata.one_line: Abolishes land revenue in Sindh for the Kharif season 1999-2000 while preserving pre-Kharif 1999 liabilities.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance was promulgated by the Governor of Sindh to immediately abolish land revenue in the province. It applies specifically to the Kharif season of 1999-2000, exempting farmers from charges during this period. However, it preserves the liability for any revenue due before Kharif 1999-2000 and maintains assessment procedures for periods prior to that date under the existing Act.

The amendment specifically includes land on which ushr or contribution in lieu thereof has been charged under the Zakat and Ushr Ordinance, 1980. It was promulgated by the Governor of Sindh on April 17, 1983, pursuant to the Proclamation of July 5, 1977 and the Provincial Constitution Order, 1981.

metadata.summary: This Ordinance amends the Sind Land Revenue Act, 1967 to promote peace and harmony in the Province of Sindh. It specifically modifies Section 9 of the parent Act by adding a proviso that excludes the Districts of Hyderabad and Karachi from its application. The legislation was promulgated by the Governor under Article 128 of the Constitution because the Provincial Assembly was not in session.

Additionally, it defines disqualification criteria for candidates who utilize political or sectarian platforms and outlines procedures for fresh elections if no candidate secures the required majority.

Additionally, it substitutes sections regarding special minority seats and redefines union council wards while omitting certain sub-sections.

It was promulgated by the Governor of Sindh on the instructions of the Chief Executive of Pakistan in June 2001 and came into force immediately.

metadata.summary: This Ordinance amends the Sindh Local Government Elections Ordinance, 2000 to regulate the process of filling vacant seats in local councils. It mandates by-elections for unfilled or vacant seats within specific timeframes depending on the position held. The text also outlines procedures for electing officiating Nazims when a seat remains unfilled and establishes rules for women's reserved seats.

The document outlines their composition, functions, powers, financial management, and mechanisms for public participation and dispute resolution.

metadata.summary: The Sindh Plantation, Maintenance of Trees and Public Parks Ordinance, 2002 was promulgated by the Governor of Sindh to regulate the planting and care of trees and public parks. It establishes the role of local government agencies and authorized officers in managing these resources. The law prohibits unauthorized felling or cutting of trees without permission and outlines penalties for violations, including fines and compounding procedures.

It mandates pre-marital blood screening for thalassemia traits, requires health care facilities to screen relatives of patients, and establishes a data bank for carrier registration. The Ordinance creates the Thalassemia and Hemoglobinopathy Foundation to manage funds and implement prevention measures across the province.

name: SINDH REGULARIZATION OF TEACHERS APPOINTED ON CONTRACT BASIS ORDINANCE, 2012

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Regularization of Teachers Appointed on Contract Basis Act, 2012
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to provide for regularization of the services of certain teachers appointed on contract basis through Institute of Business Administration Sukkur and Sindh University Testing Centre Jamshoro in the years 2008 and 2009.
key_definitions: appointment of a teacher on contract basis
metadata.administering_body: Reform Support Unit of Education and Literacy Department, Government of Sindh
metadata.one_line: This Ordinance regularizes the services of teachers appointed on contract basis in 2008-2009 as civil servants.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance provides for the regularization of services for teachers appointed on a contract basis through specific testing centers in Sindh during 2008 and 2009. It deems these teachers to have been validly appointed as regular civil servants, subject to performance verification by the Reform Support Unit. The law includes conditions regarding the completion of contract periods, possession of prescribed qualifications, and restrictions on transferring regularized teachers within a specified period.

name: SINDH REGULATION AND CONTROL (USE OF PLOTS AND CONSTRUCTION OF BUILDINGS) ORDINANCE, 2002

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Regulation and Control (Use of Plots and Construction of Buildings) Ordinance, 2002
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to provide for the regulation and control of the use of plots and construction of buildings in the Province of Sindh.
metadata.commencement: on such date as Government may, by notification, in the Official Gazette appoint
metadata.status_evidence: It shall remain in force for a period of one year from its commencement.
metadata.one_line: Regulates plot usage and building construction in Sindh, allowing regularization with fees for one year.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance regulates the use of plots and construction of buildings within the Province of Sindh. It applies to various types of plots including residential, industrial, and commercial sites, while excluding amenity plots. The law allows for the regularization of existing buildings constructed in violation of previous regulations, provided they meet specific conditions regarding environmental impact, parking space usage, road reservations, and proximity to Quaid-e-Azam's Mausoleum. It remains in force for a period of one year from its commencement.

metadata.short_title: The Sind Relief of Indebtedness (Amendment) Ordinance, 1983
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to amend the Sind Relief of Indebtedness Ordinance, 1960.

repeals: Section 5 of the Sind Relief of Indebtedness Ordinance, 1960
metadata.one_line: Amends the Sind Relief of Indebtedness Ordinance, 1960 by repealing Section 5.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance amends the Sind Relief of Indebtedness Ordinance, 1960. It was promulgated by the Governor of Sindh on March 12, 1983, pursuant to the Proclamation of July 5, 1977 and the Provincial Constitution Order, 1981. The document comes into force immediately upon enactment. Its primary mechanism is the repeal of Section 5 of the 1960 Ordinance.

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Rented Premises (Amendment) Ordinance, 2001
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to amend the Sindh Rented Premises Ordinance, 1979.
metadata.one_line: Amends the Sindh Rented Premises Ordinance, 1979 regarding rent arrears, appeals jurisdiction, and procedural provisions.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance amends the Sindh Rented Premises Ordinance, 1979 to address issues arising from the suspension of the Provincial Assembly. It modifies sections related to rent arrears payment methods, omits references to First Class Magistrates, and alters appeal procedures by transferring jurisdiction from the High Court to District Judges for specific tenancy disputes. The text also introduces provisions for compromise between parties and allows tenants to continue tenancy under enhanced rent conditions.

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Reproductive, Maternal, Neo-natal and Child Health Authority Ordinance, 2014
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to establish an Authority known as the Sindh Reproductive, Maternal, Neo-Natal and Child Health Authority in the Province of Sindh;
metadata.territorial_extent: whole of the Province of Sindh
establishes: Sindh Reproductive, Maternal, Neo-natal and Child Health Authority
metadata.one_line: Establishes an Authority in Sindh to manage affairs related to reproductive, maternal, neo-natal and child health programs.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance establishes the Sindh Reproductive, Maternal, Neo-natal and Child Health Authority within the Province of Sindh. The Authority is tasked with managing employees and staff for national primary health care and family planning programs. It possesses powers to regulate service terms, enter contracts for health improvements, and develop minimum service delivery standards in consultation with stakeholders.

name: SINDH SALES TAX ON SERVICES (AMENDMENT) ORDINANCE, 2011

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Sales Tax on Services (Amendment) Ordinance, 2011
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to AMEND THE Sindh Sales Tax on Services Act, 2011.

amends: The Sindh Sales Tax on Services Act, 2011
metadata.one_line: Amends the Sindh Sales Tax on Services Act, 2011 to update tax rates, definitions, and schedules for various services.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance amends the Sindh Sales Tax on Services Act, 2011 to address immediate circumstances while the Provincial Assembly is not in session. It modifies specific sections regarding tax rates, omissions of clauses, and additions to tariff headings covering insurance, leasing, financial institutions, and construction services. The amendments update tax percentages for various service categories and clarify descriptions for non-banking finance companies and port/airport operators.

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Sales Tax Ordinance, 2000
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to provide for levy of sales tax on the services rendered in the Province of Sindh.
metadata.commencement: at once and deemed to have taken effect on and from the 1st day of July, 2000
metadata.one_line: This Ordinance levies a fifteen percent sales tax on specific services rendered in the Province of Sindh.
metadata.summary: The Sindh Sales Tax Ordinance, 2000 was promulgated by the Governor to levy sales tax on services provided within the Province of Sindh. It applies to services rendered by hotels, marriage halls, clubs, caterers, courier services, beauty parlours, laundries, and specific advertisement categories. The tax is charged at a rate of fifteen percent on the value of these taxable services.

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Security of Vulnerable Establishments Ordinance, 2015
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to provide for effective security arrangements of vulnerable establishments.
metadata.territorial_extent: the whole of Province of Sindh
metadata.max_penalty: imprisonment which may extend to six months and fine which shall not be less than forty five thousand rupees
metadata.one_line: This Ordinance establishes security arrangements for vulnerable establishments in Sindh to prevent terrorism and crime.
metadata.summary: The Sindh Security of Vulnerable Establishments Ordinance, 2015 provides for effective security arrangements at vulnerable establishments to prevent acts of terrorism and other crimes. It establishes a Security Advisory Committee responsible for identifying establishments, inspecting them quarterly, and issuing advice on necessary security measures. The Ordinance outlines penalties for non-compliance, including imprisonment and fines, and empowers the police to collect evidence through security arrangements.

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Service Tribunals (Amendment) Ordinance, 1997
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to amend the Sind Service Tribunals Act, 1973.
metadata.one_line: Amends the Sindh Service Tribunals Act, 1973 to allow the Government to curtail the term of office for certain tribunal members.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance amends the Sind Service Tribunals Act, 1973 to grant the Government power to curtail the term of office of the Chairman or members appointed before its commencement. The amendment allows such curtailment not later than February 15, 1997. It was promulgated by the Governor of Sindh because the Provincial Assembly was not in session.

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Service Tribunals (Amendment) Ordinance, 1974
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to amend the Sind Service Tribunals Act, 1973.
metadata.one_line: Amends the Sind Service Tribunals Act, 1973 regarding post grades, appeals, limitations, and tribunal rules.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance amends the Sind Service Tribunals Act, 1973 to expand the definition of eligible posts for certain provisions. It modifies appeal procedures against departmental authority decisions regarding appointments and promotions. The text also inserts new sections concerning limitation periods for appeals and powers to make rules regarding tribunal composition and vacancy filling.

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Service Tribunals (Amendment) Ordinance, 1991
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to amend the Sind Service Tribunals Act, 1973.
establishes: Tribunal consisting of three Judges of the High Court for members of the subordinate judiciary
metadata.one_line: Amends the Sind Service Tribunals Act, 1973 to establish a new tribunal for subordinate judiciary matters.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance amends the Sind Service Tribunals Act, 1973 to empower the Chief Justice of the High Court to establish a specialized Tribunal. The new body consists of three High Court Judges and holds exclusive jurisdiction over terms, conditions, and disciplinary matters for subordinate judiciary members. It also transfers pending cases from the previous tribunal to this new entity and mandates that rules for the new tribunal be made in consultation with the High Court.

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Service Tribunals (Amendment) Ordinance, 2013
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to amend the Sindh Service Tribunals Act, 1973.
metadata.one_line: Amends the Sindh Service Tribunals Act, 1973 regarding Tribunal composition and member appointments.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance amends the Sindh Service Tribunals Act, 1973 to specify the composition of Tribunals. It mandates that a Tribunal consists of a Chairman and two Members appointed by the Government in consultation with the Chief Justice of the High Court of Sindh. The amendment details eligibility criteria for the Chairman (High Court Judge) and Members (District Judges, civil servants, or Advocates qualified as High Court Judges).

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Shops and Establishments (Security) Ordinance, 2009
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to provide security and protection to persons and property of the commercial, industrial establishments and shops in the Province of Sindh.
metadata.max_penalty: imprisonment up to one month or fine up to fifty thousand rupees or both
metadata.one_line: Provides security and protection to persons and property in commercial, industrial establishments and shops in Sindh.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance aims to provide security and protection to persons and property within commercial, industrial establishments, and shops in the Province of Sindh. It defines key terms such as commercial establishment, employer, shop, and industrial establishment to clarify its scope. The Government is empowered to issue orders for safety measures, requiring employers to report compliance within fourteen days. Penalties include imprisonment up to one month or a fine of fifty thousand rupees for non-compliance, with provisions restricting prosecution without government sanction.

metadata.short_title: The Sind Small Industries Corporation (Amendment) Ordinance, 1983
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to amend the Sind Small Industries Corporation Act, 1972.
metadata.parent_law: The Sind Small Industries Corporation Act, 1972
amends: The Sind Small Industries Corporation Act, 1972
metadata.one_line: Amends the Sind Small Industries Corporation Act, 1972 by defining 'small industry' regarding fixed assets.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance amends the Sind Small Industries Corporation Act, 1972 to update the definition of a small industry. It specifically substitutes clause (n) in section 2 of the parent Act. The new definition includes cottage industries engaged in handicrafts or the manufacture of consumer or producer goods with total fixed assets not exceeding Rupees 5.0 millions.

name: SINDH SOLID WASTE MANAGEMENT BOARD ORDINANCE, 2014.

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Solid Waste Management Board Ordinance, 2013
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to provide for the establishment of a Board called as the Sindh Solid Waste Management Board for the collection and disposal of solid and other waste in the Province of Sindh.
metadata.territorial_extent: the whole of the Province of Sindh
metadata.one_line: Establishes the Sindh Solid Waste Management Board to manage solid waste collection and disposal in Sindh.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance establishes the Sindh Solid Waste Management Board to oversee the collection, treatment, removal, and disposal of solid waste within the Province of Sindh. It defines the Board's composition, powers, and functions, including the authority to raise funds and manage a dedicated Solid Waste Management Fund. The legislation also outlines the roles of the Chairman and Managing Director, provisions for financial management, and mechanisms for delegating powers to officers.

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Sound System (Regulation) Ordinance, 2015
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to regulate and control use of sound systems in the Province of Sindh.
metadata.territorial_extent: the whole of Province of Sindh
metadata.max_penalty: imprisonment up to six months and fine between twenty five thousand rupees and fifty thousand rupees
metadata.one_line: This Ordinance regulates and controls the use of sound systems in Sindh to prevent public nuisance and disorder.
metadata.summary: The Sindh Sound System (Regulation) Ordinance, 2015 was promulgated by the Governor of Sindh to regulate and control the use of sound systems within the province. It prohibits the use of loudspeakers that generate unnecessary noise or disturb public peace, particularly near places of worship, hospitals, and educational institutions. The Ordinance empowers police officers to inspect sound systems, seize equipment used in offences, and imposes penalties including imprisonment and fines for violations.

name: SINDH SPEAKER'S AND DEPUTY SPEAKER'S (SALARIES, ALLOWANCES AND PRIVILEGES) (AMENDMENT) ORDINANCE, 2002

metadata.summary: This Ordinance amends the Sindh Speaker's and Deputy Speaker's (Salaries, Allowances and Privileges) Act, 1975. It was promulgated by the Governor of Sindh following the dissolution of the Provincial Assembly in October 1999. The document substitutes specific monetary figures for salaries, allowances, and house furnishing payments within sections 5, 6, and 10 of the parent Act.

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Sports Board (Amendment) Ordinance, 1993

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Tenancy (Amendment) Ordinance, 2002
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to amend the Sindh Tenancy Act, 1950.
metadata.one_line: Amends the Sindh Tenancy Act, 1950 by redefining tenants and updating administrative titles.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance amends the Sindh Tenancy Act, 1950 to redefine the class of tenant as permanent tenants only. It updates references from 'Deputy District Officer' to 'District Officer' or 'Executive District Officer' throughout the Act. The document also substitutes specific clauses regarding landlord responsibilities and omits several sections and sub-sections.

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Tenancy (Second Amendment) Ordinance, 2002
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to further amend Sindh Tenancy Act, 1950.
metadata.one_line: Amends the Sindh Tenancy Act, 1950 to restrict landlords from recovering debts or imposing labor on tenants.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance amends the Sindh Tenancy Act, 1950 to protect tenants from debt recovery and forced labor by landlords. It prohibits landlords from seizing agricultural produce for personal debts, requiring free labor, or transferring tenants against their will. The provisions apply throughout the Province of Sindh and come into force immediately upon promulgation.

name: SINDH TRANSFUSION OF SAFE BLOOD (AMENDMENT) ORDINANCE, 2005

metadata.summary: This Ordinance amends the Sindh Transfusion of Safe Blood Act, 1996 to update regulatory provisions. It substitutes the Chairman of the authority with the Secretary to Government of Sindh, Health Department. Additionally, it inserts new powers to seal premises used illegally for blood transfusion and increases a specific penalty period from two years to three years.

name: SINDH TRANSPLANTATION OF HUMAN ORGANS AND TISSUES ORDINANCE, 2012

metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to provide for removal, storage and transplantation of human organs and tissues for therapeutic purposes.
metadata.one_line: This Ordinance regulates the removal, storage, and transplantation of human organs and tissues for therapeutic purposes in Sindh.
metadata.summary: The Sindh Transplantation of Human Organs and Tissues Ordinance, 2012 establishes a legal framework for the donation and transplantation of human organs and tissues within the province. It defines specific terms such as 'brain dead' and 'donor', and sets out procedures for living and deceased donors, including the role of Evaluation Committees. The Ordinance prohibits commercial dealings in organs, outlines punishments for unauthorized removal or trafficking, and creates bodies like the Monitoring Authority to oversee these processes.

It defines key terms such as 'candidate', 'examiner', and 'answer-book' to clarify the scope of regulations. The document outlines specific offences ranging from impersonation to falsification of records, prescribing penalties including imprisonment up to three years and fines up to one hundred thousand rupees for general offenders, or up to one year and fifty thousand rupees for candidates.

The document prescribes severe punishments, including imprisonment up to three years and fines up to one hundred thousand rupees, for various offenses like impersonation, leaking question papers, and falsifying results.

name: SINDH URBAN IMMOVABLE PROPERTY TAX (Amendment) ORDINANCE, 1999

name: SINDH URBAN STATE LAND (CANCELLATION) OF ALLOTMENTS, CONVERSIONS AND EXCHANGES) ORDINANCE, 2000

The Government may appoint a committee to determine losses and call upon concerned persons to pay the assessed amount before regularization can occur.

metadata.short_title: The Sind Vagrancy (Amendment) Ordinance, 1983

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Water Management Ordinance, 2002

It creates new bodies including the Sindh Irrigation and Drainage Authority (SIDA), Area Water Boards (AWBs), and Flood Offices (FOs) to replace previous structures. The law outlines their composition, functions, financial management, and powers regarding water allocation and enforcement.

name: SINDH WILD LIFE PROTECTION SECOND (AMENDMENT) ORDINANCE 2001

metadata.one_line: Amends the 1972 Ordinance to include fish in protected species and ban commercial fishing in sanctuaries.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance amends the Sind Wildlife Protection Ordinance, 1972, to substitute 'birds' with 'birds, fish' in section 2. It adds a new sub-section to section 14 prohibiting the leasing or use of wildlife sanctuary waters for commercial fishing or lotus collection. Additionally, it annuls any leases or permissions granted prior to its commencement for these prohibited activities.

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Wildlife Protection (Amendment) Ordinance, 1993
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to amend the Sind Wildlife Protection Ordinance, 1972.
metadata.one_line: Amends the 1972 Ordinance to include fish in protected species and ban commercial fishing in sanctuaries.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance amends the Sind Wildlife Protection Ordinance, 1972, to expand protection to include fish alongside birds. It prohibits leasing or using fishing waters within wildlife sanctuaries for commercial fishing or collecting lotus roots. Additionally, it annuls any leases or permissions granted prior to its commencement that violated these new restrictions.

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Wildlife Protection (Amendment) Ordinance, 1998
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to amend the Sind Wildlife Protection Ordinance, 1972.
metadata.max_penalty: imprisonment of nine months or a fine of three hundred thousand rupees
metadata.one_line: Amends the Sind Wildlife Protection Ordinance, 1972 by adding penalties for hunting specific animals.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance amends the Sind Wildlife Protection Ordinance, 1972 to impose stricter penalties for hunting certain species. It specifically targets the hunting of rabbit, deer, hoodder, para, Sindh ibex, and wild-sheep in contravention of the Ordinance. The new provisions prescribe fines ranging from one hundred thousand to three hundred thousand rupees or imprisonment terms up to nine months.

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Wildlife Protection (Amendment) Ordinance, 2001
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to amend the Sindh Wildlife Protection Ordinance, 1972.
metadata.one_line: Amends the 1972 Ordinance to allow underground pipelines in sanctuaries and parks while increasing penalties.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance amends the Sindh Wildlife Protection Ordinance, 1972, to permit the laying of underground pipelines using non-blasting techniques that do not disturb wildlife. It authorizes such activities on specific terms regarding conservation and preservation within sanctuaries and national parks. Additionally, it substitutes higher monetary figures in sections 14, 15, and 33 of the parent Ordinance.

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Wildlife Protection (Amendment) Ordinance, 2011
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to amend the Sindh Wildlife Protection Ordinance, 1972.
metadata.one_line: Amends the 1972 Ordinance to allow eco-friendly activities in wildlife sanctuaries for tourism.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance amends the Sindh Wildlife Protection Ordinance, 1972, to permit specific activities within wildlife sanctuaries. It allows the Government to authorize eco-friendly resort and eco-tourism activities that do not permanently disturb wildlife or the environment. The amendment adds a new subsection to Section 14 of the parent Ordinance, subjecting these activities to prescribed terms and conditions.

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Zakat and Ushr Ordinance, 2010
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to make provisions relating to the assessment, collection and disbursement of Zakat and Ushr.
metadata.one_line: This Ordinance establishes the legal framework for assessing, collecting, and disbursing Zakat and Ushr in Sindh.
metadata.summary: The Sindh Zakat and Ushr Ordinance, 2010 provides provisions for the assessment, collection, and disbursement of Zakat and Ushr within the Province of Sindh. It establishes various committees including the Sindh Zakat Council, District Committees, and Local Committees to manage these funds. The law outlines specific rates for different assets like livestock, minerals, and financial wealth according to Shariah principles, while also defining exemptions and procedures for voluntary declarations.

name: SIR SYED UNIVERSITY OF ENGINEERING AND TECHNOLOGY ORDINANCE, 1993

metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to provide for the establishment of Sir Syed university of Engineering and Technology at Karachi.
establishes: Sir Syed University of Engineering and Technology
metadata.one_line: Establishes the Sir Syed University of Engineering and Technology at Karachi as an autonomous body.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance establishes the Sir Syed University of Engineering and Technology in Karachi as a body corporate with perpetual succession. It defines the university's powers to provide engineering instruction, admit students regardless of background, and confer degrees. The document creates various authorities including the Board of Governors, Academic Council, and committees for finance and affiliation.

metadata.short_title: The Societies Registration (Second Sindh Amendment) Ordinance, 2005
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance further to amend the Societies Registration Act, 1860, in its application to the province of Sindh.
metadata.one_line: Amends the Societies Registration Act, 1860 in Sindh to regulate Deeni Madaris registration and reporting.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance amends the Societies Registration Act, 1860 specifically for the province of Sindh. It mandates that all Deeni Madaris must register themselves, with existing institutions having until December 31, 2005, and new ones within one year of establishment. The law requires annual reports on educational activities and audits of accounts to be submitted to the Registrar. Additionally, it prohibits teaching or publishing literature that promotes militancy, sectarianism, or religious hatred, while allowing comparative religious study.

metadata.short_title: The Societies Registration (Sindh Amendment) Ordinance, 2005
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance further to amend the Societies Registration Act, 1860, in its application to the province of Sindh.
metadata.one_line: Amends the Societies Registration Act, 1860 to regulate Deeni Madaris in Sindh regarding registration, reporting, and prohibitions on militancy.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance amends the Societies Registration Act, 1860 specifically for its application to the province of Sindh. It mandates that all Deeni Madaris must be registered under the Act and submit annual reports of their activities and performance to the Registrar. Additionally, these institutions are required to maintain audited accounts and are prohibited from teaching or publishing literature that promotes militancy, sectarianism, or religious hatred.

metadata.short_title: The Societies Registration (Sind Amendment) Ordinance, 1984
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to amend the Societies Registration Act, 1860, in its application to the Province of Sind.
metadata.one_line: Amends the Societies Registration Act, 1860 in Sindh to require a hearing before superseding a governing body.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance amends the application of the Societies Registration Act, 1860 to the Province of Sind. It specifically modifies Section 16-A to ensure that no governing body is superseded without first being given an opportunity to be heard. The amendment was promulgated by the Governor of Sind on November 11, 1984, following directions from the Federal Shariat Court.

metadata.short_title: The Sind Sports Board (Amendment) Ordinance, 1984
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to amend the Sind Sports Board Ordinance, 1980.
metadata.one_line: Amends the Sind Sports Board Ordinance, 1980 by adding new members to its composition.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance amends the Sind Sports Board Ordinance, 1980 to update the composition of the Board. It inserts new clauses specifying additional official and non-official members, including representatives from various government departments and municipal corporations. Furthermore, it grants the Governor the power to amend the Board's composition via notification by appointing any person as a member.

metadata.short_title: The Sind Sports Board (Second Amendment) Ordinance, 1982
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to amend the Sind Sports Board Ordinance, 1980.
metadata.one_line: Amends the Sind Sports Board Ordinance, 1980 by substituting clauses regarding the Vice-Chairman and Secretary roles.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance amends the Sind Sports Board Ordinance, 1980 to update the composition of the board. Specifically, it substitutes clause (ii) in section 4 to designate the Minister for Vice-Chairman of Education and Sports and adds a sub-clause for the Secretary to Government of Sind as a Member of the Education Department. The Ordinance came into force immediately upon promulgation by the Governor of Sind on August 17, 1982.

metadata.short_title: The Sind Sports Board (Second Amendment) Ordinance, 1984
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to amend the Sind Sports Board Ordinance, 1980.
metadata.one_line: Amends the Sind Sports Board Ordinance, 1980 to require a hearing before removing a member.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance amends the Sind Sports Board Ordinance, 1980 in response to directions from the Federal Shariat Court. It modifies Section 5 of the parent Ordinance by adding a proviso that mandates an opportunity for a member to show cause and be heard before any order of removal is passed. The amendment ensures adherence to principles of natural justice within the board's operations.

metadata.short_title: The Sind Sports Board Ordinance, 1980
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to provide for the establishment of a Sports Board in Sind.
metadata.one_line: Establishes the Sind Sports Board to promote sports, games, and physical education in Sindh.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance establishes the Sind Sports Board as a body corporate with perpetual succession to manage sports development in Sindh. The Board consists of official members, including the Governor's nominee and various Secretaries, along with non-official members representing associations and educational institutions. It empowers the Board to formulate policies, coordinate activities, manage funds, and make regulations necessary for its functions.

metadata.short_title: The Stamp (Fifth Sindh Amendment) Ordinance, 2002

metadata.summary: This Ordinance was promulgated by the Governor of Sindh to further amend the application of the Stamp Act, 1899 within the Province. The text substitutes specific clauses in Article 19 of the Schedule to adjust ad valorem duty thresholds.

It substitutes Article 19 of the Schedule to define 'financing document' to include various instruments related to banking finance not based on interest. The definition covers sale and re-purchase agreements, hypothecation, pledges, mortgages, and floating charges executed by customers in favor of banking companies.

The Ordinance was promulgated by the Governor of Sind on October 18, 1984, and came into force immediately.

metadata.short_title: The Stamp (Sindh Amendment) Ordinance, 1996

Additionally, it introduces procedures for reporting and dealing with unstamped instruments and imposes penalties for obstructing revenue officials.

metadata.short_title: The Stamp (Sindh Amendment) Ordinance, 2000

metadata.summary: This Ordinance amends the Stamp Act, 1899 specifically for its application to the Province of Sindh. metadata.short_title: The Stamp (Sindh Amendment) Ordinance, 2002

metadata.summary: This Ordinance amends the application of the Sindh Stamp Act, 1899, specifically within the Province of Sindh. It substitutes specific article references and renumbers sections previously inserted by other Ordinances. The text details new stamp duty rates for receipts, affidavits, agreements, settlements, and transfers, along with specific exemptions for government instruments, military personnel, and certain financial documents.

metadata.summary: This Ordinance was promulgated by the Governor of Sindh on September 3, 2002, following the dissolution of the Provincial Assembly. Its purpose is to further amend the Stamp Act, 1899, specifically regarding its application within the Province of Sindh. The primary mechanism involves substituting the words 'five percent' with 'three percent' in Article 16, column 2 of the Schedule to the said Act.

metadata.short_title: The Stamp (Sindh Amendment) Ordinance, 1994

metadata.summary: This Ordinance amends the application of the Stamp Act, 1899 to the Province of Sindh. It was promulgated by the Governor because the Provincial Assembly was not in session and immediate action was deemed necessary. The primary mechanism is the deletion of clause (a) under the heading 'Exemptions' in Article 5 of Schedule I of the Stamp Act, 1899.

metadata.short_title: The Sind Tenancy (Amendment) Ordinance, 1984

It modifies sections concerning the devolution of tenancy rights for deceased Muslim tenants, management of tenancies by physically or mentally incapacitated permanent tenants, and legal representation in disputes. Additionally, it omits specific subsections and adds provisos regarding hearing opportunities for appellants.

metadata.short_title: The Sind Text Book Board (Amendment) Ordinance, 1984

It modifies Section 5 by adding a proviso that ensures the Chairman or Member is given an opportunity of being heard before any order of removal is passed. The Ordinance was promulgated by the Governor of Sindh on November 18, 1984, and came into force immediately.

metadata.short_title: The Sind Town Planning (Amendment) Ordinance, 1984

metadata.summary: This Ordinance amends the Sind Town Planning Act, 1915 in response to directives from the Federal Shariat Court. It requires every town planning scheme to earmark plots for mosques. Additionally, it modifies compensation rules by adding a fifteen percent sum on market value and an annual fifteen percent interest on compensation payments until paid.

It mandates the distribution of these forms to registered medical practitioners, private clinics, hospitals, community leaders, and in-charges of covered premises within the province. The document outlines the duties of various stakeholders, including medical practitioners, laboratories, and community representatives, regarding the notification process and record-keeping. It also defines key terms related to Tuberculosis cases and establishes penalties for non-compliance while ensuring confidentiality.

metadata.short_title: The University of Karachi (Amendment) Ordinance, 1984

It modifies sections 36, 40, and 52 of the said Act to mandate that appellants or applicants must be given an opportunity of being heard before any order in appeal or review is passed or made. Additionally, it requires actions under section 52 to be done in good faith.

The document establishes various governing bodies including the Senate, Syndicate, and Academic Council, and outlines procedures for statutes, regulations, and affiliation with educational institutions.

metadata.short_title: The University of Sind (Amendment) Ordinance, 1984

It mandates that no order in appeal or review shall be passed or made unless the appellant or applicant has been given an opportunity of being heard. Additionally, it requires certain actions to be done in good faith.

It grants the university autonomy, defines its corporate status, and outlines the composition of its governing bodies including the Senate, Syndicate, and Academic Council. The document also repeals the West Pakistan (University of Sind) Ordinance, 1961, while saving existing rights, liabilities, and appointments.

metadata.short_title: The Sind Waqf Properties (Amendment) Ordinance, 1984
