metadata.one_line: Repeals the West Pakistan Tendoo Leaves Ordinance, 1966 as it applies to Sindh.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance was promulgated by the Governor of Sind on November 3, 1973, to repeal a specific provincial application of a national ordinance. It targets the West Pakistan Tendoo Leaves (Prohibition on Possession and Use) Ordinance, 1966, specifically within the Province of Sind. The legislation came into force immediately upon promulgation due to the absence of the Provincial Assembly.

name: WEST PAKISTAN TOBACCO VEND ACT (SIND AMENDMENT) ORDINANCE, 1970

metadata.short_title: The West Pakistan Tobacco Vend Act (Sind Amendment) Ordinance, 1970
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to amend the West Pakistan Tobacco Vend Act, 1958, in its application to the Province of Sind.
metadata.parent_law: The West Pakistan Tobacco Vend Act, 1958
amends: The West Pakistan Tobacco Vend Act, 1958
metadata.one_line: Amends the West Pakistan Tobacco Vend Act, 1958 to replace Magistrates with Excise Officers in Sindh.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance amends the West Pakistan Tobacco Vend Act, 1958 specifically regarding its application to the Province of Sind. It substitutes the term 'any Magistrate' with 'an Excise and Taxation Officer' in section 7 of the parent Act. The amendment was promulgated by the Governor of Sind under Martial Law provisions on October 29, 1970.

name: WEST PAKISTAN URBAN IMMOVABLE PROPERTY TAX ACT (SIND AMENDMENT) ORDINANCE, 1971

metadata.short_title: The West Pakistan Urban Immovable Property Tax Act (Sind Amendment) Ordinance, 1971
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to amend the West Pakistan Urban Immovable Property Tax Act, 1958, in its application to the Province of Sind.
metadata.territorial_extent: the whole of the Province of Sind
metadata.parent_law: The West Pakistan Urban Immovable Property Tax Act, 1958
amends: The West Pakistan Urban Immovable Property Tax Act, 1958
key_definitions: members of the family of the owner
metadata.one_line: Amends the West Pakistan Urban Immovable Property Tax Act, 1958 to apply it to the Province of Sind.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance amends the West Pakistan Urban Immovable Property Tax Act, 1958 specifically for its application to the Province of Sind. It substitutes references to 'West Pakistan' with 'Sind' throughout the Act and defines family members as a wife or husband and dependent children. The Ordinance also omits specific sections and clauses from the original Act to align it with provincial governance structures.

metadata.short_title: The Zulfikarabad Development Authority (Amendment) Ordinance, 2011
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to amend the Zulfikarabad Development Authority Act, 2010.
metadata.one_line: Amends the Zulfikarabad Development Authority Act, 2010 to alter the composition and functions of its Governing Body.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance amends the Zulfikarabad Development Authority Act, 2010 to modify the structure of the Authority's Governing Body. It specifies new members including representatives from the Board of Revenue, Finance, and Local Government departments. Additionally, it grants the Chief Minister discretion to appoint a Vice Chairman and a Secretary for the Governing Body.

metadata.short_title: The Zulfikarabad Development Authority Ordinance, 2010
metadata.long_title: An Ordinance to provide for establishment of Zulfikarabd City in District Thatta and to establish an Authority for such purpose.
metadata.territorial_extent: District Thatta (as specified by Government notification)
metadata.one_line: Establishes the Zulfikarabad Development Authority to plan and develop Zulfikarabad City in District Thatta.
metadata.summary: This Ordinance establishes the Zulfikarabad Development Authority (ZDA) as a body corporate to plan, prepare schemes, and execute development projects for Zulfikarabad City in District Thatta. The Authority is governed by a Governing Body comprising senior government officials and possesses powers to acquire land, manage funds, and make regulations necessary for urban development. It outlines the functions of the Managing Director, provisions for compensation, land acquisition procedures, and mechanisms for the dissolution of the Authority.

metadata.short_title: Sindh Councils (Conduct of Business) Rules, 2001
repeals: The Sindh Councils (Conduct of Business) Rule 1980
metadata.administering_body: Government of Sindh, Local Government Department
metadata.one_line: Rules governing the conduct of business, meetings, and quorum for local councils in Sindh.
metadata.summary: These Rules establish the procedures for conducting business at meetings of local councils in Sindh. They specify requirements for notice periods, agenda preparation, seating arrangements, and quorum levels to ensure valid decision-making. The document also outlines the powers of the Convener, committee structures, and mechanisms for handling adjournments or suspensions of meetings.

metadata.short_title: The Sindh City Survey Rules, 1988
metadata.one_line: Rules made by the Government of Sindh to regulate city survey operations, enquiries, and issuance of Sanads under the Sindh City Survey Act, 1987.
metadata.summary: These rules provide the framework for conducting city surveys in Sindh, including traversing land, holding enquiries into ownership and encroachments, and mapping building sites. They establish the powers of the Director and Survey Officer, define key terms like 'traverse station', and prescribe procedures for issuing notices, serving summons, and granting Sanads for building sites. The rules also detail how records are maintained, inspected, and corrected.

name: KARACHI (POSSESSION OF RECTIFIED SPIRIT) AND THE MANUFACTURE OF ORIGINAL HOMOEOPATHIC TINCTURES) RULES,1965

metadata.short_title: The Karachi (Possession of Rectified Spirit and the Manufacture of Original Homoeopathic Tinctures) Rules, 1965
metadata.territorial_extent: the District of Karachi excluding 37 villages specified in the Schedule to the Karachi (Federal Territory) Order, 1960
metadata.one_line: Rules governing the possession of rectified spirit and manufacture of homoeopathic tinctures in Karachi.
metadata.summary: These rules regulate the possession of rectified spirit and the manufacture of original homoeopathic tinctures by chemists or practitioners in the District of Karachi. They establish a permit system administered by the Collector, requiring security bonds and specific account forms for compliance. The rules define application procedures, permit durations, storage conditions, and restrictions on supplying spirit to customers.

metadata.short_title: The Banking Companies (Court) Rules, 1972
metadata.administering_body: High Court of Sind and Baluchistan
metadata.one_line: Rules framed by the High Court under the Banking Companies Ordinance, 1962 to govern court practice and procedure for banking company proceedings.
metadata.summary: These rules were framed by the High Court of Sind and Baluchistan in exercise of powers conferred by section 79 of the Banking Companies Ordinance, 1962. They prescribe the short title, interpretation of terms, and the practice and procedure to be followed in court proceedings under the Ordinance. The rules mandate the maintenance of specific registers for petitions, applications, appearances, liquidations, and documents, and they detail requirements for serving notices on banking companies and other parties.

metadata.short_title: The Sind Civil Servants (Advance Increments) Rules, 1976
metadata.administering_body: Government of Sind, Services and General Administration Department (Regulation Wing)
metadata.one_line: These rules govern the grant of advance increments to civil servants in Sindh, defining eligibility, assessment criteria, and committee structures.
metadata.summary: The Sind Civil Servants (Advance Increments) Rules, 1976 establish the framework for granting advance increments to eligible civil servants in the province of Sindh. The rules specify conditions such as minimum years of service, restrictions on promotion timing, and limits on the number of increments per financial year. An Advisory Committee assesses the suitability of candidates based on integrity, behavior, output quality, and other factors before recommending grants to the Sanctioning Authority.

metadata.short_title: The Sind Civil Servants Language Examination Rules, 1981
repeals: The Sind Government Servant Language Examination Rules, 1963
metadata.administering_body: Government of Sind Services & General Administrative Department (Regulation Wing)
metadata.one_line: These rules mandate Urdu or Sindhi language examinations for civil servants in Sindh and provide rewards and increment penalties.
metadata.summary: The Sind Civil Servants Language Examination Rules, 1981 require civil servants in Grade 5 and above to pass an examination in Urdu or Sindhi if it is not their mother tongue. The rules specify the standard of examination based on grade, the frequency of conduct by the Sind Public Service Commission, and exemptions for certain officers or those over forty years old. Additionally, the rules outline financial rewards for passing the exam and consequences for failure, including withholding annual increments.

name: Coastal Development Authority (Accounts Wo0rks, Property and Record) Rules, 1999.

metadata.short_title: The Coastal Development Authority (Accounts, Works, Property and Record) Rules, 1999
metadata.parent_law: The Sindh Coastal Development Authority Act, 1994
metadata.administering_body: Government of Sindh Planning and Development Department
metadata.one_line: Rules governing accounts, works, property, and record maintenance for the Coastal Development Authority in Sindh.
metadata.summary: These rules establish the framework for maintaining accounts, managing cash books, issuing receipts, and handling property records for the Coastal Development Authority. They define key financial terms like 'appropriation' and 're-appropriation' to ensure fiscal regularity. The document also outlines procedures for classifying files into permanent or temporary categories (Class A, B, and C) based on their importance and retention periods.

metadata.short_title: The Sind Darul Atfal (Supervision & Control) Rules, 1988
metadata.parent_law: The Sind Darul Atfal (Supervision & Control) Act, 1976
metadata.administering_body: Sind Orphanages Supervision and Control Board
metadata.one_line: Rules made by the Sind Government to regulate the supervision, control, licensing, and management of Darul Atfal in Sindh.
metadata.summary: These rules were made under the powers of the Sind Darul Atfal (Supervision & Control) Act, 1976, to establish a framework for the supervision and control of orphanages in Sindh. They outline procedures for granting and renewing licenses, maintaining financial accounts, conducting medical examinations, and submitting annual reports to the Licensing Authority. The rules also specify conditions for the admission and discharge of children from Darul Atfal.

metadata.short_title: The Sind Drainage Rates Rules, 1983
metadata.one_line: These rules establish the assessment and payment procedures for drainage rates in Sindh.
metadata.summary: The Sind Drainage Rates Rules, 1983 provide the framework for levying and collecting drainage rates on cropped land in Sindh. They define key terms such as Assessing Authority and Assessment Unit, and mandate that bills be issued bi-annually at the end of the Kharif and Rabi seasons. The rules also outline procedures for remitting payments in cases of natural calamities or widespread crop failure.

name: EXECUTION OF THE PUNISHMENT OF WHIPPING RULES, 1986.

metadata.short_title: The Sind Execution of the Punishment of Whipping Rules, 1986
metadata.parent_law: Execution of the Punishment of Whipping Ordinance, 1979
metadata.one_line: Rules made by the Government of Sind under the Execution of the Punishment of Whipping Ordinance, 1979 regarding whipping execution.
metadata.summary: These rules were framed by the Government of Sind in exercise of powers conferred by section 7 of the Execution of the Punishment of Whipping Ordinance, 1979. They establish procedures for nominating warders or jail staff to execute punishment, ensuring female warders handle females and that whipping on women is not witnessed by males. The rules also provide for hearing objections regarding partiality and arranging the required number of whips.

metadata.short_title: Sindh Gothabad (Housing Scheme) Rules, 2008
metadata.administering_body: Government of Sindh, Land Utilization Department
metadata.one_line: These rules establish the framework for housing schemes, land allotment, and eligibility criteria under the Sind Gothabad (Housing Scheme) Act, 1987.
metadata.summary: The document outlines the procedures for implementing the housing scheme in Sindh, including the composition of allotment committees and the survey process. It defines eligibility for plot allotment to deserving family members holding identity cards and sets terms such as construction deadlines and restrictions on land transfer. The rules also detail the documentation required, fees involved, and the appeal process for disputes regarding orders made under the Act.

name: HIGH COURT OF SIND BENCHES RULES, 1987

metadata.short_title: The High Court of Sind Benches Rules, 1987
metadata.territorial_extent: the local limits of the jurisdiction of the High Court
metadata.parent_law: Constitution of the Islamic Republic of Pakistan
establishes: Registry of the High Court at each Bench
metadata.one_line: Rules establishing High Court Benches in Sindh, defining their jurisdiction, registry, and the powers of the Chief Justice.
metadata.summary: These rules establish the framework for High Court Benches within the local limits of the High Court's jurisdiction in Sindh. They define key terms such as Bench, Chief Justice, Judge, and High Court, and outline the Chief Justice's authority to assign areas, transfer cases, and manage registries at each Bench. The rules also apply mutatis mutandis to Circuit Courts held under Article 198 of the Constitution.

name: KATCHI ABADIS AUTHORITY, (REGULARISATION, IMPROVEMENT, AND DEVELOPMENT) REGULATIONS, 1993

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Katchi Abadis Authority, (Regularisation, Improvement, and Development) Regulations, 1993
metadata.one_line: Regulates the regularisation, improvement, and development of Katchi Abadis in Sindh under the 1987 Act.
metadata.summary: These regulations provide the framework for the Sindh Katchi Abadis Authority to prepare master lists, declare Katchi Abadis, and formulate regularization and development schemes. They outline procedures for public participation, lease rate structures for different divisions, and the delegation of powers for technical sanctions and survey planning. The document also details requirements for removing encroachments and managing disputes related to contracts and surveys.

name: KMC EMPLOYEES WELFARE BOARD FUND RULES, 1971.

metadata.short_title: The K.M.C. Employees Welfare Fund Rules, 1971
metadata.one_line: Establishes a welfare fund and board for KMC employees to provide insurance and financial assistance.
metadata.summary: These rules establish the KMC Employees Welfare Fund and constitute the KMC Employees Welfare Board. The fund is financed by employee contributions, KMC contributions, and interest, primarily used for group insurance claims and financial relief for invalided or retired employees. The rules define eligible employees, family members, and the powers of the Board and its Secretary regarding accounts, investments, and claim settlements.

metadata.short_title: The Sind Law Colleges (Board of Governors) Rules, 1983
metadata.parent_law: The Sind Government Educational and Training Institutions Ordinance, 1960
establishes: Board of Governors for Law Colleges
metadata.one_line: Rules governing the constitution, meetings, funds, accounts, and administration of Boards for Law Colleges in Sind.
metadata.summary: These rules establish the framework for the Board of Governors for Law Colleges in Sind. They define key terms such as 'Board', 'Chairman', and 'College', and prescribe procedures for holding meetings, maintaining quorums, and casting votes. The document outlines financial management requirements, including fund deposits, investments, budget preparation, and audit processes by Chartered Accountants. Additionally, it sets conditions for civil servants serving under the Board and mandates specific annual returns regarding activities, staff remuneration, student admissions, and examination results to be submitted to the Government.

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Mining Concession Rules, 2002
metadata.parent_law: Regulation of Mines, and Oil-Fields and Mineral Development (Federal Control) Act, 1948
metadata.administering_body: Government of Sindh, Mines & Mineral Development Department
metadata.one_line: Rules made by the Government of Sindh to regulate mining concessions, licenses, and royalties within the province.
metadata.summary: These rules are made by the Government of Sindh under the powers of the Regulation of Mines Act, 1948. They establish a framework for granting mineral titles, including reconnaissance licenses, exploration permits, mining permits, and mining leases. The document defines key terms such as 'Associated Minerals' and 'Authorized Officer', sets out conditions for applications, outlines royalty payment structures, and specifies offences related to pollution and data confidentiality.

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Motor Vehicles Dealers Licence Rules, 1989
metadata.one_line: Rules made by the Government of Sindh to regulate the licensing of motor vehicles dealers under the Sindh Finance Act, 1989.
metadata.summary: These rules establish the framework for granting licences to persons intending to engage in the business of motor vehicles dealers in Sindh. They define the qualifications required for applicants, conditions attached to the licence, and procedures for renewal, suspension, or cancellation. The rules also outline the process for appeals against decisions made by the licensing authority and mandate record-keeping and inspections.

name: NARA CANAL AREA WATER BOARD ELECTION (MEMBER)REGULATIONS, 2004

metadata.short_title: The Nara Canal Area Water Board Election (Member) Regulations, 2004
metadata.territorial_extent: the whole of the area falling under the Nara Canal Area Water Board
metadata.commencement: on such date, as the Nara Canal Area Water Board may, by notification, appoint
metadata.one_line: Regulates the election of the chairman of the Nara Canal Area Water Board under the Sindh Water Management Ordinance, 2002.
metadata.summary: These regulations govern the elections for the chairman of the Nara Canal Area Water Board. They define qualifications and disqualifications for candidates, establish voting procedures, and outline the powers of the Election Committee. The document also provides mechanisms for appeals to the Governor and specifies the administrative framework for conducting transparent and fair elections.

metadata.short_title: The Sind Provincial Assembly (Members) Welfare Fund Rules, 1976
metadata.parent_law: The Sind Provincial Assembly (Members) Welfare Fund Act, 1975
metadata.one_line: Rules made by the Members Welfare Committee to manage the Sind Provincial Assembly (Members) Welfare Fund.
metadata.summary: These rules were made under section 9 of the Sind Provincial Assembly (Members) Welfare Fund Act, 1975. They establish the Members Welfare's Committee and define its powers regarding the custody, investment, and withdrawal of funds. The rules also prescribe procedures for committee meetings, quorum requirements, auditing processes, and the disbursement of grants to members.

name: PROVINCIAL COUNCIL REHABILITATION OF DISABLED PERSONS RULES, 1983.

metadata.short_title: Sind Provincial Council for Rehabilitation of Disabled Persons Rules, 1983
establishes: Provincial Council for Rehabilitation of Disabled Persons, Sind
metadata.administering_body: Social Welfare, Excise and Taxation Department, Government of Sind
metadata.one_line: Rules made by the Government of Sindh to regulate the Provincial Council for Rehabilitation of Disabled Persons.
metadata.summary: These rules establish the procedural framework for the Provincial Council for Rehabilitation of Disabled Persons in Sindh. They define key terms, outline meeting procedures including quorum and notice periods, and set guidelines for motions, amendments, and minutes. The document also covers membership resignation, financial powers regarding fund reappropriation, and provides forms for assessing disabled persons.

name: PROVINCIAL LOCAL GOVERNMENT COMMISSION (CONDUCT OF BUSINESS) RULES, 2017

metadata.short_title: The Provincial Local Government Commission (Conduct of Business) Rules, 2017
metadata.one_line: Rules governing the conduct of business, meetings, inspections, and inquiries for the Provincial Local Government Commission in Sindh.
metadata.summary: These rules establish the framework for conducting business within the Provincial Local Government Commission. They define key terms such as 'Commission', 'Chairperson', and 'Audit Officer', and mandate that ordinary meetings be held at least once a month. The document grants the Commission powers of a civil court for summoning witnesses and inspecting documents, outlines procedures for inquiries into local councils, and provides immunity to members acting in good faith.

name: REGIONAL PLAN ORGANIZATION EMPLOYEES ((GENERAL SONDITIONS OF sERVICE) RULES, 1987.docx 13-7-2015

metadata.short_title: The Sind Regional Plan Organization Employees (General Conditions of Service) Rules, 1987
metadata.parent_law: The Sind Regional Plan Organization Act, 1975
metadata.administering_body: Planning and Development Department, Government of Sindh
metadata.one_line: Rules governing general conditions of service, pay, allowances, and employment terms for Sind Regional Plan Organization employees.
metadata.summary: These rules establish the general conditions of service for employees of the Sind Regional Plan Organization. They cover pay scales, allowances, honoraria, transfers, termination, appeals, and contractual engagements. The rules apply to substantive employees but exclude casual staff with less than three years of service and those on contract or deputation.

name: REGIONAL PLAN ORGANIZATION EMPLOYEES (EFFICIENCY AND DISCIPLINE) RULES, 1988.docx

metadata.short_title: The Sind Regional Plan Organization Employees (Efficiency and Discipline) Rules, 1988
metadata.parent_law: The Sind Regional Plan Organization Act, 1976
metadata.administering_body: Planning and Development Department, Government of Sindh
metadata.one_line: Rules governing efficiency, discipline, penalties, and inquiry procedures for employees of the Sind Regional Plan Organization.
metadata.summary: These rules establish the framework for maintaining efficiency and discipline among employees of the Sind Regional Plan Organization. They define grounds for penalties such as inefficiency, misconduct, corruption, and subversive activities. The document outlines minor and major penalties, including censure, withholding promotion, reduction to a lower post, compulsory retirement, removal from service, and dismissal. It also details the inquiry procedure, appeal mechanisms, and the powers of authorized officers and appellate authorities.

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Registration of Godowns Rules, 1996
metadata.parent_law: The Sindh Registration of Godowns Act, 1996
metadata.one_line: Rules made by the Government of Sindh to regulate the registration and renewal of godowns.
metadata.summary: These rules were made under section 9 of the Sindh Registration of Godowns Act, 1996, by the Government of Sindh. They establish procedures for applying for godown registration using specific forms and paying fees not exceeding one thousand rupees. The rules also mandate the maintenance of stock registers and fortnightly returns for essential articles stored in registered godowns.

name: RULES OF PROCEDURE OF THE PROVINCIAL ASSEMBLY OF SINDH

metadata.short_title: Rules of Procedure of the Provincial Assembly of Sindh
repeals: Rules of Procedure of the Provincial Assembly of Sindh, 1973
metadata.one_line: These rules govern the procedure, business, and privileges of the Provincial Assembly of Sindh.
metadata.summary: These Rules of Procedure were made by the Governor of Sindh in pursuance of Article 67 of the Constitution to regulate the functioning of the Provincial Assembly. They cover the summoning and prorogation of the Assembly, the election and powers of the Speaker, the conduct of business including questions and motions, and the procedures for committees. The rules also address privileges, voting divisions, and transitional provisions following the 18th Amendment.

name: SIND INFORMATION AND PUBLIC RELATIONS DEPARTMENT DELEGATION OF POWERS RULES, 1970.

metadata.short_title: The Sind Information and Public Relations Department Delegation of Powers Rules, 1970
amends: Information Department Delegation of Powers Rules, 1962
metadata.administering_body: Government of Sind, Services, General Administration and Information Department
metadata.one_line: Rules made by the Governor of Sind to delegate powers for appointment, punishment, and transfer within the Information Department.
metadata.summary: These rules were made by the Governor of Sind in pursuance of the Martial Law Proclamation of 1969 and the Province of West Pakistan (Dissolution) Order, 1970. They supersede the Information Department Delegation of Powers Rules, 1962, as applicable to Sind. The rules specify authorities for appointment, appeal, punishment, transfer, and controlling travelling allowance for posts in the Information Department, regardless of who appointed the holder.

name: SIND LOCAL COUNCIL AND MUNICIPAL COMMITTEE SERVANTS (REST AND RECREATION ALLOWANCE) RULES, 1970.

metadata.short_title: The Sind Local Council and Municipal Committee Servants (Rest and Recreation Allowance) Rules, 1970
metadata.parent_law: Article 47(a) read with Article 89 of the Basic Democracies Order, 1959 (P.O.18 of 1959), and section 29 read with section 121 and item 9 of Fourth Schedule to the Municipal Administration Ordinance, 1960
metadata.administering_body: Government of Sind, Local Government Department
metadata.one_line: These rules grant recreation leave and allowance to servants of Local Councils and Municipal Committees in Sindh.
metadata.summary: These rules provide for the granting of recreation leave and a corresponding recreation allowance to members of the Local Council Service and servants of Local Councils or Municipal Committees in Sindh. Eligibility for the allowance depends on the likelihood of continuing service for at least three years, with specific provisions for those due for retirement or employed in the Vacation Department. The rules define the duration of leave, the calculation of the allowance based on pay components, and the authority required to sanction such allowances.

metadata.short_title: The Sind Prohibition Rules, 1979
metadata.administering_body: Excise and Taxation Department, Government of Sind
metadata.one_line: Rules made by the Government of Sind to carry into effect the Prohibition (Enforcement of Hadd) Order, 1979.
metadata.summary: These rules were made by the Government of Sind under the powers of Articles 21 and 31 of the Prohibition (Enforcement of Hadd) Order, 1979. They define key terms such as 'Director', 'Government', and various types of permits for intoxicants. The rules establish the hierarchy of officers, including the Director General as Collector, outline procedures for appeals against orders, and specify conditions for granting licenses for the purchase, possession, transport, or consumption of liquor.

metadata.short_title: The Sind Ushr (Assessment and Collection) Rules, 1983
metadata.one_line: Rules made by the Central Zakat Council for the assessment and collection of Ushr in Sindh under the Zakat and Ushr Ordinance, 1980.
metadata.summary: These rules provide the framework for assessing and collecting Ushr in the Province of Sind. They define key terms such as 'assessee' and 'fasal', establish procedures for determining low average yields and farm-gate prices, and outline the powers of Local, Taluka, Sub-Divisional, and District Committees. The document details the process for self-assessment by farmers, the preparation of assessment statements, and the mechanisms for recovering unpaid Ushr.

name: SINDH COUNCILS MAYOR, DEPUTY MAYOR, CHAIRMAN, AND VICE CHAIRMAN (HONORARIA AND PRIVILEGES) RULES, 2017

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Councils Mayor, Deputy Mayor, Chairman and Vice Chairman (Honoraria and Privileges) Rules, 2017
metadata.administering_body: Local Government and Housing Town Planning Department
metadata.one_line: These rules prescribe honoraria, privileges, allowances, and facilities for local government officials in Sindh.
metadata.summary: The document establishes the Sindh Councils Mayor, Deputy Mayor, Chairman and Vice Chairman (Honoraria and Privileges) Rules, 2017. It defines key terms such as 'Act' and 'Government' within the context of the Sindh Local Government Act, 2013. The rules specify honoraria amounts for various positions across different council types, entitlements to official residence, vehicles, telephones, medical facilities, office accommodation, and travel allowances based on Basic Scale (BS) ranks.

name: SINDH HIGH COURT ESTABLISHMENT (APPOINTMENT AND CONDITIONS OF SERVICE) RULES, 2006.

metadata.short_title: The High Court Establishment (Appointment and Conditions of Service) Rules, 2006
metadata.commencement: on publication in the official Gazette
repeals: The High Court Establishment (Appointment and Conditions of Service) Rules, made under the authority of the constitution 1956
metadata.one_line: These rules regulate the appointment and conditions of service for officers and servants of the High Court of Sindh.
metadata.summary: The High Court Establishment (Appointment and Conditions of Service) Rules, 2006, were made to regulate the appointment and employment conditions of officers and servants of the High Court of Sindh. The rules define various terms such as 'Administrative committees', 'Chief Justice', and 'Judicial Officer', and establish the strength of staff comprising persons holding specified posts. They outline methods of appointment including direct recruitment, promotion, and contract appointments, while also detailing qualifications, seniority, vacations, and disciplinary procedures.

metadata.short_title: SKAA Low-Cost Housing Scheme Regulations 2008
metadata.one_line: Regulations governing the SKAA Low-Cost Housing Scheme for plot allocation and management in Sindh.
metadata.summary: These regulations establish the framework for the Sindh Katchi Abadis Authority (SKAA) to implement low-cost housing schemes in the province of Sindh. They define key terms such as 'Allocation' and 'Low-cost Housing Scheme', outlining the powers of the Authority to acquire land, manage funds, and establish committees for oversight. The document details procedures for plot disposal, lease management, utility service provision, and restrictions on land use changes or commercial activities.

name: Sindh law Officer (Conditions of Service) Rules, 1940.

metadata.short_title: Sindh law Officer (Conditions of Service) Rules, 1940
amends: Rules referred to in Government notification No. 1778, dated the 31st August, 1923
metadata.one_line: Regulates conditions of service, appointments, and conduct of Law Officers in Sindh under the Government of India Act, 1935.
metadata.summary: These rules regulate the conditions of service for Law Officers in Sindh, superseding earlier 1923 rules. They define key terms like 'Government Pleader' and 'Public prosecutor', outline appointment procedures by a committee or Chief Minister, and set eligibility criteria based on years standing at the Bar. The document also establishes restrictions on appearing against the government, tenure limits, and provisions for fees and contingent expenses.

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Local Council (Contract) Rules, 2016
metadata.administering_body: Local Government and Housing Town Planning Department
metadata.one_line: Rules made by the Government of Sindh to regulate contracts, tenders, and procurement for local councils.
metadata.summary: These rules provide the legal framework for local councils in Sindh to enter into contracts for goods, works, and services. They mandate that contracts be made by the Authority (Mayor or Chairman) and require adherence to public procurement procedures, including tender invitations and security deposits. The rules define key terms like 'agreement' and 'contractor', specify limits on contract values based on council type, and establish registers for recording contracts.

name: SINDH LOCAL COUNCILS (AUCTIONING OF COLLECTION RIGHTS) RULES, 2016

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Local Councils (Auctioning of Collection Rights) Rules, 2016
metadata.administering_body: Local Government and Housing Town Planning Department
metadata.one_line: Rules governing the auctioning of collection rights for local council incomes in Sindh.
metadata.summary: These rules empower the Government of Sindh to regulate the auctioning of collection rights for various local council incomes. They establish procedures for public notices, bid acceptance, reserve price determination, and contract awarding through open auctions or negotiation. The document also outlines mechanisms for dispute resolution via arbitration and conditions under which contracts may be cancelled.

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Local Government Contract Rules, 2001
metadata.administering_body: Local Government, Rural Development and Katchi Abadis Department
metadata.one_line: Rules made by the Government of Sindh to regulate contracts, tenders, and appointments for local governments.
metadata.summary: These Rules provide the framework for Local Governments in Sindh to make contracts, invite tenders, and appoint consultants. They define the authority responsible for signing contracts, the requirements for tender submission including earnest money, and the security deposits needed for performance. The Rules also specify financial limits at which council approval is required and mandate public notices for significant expenditures.

name: SINDH LOCAL GOVERNMENT TMA UA SERVANTS (EFFICIENCY AND DISCIPLINE RULES, 2001.

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Local Government TMA/UA Servants (Efficiency and Discipline) Rules, 2001
metadata.parent_law: The Sindh Local Government Ordinance, 2001 (Sindh Ordinance No. XXVII)
repeals: Sindh Local Council Servants (E&D) Rules, 1974
metadata.administering_body: Local Government, Rural Development and Katchi Abadis Department
metadata.one_line: These rules govern the efficiency and discipline of TMA/UA servants in Sindh, defining penalties and inquiry procedures.
metadata.summary: These rules establish the framework for maintaining efficiency and discipline among servants of Taluka Municipal Administration (TMA) and Union Administration in Sindh. They establish authorities to handle property restoration cases for bonded labourers and confer specific powers on Deputy Commissioners to inspect workplaces and mobilize organizations for rehabilitation.
