metadata.short_title: The Karachi Water and Sewerage Board Employees (Appointment, Promotion and Transfer) Rules, 1987
metadata.administering_body: Government of Sindh, Housing, Town Planning, Local Government and Rural Development Department
metadata.one_line: Rules governing appointment, promotion, transfer, and related procedures for employees of the Karachi Water and Sewerage Board.
metadata.summary: These rules establish the framework for appointing, promoting, and transferring employees of the Karachi Water and Sewerage Board. They define various terms such as 'Board', 'employee', and 'deputation', and set out the methods of appointment including initial appointment, promotion, and transfer. The rules specify the qualifications, age limits, and selection processes involving Selection Committees and Promotion Committees. Additionally, they provide for adhoc appointments in cases of urgent public interest.

metadata.short_title: Sindh Colonization and Disposal of Government Lands Rules, 2005
metadata.parent_law: Colonization and Disposal of Government Lands Act, 1912
metadata.one_line: Rules made by the Government of Sindh regarding the grant, auction, and management of non-agricultural government lands.
metadata.summary: These rules govern the granting of land for non-agricultural purposes in Sindh under the Colonization and Disposal of Government Lands Act, 1912. They establish committees to determine market prices and oversee the scrutiny of applications. The rules detail procedures for auctions, deposit requirements, lease terms up to ninety-nine years, and conditions for resuming land for public purposes.

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Legal Practitioners and Bar Council Rules, 1991
metadata.parent_law: Legal Practitioners and Bar Council Act 1973 (Act XXXV of 1973)
repeals: The Sindh Legal Practitioners and Bar Council Rules, 1969
Sindh and Baluchistan Legal Practitioners and Bar Council Rules, 1975
metadata.one_line: These rules frame the constitution, meetings, and disciplinary procedures for the Sindh Provincial Bar Council.
metadata.summary: The document repeals and reframes previous rules governing the Sindh Legal Practitioners and Bar Council. It defines key terms such as 'Act', 'Bar Council', and 'Member' and establishes the structure for the First Meeting and elections. The rules detail the functions of the Chairman, Vice-Chairman, and Secretary, prescribe notice periods for meetings, set quorum requirements, and outline fees for various proceedings.

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Local Government (Citizen Community Boards) Rules, 2004
metadata.administering_body: Local Government Department, Government of Sindh
metadata.one_line: These rules regulate the registration, name change, project implementation, and financial management of Citizen Community Boards in Sindh.
metadata.summary: The Sindh Local Government (Citizen Community Boards) Rules, 2004 establish the framework for registering Citizen Community Boards within Union Councils. The document outlines procedures for name availability, charter subscription by founder members, and the submission of project proposals to local councils. It also details financial protocols including budget re-appropriation, audit requirements, and the management of excesses or surrenders in funds.

name: LOCAL GOVERNMENT NAZIMS, NAIB NAZIMS & MEMBERS (HONORARIA AND PRIVILAGES) RULES, 2001

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Local Government Nazims, Naib Nazims & Members (Honoraria and Privileges) Rules, 2001
repeals: The Sindh Local Councils Mayor and Chairman (Honoraria & privileges) Rules, 1980
metadata.administering_body: Local Government, Rural Development and Katchi Abadis Department (Sindh Local Government Board)
metadata.one_line: These rules prescribe honoraria, privileges, allowances, and facilities for local government officials in Sindh.
metadata.summary: These rules were made by the Government of Sindh to regulate the honoraria, house rent, official vehicle usage, travel allowances, and other privileges for Nazims, Naib Nazims, and Members. They specify payment rates based on district types and provide entitlements for medical facilities, office accommodation, and leave of absence. The rules also establish controlling authorities for adjudicating allowances and explicitly repeal the 1980 rules regarding local council mayors and chairmen.

name: Market Committee, non-unfilled, Employees (Efficiency and discipline) Byelaws, 1985.

metadata.short_title: The Market Committee, non-unfilled, Employees (Efficiency and discipline) Byelaws, 1985
metadata.one_line: Byelaws governing efficiency, discipline, misconduct, and penalties for employees of the Market Committee in Sindh.
metadata.summary: These byelaws establish the rules for maintaining efficiency and discipline among employees of the Market Committee. They define key terms such as 'misconduct' and 'corruption', outline minor and major penalties including dismissal, and prescribe procedures for inquiries and appeals. The document applies to all employees except members of the Sindh market Committees Unified Grade.

metadata.short_title: Market Committee Employees Service Bye-Laws, 1984
metadata.one_line: These bye-laws regulate the appointment, probation, confirmation, and gratuity of employees in Sindh Market Committees.
metadata.summary: The Market Committee Employees Service Bye-Laws, 1984 govern the service conditions for employees of Market Committees in Sindh. They establish procedures for initial recruitment and promotion through selection committees, defining eligibility criteria such as age limits and educational qualifications found in the Schedule. The document also outlines rules regarding probation periods, confirmation processes, seniority lists, and entitlement to gratuity upon retirement or death.

metadata.short_title: Sindh Minimum Wages Rules, 2021
repeals: Minimum Wages Rules, 1962
metadata.administering_body: Labour and Human Resources Department, Government of Sindh
metadata.one_line: These rules establish the Minimum Wages Board and procedures for determining minimum wages in Sindh.
metadata.summary: The Sindh Minimum Wages Rules, 2021 provide the framework for regulating minimum rates of wages, allowances, and relief for workers in industrial and commercial undertakings within Sindh. They define key terms such as the Authority, Board, Chairperson, and members, outlining their terms of office, appointment processes, and disqualification criteria. The rules also prescribe formats for wage slips, muster rolls, and applications for claims regarding unpaid minimum wages.

name: NARA CANAL AREA WATER BOARD ELECTION (CHAIRMAN) REGULATINS, 2004.

metadata.short_title: The Nara Canal Area Water Board Election (Chairman) Regulations, 2004
metadata.territorial_extent: the whole of the area falling under the Nara Canal Area Water Board
metadata.commencement: on such date, as the Nara Canal Area Water Board may, by notification, appoint
metadata.one_line: Regulates the election of the chairman for the Nara Canal Area Water Board under the Sindh Water Management Ordinance, 2002.
metadata.summary: These regulations govern the election process for the chairman of the Nara Canal Area Water Board. They define qualifications and disqualifications for candidates, establish procedures for voter lists and polling, and outline the powers of the Election Committee. The document also provides mechanisms for appeals to the Governor regarding election limitations or results.

metadata.short_title: The Sind Paddy Development Fee Rules, 1976
metadata.one_line: Rules made by the Government of Sind for the assessment and collection of paddy development fee from rice husking mills.
metadata.summary: These rules were made under section 9 of the Sind Finance Act, 1975 to regulate the assessment and collection of paddy development fees. They define key terms such as 'Mill', 'Occupier', and 'Paddy' and mandate that occupiers register their mills with the District Excise and Taxation Officer. The rules prescribe specific procedures for collecting fees, maintaining daily accounts in prescribed forms, issuing receipts, and submitting weekly returns to the officer.

metadata.short_title: The Panchayat (Appeal) Rules, 1981
metadata.administering_body: Housing, Town Planning, Local Government and Rural Development Department
metadata.one_line: These rules prescribe the procedure for filing appeals against Panchayat orders to a Magistrate of First Class in Sindh.
metadata.summary: The Panchayat (Appeal) Rules, 1981 were made by the Government of Sind under the Sind Local Government Ordinance, 1979. They establish the procedure for filing appeals against orders passed by a Panchayat to a Magistrate of First Class acting as an appellate court. An appeal must be filed within thirty days in the form of a petition accompanied by a copy of the order appealed against. The rules also specify that if the appellant is in jail, the petition can be submitted to the officer in charge of the jail for forwarding.

metadata.short_title: The People's Local Councils (Land) Rules, 1975
metadata.parent_law: The Sind People's Local Government Ordinance, 1972 (Ordinance-II of 1972)
metadata.administering_body: Housing, Town Planning and Local Government Department
metadata.one_line: Rules made by the Government of Sind regarding land vesting, leasing, rent fixation, and management for People's Local Councils.
metadata.summary: These rules were framed under the Sind People's Local Government Ordinance, 1972 to regulate land matters for People's Local Councils in Sindh. They cover the vesting of land in councils, the continuation and renewal of existing leases, and the granting of new leases for cultivation, building sites, or special purposes. The rules also establish procedures for public auctions, rent fixation, mutation of names, and the collection of fees.

name: PROCEDURE OF THE BUSINESS OF THE PROVINCIAL COUNCIL OF SINDH,1980

metadata.short_title: The Procedure of the Business of the Provincial Council of Sind, 1980
metadata.administering_body: Government of Sindh Services and General Administration Department
metadata.one_line: Lays down the constitution, functions, meetings, and allowances for the Provincial Council of Sind under Martial Law.
metadata.summary: This notification establishes the Provincial Council of Sind and defines its composition, including the Chairman, Ministers, and ex-officio members. It outlines the procedures for meetings, notice requirements, agenda setting, and the appointment of committees to facilitate functions. The document also specifies travelling and daily allowances for members based on West Pakistan Travelling Allowance Rules.

metadata.short_title: The Provincial Assembly of Sind (Finance Committee) Rules, 1973
metadata.parent_law: Constitution of the Islamic Republic of Pakistan
metadata.administering_body: Secretariat of the Provincial Assembly of Sind
metadata.one_line: Rules regulating the procedure, composition, functions, and financial control powers of the Finance Committee of the Provincial Assembly of Sind.
metadata.summary: These rules establish the Provincial Assembly of Sind (Finance Committee) Rules, 1973 to regulate the procedure of the Finance Committee. The Committee consists of the Speaker, the Finance Minister, and elected members, with functions including budget preparation and advising on expenditure. It exercises control over Secretariat expenditure within authorized appropriations and handles financial sanctions, delegations of power, and supplementary estimates.

metadata.short_title: Provincial Ombudsman (Employees) Service Rules, 1997
metadata.parent_law: Establishment of the Office of Ombudsman for the Province of Sindh Act, 1991
metadata.one_line: Rules governing the appointment, promotion, transfer, and conditions of service for employees of the Provincial Ombudsman in Sindh.
metadata.summary: These rules prescribe the method, qualifications, and conditions of employment for posts ranging from BPS-1 to BPS-17 within the Secretariat and Regional Offices of the Provincial Ombudsman (Mohtasib) Sindh. They establish Promotion and Selection Committees to oversee appointments by promotion, transfer, or initial recruitment based on merit, seniority, and fitness. The document also defines key terms such as 'Acting Charge' appointment and outlines specific eligibility criteria for various clerical and support staff positions.

name: REGISTRATION OF FARMERS ORGANIZATION, WATER COURSE ASSOCIATION AND DRAINAGE BENEFICIARY GROUP REGULATIONS , 2004.

metadata.short_title: The Registration of Farmers' Organization, Water Course Association and Drainage Beneficiary Groups Regulations, 2004
metadata.territorial_extent: the whole of the area falling under the regulatory authority
metadata.commencement: on such date as the regulatory authority may, by notification, appoint
repeals: all previous Regulations, Rules, Orders, and instructions dealing with the registration of FOs, WCAs and DBGs
metadata.one_line: These regulations establish the procedure for registering farmers' organizations, water course associations, and drainage beneficiary groups.
metadata.summary: These regulations provide the legal framework for the registration of Farmers' Organizations (FOs), Water Course Associations (WCAs), and Drainage Beneficiary Groups (DBGs). They specify the requirements for application, including necessary information regarding land titles, member lists, and financial deposits. The Regulatory Authority is empowered to process applications, issue notices, and prescribe forms, while repealing all previous regulations on this subject.

metadata.short_title: The Employees (Efficiency & Discipline) Rules, 1999
metadata.territorial_extent: all SASO Employees wherever they may be
repeals: The Sindh Civil Servants(Efficiency and Discipline) Rules, 1973 as adopted by SASO in their application to SASO employees
metadata.one_line: Rules governing efficiency, discipline, penalties, and inquiry procedures for SASO employees in Sindh.
metadata.summary: These rules establish the framework for maintaining efficiency and discipline among employees of the Sindh Agricultural Supplies Organization (SASO). They define grounds for penalties such as inefficiency, misconduct, corruption, and subversive activities. The document outlines minor and major penalties, inquiry procedures, appeal mechanisms, and the specific authorities designated to handle cases based on employee rank.

metadata.short_title: The SIDA Election (Members) Regulations, 2004
metadata.territorial_extent: the whole of the area falling under the SIDA
metadata.commencement: on such date, as the SIDA may, by notification, fix in this behalf
metadata.one_line: Regulates the election of members for the Sindh Irrigation and Drainage Authority.
metadata.summary: These regulations govern the elections of elected members of the SIDA, establishing qualifications and disqualifications for candidates. They define the structure of constituencies, voting procedures, and the powers of the Election Committee. The document also outlines the process for appeals to the Government under the parent Ordinance.

name: SIND zakat committees (chairman and members) (review application) rules, 1985.

metadata.short_title: The Sind Zakat Committees (Chairman and Members) (Review Application) Rules, 1985
metadata.one_line: Rules governing the filing and disposal of review applications by removed or ceased Zakat committee members.
metadata.summary: These rules provide a mechanism for the Chairman or member of a Zakat Committee to apply for a review of their removal or cessation from office. The application must be filed within thirty days with the Sind Zakat Council on plain paper addressed to the Secretary. The Council considers the application in a meeting, allowing the applicant to appear before them; if they fail to appear despite notice, the matter is decided ex parte. If the review is successful, the individual is reinstated with effect from the date specified in the resolution.

name: Sind (Gazetted) Civil Services (National Scales of Pay) Rules, 1974.

metadata.short_title: The Sind (Gazetted) Civil Services (National Scales of Pay) Rules, 1974
metadata.one_line: These rules establish national pay scales for gazetted civil servants in the Province of Sind.
metadata.summary: These rules prescribe national scales of pay applicable to gazetted civil servants serving in the affairs of the Province of Sind. They provide existing civil servants with the right to opt for these new scales or retain their existing pay scales, subject to specific conditions and timelines. The rules detail how pay is fixed upon opting for the new scales, including provisions for increments, promotions, and special pay for various departments.

metadata.short_title: Sind Assembly Secretariat (Recruitment) Rules, 1974
metadata.territorial_extent: the Secretariat of the Provincial Assembly of Sind
metadata.parent_law: Constitution of the Islamic Republic of Pakistan
repeals: The West Pakistan Provincial Assembly Secretariat (Secretary, Deputy Secretaries and Assistant Secretaries) Recruitment Rules, 1965
The West Pakistan Provincial Assembly Secretariat Ministerial Service Rules, 1967
metadata.one_line: Regulates recruitment, promotion, transfer, and appointment methods for the Secretariat of the Provincial Assembly of Sind.
metadata.summary: These rules regulate the recruitment of persons to the Secretariat of the Provincial Assembly of Sind. They establish methods for recruitment including promotion, transfer, and direct recruitment, along with specific qualifications and authority requirements. The document also details the strength and composition of the Secretariat, defining various posts and grades within both permanent and temporary categories.

metadata.short_title: The Sind Cinematograph Rules, 1982
metadata.one_line: Rules made by the Government of Sind to regulate cinematograph exhibitions and licensing within the province.
metadata.summary: These rules were made under the Motion Pictures Ordinance, 1979, to regulate public cinematograph exhibitions in Sindh. They establish procedures for granting No Objection Certificates and licenses, defining terms like 'cinema' and 'auditorium', and setting conditions for seating, fire safety, sanitation, and admission rates. The rules also cover temporary permits, touring cinemas, and the appointment of staff and operators.

metadata.short_title: The Sind Civil Servants (Appeal) Rules, 1980
repeals: The Sind Civil Servants (Appeal) Rules, 1975
metadata.administering_body: Government of Sind Services & General Administration Department
metadata.one_line: These rules establish the procedure for civil servants in Sindh to prefer appeals against orders regarding their terms and conditions of service.
metadata.summary: The Sind Civil Servants (Appeal) Rules, 1980 provide a framework for civil servants aggrieved by orders relating to their terms and conditions to file appeals. The rules define the competent authority and appellate authority based on the rank of the officer making the order. An appeal must be filed within 30 days of the order, though delays may be condoned under specific circumstances. The process involves submitting a memorandum of appeal through the head of the office, which is then transmitted to the competent authority and subsequently to the appellate authority for review and final orders.

name: SIND CIVIL SERVANTS (CHANGE IN NOMENCLATURE OF SERVICES AND ABOLITION OF CLASSES) RULES, 1974

metadata.short_title: The Sind Civil Servants (Change in Nomenclature of Services and Abolition of Classes) Rules, 1974
metadata.one_line: These rules change service nomenclature to Sind Unified Basic Scales and abolish existing classes and post reservations in Sindh.
metadata.summary: These rules were made by the Government of Sind under the powers of the Sind Civil Servants Act, 1973. They immediately change the names of services to the Sind Unified Basic Scales and abolish all previous classifications of services and posts into Classes I through IV. The rules also abolish reservations for specific cadres or posts and establish a correspondence between old class designations and new basic scales.

name: SIND CIVIL SERVANTS (PROBATION, CONFIRMATION AND SENIORITY) RULES, 1975

metadata.short_title: The Sind Civil Servants (Probation, Confirmation and Seniority) Rules, 1975
metadata.administering_body: Government of Sind Services & General Administration Department
metadata.one_line: These rules regulate the probation, confirmation, and seniority of civil servants in Sindh.
metadata.summary: The document establishes the framework for the probation period for newly recruited and other appointed civil servants in Sindh. It outlines the procedures for confirming a civil servant to a permanent post, including conditions regarding liens and consent from departments. The rules also define how seniority is calculated based on regular appointment dates, transfers, promotions, and age, as well as grounds for deferring confirmation or promotion.

name: SIND CIVIL SERVANTS (RESTRICTION ON MARRIAGE WITH FOREIGN NATIONALS)RULES, 1982

metadata.short_title: The Sind Civil Servants (Restriction on Marriage with Foreign Nationals) Rules, 1982
repeals: The West Pakistan Government Servants (Restriction on Marriages with Foreign Nationals) Rules, 1963
metadata.max_penalty: major penalties specified in the Sind Civil Servants (Efficiency & Discipline) Rules, 1973
metadata.one_line: Restricts civil servants in Sindh from marrying foreign nationals without government permission.
metadata.summary: These rules prohibit civil servants in Sindh from marrying or promising to marry a foreign national without prior government permission. Such unauthorized marriages constitute misconduct subject to major disciplinary penalties. The rules grant the Government discretion to permit marriage under specified conditions and rescind earlier West Pakistan regulations.

name: SIND CIVIL SERVANTS LANGUAGE EXAMIANTION RUELS 1981

metadata.short_title: The Sind Civil Servants Language Examination Rules, 1981
repeals: The Sind Government Servants Language Examination Rules, 1963
metadata.one_line: These rules mandate Urdu or Sindhi language examinations for civil servants in Sindh and repeal the 1963 rules.
metadata.summary: The Sind Civil Servants Language Examination Rules, 1981 were made by the Government of Sindh under section 26 of the Sind Civil Servants Act, 1973. They require civil servants in Grade 5 and above to pass an examination in Urdu or Sindhi depending on their mother tongue. The rules specify examination standards, conduct procedures, exemptions, rewards for passing, and penalties for failure, while repealing the previous 1963 regulations.

name: Sind Civil Servants Welfare Fund Rules, 1980.

metadata.short_title: Sind Civil Servants Welfare Fund Rules, 1980
metadata.parent_law: Sind Civil Servant Welfare Fund Ordinance, 1979
metadata.one_line: Rules governing contributions, nominations, and death benefits for the Sind Civil Servants Welfare Fund.
metadata.summary: These rules establish the framework for the Sind Civil Servants Welfare Fund under the powers of the 1979 Ordinance. They mandate annual contributions from civil servants in Grade-5 or above, with lower-grade contributions funded by the Government. The rules detail procedures for nominating beneficiaries for death benefits, managing fund accounts within the Government treasury, and processing claims upon a civil servant's death.

metadata.short_title: the Sind Co-operative Housing Authority Rules, 1986
metadata.one_line: Rules made by the Government of Sindh to regulate the administration, finance, and enquiry procedures of the Sind Co-operative Housing Authority.
metadata.summary: These rules were made under the powers of the Sind Co-operative Housing Authority Ordinance, 1982, to govern the functioning of the Authority. They establish the location of the head office in Karachi, define the appointment process for the Managing Director, and outline procedures for enquiries into charges against societies. The rules also mandate financial management practices, including budget preparation, fund administration, audit reporting, and the submission of annual reports to the Government.

name: Sind Coal and Metalliferous Mines (Supplementary) Regulations 1986.

metadata.short_title: The Sind Coal and Metalliferous Mines (Supplementary) Regulations, 1986
metadata.commencement: on such date as the Government may by notification in the official Gazette, appoint
metadata.administering_body: Labour and Cooperation Department, Government of Sind
metadata.one_line: These regulations supplement existing mine laws regarding welfare officers, training, safety equipment, and disease reporting in Sindh mines.
metadata.summary: The Sind Coal and Metalliferous Mines (Supplementary) Regulations, 1986 were made by the Government of Sind to supplement existing coal and metalliferous mine regulations. They establish requirements for appointing qualified Welfare and Safety Officers in large mines, detailing their duties regarding employee welfare, safety supervision, and training organization. The document also outlines provisions for vocational training exemptions, safety standards for pressure equipment like air receivers, and provides a specific form for reporting occupational diseases to authorities.

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Councils (Appeal) Rules, 1982
repeals: Basic Democracies and Local Government Department Notification No. SOXI-64/80, dated the 31st December, 1960
metadata.one_line: These rules establish Tribunals and procedures for filing and disposing of appeals against orders passed under the Sindh Local Government Ordinance, 1979.
metadata.summary: The Sindh Councils (Appeal) Rules, 1982 were made by the Government of Sindh to regulate appeals against orders passed under the Sindh Local Government Ordinance, 1979. The rules establish Tribunals consisting of a person who is or has been a district judge and define the period for filing appeals as thirty days from the date of the order. They prescribe the manner in which appeals must be filed, including the requirement for a written memorandum signed by the appellant, and outline the procedure for the disposal of appeals, including interim orders and the awarding of costs.

metadata.short_title: The Sind Drainage Rates Rules, 1983
metadata.one_line: These rules establish drainage rates for cultivated land in Sindh's Salinity Control and Reclamation Projects.
metadata.summary: The Sind Drainage Rates Rules, 1983 were made by the Government of Sindh to levy drainage rates on cultivated land within specific Salinity Control and Reclamation Projects. The rules define terms such as 'Assessing Authority' and 'drainage rate', and specify that bills for assessment are issued bi-annually at the end of the Kharif and Rabi crop seasons. Payments are due by December 31st for Kharif crops and June 30th for Rabi crops, with provisions for remission in cases of natural calamities or crop failure.

metadata.short_title: The Sind Factories (Adult Exemption) Rules, 1973
metadata.one_line: Rules exempting adult male workers from certain provisions of the Factories Act, 1934 for specific roles and urgent tasks.
metadata.summary: These rules were framed by the Government of Sind under Section 43 of the Factories Act, 1934 to define exemptions for adult male workers. They specify categories of persons in supervision or confidential positions, as well as those engaged in urgent repairs, preparatory work, and intermittent tasks. The rules impose conditions on working hours, rest intervals, and record-keeping requirements for managers.

metadata.short_title: The Sind Land Commission (Pre-emption) Rules, 1974
metadata.one_line: These rules establish the procedure for tenants to claim first right of pre-emption on land sales within Sindh.
metadata.summary: The Sind Land Commission (Pre-emption) Rules, 1974 provide a legal framework for tenants in Sindh to claim their first right of pre-emption when land is sold. Tenants must apply to the Revenue Court exercising Tribunal powers within twelve months of the sale execution or enforcement. If the Tribunal determines the sale lacked tenant consent, it orders the sale in favor of the tenant-applicant upon payment of the sale price. The rules define key terms by reference to the Land Reforms Regulations, 1972 and the Sind Tenancy Act, 1950.

name: Sind Land Revenue Flat Rate Assessment Rules, 1973.

metadata.short_title: the Sind Land Revenue Flat Rate Assessment Rules, 1973
metadata.commencement: at the commencement of the agricultural year 1972-73
metadata.parent_law: West Pakistan Land Revenue Act, 1967 (West Pakistan Act XVII of 1967)
metadata.one_line: These rules establish the flat rate for land revenue assessment in Sindh based on produce index units and area.
metadata.summary: The Sind Land Revenue Flat Rate Assessment Rules, 1973 were made by the Government of Sind under the West Pakistan Land Revenue Act, 1967. They provide a method to ascertain a flat rate of land revenue by dividing the average Jamabandi by the average area expressed in produce index units for the five years ending 1970-71. The rules define specific terms related to land classification, irrigation methods, and cultivation status, including provisions for relief for small khatedars and those with uncultivated land due to natural causes.

name: SIND LOCAL, TALUKA AND SUB-DIVISIONAL ZAKAT AND USHR COMMITTEES (CONSTITUTION) RULES, 1979.

metadata.short_title: The Sind Local, Taluka and Sub-Divisional Zakat and Ushr Committees (Constitution) Rules, 1979
metadata.administering_body: Sind Zakat Council / Provincial Zakat Administration
metadata.one_line: Rules for the constitution of Local, Taluka and Sub-Divisional Zakat and Ushr Committees in Sindh.
metadata.summary: These Rules provide the framework for constituting Local, Taluka, and Sub-Divisional Zakat and Ushr Committees in the Province of Sind. They outline the procedures for selecting members through local gatherings, electing Chairmen, and handling objections or appeals. The rules are made under the authority of the Zakat and Ushr (Organisation) Ordinance, 1979, with the approval of the Central Zakat Council.

name: Sind Market Committees Unified Grade Service Rules, 1983.

metadata.short_title: Sind Market Committees Unified Grade Service Rules, 1983
metadata.one_line: Rules governing the unified grade service, recruitment, promotion, and seniority for Sind Market Committees.
metadata.summary: These rules establish a unified grade service for market committees in Sindh under the Agricultural Produce Markets Act, 1939. They define terms related to appointments, grades, and the Bureau of Supply and Prices. The document outlines procedures for initial recruitment through selection committees and promotion based on seniority-cum-fitness. It also sets qualification requirements, age limits, and probation periods for various posts within the service.

metadata.short_title: The Sind Paddy Development Fee Rules, 1976
metadata.one_line: Rules made by the Government of Sind for the assessment and collection of paddy development fee from rice husking mills.
metadata.summary: These rules were made under section 9 of the Sind Finance Act, 1975 to regulate the assessment and collection of fees on paddy husked at mills in Sindh. They define key terms such as 'Mill', 'Occupier', and 'Paddy' and mandate specific record-keeping procedures including daily registers and receipt books. Occupiers are required to collect fees, credit them to the government treasury by the end of the week, and submit weekly returns for verification by the District Excise and Taxation Officer.

name: SIND PENCHAYATS ( FUNCTIONS AND CONDUCT OF BUSINESS) RULES, 1980.

metadata.short_title: The Sind Panchayats (Functions and Conduct of Business) Rules, 1980
metadata.administering_body: Government of Sind, Housing, Town Planning, Local Government and Rural Development Department
metadata.one_line: These rules prescribe the functions, conduct of business, meetings, quorum, and optional duties for Panchayats in Sindh.
metadata.summary: These rules define the short title and commencement for the governance of Panchayats in Sindh. They establish the definitions for key terms like Chairman, Member, and Meeting within the context of the Sind Local Government Ordinance, 1979. The document outlines specific functions for the Panchayat and its Chairman, including meeting frequency, quorum requirements, and optional duties such as mosque supervision and adult education promotion.

name: Sind People’s Local Council Service Welfare Fund Rules, 1973.

metadata.short_title: the Sind People's Local Council Service Welfare Fund Rules, 1973
metadata.parent_law: Sind People's Local Government Ordinance, 1972 (Sind Ordinance II of 1972)
establishes: Sind People's Local Councils Service Welfare Fund Board
People's Local Council Service Welfare Fund
metadata.administering_body: Housing, Town Planning and Local Government Department, Government of Sindh
metadata.one_line: These rules establish a welfare fund and insurance scheme for members of the Sind People's Local Councils Service.
metadata.summary: These rules establish the Sind People's Local Councils Service Welfare Fund to provide financial assistance and group insurance for employees of the Sind People's Local Councils Service. A Board is constituted to manage the fund, arrange insurance with approved companies, and sanction grants for retired or invalided-out employees. The rules define key terms regarding family members, pay, and the accounts officer responsible for auditing the fund annually.

metadata.short_title: The Sind Permanent Residence Certificate Rules, 1971
establishes: Committee for appeals regarding certificate grants or refusals
metadata.one_line: These rules establish the procedure and criteria for obtaining permanent residence certificates in Sindh for educational admission and public service recruitment.
metadata.summary: The Sind Permanent Residence Certificate Rules, 1971 were framed by the Governor of Sind to regulate the issuance of permanent residence certificates. These certificates are required for admission to medical or engineering colleges and other educational institutions in Sindh, as well as for recruitment to public services under the rule-making authority of the Governor. The rules specify eligibility criteria based on birthplace, domicile, parental service, or residence duration, and outline the application process involving specific forms and affidavits handled by District Magistrates.

metadata.short_title: The Sind Private Colleges Service Rules, 1970
metadata.parent_law: Sind Private Colleges (Management and Control) Ordinance, 1970
metadata.one_line: Rules governing appointments, qualifications, pay, and dismissal for teachers in private colleges in Sindh.
metadata.summary: These rules establish the framework for appointing teachers to private colleges in Sindh, requiring specific academic qualifications and barring those with a history of dismissal or conviction. They define the roles of the Governing Body and selection committees in appointments, set probation periods and pay scales, and outline strict procedures for termination, dismissal, and retirement.

name: SIND PRIVATE COLLEGES (ELECTION OF THE CHAIRMAN) RULES, 1970

metadata.short_title: The Sind Private Colleges (Election of the Chairman) Rules, 1970
metadata.parent_law: The Sind Private Colleges (Management and Control) Ordinance, 1970
metadata.one_line: These rules prescribe the procedure for electing the Chairman of Governing Bodies in private colleges under the Sind Private Colleges (Management and Control) Ordinance, 1970.
metadata.summary: These rules were made by the Government of Sind to prescribe the procedure for the election of the Chairman of Governing Bodies of private colleges. They define key terms such as 'Qualified Members' and outline the timeline for holding elections, including notice periods and quorum requirements. The document details the process for proposing candidates, conducting polls via ballot papers, handling uncontested elections, and resolving disputes through appeals to a competent authority.

name: SIND PRIVATE COLLEGES CONTRIBUTORY PROVIDENT FUND RULES, 1970

metadata.short_title: The Sind Private Colleges Contributory Provident Fund Rules, 1970
metadata.parent_law: Sind Private Colleges (Management and Control) Ordinance, 1970
metadata.one_line: These rules establish a contributory provident fund for teachers in private colleges in Sindh, defining contributions, management, and investment.
metadata.summary: The document establishes a Contributory Provident Fund for all private colleges in Sindh. It defines the composition of the Managing Committee, which includes elected teacher representatives and nominees from the Governing Body. Teachers are required to contribute 5% of their pay, matched by the Governing Body, with funds invested in approved bank accounts or securities. The rules also cover account maintenance, nomination procedures for death benefits, and audit requirements.

name: SIND PROFESSIONS, TRADES, CALLINGS AND EMPLOYMENT TAX RULES, 1976.

metadata.short_title: The Sind Professions, Trades, Callings and Employment Tax Rules, 1976
repeals: The West Pakistan Profession and Trade Tax Rules, 1965
metadata.administering_body: Excise and Taxation Department, Government of Sind
metadata.one_line: These rules establish the framework for levying and collecting tax on professions, trades, callings, and employment in Sindh.
metadata.summary: The document lays down rules for the imposition and collection of tax on professions, trades, callings, and employment within the Province of Sindh. It outlines procedures for enrolling persons liable to tax, issuing assessee's cards, conducting inspections by authorized officers, and determining tax liability. The rules also specify mechanisms for demanding tax payment, imposing penalties for non-compliance, and recovering dues through coercive measures.

name: Sind Public Service Commission (Conditions of Service) Rules, 1981.

metadata.short_title: The Sind Public Service Commission (Conditions of Service) Rules, 1981
metadata.parent_law: The Sind Public Service Commission Ordinance, 1978
repeals: The Sind Public Service Commission (Conditions of Service) Rules, 1974
metadata.administering_body: Government of Sind Services and General Administration Department (Regulation Wing)
metadata.one_line: These rules define the conditions of service, pay, allowances, and benefits for the Chairman and Members of the Sindh Public Service Commission.
metadata.summary: These rules were framed by the Government of Sind under the powers of the Sind Public Service Commission Ordinance, 1978. They specify the short title, commencement date, and various conditions of service for the Chairman and Members of the Commission. The document details entitlements regarding pay, residential accommodation, staff cars, pension, provident fund subscriptions, leave, travelling allowances, and medical facilities. Additionally, it rescinds the previous rules from 1974.

name: Sind Re-inbursement of Medical Charges Rules, 1972.

metadata.short_title: The Sind Re-inbursement of Medical Charges Rules, 1972
metadata.parent_law: Discontinuance of Re-inbursement of Medical charges Ordinance, 1972 (XIII of 1972)
metadata.one_line: These rules govern medical treatment amenities and reimbursement for government servants in Sindh.
metadata.summary: These Rules were made by the Governor of Sind to regulate medical treatment entitlements for government servants and their families. They clarify that while free medical treatment continues, reimbursement for purchasing medicines is discontinued. Authorized Medical Attendants are directed to provide medicines from hospitals or purchase them locally if unavailable, keeping separate accounts for these transactions.

name: Sind Regional Plan Organization Employees (General Conditions of Service) Rules, 1987.

metadata.short_title: Sind Regional Plan Organization Employees (General Conditions of Service) Rules, 1987
metadata.administering_body: Government of Sindh, Planning and Development Department
metadata.one_line: Rules governing general conditions of service, pay, allowances, and discipline for employees of the Sind Regional Plan Organization.
metadata.summary: These rules establish the general conditions of service for employees of the Sind Regional Plan Organization. They define terms related to appointments, pay scales, allowances, and specific types of posts such as tenure or temporary posts. The document outlines procedures for initial pay fixation, promotion transfers, leave preparatory to retirement, and disciplinary appeals within the organization.

name: Sind Road Transport Corporation (General Conditions of Service) Rules. 1986.

metadata.short_title: The Sind Road Transport Corporation (General Conditions of Service) Rules, 1986
repeals: all rules made in that behalf
metadata.one_line: Rules governing the general conditions of service, pay, allowances, and retirement for employees of the Sind Road Transport Corporation.
metadata.summary: These rules establish the general conditions of service for all employees of the Sind Road Transport Corporation. They define key terms such as 'employee', 'pay', and 'cadre', and classify staff into categories like executives, officers, workers, and security personnel. The document outlines provisions regarding pay scales, allowances, retirement age, re-employment, and various terms and conditions of service including suspension and termination.

name: Sind Standard Weights and Measures Enforcement Rules 1976.

metadata.short_title: Sind Standard Weights and Measures Enforcement Rules 1976
metadata.parent_law: Sindh Standard Weights and Measures Enforcement Act, 1975
metadata.administering_body: Controller of Weights and Measures, Government of Sindh
metadata.one_line: Rules made by the Government of Sindh to enforce standards for weights and measures in trade.
metadata.summary: These rules were made under the Sind Standard Weights and Measures Enforcement Act, 1975, to establish working and secondary standards for weights and measures. They specify requirements for commercial weighing instruments, limits of error, verification procedures, and security deposits for manufacturers and inspectors. The rules apply throughout the Province of Sindh and cover various classes of traders and specific types of scales.

name: SIND TEXTBOOK BOARD EMPLOYEES (EFFICIENCY AND DISCIPLINE)RULES, 1977.

metadata.short_title: The Sind Textbook Board Employees (Efficiency and Discipline) Rules, 1977
metadata.parent_law: Sind Textbook Board Ordinance, 1970 (Sind Ordinance No. XII of 1970)
repeals: the efficiency and discipline rules in force here before
metadata.one_line: Rules governing efficiency and discipline, penalties, inquiries, and appeals for employees of the Sind Textbook Board.
metadata.summary: These rules establish the framework for imposing penalties on employees of the Sind Textbook Board due to inefficiency, misconduct, corruption, or subversive activities. They define key terms such as 'accused' and 'misconduct', outline minor and major penalties including dismissal, and prescribe procedures for inquiries and appeals. The rules also address specific scenarios involving lent employees and clarify that previous efficiency and discipline rules are repealed.

metadata.short_title: The Sind University Employees Pension Statutes
metadata.administering_body: Education Department, Government of Sindh (via the Syndicate)
metadata.one_line: Statutes governing pension and gratuity for employees of the University of Sind.
metadata.summary: These Statutes establish a pension scheme for current and former employees of the University of Sind who opt into the plan rather than the Provident Fund. The document defines eligibility, exclusion criteria, and procedures for claiming pensions or gratuities upon retirement or death. It outlines the powers of the Syndicate regarding conduct, recovery of funds due to negligence, and medical examinations for commutation.

name: Sind Wildlife Management Board Financial Rules 1972.

metadata.short_title: The Sind Wildlife Management Board Financial Rules, 1972
metadata.parent_law: The Sind Wildlife Protection Ordinance, 1972 (Sind Ordinance V of 1972)
metadata.one_line: These rules establish financial management procedures for the Sind Wildlife Management Board under the 1972 Ordinance.
metadata.summary: The Sind Wildlife Management Board Financial Rules, 1972 were made by the Governor of Sind to regulate the financial administration of the Board. The rules define the composition of the Board Fund, which includes government grants, loans, fees, fines, and donations. They outline procedures for imposing entry fees, maintaining accounts, submitting annual budgets, and conducting quarterly audits by the External Audit Party.

name: SIND ZAKAT AND USHR COMMITTEES (PROCEDURE) RULES, 1980.

metadata.short_title: The Sind Zakat and Ushr Committees (Procedure) Rules, 1980
metadata.one_line: Rules regulating the proceedings of District, Taluka, Sub-divisional and Local Zakat and Ushr Committees in Sindh.
metadata.summary: These rules regulate the proceedings of various Zakat and Ushr Committees within the province of Sind. They define key terms such as Chairman, Committee, meeting, and Member, and establish requirements for committee seats, language of proceedings, and meeting frequencies. The document outlines procedures for convening meetings, maintaining quorum, conducting votes, recording minutes, and managing conflicts of interest regarding Zakat-aided institutions.

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Auqaf (Employees Pension) Rules, 1990
metadata.administering_body: Government of Sindh, Zakat, Ushr, Religious Affairs Social Welfare & Auqaf Deptt.
metadata.one_line: These rules establish the pension fund and grant mechanisms for employees of the Sindh Waqf Properties Ordinance, 1979.
metadata.summary: The Sindh Auqaf (Employees Pension) Rules, 1990 were made by the Government of Sindh under the powers of the Sindh Waqf Properties Ordinance, 1979. These rules came into force on July 1, 1989, replacing the Contributory Provident Fund with a new Employee's Pension Fund for eligible employees. The document outlines various types of pensions including superannuation, retiring, invalid, compassionate, and family pensions, along with the calculation methods and medical certification requirements.

name: SINDH GOVERNMENT LAND (CANCELLATION OF ALLOTMENTS, CONVERSIONS, EXCHANGES) RULES, 2003

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Govt. Land (Cancellation of Allotments Conversions Exchanges), Rules, 2003
metadata.parent_law: The Sindh Government Land (Cancellation of Allotments Conversions, Exchange) Ordinance, 2001
metadata.administering_body: Land Utilization Department, Government of Sindh
metadata.one_line: Rules made by the Government of Sindh regarding cancellation, conversions, and exchanges of government land.
metadata.summary: These rules were made under the powers of the Sindh Government Land (Cancellation of Allotments Conversions, Exchange) Ordinance, 2001. They establish a Committee to determine market prices for land transactions and calculate losses associated with cancellations or conversions. The rules outline procedures for paying determined losses in lump sums or installments and provide mechanisms for the resumption of land if payments are not made or rules are breached.

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Juvenile Justice Rules, 2002
metadata.territorial_extent: the whole of the Province of Sindh
metadata.one_line: Rules governing the establishment, management, and treatment of juveniles in borstal institutions in Sindh.
metadata.summary: These rules establish the framework for juvenile justice within the Province of Sindh, specifically focusing on borstal institutions. They mandate the provision of legal assistance, medical care, education, and moral training for child offenders admitted to these facilities. The document also outlines specific protocols for female inmates, dietary requirements, discipline, and procedures for production before courts.

name: SINDH REGULATION AND CONTROL (USE OF PLOTS AND CONSTRCUTION OF BUILDINGS) RULES , 2002..

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Regulation and Control (Use of Plots and Construction of Buildings) Rules, 2002
metadata.parent_law: The Sindh Regulation and Control (Use of plots and Construction of Buildings Ordinance, 2002)
metadata.administering_body: Housing & Town Planning Department, Government of Sindh
metadata.one_line: Rules made by the Government of Sindh to regulate plot usage and building construction fees under a specific Ordinance.
metadata.summary: These rules were made by the Government of Sindh in exercise of powers conferred by section 6 of the Sindh Regulation and Control (Use of plots and Construction of Buildings Ordinance, 2002). They define key terms such as 'competent authority' and 'owner', and establish fee structures for converting residential plots to commercial or industrial use based on valuation categories. The rules also provide mechanisms for regularizing buildings constructed in violation of the Sindh Building Control Ordinance, 1979, upon payment of enhanced composition fees and obtaining a structural stability certificate.

metadata.short_title: The Sindh (Fiscal Transfer) Rules, 2004
key_definitions: annual finance account of Local Government
metadata.one_line: These rules govern fiscal transfers, accounting, and financial management for Local Governments in Sindh.
metadata.summary: The Sindh (Fiscal Transfer) Rules, 2004 were made by the Governor of Sindh under the powers of the Sindh Local Government Ordinance, 2001. They establish definitions for financial terms such as 'appropriation', 'accounts', and 'Provincial Consolidated Fund' relevant to local governments in the province. The rules outline procedures for submitting reports, maintaining accounts, and managing cash balances for local authorities. Additionally, they provide a framework for forms used to notify fund distributions and certify receipts by banking institutions.

name: Sindh and Punjab Judicial Services Rules, 1994

metadata.short_title: Sindh Judicial Service Rules, 1994
repeals: West Pakistan Civil Service (Judicial Branch) Rules, 1962
notification No.CI-14-2/76 dated 28th September, 1976
metadata.one_line: Regulates recruitment and conditions of service for the Sindh Judicial Service.
metadata.summary: These rules regulate the recruitment to the Sindh Judicial Service and prescribe the conditions of service for appointed persons. They define key terms such as 'Service' and 'Provincial Selection Board', and establish age limits and educational qualifications for initial appointments at various grades. The rules also cover promotion procedures, probation periods, liability to transfer, and the authority of the Chief Minister to relax rules in cases of hardship.

name: Sindh Boiler Attendants and Boiler Engineers Rules, 1989.

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Boiler Attendants and Boiler Engineers Rules, 1989
repeals: all other rules on the subject
establishes: Sindh Board of Boiler (Competency Certificate) Examiners
metadata.administering_body: Government of Sindh, Industries & Mineral Development Department
metadata.one_line: These rules establish competency certificates for boiler attendants and engineers in Sindh under the Boilers Act, 1923.
metadata.summary: The Sindh Boiler Attendants and Boiler Engineers Rules, 1989 were made by the Government of Sindh to regulate the attendance and charge of boilers and steam pipes. They establish a Board of Examiners to grant competency certificates for different classes of attendants and engineers based on experience and examination results. The rules define specific capacities and conditions under which certified personnel may operate boilers, including relief provisions and distance restrictions between connected boilers.

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Censorship of Film Rules, 2014
repeals: Censorship of Films Rules, 1980
metadata.one_line: Rules made by the Government of Sindh to regulate the censorship and certification of films for public exhibition.
metadata.summary: These rules establish the Sindh Board of Film Censors and define its powers regarding the examination and certification of films. They outline procedures for submitting applications, fees for different types of films, and the duties of film inspectors. The rules also provide mechanisms for appeals to the Government and the recall of certified films.

name: SINDH CIVIL SERVANTS HOUSING FOUNDATION, RULES, 2008

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Civil Servants Housing Foundation Rules, 2008
metadata.parent_law: The Sindh Civil Servants Housing Foundation Act, 2005
metadata.administering_body: Government of Sindh, Services, General Administration and Coordination Department (Regulation Wing)
metadata.one_line: Rules made by the Government of Sindh to regulate the membership, contributions, and housing allocation for civil servants under the Sindh Civil Servants Housing Foundation.
metadata.summary: These rules were made by the Government of Sindh in exercise of powers conferred by the Sindh Civil Servants Housing Foundation Act, 2005. They define eligibility criteria for civil servants to become members, establish contribution rates based on pay bands, and outline procedures for membership termination and allocation cancellation. The document also sets conditions regarding the maintenance of residential and commercial units, restrictions on land use conversion, and access to public records.

metadata.short_title: The Sind Council (Budget) Rules, 1985
metadata.one_line: These rules prescribe the format and procedure for preparing budget estimates, demands for grants, and financial schedules for Sindh Councils.
metadata.summary: The Sind Council (Budget) Rules, 1985 were made by the Government of Sind under the powers of the Sind Local Government Ordinance, 1979. They establish the structure for two volumes of the budget, detailing estimates of revenue and expenditure, demands for grants, and various financial schedules. The rules define key terms such as 'Appropriation' and 'Department', mandate specific forms for financial data, and outline procedures for handling unspent balances and financial irregularities.

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Council (Conduct of Business) Rules, 2016
metadata.one_line: Rules made by the Government of Sindh to regulate the conduct of business in local councils.
metadata.summary: These rules were made under the powers of the Sindh Local Government Act, 2013 to govern the meetings, agendas, and quorum requirements of local councils. They define key terms such as 'business', 'motion', and 'Presiding Officer' applicable to council proceedings. The rules also outline the functions of various committees established by the Council, covering areas from education to legal affairs.

name: SINDH COUNCILS (IMPOSITION, ASSESSMENT, COLLECTION AND ADMINISTRATION OF TAXES, RATES, TOLL AND FEES) RULES, 2016

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Councils (Imposition, Assessment, Collection and Administration of Taxes, Rates, Toll and Fees) Rules, 2016
metadata.administering_body: Local Government and Housing Town Planning Department, Government of Sindh
metadata.one_line: Rules made by the Government of Sindh to regulate the imposition, assessment, collection, and administration of taxes by local councils.
metadata.summary: These rules empower local councils in Sindh to formulate taxation proposals for the imposition or modification of taxes, rates, tolls, and fees. The process requires publishing a notice inviting objections, holding public hearings before the Finance Committee, and obtaining Government sanction. Rules define key terms like 'inhabitant' and outline the procedural steps from proposal formulation to final notification.

name: Sindh Councils Unified Grade Service Departmental Examination & Training Rules, 1996.

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Councils Unified Grade Service Departmental Examination & Training Rules, 1996
metadata.parent_law: The Sindh Local Government Ordinance, 1970; The Sindh Council Unified Grades Service Rules, 1982
amends: The Sindh Councils Unified Grade Service Departmental Examination & Training Rules, 1994
metadata.administering_body: Sindh Local Government, Public Health, Engineering, Rural Development and Katchi Abadis Department
metadata.one_line: These rules prescribe departmental examinations and training for members of the Sindh Councils Unified Grades Service.
metadata.summary: The Government of Sindh made these rules to regulate departmental examinations and training for members of the Sindh Councils Unified Grades Service. The rules define key terms such as 'Academy', 'Examination', and 'Training' and mandate that appointed members take specific exams and undergo training as directed by the appointing authority with Government approval. The syllabus includes subjects like Primary Health Care Services, Water & Environmental issues, and duties of Municipal Health Officers.

name: Sindh Development and Maintenance of Infrastructure [Cess] Rules, 1994

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Development and Maintenance of Infrastructure [Cess] Rules, 1994
metadata.max_penalty: equal to the amount of fee evaded
metadata.administering_body: Excise and Taxation Department, Government of Sindh
metadata.one_line: Rules made by the Government of Sindh to levy a cess on goods entering or leaving the province for infrastructure maintenance.
metadata.summary: These rules empower the Government of Sindh to impose a cess on moveable goods entering or leaving the province via air, land, or sea. The rules define key terms such as 'goods', 'owner', and 'Director', establish procedures for declaring goods and paying the cess, and outline penalties for non-payment. They also provide mechanisms for appeals, revisions by the Director General, refunds of excess payments, and specific exemptions for government goods and foreign aid.

name: SINDH DISTRICT GOVERNMENTS (CONDUCT OF BUSINESS) RULES, 2001

metadata.short_title: The Sindh District Governments (Conduct of Business) Rules, 2001
metadata.administering_body: Local Government, Rural Development and Katchi Abadis Department
metadata.one_line: These rules allocate business and define functions for district officers in Sindh under the Local Government Ordinance, 2001.
metadata.summary: The Sindh District Governments (Conduct of Business) Rules, 2001 were made by the Governor of Sindh to regulate the conduct of business in district administrations. They define key terms such as 'District', 'Zila Nazim', and 'Executive District Officer' and outline their respective functions and powers. The rules distribute business among groups of offices and establish procedures for consultation, financial approval, and information submission to the Zila Nazim.

name: Sindh Education Foundation (Grant of Loans and lease of land) Rules, 1993.

metadata.short_title: Sindh Education Foundation (Grant of Loans and lease of land) Rules, 1993
metadata.one_line: Rules made by the Government of Sindh to regulate grants, loans, and land leases for educational institutions run by NGOs.
metadata.summary: These rules empower the Sindh Education Foundation to provide financial assistance in the form of grants-in-aid, loans, or land leases to non-governmental organizations (NGOs) for establishing and running educational institutions. The document outlines strict eligibility criteria, including mandatory registration under relevant ordinances, ideological alignment of staff, minimum student enrollment numbers, and adherence to prescribed fee scales and building standards. It further details the procedural requirements for applying for assistance, the conditions attached to land leases (such as a maximum 99-year term), and the obligations regarding construction timelines and maintenance of records.

metadata.short_title: Sindh Enquiries and Anti-Corruption Rules, 1993
repeals: West Pakistan Anti-Corruption Rules, 1965
metadata.administering_body: Government of Sindh, Services and General Administration Department (Regulation Wing)
metadata.one_line: These rules establish anti-corruption committees in Sindh to review misconduct cases and coordinate corruption eradication efforts.
metadata.summary: The Sindh Enquiries and Anti-Corruption Rules, 1993 were made by the Government of Sindh under the powers of the Sindh Enquiries and Anti-Corruption Act, 1991. They establish three levels of committees: Provincial, Divisional, and District Anti-Corruption Committees to review corruption cases and suggest measures for eradication. The rules define various authorities, grant specific powers to officers for investigations and seizures, and outline the jurisdiction and functions of these committees across the province.

name: SINDH ENVIRONMENTAL PROTECTION (COMPOSITION OF OFENCES AND PAYMENT OF AMDINISTRATIVE PENALTY) RULES, 2014.

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Environmental Protection (Composition of Offences and Payment of Administrative Penalty) Rules, 2014
repeals: Provincial Sustainable Development Fund Board (Procedure) Rules, 2001
Provincial Sustainable Development Fund (Utilization) Rules, 2001
metadata.one_line: Rules made by the Sindh Environment Protection Agency to prescribe procedures for compounding offences and paying administrative penalties in Sindh.
metadata.summary: These rules provide a framework for the Director General of the Sindh Environment Protection Agency to compound environmental offences and impose administrative penalties. They outline the process for accused persons to apply for compounding, the requirements for affidavits and applications, and the conditions under which complaints are withdrawn or trials proceed. The rules also establish forms for notices, registers for tracking applications and penalties, and repeal previous related rules applicable to Sindh.

name: SINDH ENVIRONMENTAL PROTECTION AGENCY (REVIEW OF INITIAL ENVIRONMENTAL EXAMINATION AND ENVIRONMENTAL IMPACT ASSESSMENT) REGULATIONS, 2014

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Environmental Protection Agency (Review of Initial Environmental Examination and Environmental Impact Assessment) Regulations, 2014
repeals: Pakistan Environmental Protection Agency Review of Initial Environmental Examination and Environmental Assessment Impact Regulations 2000
metadata.one_line: Regulates the review of Initial Environmental Examinations and Environmental Impact Assessments for projects in Sindh.
metadata.summary: These regulations establish the framework for the Sindh Environmental Protection Agency to review Initial Environmental Examinations (IEE) and Environmental Impact Assessments (EIA). They categorize projects requiring specific assessments, outline filing procedures including public participation, and set conditions for approval. The document also repeals earlier regulations applicable to the province of Sindh.

name: SINDH ENVIRONMENTAL PROTECTION AGENCY (REVIEW OF INITIAL ENVIRONMENTAL EXAMINATION AND ENVIRONMENTAL IMPACT ASSESSMENT) REGULATIONS, 2014.

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Environmental Protection Agency (Review of Initial Environmental Examination and Environmental Impact Assessment) Regulations, 2014
repeals: Pakistan Environmental Protection Agency Review of Initial Environmental Examination and Environmental Assessment Impact Regulations 2000
metadata.one_line: Regulates the review of initial environmental examinations and impact assessments for projects in Sindh.
metadata.summary: These regulations establish the framework for reviewing Initial Environmental Examinations (IEE) and Environmental Impact Assessments (EIA) for various projects in Sindh. They define specific categories of projects requiring IEE, EIA, or checklists, outline filing procedures, review fees, and public participation requirements. The regulations also create an Environmental Assessment Advisory Committee to assist in the review process and repeal previous 2000 regulations applicable to the province.

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Environmental Protection Tribunal Rules, 2014
repeals: Environmental Tribunal Rules, 1999
metadata.one_line: These rules establish the Sindh Environmental Protection Tribunal, defining its composition, staff, and procedures.
metadata.summary: The Sindh Environmental Protection Tribunal Rules, 2014 were made by the Governor of Sindh under the powers of the Sindh Environmental Protection Act, 2014. These rules define the short title, commencement, definitions, term of office, qualifications, salary, and functions of the Tribunal's Chairperson and Members. They also outline the staff structure, seal usage, language, application of criminal procedure code, cause lists, appeals process, public access to proceedings, service of process, and the repeal of the 1999 rules.

name: SINDH ENVIRONMENTAL QUALITY STANDARDS (CERTIFICATION OF ENVIRONMENTAL LABORATORIES) REGULATIONS, 2014.

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Environmental Quality Standards (Certification of Environmental Laboratories) Regulations, 2014
repeals: National Environmental Quality Standard (Certification of Environmental Laboratories) Regulations, 2000
metadata.one_line: Regulates the certification, functions, and criteria for environmental laboratories in Sindh.
metadata.summary: These regulations establish the framework for certifying environmental laboratories in the Province of Sindh. They define the specific functions of certified labs, including testing air, water, soil, and noise levels. The document outlines strict criteria for laboratory location, equipment, and staff qualifications required to obtain certification. It also details the application process, scrutiny procedures, fees, and the mechanism for appeals against agency decisions.

name: SINDH ENVIRONMENTAL QUALITY STANDARDS (SELF-MONITORING AND REPORTING BY INDUSTRY) RULES, 2014

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Environmental Quality Standards (Self-Monitoring and Reporting by Industry) Rules, 2014
repeals: National Environmental Quality Standard (Self-Monitoring and Report by Industry) Rules, 2001
metadata.one_line: These rules establish self-monitoring and reporting requirements for industrial units in Sindh regarding liquid effluents and gaseous emissions.
metadata.summary: These rules mandate that all industrial units in Sindh submit environmental monitoring reports to the Sindh Environmental Protection Agency. The rules classify industries into categories A, B, or C based on pollution levels, dictating the frequency of reporting (monthly, quarterly, or biannual) and specific parameters for liquid effluents and gaseous emissions. Industrial units must use certified environmental laboratories that are independent of the unit to conduct testing, while the Agency is responsible for compiling data and enforcing standards.

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Farmers Organizations Financial Regulations, 2004
metadata.one_line: These regulations govern the financial management, accounting, and expenditure powers of Farmers Organizations in Sindh.
metadata.summary: The Sindh Farmers Organizations Financial Regulations, 2004 establish a fund for Farmers Organizations (FOs) and define their composition, including member subscriptions and government grants. The document outlines strict procedures for bank account management, budget preparation, voucher usage, and receipt issuance. It further details the powers of the Board of Management and Treasurer regarding revenue expenditure, salaries, and consultancy contracts within approved budgets.

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Fisheries Rules, 1983
metadata.administering_body: Agriculture, Livestock & Fisheries Department, Government of Sindh
metadata.one_line: These rules regulate fishing licenses, permits, auctions, and penalties under the Sindh Fisheries Ordinance, 1980.
metadata.summary: The Sindh Fisheries Rules, 1983 were made by the Government of Sindh to regulate fishing operations within the province. They establish procedures for obtaining licenses and permits, define terms related to fish processing plants and licensing authorities, and set fees for various activities. The rules also cover the leasing of public water fishing rights through auction, restrictions on mesh sizes, and penalties for blocking navigational channels or violating conditions.

name: SINDH HIGH DENSITY DEVELOPMENT BOARD (RULES AND PROCEDURE), 2011

metadata.short_title: The Sindh High Density Development Board (Rules and Procedure), 2011
metadata.parent_law: The Sindh High Density Development Board Act, 2010
metadata.administering_body: Government of Sindh, Local Government Department
metadata.one_line: Rules and procedure for the Sindh High Density Development Board regarding building standards, land use, and development procedures.
metadata.summary: These rules were made by the Government of Sindh under the powers of The Sindh High Density Development Board Act, 2010. They establish specific standards for high density zones, including plot amalgamation, land use changes, recreational spaces, and building bulk standards like FAR and food print. The document also outlines mandatory conditions such as Environment Impact Assessments and fire fighting provisions, along with a detailed procedure for plan submission and scrutiny by the SBCA.

name: SINDH HUMAN RIGHTS COMMISSION (CHAIRPERSON AND MEMBERS) CONDITION OF SERVICE RULES, 2014.

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Human Rights Commission (Chairperson and Members) Condition of Service Rules, 2014
metadata.parent_law: The Sindh Protection of Human Rights Act, 2011
metadata.administering_body: Government of Sindh Law, Parliamentary Affairs and Human Rights Department
metadata.one_line: These rules specify the pay, allowances, leave, medical facilities, and conditions of service for the Chairperson and Members of the Sindh Human Rights Commission.
metadata.summary: The document establishes the conditions of service for the Chairperson and Members of the Sindh Human Rights Commission. It details their entitlements regarding pay, allowances, housing, utilities, and official car usage based on their status as full-time or honorary members. The rules also outline provisions for leave, medical attendance, and pension eligibility, referencing existing civil servant regulations.

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Human Rights Commission Rules, 2013
metadata.parent_law: The Sindh Protection of Human Rights Act, 2011
metadata.administering_body: Law, Parliamentary Affairs and Human Rights Department
metadata.one_line: Rules made by the Government of Sindh to regulate the conduct of business of the Sindh Human Rights Commission.
metadata.summary: These rules were made under the powers of the Sindh Protection of Human Rights Act, 2011, to regulate the conduct of business for the Sindh Human Rights Commission. They define key terms such as 'Commission', 'Chairperson', and 'human rights', and establish the headquarters at Karachi with potential district offices. The document outlines procedures for meetings, agendas, notice periods, and the disposal of petitions, applications, and suo-moto actions.

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Institute of Animal Health (Conduct) Rules, 2021
metadata.parent_law: The Sindh Institute of Animal Health at Karachi Act, 2017 (Sindh Act No.XXIX of 2018)
key_definitions: Government (deemed to be Sindh Institute of Animal Health)
Civil Servants (deemed to be employees of the Institute)
Secretary to Government/Administrative Secretary (deemed to be Chairman of the Board)
Head of Department (deemed to be Director General)
Non-gazetted Government Servant (deemed to be employee in grade 16 or below)
Gazetted Government Servant (deemed to be employee in grade 16 or above)
metadata.one_line: Applies Sindh Civil Servants Conduct Rules, 2008 mutatis mutandis to Institute employees with specific modifications.
metadata.summary: This notification applies the Sindh Civil Servants (Conduct) Rules, 2008 to all employees of the Sindh Institute of Animal Health. It directs that references in those rules to 'Government' are deemed to refer to the Institute, and references to 'Civil Servants' refer to Institute employees. Specific modifications redefine roles such as the Secretary to Government as the Chairman of the Board and the Head of Department as the Director General.

name: SINDH INSTITUTE OF ANIMAL HEALTH EMPLOYEES (APPOINTMENT, PROMOTION & TRANSFER) RULES, 2020

metadata.summary: These rules govern the appointment, promotion, and transfer of employees at the Sindh Institute of Animal Health at Karachi. They define various terms such as 'cadre', 'appointing authority', and 'Selection Committee'. The rules specify methods for initial appointments based on interviews or tests, qualifications required, age limits, and nationality requirements. Appointments are made by different authorities depending on the basic pay scale of the post.

name: SINDH INSTITUTE OF ANIMAL HEALTH EMPLOYEES (GENERAL CONDITIONS OF SERVICE) RULES, 2021

metadata.short_title: Sindh Institute of Animal Health Employees (General Conditions of Service) Rules, 2021
