metadata.administering_body: The Board of the Sindh Institute of Animal Health at Karachi
metadata.one_line: These rules establish general conditions of service, pay scales, leave, and disciplinary procedures for employees of the Sindh Institute of Animal Health.
metadata.summary: These rules govern the general conditions of service for employees of the Sindh Institute of Animal Health at Karachi. They define key employment terms such as 'cadre', 'pay scale', and 'deputation' and establish the authority responsible for appointments and pay fixation. The document outlines entitlements to allowances, procedures for promotion, reduction in rank, leave, retirement, resignation, and the process for appealing service-related orders.

name: SINDH INSTITUTE OF ANIMAL HEALTH EMPLOYEES (PROBATION, CONFIRMATION & SENIORITY) RULES, 2020

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Institute of Animal Health Employees (Probation, Confirmation and Seniority) Rules, 2020
metadata.territorial_extent: The Institute wherever they may be
metadata.parent_law: The Sindh Institute of Animal Health at Karachi Act, 2017 (Sindh Act No.XXIX of 2018)
metadata.administering_body: The Sindh Institute of Animal Health at Karachi
metadata.one_line: Rules governing probation, confirmation, and seniority for employees of the Sindh Institute of Animal Health.
metadata.summary: These rules establish the framework for the probation, confirmation, and seniority of employees at the Sindh Institute of Animal Health. They define key terms such as 'employee', 'confirmation', and 'lien' regarding permanent posts. The document outlines procedures for handling unsatisfactory conduct during probation, eligibility for confirmation in specific posts, and the preparation of seniority lists.

name: SINDH IRRIGATION & DRAINAGE FINANCIAL REGULAITONS AND POWERS, 2003.

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Irrigation & Drainage Authority Financial Regulations and Powers, 2003
metadata.one_line: These regulations establish the SIDA, define its powers, duties, financial rules, and accounting policies for irrigation and drainage in Sindh.
metadata.summary: This document establishes the Sindh Irrigation & Drainage Authority (SIDA) as a body corporate with perpetual succession. It outlines the Authority's general powers to operate irrigation and drainage systems, maintain infrastructure, levy service fees, and advise the Government on water management strategies. The regulations also detail financial procedures including budgeting, accounting conventions, fund re-appropriation, and the constitution of the SIDA Finance Committee.

metadata.short_title: The Sind Land Reforms Rules, 1972
metadata.territorial_extent: the whole of the Province of Sind
amends: Sind Land Reforms Rules, 1972 published with the Sind Land Commission Notification No. SLC-1/72/15, dated the 25th March, 1972
metadata.one_line: Rules made by the Sind Land Commission to implement the Land Reforms Regulation, 1972 in Sindh.
metadata.summary: These Rules were made by the Sind Land Commission under the powers of the Land Reforms Regulation, 1972. They define key terms such as 'Chief Land Commissioner' and 'Officer', and establish the territorial extent covering the whole of the Province of Sind. The document outlines the powers of the Chief Land Commissioner regarding case transfers, inquiries, and appeals, while also defining the procedural powers of land officers acting as civil courts.

name: SINDH LOCAL COUNCIL SERVANTS (MEDICAL ATTENDANT) RULES, 2017.

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Local Council Servants (Medical Attendent) Rules, 2017
metadata.administering_body: Local Government and Housing Town Planning Department, Government of Sindh
metadata.one_line: These rules provide free medical treatment and reimbursement for servants of Local Councils in Sindh.
metadata.summary: The Sindh Local Council Servants (Medical Attendent) Rules, 2017 were made by the Government of Sindh under the powers of the Sindh Local Government Act, 2013. These rules apply to all servants of Local Councils, Members of the Sindh Councils Unified Grades Service, and Employees of the Sindh Local Government Board. They establish entitlement to free medical attendance for a servant and their family, including reimbursement for any amounts paid in advance upon verification. The rules define various terms such as 'authorised medical attendant', 'hospital', and 'treatment', and specify the scope of dental treatment covered.

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Local Councils (Election) Rules, 2013
repeals: Notification of even number dated 1st November-2013
metadata.administering_body: Government of Sindh, Local Government, Rural Development, Public Health Engineering and Housing Town Planning Department
metadata.one_line: Rules governing the conduct of elections to local councils in Sindh under the Sindh Local Government Act, 2013.
metadata.summary: These rules prescribe the procedures for conducting elections to local councils, including delimitation, nomination, scrutiny, polling, and declaration of results. They define key terms such as 'candidate' and 'elector', establish the powers of the Election Commission and Returning Officers, and outline the process for handling election petitions and expenses. The rules apply to the whole of Sindh and come into force immediately upon notification.

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Local Councils (Election) Rules, 2015
repeals: Notification of even number dated 27th November, 2013
metadata.one_line: Rules made by the Government of Sindh to regulate local council elections under the Sindh Local Government Act, 2013.
metadata.summary: These rules are made in exercise of powers under the Sindh Local Government Act, 2013 to regulate local council elections. They define key terms like candidate and election commission, establish the organization of elections by the Election Commission, and provide for the delimitation of electoral units. The rules also outline procedures for polling stations, personnel designation, and the submission of election returns.

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Local Councils (Property) Rules, 2017
metadata.administering_body: Local Government and Housing Town Planning Department
metadata.one_line: Rules made by the Government of Sindh to regulate the management, maintenance, and disposal of property vested in local councils.
metadata.summary: These rules are made under the Sindh Local Government Act, 2013 to govern the management and maintenance of property vested in local councils. They define key terms like 'property' and 'Officer Incharge', assigning responsibilities for repairs, rent collection, and preventing encroachments to the Mayor, Chairman, or Officer Incharge. The rules also cover procedures for writing off unserviceable articles, acquiring new property, maintaining registers and maps, and managing financial estimates and grants.

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Local Councils Employees (Service Rules), 2017
metadata.territorial_extent: all employees of the Council wherever they may be
metadata.administering_body: Government of Sindh, Local Government and Housing Town Planning Department
metadata.one_line: These rules govern the service conditions, appointments, promotions, and transfers for employees of Local Councils in Sindh.
metadata.summary: The Sindh Local Councils Employees (Service Rules), 2017 establish a service framework for all employees of Local Councils in Sindh. The rules define key terms such as 'cadre', 'pay scale', and 'appointing authority' to regulate recruitment, promotion, and transfer processes. Appointments are made by the Council or the Public Service Commission depending on the pay scale, subject to government approval. The document also outlines provisions for probation, retirement age, and relaxation of rules in individual cases where hardship is proven.

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Local Government (Election Authority) Rules, 2004
metadata.administering_body: Local Government Department, Government of Sindh
metadata.one_line: These rules establish the Election Authority and procedures for recall motions in Sindh local government elections.
metadata.summary: The Sindh Local Government (Election Authority) Rules, 2004 were made by the Government of Sindh under the powers of the Sindh Local Government Ordinance, 2001. These rules establish an Election Authority consisting of a Chairman and members to oversee local government elections in Sindh. The document outlines the appointment, terms, and functions of the Authority, including its role in managing recall motions for various Nazims and Naib Nazims. It also details procedures for ballot supply, public inspection of documents, and the consolidation of election results.

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Local Government (Property) Rules, 2001
metadata.administering_body: Local Government, Rural Development and Katchi Abadis Department
metadata.one_line: Rules governing the vesting, management, maintenance, acquisition, and alienation of property by Local Governments in Sindh.
metadata.summary: These rules provide a framework for Local Governments in Sindh to manage and maintain their property assets effectively. They cover the registration and verification of both movable and immovable property, including the maintenance of maps and plans. The document also outlines procedures for acquiring new property, disposing of unserviceable items, and ensuring that public property is used only for official purposes.

name: SINDH LOCAL GOVERNMENT (TALUKA,TOWN MUNICIPAL ADMINISTRATION,UNION ADMINISTRATION) RULES, 2001.

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Local Government (Taluka / Town Municipal Administration / Union Administration) Rules, 2001
repeals: Sindh Local Councils (Delegation of Financial and Administrative Powers) Rules, 1980
metadata.administering_body: Local Government, Rural Development and Katchi Abadis Department
metadata.one_line: These rules define the executive powers of Nazims and TMOs in Sindh local government bodies.
metadata.summary: The Sindh Local Government (Taluka / Town Municipal Administration / Union Administration) Rules, 2001 were made by the Government of Sindh under the Sindh Local Government Ordinance, 2001. They outline the executive powers of the Nazim regarding appointments and penalties for staff in Taluka, Town Municipal, and Union Administrations. The rules also specify the administrative powers of the Town Municipal Officer (TMO) and Town Officers (TOs), subject to the overall control of the Nazim. Finally, these rules repeal the Sindh Local Councils (Delegation of Financial and Administrative Powers) Rules, 1980.

name: SINDH MARKET COMMITEE UNIFIED GRADE SERVICE EMPLOYEES EFFICIENCY AND DISCIPLINE RULES 1983.

metadata.summary: These rules establish the framework for maintaining efficiency and discipline among members of the Sindh Market Committees Unified Grade Service. They define key terms such as misconduct and corruption, outline grounds for imposing minor and major penalties including dismissal, and prescribe the procedure for inquiries and appeals to the Government.

name: SINDH MARKET COMMITTEE UNIFIED GRADE EMPLOYEES LEAVE RULES 1986.

metadata.short_title: Sindh Market Committees Unified Grade Leave Rules, 1986
metadata.administering_body: Bureau of Supply and Prices, Sindh
metadata.one_line: Rules governing leave entitlements, calculations, and procedures for unified grade employees of Sindh Market Committees.
metadata.summary: These rules establish the framework for earned leave for employees of Sindh Market Committees. They define how leave is calculated based on duty rendered, the maximum periods allowed with or without medical certificates, and procedures for applying for leave. The rules also cover specific scenarios such as leave ex-Pakistan, conversion of full pay to half pay leave, and the maintenance of leave accounts.

name: SINDH MARKET COMMITTEE NON-UNIFIED GRADE LEAVE BYE-LAWS, 1989.

metadata.short_title: Sindh Market Committee Non-unified Grade Leave Bye-laws, 1989
metadata.one_line: These bye-laws regulate leave entitlements, calculations, and procedures for employees of Sindh Market Committees.
metadata.summary: The Sindh Market Committee Non-unified Grade Leave Bye-laws, 1989, were made under the Agricultural Produce Market Act, 1939 to govern leave for all employees of Sindh Market Committees. The document defines various types of leave, including earned leave, leave on full pay, and leave preparatory to retirement, along with specific calculation rates and limits. It outlines procedures for applying for leave, converting leave types, granting leave ex-Pakistan, and handling leave accounts upon joining or quitting service.

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Mental Health Rules, 2014
metadata.one_line: These rules establish the Sindh Mental Health Authority and procedures for licensing psychiatric facilities and patient care.
metadata.summary: The Sindh Mental Health Rules, 2014 were made by the Government of Sindh under the powers of the Sindh Mental Health Act, 2013. They constitute the Sindh Mental Health Authority and define its composition, meeting procedures, and quorum requirements. The rules also outline the process for applying for and renewing licenses to operate psychiatric facilities, including specific conditions and fees. Additionally, they provide forms and guidelines for the admission, detention, and treatment of patients in mental health institutions.

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Mental Health Rules, 2014
metadata.one_line: These rules establish the Sindh Mental Health Authority and regulate licensing, meetings, and patient care procedures.
metadata.summary: The Sindh Mental Health Rules, 2014 were made by the Government of Sindh under the powers of the Sindh Mental Health Act, 2013. They constitute the Sindh Mental Health Authority, define key terms like 'applicant' and 'licensee', and prescribe procedures for holding meetings and granting licenses for psychiatric facilities. The rules also outline requirements for the admission, care, and detention of patients, including specific forms for medical opinions on mental disorders.

name: SINDH POULTRY VACCINE CENTRE (EFFICIENCY AND DISCIPLINARY) REGULATION 1997.

metadata.one_line: Regulations governing efficiency, discipline, penalties, and inquiry procedures for employees of the Sindh Poultry Vaccine Centre.
metadata.summary: These regulations establish the framework for maintaining efficiency and discipline among employees of the Sindh Poultry Vaccine Centre. They define key terms such as 'employee', 'misconduct', and 'authority' and outline grounds for imposing penalties ranging from minor censure to major dismissal. The document details the procedure for initiating action, conducting inquiries, handling appeals or reviews, and ensuring the correctness of findings.

The fund consists of contributions from employees and the Centre, along with interest earned, and is administered by a Committee. It outlines contribution rates based on Basic Pay Scale (BPS), procedures for nominations upon death, and the utilization of funds for insurance premia and administration.

name: SINDH POULTRY VACCINE CENTRE (PROBATION, CONFIRMATION AND SENIORITY) REGULATION 1997.

The rules establish specific periods for probation, procedures for confirmation in permanent posts, and criteria for determining seniority among employees based on appointment type, age, and transfer status.

name: SINDH POULTRY VACCINE CENTRE (APPOINTMENT, PROMOTION AND TRANSFER) REGULATION 1997.

It defines various terms related to employment status and establishes the roles of different authorities based on pay scales. The rules specify requirements regarding qualifications, age limits, nationality, and domicile for initial appointments.

name: SINDH PREVENTION AND CONTROL OF DENGUE TEMPORARY REGULATIONS, 2013

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Prevention and Control of Dengue (Temporary) Regulations, 2013

metadata.one_line: Temporary regulations for preventing and controlling dengue by mandating mosquito breeding prevention measures in Sindh.
metadata.summary: These temporary regulations empower the Government of Sindh to prescribe measures for the prevention and control of dengue fever. They impose specific duties on owners and occupiers regarding waste disposal, water management, and vegetation removal to prevent mosquito breeding. The regulations also grant Health Inspectors powers to direct spraying, issue notices for repairs or drainage, and conduct inspections, with penalties for non-compliance.

name: SINDH PROHIBITION OF NON-DEGRADABLE PLASTIC PRODUCTS (MANUFACTURING, SALE AND USAGE) RULES 2014.

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Prohibition of Non-degradable Plastic Products (Manufacturing, Sale and Usage) Rules, 2014
metadata.one_line: Rules prohibiting non-degradable plastics and mandating registration for oxo-biodegradable alternatives in Sindh.
metadata.summary: These rules prohibit the manufacturing, sale, and usage of non-degradable plastic products within Sindh. They mandate the registration of manufacturers, wholesalers, and retailers dealing with oxo-biodegradable products and pro-degradant additives with the Sindh Environmental Protection Agency. The rules specify identification requirements for compliant products, outline the powers of authorized officers for inspection and investigation, and list specific scheduled plastic products covered by the prohibition.

metadata.short_title: The Sind Property (Vacant Plots) Tax Rules, 1976

metadata.summary: These rules empower the District Excise and Taxation Officer to prepare lists of vacant plots within their jurisdiction for taxation purposes. The Assessing Authority is responsible for ascertaining ownership details, issuing public notices, collecting information, and examining documents related to these plots. The rules specify payment deadlines, procedures for issuing demand notices, penalties for non-payment, and mechanisms for refunds or remissions if a plot is no longer vacant due to construction or transfer.

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Public Security Rules, 1999

metadata.one_line: Rules for appointing village watchmen, establishing neighborhood security committees, and registering domestic servants in Sindh.
metadata.summary: These rules empower the Deputy Commissioner to appoint Village Watchmen and establish Mohallah Muhafiz Committees to maintain local security. They define the functions of these bodies, including keeping watch, preventing offenses, and reporting suspicious activities to police authorities. The rules also provide for the formation of Neighborhood Care Associations and mandate the registration of domestic servants through specific forms.

name: SINDH PUBLIC SERVICE COMMISSION (CONDITION OF SERVICE) RULES, 2002

metadata.summary: The Sindh Public Service Commission (Condition of Service) Rules, 2002 were made by the Governor of Sindh under the powers of the Sindh Public Service Commission Act, 1989. These rules come into force immediately and define the short title, allowances, pension, leave, and medical facilities for the Chairman and Members of the Commission. The rules also specify salary details in the Schedule and repeal the previous 1981 rules.

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Public Service Commission (Functions) Rules, 1990

They specify which posts require Commission-conducted tests, including written examinations, interviews, and viva voce. The rules also outline the constitution of committees, the obligation to consult the Commission, and procedures for handling advice from the Commission regarding appointments.

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Remand Home Rules, 2011

metadata.summary: These rules establish the framework for declaring and operating Remand Homes in the Province of Sindh for the custody and care of children. They define the roles of superintendents and in-charges, mandate medical examinations and hygiene standards, and ensure separate facilities for female inmates. The document also outlines procedures for admission, discharge, meeting with legal advisers, and prohibits corporal punishment or stigmatization.

name: SINDH SERVICE TRIBUNAL (CHAIRMAN AND MEMBERS) CONDITION OF SERVICE RULES, 1985

The provisions align these benefits with those admissible to a Judge of the High Court or a Secretary to Government, as applicable.

name: SINDH SERVICE TRIBUNAL ESTABLISHMENT ( APPOINTMENT, PROMOTION AND CONDITIONS OF SERVICE) RULES, 2015

It defines various committees responsible for selection and promotion, sets probation periods, and outlines vacation entitlements. metadata.short_title: The Sindh Service Tribunals (Procedure) Rules, 1974

They define the roles of the Registrar and Tribunal members, specify office hours and holidays, and outline requirements for presenting appeals and serving notices. The rules also cover the admission of appeals, preliminary hearings, costs, and the composition of full benches for decision-making.

name: SINDH SUSTAINABLE DEVELOPMENT FUND (PROCEDURE AND UTILIZATION) RULES, 2014.

metadata.summary: These rules establish the procedural framework for the Sindh Sustainable Development Fund, including the constitution and functioning of its Board and Committees. They outline the process for filing and appraising project proposals related to environmental improvement and institutional strengthening. name: SINDH TECHNICAL EDUCATION AND VOCATIONAL TRAINING AUTHORITY EMPLOYEES (APPOINTMENT, PROMOTION AND TRANSFER) RULES, 2012

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Workers Compensation Rules, 2020

name: SINDH, LOCAL GOVERNMENT (LOCAL FUND BUDGET) Rules 2001

metadata.one_line: These rules grant gratuity entitlements to Sindh Education Foundation employees upon resignation, termination, death, or superannuation.
metadata.summary: The Sindh Education Foundation (Employees Gratuity Rules) 2021 establish the framework for granting gratuity to employees of the Sindh Education Foundation. The rules define eligibility criteria based on years of service, specify conditions under which an employee can claim gratuity such as resignation or superannuation, and exclude entitlement in cases of misconduct. They also outline procedures for nominations, deductions for dues, appeals, and the constitution of a committee to manage assessments.

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Hazardous Occupations (Silicon) Rules, 2019
metadata.parent_law: The Sindh Factories Act, 2015 (Sindh Act No. XIII of 2016)
metadata.one_line: Rules made by the Government of Sindh under the Sindh Factories Act, 2015 to regulate hazardous silicon occupations.
metadata.summary: These rules apply to all factories in Sindh where operations specified in the Schedule are carried on. They declare these operations as hazardous and mandate material testing every twelve months. The rules define specific duties for occupiers, managers, and employees regarding protective equipment, hygiene, and health screenings.

name: MAJID BHURGRI LANGUAGE ENGINNEERING INSTITUTE EMPLOYEES (SERVICES) RULES, 2018

metadata.short_title: The Majid Bhurgri Language Engineering Institute Employees (Services) Rules, 2018
metadata.parent_law: The Majid Bhurgri Language Engineering Institute Act, 2018
metadata.one_line: Rules governing the appointment, promotion, transfer, and service conditions of employees of the Majid Bhurgri Language Engineering Institute.
metadata.summary: These rules regulate the recruitment, appointment, promotion, and transfer of employees within the Majid Bhurgri Language Engineering Institute. They define various terms related to service, pay scales, and committees responsible for selection. The rules specify that appointments are made based on recommendations from Selection Committees and adhere to minimum qualifications laid down in an appendix.

name: SINDH HIGH DENSITY DEVELOPMENT BOARD ACT, 2010 (REGULATIONS, 2022

metadata.short_title: The Sindh High Density Development Board Act, 2010 (Regulations, 2022)
metadata.parent_law: The Sindh High Density Development Board Act, 2010
repeals: Sindh High Density Development Board Act, 2010 (Repealed rules notified earlier in 2011)
metadata.one_line: Regulates building standards, zoning, and parking for high-density areas in Sindh.
metadata.summary: These regulations amend the Karachi Building & Town Planning Regulations, 2002 to address high-density development zones. They establish specific Floor Area Ratios (FAR), setbacks, and parking requirements for commercial and residential plots. The rules also mandate Environment Impact Assessments and adherence to international standards for mechanical and electrical systems.

name: SINDH LOCAL COUNCILS (AUCTIONING OF COLLECTION RIGHTS) RULES, 2016

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Local Councils (Auctioning of Collection Rights) Rules, 2016
metadata.administering_body: Local Government and Housing Town Planning Department
metadata.one_line: Rules governing the auctioning of collection rights for local council income in Sindh.
metadata.summary: These rules prescribe the procedure for Local Councils in Sindh to award contracts for the collection of income through public auctions. They define eligibility criteria for contractors, establish requirements for public notices and bid security, and set mechanisms for determining reserve prices based on historical income data. The document also outlines dispute resolution via arbitration under the Arbitration Act, 1940, conditions for contract cancellation, and the responsibilities of sureties and guarantors.

name: SINDH KATCHI ABADIS AUTHORITY LAW-COST HOUSING SCHEME REGULATION, 2009

metadata.short_title: SKAA Low-Cost Housing Scheme Regulations 2008
metadata.one_line: Regulations for low-cost housing schemes in Sindh, covering land allocation, utility services, and lease management.
metadata.summary: These regulations establish the framework for the Sindh Katchi Abadis Authority to launch low-cost housing schemes providing plots ranging from 80 to 120 sq. yards to shelterless persons. The document outlines the powers of the Authority and Director General regarding land acquisition, fund raising, and scheme implementation. It details procedures for plot allocation, utility service provision, lease management, and restrictions on land use changes or subdivision.

name: SINDH LOCAL COUNCILS (AUCTIONING OF COLLECTION RIGHTS) RULES, 2016

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Local Councils (Auctioning of Collection Rights) Rules, 2016
metadata.administering_body: Local Government and Housing Town Planning Department
metadata.one_line: Rules governing the auctioning of collection rights for Local Council income in Sindh.
metadata.summary: These rules prescribe the procedure for Local Councils in Sindh to award contracts for the collection of income through public auctions. They define eligible contractors, establish requirements for public notices and bid security, and set mechanisms for determining reserve prices based on historical income data. The document also outlines dispute resolution via arbitration under the Arbitration Act, 1940, and conditions for contract cancellation or repudiation.

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Industrial Relations Rules, 2021
metadata.parent_law: The Sindh Industrial Relations Act, 2013 (Sindh Act No. XXIX of 2013)
repeals: The Industrial Relations (Sind) Rules, 1973
metadata.one_line: Rules made by the Government of Sindh to regulate trade unions, strikes, and industrial relations under the Sindh Industrial Relations Act, 2013.
metadata.summary: These rules are made by the Government of Sindh in exercise of powers under the Sindh Industrial Relations Act, 2013. They establish definitions for workers and employers, prescribe forms for union registration and strike notices, and set limits on trade union executive membership. The rules also outline procedures for conciliation, settlement of disputes, and the maintenance of records in electronic form.

name: SINDH OCCUPATIONAL SAFETY AND HEALTH RUES, 2019

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Occupational Safety and Health Rules, 2019
metadata.parent_law: The Sindh Occupational Safety and Health Act, 2017
metadata.administering_body: Government of Sindh, Labour & Human Resources Department
metadata.one_line: Rules made by the Government of Sindh to prescribe safety standards and duties under the Sindh Occupational Safety and Health Act, 2017.
metadata.summary: These rules are made by the Government of Sindh in exercise of powers conferred by the Sindh Occupational Safety and Health Act, 2017. They define key terms such as 'construction site', 'lifting equipment', and 'biological monitoring' to ensure workplace safety. The rules assign general duties to employers regarding cleanliness, structural safety of buildings, and adherence to government regulations. Additionally, they establish standards for signage colors and provide forms for stability certificates and injury reporting.

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Public Service Commission (Functions) Rules, 2022
metadata.parent_law: The Sindh Public Service Commission Act, 2022
repeals: The Sindh Public Service Commission (Functions) Rules, 1990
metadata.administering_body: Government of Sindh, Services, General Administration and Coordination Department (Regulation Wing)
metadata.one_line: These rules define the functions of the Sindh Public Service Commission regarding recruitment and appointments.
metadata.summary: The Sindh Public Service Commission (Functions) Rules, 2022 were made by the Government of Sindh under section 12 of the Sindh Public Service Commission Act, 2022. These rules establish the procedures for conducting tests for initial recruitment to civil posts and other specified positions within the Province. They also define key terms such as 'appointing authority', 'Basic pay scale', and 'Test', and outline the process for submitting the Commission's advice to relevant authorities.

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Public Service Commission Regulations, 2021
metadata.parent_law: The Sindh Public Service Commission Act, 1989 (Sindh Act XI of 1989)
repeals: The Sindh Public Service Commission Regulations, 2006
metadata.one_line: Regulates the selection, recruitment, and allocation of services for posts in Sindh through competitive examinations.
metadata.summary: These regulations establish the framework for the Sindh Public Service Commission to conduct fair and transparent selection processes. They define terms related to applications, interviews, and examinations, including provisions for differently abled persons. The document outlines procedures for merit list preparation, candidate option allocation, and the power to remove anomalies.

name: SINDH REGISTRATION AND REGULATION OF FISHING JETTIES RULES 2022

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Registration and Regulation of Fishing Jetties Rules, 2022
metadata.max_penalty: seizure of jetty alongwith all equipment and fish
metadata.one_line: Rules for registration, licensing, and regulation of fishing jetties along the Sindh coast.
metadata.summary: These rules provide for the registration and licensing of all jetties operating along the Sindh coast. They establish a Marine Police force to monitor fisheries resources and create a Fisheries Conservation Fund. The rules specify fees for licenses based on jetty capacity and require prior approval for construction or alteration.

name: SINDH SALE TAX SPECIAL PROCEDURE (ONLINE INTEGRATION OF BUSINESS) RULES,2022

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Sales Tax Special Procedure (Online Integration of Business) Rules, 2022
metadata.parent_law: The Sindh Sales Tax on Services Act, 2011 (Sindh Act No. XII of 2011)
metadata.one_line: Rules for online integration of business POS systems with the Sindh Revenue Board for real-time sales reporting.
metadata.summary: These rules apply to registered persons providing specified services and online marketplaces acting as facilitators in Sindh. They mandate the integration of Point of Sale (POS) systems with the Board's computerized system for real-time reporting within 45 days of notification. The rules prescribe a service fee of one rupee per invoice, requirements for tax invoices generated by integrated POS, and procedures for mystery shopping and prize draws for compliant businesses.

name: SINDH SALE TAX SPECIAL PROCEDURE (ONLINE INTEGRATION OF BUSINESS) RULES,2022

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Sales Tax Special Procedure (Online Integration of Business) Rules, 2022
metadata.parent_law: The Sindh Sales Tax on Services Act, 2011 (Sindh Act No. XII of 2011) and the Sindh Revenue Board Act, 2010 (Sindh Act No. XI of 2010)
metadata.one_line: Rules for online integration of business POS systems with the Sindh Revenue Board for real-time sales reporting.
metadata.summary: These rules apply to registered persons providing specified services and online marketplaces acting as facilitators in Sindh. They mandate the integration of Point of Sale (POS) systems with the Board's computerized system for real-time reporting within 45 days of notification. The rules prescribe a service fee of one rupee per invoice, requirements for tax invoices generated by integrated POS, and procedures for mystery shopping and prize draws for compliant businesses.

name: SINDH MINES AND MINERALS GOVERNANCE RULES, 2023

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Mines and Minerals Governance Rules, 2023
metadata.territorial_extent: whole of the Province of Sindh
metadata.parent_law: The Sindh Mines and Minerals Governance Act, 2021
metadata.administering_body: Director General, Mines & Mineral Development Department, Govt. of Sindh
metadata.one_line: Rules made by the Government of Sindh to govern mining operations, licensing, and auctions under the 2021 Act.
metadata.summary: These rules are made by the Government of Sindh in exercise of powers conferred by the Sindh Mines and Minerals Governance Act, 2021. They establish the Mines Committee and Auction Committee to oversee mineral exploration, mining operations, and title grants within the Province of Sindh. The rules define key terms like drilling and environmental pollution, set conditions for mineral titles including foreign investment agreements, and outline procedures for licensing applications and royalty payments.

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Trust Rules, 2020
metadata.one_line: Rules made by the Government of Sindh to regulate the registration, maintenance, and annual reporting of trusts under the Sindh Trust Act, 2020.
metadata.summary: These rules provide the framework for registering trusts in Sindh, specifying required documents such as the Trust Deed, Memorandum of Association, and affidavits. They mandate verification processes involving the Director, Assistant Director, and Special Branch Police to check member backgrounds and criminal records. The rules also outline requirements for maintaining accounts, submitting annual asset details, and filing complaints regarding violations.

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Cooperative Societies Rules, 2020
repeals: Cooperative Societies Rules, 1927
metadata.one_line: Rules made by the Government of Sindh to regulate cooperative societies under the Sindh Cooperative Societies Act, 2020.
metadata.summary: These rules provide the framework for registering cooperative societies in Sindh, including application forms and bye-law requirements. They specify matters that societies must address in their bye-laws, such as member rights, fund custody, and profit distribution. The rules also outline the Registrar's powers regarding record-keeping, special meetings, and restrictions on loans and dividends.

metadata.short_title: Sindh Workers Compensation Rules, 2020
metadata.parent_law: Sindh Workers Compensation Act, 2015 (Sindh Act No.VII of 2016)
repeals: West Pakistan Women's Compensation Commencement Rules, 1961
metadata.administering_body: Government of Sindh (Department of Labour & Human Resources)
metadata.one_line: Rules made by the Government of Sindh to prescribe procedures for workers' compensation under the Sindh Workers Compensation Act, 2015.
metadata.summary: These rules were made by the Government of Sindh in exercise of powers conferred by Section 39 of the Sindh Workers Compensation Act, 2015. They provide for the short title and commencement, definitions, procedures for reviewing half-monthly payments, commutation of payments into lump sums, and the deposit of compensation for fatal accidents. The rules also outline the Commissioner's powers regarding inquiries, distribution of funds to dependents, investment of deposits, and the handling of appeals to the Tribunal.

name: SINDH PRISONS AND CORRECTIONS SERVICES RULES, 2019

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Prisons and Corrections Services Rules, 2019
metadata.territorial_extent: the whole of the Province of Sindh
metadata.parent_law: The Sindh Prisons and Corrections Services Act, 2019
establishes: Directorate of Corrections and Welfare of the Prisoners
metadata.one_line: Rules made by the Government of Sindh to regulate prisons and corrections services in the province.
metadata.summary: These rules are framed under the powers conferred by section 80 of the Sindh Prisons and Corrections Services Act, 2019. They extend to the whole of the Province of Sindh and cover the classification, establishment, management, discipline, and welfare of prisoners and prison staff. The rules define various terms related to prisons, officers, and procedures, and establish bodies like the Policy Board and the Directorate of Corrections.

name: SINDH WILDLIFE PROTECTION, PRESERVATION, CONSERVATION AND M MANAGEMENT RULES 2022

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Wildlife Protection, Preservation, Conservation and Management Rules, 2022
metadata.commencement: at once and deemed to have taken effect on and from commencement of Sindh Wildlife Protection, Preservation, Conservation and Management Act 2020
metadata.parent_law: Sindh Wildlife Protection, Preservation, Conservation and Management Act, 2020
metadata.one_line: Rules made by the Government of Sindh to regulate wildlife protection, preservation, conservation and management under the 2020 Act.
metadata.summary: These rules are made by the Government of Sindh in exercise of powers under the Sindh Wildlife Protection, Preservation, Conservation and Management Act, 2020. They define key terms related to wildlife species, trade permits, community involvement, and conservation principles specific to the province. The document outlines procedures for compensation, emergency rescue operations, and encourages volunteer participation in protecting endangered species like sea turtles and the Indus Dolphin.

metadata.one_line: This Act repeals various federal and provincial laws in Sindh and amends others to align with local statutes.
metadata.summary: The Sind Repealing and Amending Act, 1975 was enacted by the Provincial Assembly of Sindh to address obsolete or unnecessary laws. It expressly repeals a long list of Federal Acts, Ordinances, and previous Provincial Acts that were spent, unnecessary, or ceased to be in force. Additionally, the Act amends numerous other existing laws to update references, substitute specific clauses, and align provincial legislation with current administrative needs.

metadata.short_title: Sindh Hindu Marriage Rules, 2017
metadata.one_line: Rules for registering Hindu marriages in Sindh under the Sindh Hindus Marriage Act, 2016.
metadata.summary: These rules provide the framework for registering Hindu marriages within the Province of Sindh. They specify that registration must occur within 45 days of solemnization and require payment of prescribed fees along with CNICs of both spouses. The Union Council is mandated to maintain a specific register format, and an officer may issue a marriage certificate upon satisfaction of the form and witnesses.

name: Essential Commodities Price Control and Prevention of Profiteering and Hoarding Act, 2005

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Essential Commodities Price Control and Prevention of Profiteering and Hoarding Act, 2005
metadata.long_title: An act to provide for price control and prevention of profiteering on and hoarding of essential commodities.
establishes: District Controller of Prices and supplies
metadata.one_line: This Act provides for price control and prevention of profiteering and hoarding of essential commodities in Sindh.
metadata.summary: The Act empowers the Government of Sindh to regulate prices, production, movement, and distribution of essential commodities. It defines key terms such as 'dealer', 'essential commodity', and 'hoarding' to establish clear legal boundaries for market participants. The legislation grants District Controllers and Inspectors powers to check prices, seize articles, and impose fines for violations like failure to display price lists or selling above notified rates.

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Child Marriages Restraint Rules, 2016
metadata.parent_law: The Sindh Child Marriages Restraint Act, 2013 (Sindh Act No. XV of 2014)
metadata.one_line: Rules made by the Government of Sindh to regulate child marriages, define committees, and establish complaint mechanisms.
metadata.summary: These rules are made under the Sindh Child Marriages Restraint Act, 2013 to provide specific procedures for preventing child marriage. They establish Provincial and District Committees responsible for monitoring cases and assisting victims. The rules mandate age verification through CNICs or medical certificates and outline processes for filing complaints with Magistrates or Police.

name: PROVINCIAL DISASTER MANAGEMENT AUTHORITY SINDH SERVICE RULES 2016

metadata.short_title: The Provincial Disaster Management Authority Sindh Service Rules, 2016
metadata.one_line: Service rules for the Provincial Disaster Management Authority Sindh governing appointments, conduct, and administration.
metadata.summary: These rules establish the service framework for employees of the Provincial Disaster Management Authority Sindh. They cover initial appointments, probation periods, confirmation processes, and definitions of key terms like 'employee' and 'Authority'. The document also outlines regulations regarding employee conduct, asset disclosure, delegation of powers, and the constitution of committees to carry out routine functions.

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Senior Citizens Welfare Rules, 2021
metadata.parent_law: The Sindh Senior Citizens Welfare Act, 2014 (Sindh Act No. XXI of 2016)
metadata.administering_body: Social Welfare Department, Government of Sindh
metadata.one_line: Rules made by the Government of Sindh to regulate the Sindh Senior Citizens Council and District Committees under the 2014 Act.
metadata.summary: These rules establish the framework for the Sindh Senior Citizens Council and District Committees to manage welfare activities in the Province of Sindh. They define key terms, outline procedures for issuing the Senior Citizen (Azadi) Card, and set guidelines for conducting ordinary, special, and emergency meetings. The rules also mandate annual reporting, awareness campaigns, and coordination among government departments to support the elderly.

name: THE SINDH CENSARSHIP OF FILM RULES, 2014

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Censorship of Film Rules, 2014
repeals: Censorship of Films Rules, 1983
metadata.one_line: Rules made by the Government of Sindh to regulate the certification and censorship of films for public exhibition.
metadata.summary: These rules were framed under the powers conferred by section 19 of the Sindh Motion Pictures Act, 2011. They establish the Sindh Board of Film Censors and define terms such as 'applicant', 'Board', and 'foreign film'. The rules outline procedures for applying for certification, including submission requirements for prints and press books. Fees for various types of films and services are specified in the schedules. The rules also provide for the constitution of an Appellate Committee and repeal previous censorship rules from 1983.

name: THE SINDH EDUCATION FOUNDATION (EMPLOYEES SERVICE) RULES, 2021

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Education Foundation (Employees Service) Rules, 2021
repeals: Sindh Education Foundation, Employees Service Rules, 1999
metadata.administering_body: School Education and Literacy Department, Government of Sindh
metadata.one_line: These rules govern the service conditions, appointments, promotions, and benefits for employees of the Sindh Education Foundation.
metadata.summary: The Sindh Education Foundation (Employees Service) Rules, 2021 establish the framework for appointments, promotions, and service conditions for employees of the Sindh Education Foundation. The rules define key terms such as 'Appointing Authority' and 'Deputation', mandate advertising vacancies in three leading newspapers, and set age limits for initial appointments. Furthermore, the document outlines provisions regarding leave entitlements, gratuity calculations, conduct during probation, and the right to appeal against orders concerning gratuity sanctions.

name: NEW CAPTIVE POWER PLANTS SUBSIDY RULES, 2017

metadata.short_title: Sindh New Captive Power Plants Subsidy Rules, 2017
metadata.territorial_extent: whole of the Province of Sindh
metadata.parent_law: Sindh New Captive Power Plants Subsidy Act, 2017
metadata.one_line: These rules establish the NCPP Subsidy Committee and procedures for claiming tariff differential subsidies under the Sindh New Captive Power Plants Subsidy Act, 2017.
metadata.summary: The Sindh New Captive Power Plants Subsidy Rules, 2017 were made by the Government of Sindh to carry out the purposes of the Sindh New Captive Power Plants Subsidy Act, 2017. They establish the NCPP Subsidy Committee and define its composition, meeting procedures, and decision-making powers. The rules prescribe the method for power producers (claimants) to apply for tariff differential subsidies, including required documentation like invoices, payment proofs, and chartered accountant certificates. Applications must be submitted within specific timelines after invoice payment or the promulgation of the Act.

name: SINDH LETTERS OF ADMINISTRATION AND SUCCESSION CERTIFICATES RULES, 2020

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Letters of Administration and Succession Certificates Rules, 2021
metadata.parent_law: The Sindh Letters of Administration and Succession Certificates Act, 2021
metadata.one_line: Rules made by the Government of Sindh to prescribe procedures for Letters of Administration and Succession Certificates.
metadata.summary: These rules, made under the Sindh Letters of Administration and Succession Certificates Act, 2021, establish the procedure for applying for Letters of Administration or Succession Certificates. They define key terms such as 'applicant' and 'Authority', outline the required documents including death certificates and CNICs, and detail the process for publication of notices and bio-metric verification. The rules also specify fees for initial applications, duplicates, and amendments, along with provisions for refunds in case of declined applications.

name: INSTITUTE OF OPHTHALMOLOGY AND VISUAL SCIENCES EMPLOYEES (TERMS AND CONDITIONS OF SERVICE) RULES, 2021

metadata.short_title: Sindh Institute of Ophthalmology and Visual Sciences Employees (Terms and Conditions of Service) Rules, 2021
metadata.parent_law: Sindh Institute of Ophthalmology and Visual Sciences Act, 2013
repeals: Any legal instrument(s) governing the terms and condition of employees, existing immediately before the commencement of these rules
metadata.administering_body: Board of Directors of the Institute
metadata.one_line: Rules governing terms, conditions, recruitment, promotion, and service for employees of the Sindh Institute of Ophthalmology and Visual Sciences.
metadata.summary: These rules establish the terms and conditions of service for employees of the Sindh Institute of Ophthalmology and Visual Sciences. They define key terms such as 'employee', 'Board', and 'pay scale', and outline procedures for recruitment, promotion, probation, and retirement. The rules also cover provident fund contributions and empower the Board to remove difficulties in implementation.

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Human Rights Commission Rules, 2013
metadata.parent_law: The Sindh Protection of Human Rights Act, 2011
metadata.administering_body: Law, Parliamentary Affairs and Human Rights Department
metadata.one_line: Rules made by the Government of Sindh to regulate the conduct of business of the Sindh Human Rights Commission.
metadata.summary: These rules were made under the powers conferred by section 4(113-2013. 12) of the Sindh Protection of Human Rights Act, 2011. They define key terms such as 'Commission', 'Chairperson', and 'human rights' within the context of the Islamic Republic of Pakistan's 1973 Constitution. The rules establish the headquarters in Karachi, outline procedures for holding ordinary and special meetings, and detail the powers and functions of the Commission regarding studies, inspections, and case disposal.

name: SINDH NEW CAPTIVE POWER PLANTS SUBSIDY RULES, 2017

metadata.short_title: Sindh New Captive Power Plants Subsidy Rules, 2017
metadata.territorial_extent: whole of the Province of Sindh
metadata.parent_law: Sindh New Captive Power Plants Subsidy Act, 2017
metadata.one_line: These rules establish the NCPP Subsidy Committee and procedures for claiming tariff differential subsidies under the Act.
metadata.summary: These rules are made by the Government of Sindh to carry out the purposes of the Sindh New Captive Power Plants Subsidy Act, 2017. They establish the NCPP Subsidy Committee consisting of representatives from the Energy and Finance Departments to review subsidy applications. The rules define the application process, required documentation including chartered accountant certificates, and timelines for submitting claims for tariff differential amounts.

name: SINDH PROSCUTOTORS (APPOINTMENT AND CONDITIONS OF SERVICE) RULES, 2006

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Prosecutors (Appointment and Conditions of Service) Rules, 2006
metadata.parent_law: The Sindh Criminal Prosecution Service (Constitution, Functions and Powers) Ordinance, 2006
metadata.one_line: Rules made by the Government of Sindh regarding the appointment, conditions of service, and conduct of prosecutors.
metadata.summary: These rules are made under the powers of the Sindh Criminal Prosecution Service (Constitution, Functions and Powers) Ordinance, 2006 to regulate the appointment and service conditions of prosecutors in Sindh. They establish a Selection Committee for contract-based appointments and define procedures for initial appointments, promotions, transfers, and acting charges. The rules also outline eligibility criteria, conflict of interest provisions, removal processes, and pay scales for various prosecutorial positions.

name: SINDH PUBLIC SERVICE COMMISSION (APPOINTMENT OF CHAIRPERSON AND MEMBERS) RULES, 2022

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Public Service Commission (Appointment of Chairperson and Members) Rules, 2022
amends: The Sindh Public Service Commission (Appointment of Chairman and Members) Rules, 2017
repeals: The Sindh Public Service Commission (Appointment of Chairman and Members) Rules, 2017
metadata.administering_body: Services, General Administration & Coordination Department, Government of Sindh
metadata.one_line: These rules prescribe the appointment and removal procedures for the Chairperson and Members of the Sindh Public Service Commission.
metadata.summary: These rules provide the framework for appointing the Chairperson and Members of the Sindh Public Service Commission. They establish a Permanent High Powered Committee to scrutinize candidates based on specific criteria of eminence and integrity. The rules also outline the procedure for removal, financial provisions, and explicitly repeal the previous 2017 rules upon commencement.

name: SINDH WORKERS WELFARE BOARD EMPLOYEES (SERVICE) RULES, 2021

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Workers Welfare Board Employees (Service) Rules, 2021
metadata.parent_law: The Sindh Workers Welfare Fund Act, 2014
metadata.one_line: Rules made by the Government of Sindh to regulate and administer services of employees of the Sindh Workers Welfare Board.
metadata.summary: These rules are made under the powers of the Sindh Workers Welfare Fund Act, 2014 to regulate the services of employees of the Sindh Workers Welfare Board. They apply to persons appointed on regular basis in whole-time employment, excluding the Chairman, contract appointees, and deputation staff. The document defines key terms such as 'employee', 'pay', 'leave', and 'promotion' and outlines procedures for appointments by transfer and promotion.

name: THE DOMESTIC VIOLENCE (PREVENTION AND PROTECTION) RULES, 2016

metadata.short_title: The Domestic Violence (Prevention and Protection) Rules, 2016
metadata.parent_law: The Domestic Violence (Prevention and Protection) Act, 2013
metadata.one_line: These rules establish the Domestic Violence Commission and define procedures for protection officers, shelter homes, and medical facilities under the Act.
metadata.summary: These rules are made by the Government of Sindh to regulate the implementation of the Domestic Violence (Prevention and Protection) Act, 2013. They establish a Domestic Violence Commission consisting of sixteen members, including representatives from various departments, civil society, and the legal fraternity. The rules define key terms such as 'Complaint' and 'Counsellor', outline qualifications for commission members, and specify the roles and responsibilities of protection officers regarding shelter homes and medical facilities.

name: THE SINDH CIVIL SERVANTS ( PROVINCIAL MANAGEMENT SERVICE) RULES 2018

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Civil Servants (Provincial Management Service) Rules, 2018
repeals: The West Pakistan Civil Service (Executive Branch) Rules, 1964
Services and General Administration Department Notification No. SOI(S&GAD)1-5/92 dated the 25th September, 1993
S&GAD Notification No. SOX(SGA&CD)3-58/84 dated the 10 October, 1993
metadata.administering_body: Services, General Administration and Coordination Department
metadata.one_line: These rules establish the Provincial Management Service in Sindh, defining posts, appointment methods, and repealing earlier regulations.
metadata.summary: The Sindh Civil Servants (Provincial Management Service) Rules, 2018 were made by the Government of Sindh under section 26 of the Sindh Civil Servants Act, 1973. They define the Provincial Management Service (PMS), specify the nomenclature and grades of posts, and outline the method of appointment and qualifications. The rules also repeal specific earlier notifications regarding Deputy Secretary and Section Officer appointments in the Secretariat while providing transitional arrangements for existing incumbents.

name: THE SINDH CIVIL SERVANTS PROMOTION (BPS-18 TO BPS-21) RULES, 2022

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Civil Servants Promotion (BPS-18 to BPS-21) Rules, 2022
metadata.parent_law: The Sindh Civil Servants Act, 1973 (XIV of 1973)
subjects: Basic Pay Scales BPS-18 to BPS-21
metadata.administering_body: Services, General Administration and Coordination Department
metadata.one_line: Rules governing promotion of Sindh civil servants to Basic Pay Scales 18 through 21.
metadata.summary: These rules apply to the promotion of Civil Servants in the Province of Sindh to all posts reserved for promotion in their respective services or cadres within Basic Pay Scales 18 to 21. They establish the composition and meeting intervals for Provincial Selection Boards (PSB-I, PSB-II) and Departmental Promotion Committees (DPC). The rules define conditions for promotion, deferment, supersession, and acting charge appointments, including requirements for mandatory training.

name: THE SINDH PRIVATE EDUCATIONAL INSTITUTIONS (REGULATION & CONTROL) RULES, 2005.

metadata.short_title: The Sindh Private Educational Institutions (Regulation & Control) Rules, 2005
metadata.parent_law: The Sindh Private Educational Institutions (Regulation and Control) Ordinance, 2001
repeals: The Private Educational Institution (Regulation & Control) Rules, 2002
establishes: Monitoring, Evaluation and Quality Assurance Fund
metadata.administering_body: Government of Sindh, Education & Literacy Department
metadata.one_line: These rules regulate and control private educational institutions in Sindh regarding registration, inspection, and fees.
metadata.summary: These rules were made by the Government of Sindh under the powers of the Sindh Private Educational Institutions (Regulation and Control) Ordinance, 2001. They establish procedures for registering private educational institutions, constituting inspection committees, and setting fee structures. The rules also define the infrastructure, curriculum, and staff requirements that institutions must meet to obtain or renew registration.
